Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy 31, 190 (1958). toroidal_electric_field Convention-sensitive source toroidal_electric_field(r, dpsi_dt) Toroidal electric field $E_\varphi = -\dfrac{1}{2\pi R}\dfrac{\partial\psi}{\partial t}$. The inductive drive a startup has to work with: the loop voltage $-\partial\psi/\partial t$ spread around the torus at each major radius. NameTypeUnitDescription rarray_likemMajor radius. dpsi_dtarray_likeWb/sTime derivative of the full-weber poloidal flux, broadcastable against r. Returns —np.ndarrayV/mToroidal electric field. Convention dpsi_dt is in weber, not weber per radian: the $2\pi$ here is the one that turns a flux into a loop voltage, so passing a per-radian flux gives an answer $2\pi$ too small. Green’s-function flux (vaft.formula.green.green_psi_exact) is already full weber and needs no conversion. The sign is the one this expression gives; loop_voltage_from_total_flux disagrees with it on both sign and flux normalisation, which is #354 <https://github.com/VEST-Tokamak/vaft/issues/354>_ and still open. The start-up chain in vaft.formula.startup takes the magnitude of this field – an avalanche has no preferred direction – so it does not inherit the disagreement and must not be used to settle it. Validity · See Also · References Validity Machine-independent. Faraday’s law in axisymmetry, so it holds wherever the flux does; it says nothing on its own about whether that field will break the gas down, which also needs the connection length and the fill pressure. See Also vaft.formula.startup.lloyd_breakdown_field vaft.formula.startup.breakdown_margin References B. Lloyd et al., Nucl. Fusion 31 (1991) 2031, Sec. 2 (the toroidal electric field required for tokamak start-up). J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 11.1 (start-up and breakdown). toroidal_flux_from_q_psi Convention-sensitive source toroidal_flux_from_q_psi(q, psi_wb) Cumulative toroidal flux $\Phi(\psi)$ from the $q$ profile on a full-weber grid. \[\Phi(\psi) = \int_{\psi_a}^{\psi} q\,d\psi', \qquad \psi\ 	ext{in Wb}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qnp.ndarray-Safety factor on the flux grid. psi_wbnp.ndarrayWbPoloidal flux of the same surfaces, monotonic, full weber. Returns —np.ndarrayWbToroidal flux enclosed by each surface, starting at zero. Convention psi_wb is the IMAS Data Dictionary flux (COCOS 11-18). No $2\pi$ appears because $d\Phi/d\psi_{rad} = 2\pi q$ and $\psi_{wb} = 2\pi \psi_{rad}$ cancel; pass 2*np.pi*psi_rad for an EFIT or VFIT per-radian profile (vaft.data.eqdsk.ods_psi_to_wb_per_radian_factor settles which family an ODS holds). The orientation sign of $q$ and $\psi$ is not applied: a COCOS with $\sigma_{ho	heta\varphi} = -1$ gives a negative $\Phi$. Numerical notes · References Numerical notes Cumulative trapezoidal rule (scipy.integrate.cumulative_trapezoid via vaft.compat.cumtrapz_compat); second order in the grid spacing, and the result is the running integral, so its first element is zero. References O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. (17) and Table I. IMAS Data Dictionary, equilibrium.time_slice[:].profiles_1d.phi. triangularity_from_RZ_boundary Convention-sensitive source triangularity_from_RZ_boundary(R, Z, R0) Boundary triangularity $\delta$, the mean of the upper and lower values. \[\delta = 	frac{1}{2}(\delta_u + \delta_l), \qquad \delta_{u,l} =  rac{R_0 - R_{Z_{\max,\min}}}{a}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the boundary points. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the boundary points. R0floatmReference major radius; pass the geometric centre $(R_{\max} + R_{\min})/2$ for the IMAS definition. Returns —float-Mean triangularity. Convention The IMAS boundary.triangularity, which is defined as the mean of the two extremity values and not as a separate measurement. Measured at the two vertically extremal points. Until #365 this function read the boundary sample nearest $Z=0$ instead, which returned exactly $-1$ for every boundary whose parameterisation starts at the outboard midplane – that is, for every standard one – so no caller can have depended on the old number. Positive means the extremities sit inboard of R0. Limitations · See Also · References Limitations The mean is the right summary only for a boundary that is close to up-down symmetric; report $\delta_u$ and $\delta_l$ separately for a strongly asymmetric one. See Also triangularity_upper_from_RZ_boundary triangularity_lower_from_RZ_boundary vaft.process.equilibrium.contour_shape_parameters References IMAS Data Dictionary, equilibrium.time_slice[:].boundary.triangularity. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.1. triangularity_lower_from_RZ_boundary Convention-sensitive source triangularity_lower_from_RZ_boundary(R, Z, R0) Lower boundary triangularity $\delta_l$ from the contour’s lowest point. \[\delta_l =  rac{R_0 - R_{Z_{\min}}}{a}, \qquad a =  rac{R_{\max} - R_{\min}}{2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the boundary points. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the boundary points. R0floatmReference major radius; pass the geometric centre $(R_{\max} + R_{\min})/2$ for the IMAS definition. Returns —float-Lower triangularity. Convention The IMAS boundary.triangularity_lower definition, measured at the vertically extremal point rather than at a midplane crossing. Positive means the bottom of the plasma sits inboard of R0. An up-down symmetric boundary has $\delta_l = \delta_u$; the two differ only for an asymmetric one, which is why IMAS stores both. Limitations · See Also · References Limitations A degenerate contour of zero width divides by zero; no validation. The extremum is located to sub-vertex accuracy, so the result is only as good as the contour’s sampling near the bottom. See Also triangularity_upper_from_RZ_boundary triangularity_from_RZ_boundary References IMAS Data Dictionary, equilibrium.time_slice[:].boundary.triangularity_lower. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.1. triangularity_upper_from_RZ_boundary Convention-sensitive source triangularity_upper_from_RZ_boundary(R, Z, R0) Upper boundary triangularity $\delta_u$ from the contour’s highest point. \[\delta_u =  rac{R_0 - R_{Z_{\max}}}{a}, \qquad a =  rac{R_{\max} - R_{\min}}{2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the boundary points. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the boundary points. R0floatmReference major radius; pass the geometric centre $(R_{\max} + R_{\min})/2$ for the IMAS definition. Returns —float-Upper triangularity. Convention The IMAS boundary.triangularity_upper definition, measured at the vertically extremal point rather than at a midplane crossing. Positive means the top of the plasma sits inboard of R0. R0 is the caller’s to choose because a boundary offset from its own bounding box has no single right centre; the IMAS value is the geometric centre, which is what vaft.process.equilibrium.contour_shape_parameters uses. Limitations · See Also · References Limitations A degenerate contour of zero width divides by zero; no validation. The extremum is located to sub-vertex accuracy, so the result is only as good as the contour’s sampling near the top. See Also triangularity_lower_from_RZ_boundary triangularity_from_RZ_boundary r_at_z_extremum_from_RZ_contour References IMAS Data Dictionary, equilibrium.time_slice[:].boundary.triangularity_upper. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.1. vacuum_toroidal_field Convention-sensitive source vacuum_toroidal_field(B0, R0, R) Vacuum toroidal field of a set of toroidal-field coils. \[B_\phi(R) =  rac{B_0 R_0}{R}\] NameTypeUnitDescription B0float or np.ndarrayTToroidal field at the reference radius $R_0$. R0float or np.ndarraymReference major radius. Rfloat or np.ndarraymMajor radius at which the field is wanted. Returns —float or np.ndarrayTToroidal field, with the sign of B0. Convention Signed: $B_\phi$ carries the sign of B0 along $+\hat\phi$ (counter-clockwise seen from above). $R B_\phi$ is the constant $F$ of a vacuum region. Raises ValueError R or R0 is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · See Also · References Physical interpretation Ampère’s law around the torus: the coil current linked by a circle of radius $R$ is the same for every $R$ inside the coils, so the field falls as $1/R$ – stronger on the high-field (inboard) side, and the origin of the grad-B and curvature drifts. Assumptions Axisymmetric coils (no ripple), no plasma current or diamagnetism. See Also vaft.diagram.hfs_lfs_field : the canonical diagram of this relation. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.1. verify_kadomtsev_constraint source verify_kadomtsev_constraint(mu_rho, mu_beta, mu_nu, a_P) Reconstruct the Kadomtsev constraint value from dimensionless indices. \[x = 5 + \mu_ho(1 + \alpha_P) -  rac{3}{2}\left(\mu_ho + 2\mu_ eta - 4\mu_
u - 2ight)\] which should return 5 when the dimensionless mapping of dimensionless_scaling_coeffs_from_engineering_scaling_coeffs preserves the identity $\alpha_L + 2\alpha_n + \alpha_B^* - 3\alpha_P = 5$. NameTypeUnitDescription mu_rhofloat-Gyroradius index. mu_betafloat-Beta index. mu_nufloat-Collisionality index. a_Pfloat-Engineering exponent of the heating power. Returns —float-Reconstructed constraint value, 5 for a consistent mapping. Limitations · References Limitations Evaluates a different expression from check_kadomtsev_constraint (which uses the engineering exponents directly) and the two need not agree; tracked in #351. References B. B. Kadomtsev, Sov. J. Plasma Phys. 1 (1975) 295. T. C. Luce, C. C. Petty and J. G. Cordey, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 50 (2008) 043001. vertical_magnetic_field_from_psi Convention-sensitive source vertical_magnetic_field_from_psi(psi, R, Z, cocos=None) Vertical magnetic field $B_Z$ from the poloidal flux map. \[B_Z = - rac{k}{R}\, rac{\partial\psi}{\partial R}, \qquad k =  rac{\sigma_{R\varphi Z}\,\sigma_{B_p}}{(2\pi)^{e_{B_p}}}\] with $k$ from poloidal_field_factor (Sauter Eq. 20). NameTypeUnitDescription psinp.ndarrayWb/rad or WbPoloidal flux along the radial direction; a 1-D cut in $R$. Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the samples, monotonic. Znp.ndarraymVertical coordinate of the samples, unused by the derivative. cocosint or None, optional-COCOS index fixing sign and $2\pi$; None = per-radian, $k=-1$. Returns —np.ndarrayTVertical field on the samples. Convention cocos=None assumes psi in Wb/rad with $\sigma_{B_p}\sigma_{R\varphi Z} =-1$ (COCOS 2/3/6/7). A full-weber map (IMAS Data Dictionary, vaft.formula.green.green_psi_exact) passed without cocos overestimates $|B_Z|$ by $2\pi$; convert with vaft.data.eqdsk.ods_psi_to_wb_per_radian_factor or pass the index. Assumptions · Numerical notes · References Assumptions Axisymmetry. The derivative is taken along the first axis of psi against R, so the map must be indexed [R] or [R, Z]. Numerical notes numpy.gradient (second-order interior, first-order one-sided ends). References O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. (20) and Table I. volume_from_RZ_boundary source volume_from_RZ_boundary(R, Z) Plasma volume from a boundary polygon, mean-radius approximation. \[V = 2\pi\oint R\,Z\,dR \approx 2\pi\,A_{\mathrm{poly}}\, ar R\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the boundary vertices, closed or open polygon. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the boundary vertices. Returns —floatm^3Volume of the solid of revolution. Assumptions · Limitations · Numerical notes · References Assumptions $ ar R$ is the arithmetic mean of the vertex radii, not the area centroid demanded by Pappus’ theorem; exact only for a boundary symmetric about $ ar R$. Limitations On VEST flux surfaces the mean-radius factorisation differs from the exact contour integral by up to ~6 % at the edge; use exact_volume_from_RZ_contour for a reported volume. Numerical notes Shoelace formula for the polygon area (exact for straight edges); the polygon is implicitly closed by numpy.roll. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.1 (plasma volume of a toroidal cross-section).

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/stabilit.title: Formula reference: stability
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/stabilit.body:
Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.stability: 37 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("stability.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview This module provides functions for calculating various stability parameters including beta limits, ballooning stability, MHD stability criteria, operational limits, and transport parameters. SymbolMeaningUnit β_Nnormalized beta- β_ppoloidal beta- β_ttoroidal beta- q_95safety factor at 95% flux surface- αballooning parameter- smagnetic shear- n_GGreenwald density limit10¹⁹ m⁻³ P_Lpower limitW ν*effective collisionality- v_AAlfven speedm/s c_sion-sound speedm/s τ_Eenergy confinement times Functions ballooning_alpha_from_p_B_RNormalised pressure gradient $\alpha$ of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning model. Convention ballooning_radial_wavenumberRadial wavenumber of a ballooning mode along the field line, in the $s$-$\alpha$ local frame. Convention ballooning_stability_criterionDistance from the first ballooning stability boundary $\alpha_{crit} \approx 0.6\,s$. Empirical beta_N_from_beta_a_B0_IpNormalised beta in the Troyon convention, %·m·T/MA. Convention beta_pol_from_beta_torPoloidal beta from toroidal beta, cylindrical relation. beta_stability_boundaryDeprecated: fraction-convention twin of kink_stability_criterion; use the troyon boundary. Empirical Deprecated beta_tor_from_beta_polToroidal beta from poloidal beta, cylindrical relation. c_s_from_Te_Ti_miIsothermal ion sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(T_e + T_i)/m_i}$. Convention collisionality_from_n_T_B_RElectron collisionality figure $6.921	imes10^{-18}\,n_e R_0/(T_e^2 B_t)$. Convention delta_prime_from_outer_derivativesTearing stability index from the outer solution’s derivatives at the rational surface. Convention empirical_li_qaSurveyed $(q_a, l_i)$ operating points from the JET disruption study. Empirical field_line_labelClebsch field-line label on a flux surface in straight-field-line coordinates. Convention greenwald_densityGreenwald density limit $n_G$. Empirical Convention greenwald_fractionGreenwald fraction $f_G = n_e/n_G$. Convention helical_harmonicThe real perturbation carried by one complex $m/n$ Fourier coefficient. Convention helical_phaseHelical phase of an $m/n$ perturbation at a point on a flux surface. Convention island_pendulum_hamiltonianLocal flux function of a constant-$\psi$ magnetic island. Convention island_separatrix_half_widthRadial half-width of the island separatrix at a given helical phase. Convention island_width_from_resonant_fluxFull magnetic island width from the pitch-resonant flux. Convention kadomtsev_mixing_radiusKadomtsev mixing radius: where the $m/n = 1/1$ helical flux returns to its axis value. Convention kink_stability_criterionDeprecated: heuristic margin against an unsourced $ eta_{N,crit} = 2.8\,q_{95}$; use the troyon boundary. Empirical Deprecated li_from_qa_empiricalInternal inductance at a given $q_a$ by interpolating the JET survey points. Empirical magnetosonic_phase_speedsFast and slow magnetosonic phase speeds at angle $	heta$ to $\mathbf B_0$. plasma_stability_marginsDeprecated: beta, $q_{95}$ and density margins built on the unsourced $0.028\,q_{95}$ beta limit. Convention Deprecated power_limit_from_betaEnergy-like figure $ eta_N B_0^2 V/(2\mu_0)$ labelled a power limit. power_limit_from_qExpression $2\pi R_0 I_p/(\mu_0 q_{95})$ labelled a power limit. resonant_flux_from_deltaPitch-resonant flux from the resonance parameter and the surface geometry. Convention rhostar_from_Te_a_BtNormalised electron gyroradius $ho_e/a$. Convention s_alpha_ballooning_eigenmodeThe most unstable localised eigenmode of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation with inertia. Convention s_alpha_ballooning_solutionThe even solution $F(	heta)$ of the marginal $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation. Convention s_alpha_ballooning_stableIdeal ballooning stability of the circular $s$-$\alpha$ model. Convention s_alpha_curvature_driveNormal-curvature drive of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation along the extended angle. Convention s_alpha_marginal_alphaFirst and second ballooning stability boundaries of the $s$-$\alpha$ model. Convention sawtooth_stability_criterionDeprecated: heuristic margin against an unsourced $ eta_{p,crit} = 0.3\,(1 - q_0)$; no replacement. Empirical Deprecated shear_alfven_frequencyFrequency of the ideal shear Alfven wave in a uniform plasma. slab_perturbed_fluxHelical flux of a sheared slab with a tearing- or twisting-parity perturbation. Convention v_alfven_from_B_n_miAlfven speed $v_A = B/\sqrt{\mu_0 n m_i}$. No function matches. ballooning_alpha_from_p_B_R Convention-sensitive source ballooning_alpha_from_p_B_R(p, B, R, q) Normalised pressure gradient $\alpha$ of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning model. \[\alpha = - rac{2\mu_0 R q^2}{B^2}\, rac{dp}{dr}\] NameTypeUnitDescription pfloat or np.ndarrayPaPressure along a radial cut. Bfloat or np.ndarrayTMagnetic field strength. Rfloat or np.ndarraymMajor radius of the samples, monotonic. qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor on the same surfaces. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Ballooning parameter in the Connor-Hastie-Taylor normalisation. Convention Connor, Hastie and Taylor [1] define $\alpha$ with the $q^2$ and with $r$ the minor radius. Until #364 this omitted the $q^2$ entirely, so it returned $\alpha/q^2$ – an order of magnitude at $q \simeq 3$ – while ballooning_stability_criterion compared the result against $0.6\,s$ as though it were the standard $\alpha$. Limitations · Numerical notes · References Limitations The derivative is still taken against the major radius $R$, not the minor radius $r$ of the definition. For a large-aspect-ratio circular plasma on the outboard midplane the two coincide, which is the case this is used for; anywhere else the caller must supply a minor-radius abscissa. Numerical notes numpy.gradient along the supplied axis (second-order interior, first-order ends), sign-sensitive to the direction of R. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40 (1978) 396, Eq. (2). J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.13 (ballooning modes). ballooning_radial_wavenumber Convention-sensitive source ballooning_radial_wavenumber(k_y, s, theta, alpha=0.0, theta0=0.0) Radial wavenumber of a ballooning mode along the field line, in the $s$-$\alpha$ local frame. \[k_x = k_y\,\Lambda,\qquad \Lambda = s(	heta - 	heta_0) - \alpha(\sin	heta - \sin	heta_0)\] NameTypeUnitDescription k_yfloat or np.ndarray1/mBinormal wavenumber, set by the toroidal mode number. sfloat or np.ndarray-Magnetic shear. thetafloat or np.ndarrayradExtended poloidal angle along the field line, the parallel coordinate $z$. alphafloat or np.ndarray-Normalised pressure gradient; zero gives the sheared-slab relation. theta0float or np.ndarrayradBallooning angle, where $k_x$ vanishes. Returns —float or np.ndarray1/m$k_x$, same units as k_y. Convention The $\Lambda$ of s_alpha_curvature_drive and s_alpha_ballooning_solution: $k_\perp^2 = k_y^2(1 + \Lambda^2)$. With $\alpha = 0$ it is the sheared slab’s $k_x(z) = k_{x0} + k_y\hat s z$ with $z = 	heta$ and $k_{x0} = -k_y\hat s	heta_0$; in physical length $z_\mathrm{phys} = qR	heta$ and $\hat s = qR/L_s$. Constant $k_y$ along the line, as in the field-aligned $(x, y, z)$ frame. Codes differ in the sign of $	heta_0$: gyrokinetic flux-tube codes (GS2, GENE) define it through $k_{x0}/(\hat s k_y)$, which is $-	heta_0$ here. Raises ValueError A non-finite input. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Magnetic shear tilts the phase fronts of a mode that is aligned with the field: moving along the line, neighbouring field lines slide past each other, so a fixed binormal structure acquires a growing radial wavenumber – the link between ballooning geometry and sheared-slab models. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Proc. R. Soc. A 365, 1 (1979). ballooning_stability_criterion Empirical fit source ballooning_stability_criterion(alpha, s) Distance from the first ballooning stability boundary $\alpha_{crit} \approx 0.6\,s$. \[\Delta = \alpha - \alpha_{crit}, \qquad \alpha_{crit} = 0.6\,s\] NameTypeUnitDescription alphafloat or np.ndarray-Ballooning parameter in the Connor-Hastie-Taylor normalisation. sfloat or np.ndarray-Magnetic shear. Returns marginfloat or np.ndarray-$\alpha - \alpha_{crit}$; positive means unstable. alpha_critfloat or np.ndarray-The threshold $0.6\,s$. Validity · Limitations · References Validity Empirical fit. A straight-line approximation of the first-stability boundary of the circular $s$-$\alpha$ diagram [1] for moderate shear ($0.3 \lesssim s \lesssim 1.5$). The boundary itself, computed from the ballooning equation, is s_alpha_marginal_alpha: it leaves this line at small shear and has a second-stable region beyond $\alpha_2(s)$. Limitations Ignores shaping, which raises the boundary, and the second-stable region; uncited coefficient (read from the diagram). References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40 (1978) 396, Fig. 1. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.13. beta_N_from_beta_a_B0_Ip Convention-sensitive source beta_N_from_beta_a_B0_Ip(beta_percent, a, B0, I_p_MA) Normalised beta in the Troyon convention, %·m·T/MA. \[ eta_N =  rac{ eta[\%]\;a[\mathrm{m}]\;B_0[\mathrm{T}]}{I_p[\mathrm{MA}]}\] NameTypeUnitDescription beta_percentfloat%Toroidal beta in percent, not as a fraction. afloatmMinor radius. B0floatTToroidal field on axis. I_p_MAfloatMAPlasma current in megaamperes. Returns —float%·m·T/MANormalised beta, directly comparable with the Troyon limit. Convention Percent and megaamperes, which is how Troyon [1] and the ITER Physics Basis [2] quote $ eta_N$ and the only convention in which the limit $ eta_N \lesssim 2.8$ means anything. The parameter names carry their units because this function used to take SI – a fraction and amperes – and return $10^{-8}$ times the conventional number, which no rescaling of the output fixes for a reader comparing against 2.8 (#349). Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The pressure a tokamak can hold scales with $I_p/(aB_0)$, so dividing it out leaves a figure that is comparable across machines; exceeding ~2.8 means an ideal-MHD beta limit rather than a machine-specific one. References F. Troyon et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 26 (1984) 209. ITER Physics Expert Groups, Nucl. Fusion 39 (1999) 2175, Ch. 3, Sec. 2.1 (definition of $ eta_N$). beta_pol_from_beta_tor source beta_pol_from_beta_tor(beta_tor, q_95, epsilon) Poloidal beta from toroidal beta, cylindrical relation. \[ eta_p =  eta_t\left( rac{q}{\varepsilon}ight)^2\] NameTypeUnitDescription beta_torfloat-Toroidal beta. q_95float-Safety factor at the 95% flux surface. epsilonfloat-Inverse aspect ratio $a/R_0$, strictly positive. Returns —float-Poloidal beta. Raises ValueError When epsilon is not strictly positive, since the relation divides by it [-]. Assumptions · Limitations · References Assumptions Circular, large-aspect-ratio cylinder in which $B_p/B_t = \varepsilon/q$. Limitations Until #363 the $1/\varepsilon^2$ was missing, so the result was right only at $\varepsilon = 1$ and low by $\varepsilon^2$ everywhere else – a factor of about 2 at the $\varepsilon \simeq 0.7$ of a spherical tokamak and more than 10 at a conventional $\varepsilon \simeq 0.3$. Round-tripping through beta_tor_from_beta_pol hid it, because both directions were wrong by the same factor. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.5 (relation between $ eta$, $ eta_p$ and $q$). beta_stability_boundary Empirical fitDeprecated source beta_stability_boundary(beta_N, q_95) Deprecated: fraction-convention twin of kink_stability_criterion; use the troyon boundary. The $q_{95}$ factor has no source (#350). Since #349 $ eta_N$ is in %·m·T/MA, where the sourced limit is vaft.formula.boundaries.get_boundary("troyon") ($\approx 2.76$). Results are unchanged; a DeprecationWarning is emitted. \[\Delta =  eta_N -  eta_{N,crit}, \qquad  eta_{N,crit} = 0.028\,q_{95}\] NameTypeUnitDescription beta_Nfloat-Normalised beta as a fraction (Troyon’s 2.8 % is 0.028). q_95float-Safety factor at the 95% flux surface. Returns marginfloat-$ eta_N -  eta_{N,crit}$; positive means the limit is exceeded. beta_N_critfloat-The threshold $0.028\,q_{95}$. Validity · References Validity Empirical fit. The fraction-convention twin of kink_stability_criterion (2.8 versus 0.028); the Troyon coefficient [1] is the only sourced part, the $q_{95}$ factor is not. plasma_stability_margins builds on this function, so it lives in the fraction convention. Tracked in #350. References F. Troyon et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 26 (1984) 209. beta_tor_from_beta_pol source beta_tor_from_beta_pol(beta_pol, q_95, epsilon) Toroidal beta from poloidal beta, cylindrical relation. \[ eta_t =  eta_p\left( rac{\varepsilon}{q}ight)^2\] NameTypeUnitDescription beta_polfloat-Poloidal beta. q_95float-Safety factor at the 95% flux surface. epsilonfloat-Inverse aspect ratio $a/R_0$, strictly positive. Returns —float-Toroidal beta. Raises ValueError When epsilon is not strictly positive [-]. Assumptions · Limitations · References Assumptions Circular, large-aspect-ratio cylinder; exact inverse of beta_pol_from_beta_tor. Limitations Carried the same missing $\varepsilon^2$ as its inverse until #363. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.5. c_s_from_Te_Ti_mi Convention-sensitive source c_s_from_Te_Ti_mi(T_e_keV, T_i_keV, m_i=1.67262192e-27) Isothermal ion sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(T_e + T_i)/m_i}$. \[c_s = \sqrt{ rac{\gamma_eT_e + \gamma_iT_i}{m_i}}, \qquad \gamma_e = \gamma_i = 1\] NameTypeUnitDescription T_e_keVfloatkeVElectron temperature. T_i_keVfloatkeVIon temperature. m_ifloat, optionalkgIon mass; default the proton mass. Returns —floatm/sIon sound speed. Convention Isothermal closure ($\gamma = 1$ for both species); the adiabatic $\gamma_i = 3$ used for ion acoustic waves gives a speed larger by up to $\sqrt{(T_e + 3T_i)/(T_e + T_i)}$. Both depend on the flux surface and not on the perturbation, so $G$ is a property of the equilibrium and is measured once for it rather than rebuilt per run. Raises ValueError n_tor is not a positive mode number. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · Validity · Limitations · References Physical interpretation $\Delta$ says how much the resonant field is discontinuous across the surface; $G$ converts that discontinuity into the flux the singular current drives. The minus sign is GPEC’s: measured, the phase of $n\,\Phi_\mathrm{res}/\Delta$ is exactly 180 degrees. Assumptions That $G$ was measured on the same equilibrium. It is not transferable between equilibria, and nothing here can detect a mismatch. Validity Measured on the DIII-D 147131 reference, $n\,\Phi_\mathrm{res}/\Delta$ agrees across n = 1, 2 and 3 at every shared rational surface to within 0.6 per cent, and the values the three modes report at different surfaces fall on one smooth curve in $q$ – which is what makes $G$ interpolable in $\psi$ from the surfaces any single run reaches. Limitations The 0.6 per cent spread is systematic rather than noise: it grows monotonically from n = 1 to n = 3, which is the vacuum Green’s function’s own weak dependence on the toroidal mode number. A study needing better than that has to build the inductance rather than measure $G$. References GPEC/gpec/gpout.f:1690-1705 for the chain $\Delta 	o I_\mathrm{res} 	o \Phi_\mathrm{res}$, and GPEC/gpec/gpvacuum.f:236-342 for the inductance $G$ absorbs. rhostar_from_Te_a_Bt Convention-sensitive source rhostar_from_Te_a_Bt(Te_eV, a_minor, B_t) Normalised electron gyroradius $ho_e/a$. \[ho_* =  rac{ho_e}{a}, \qquad ho_e =  rac{\sqrt{2 m_e e T_e}}{e B_t} = \sqrt{ rac{2m_e}{e}}\; rac{\sqrt{T_e}}{B_t}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Te_eVfloateVElectron temperature. a_minorfloatmMinor radius. B_tfloatTToroidal field. Returns —float-Normalised electron gyroradius. Convention Thermal speed $\sqrt{2T/m}$ and the toroidal field, normalised by the minor radius: the ITER Physics Basis definition [1], and the electron counterpart of vaft.formula.equilibrium.normalized_larmor_radius_from_M_T_a_Bt, which this delegates to so the two cannot drift. Until #348 this multiplied by $a$ instead of dividing, omitted the constant $\sqrt{2m_e/e} = 3.37	imes10^{-6}$ m T eV$^{-1/2}$, and ignored an m_e argument it accepted – so the result was neither dimensionless nor proportional to $ho_*$ across devices, and no rescaling recovered it. The dead m_e parameter is gone with the defect. References References ITER Physics Expert Groups, Nucl. Fusion 39 (1999) 2175, Ch. 2, Sec. 6 (dimensionless parameters). s_alpha_ballooning_eigenmode Convention-sensitive source s_alpha_ballooning_eigenmode(s, alpha, theta_max=18.84955592153876, n_points=1201) The most unstable localised eigenmode of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation with inertia. \[ rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	heta}\left[(1+\Lambda^{2}) rac{\mathrm{d}F}{\mathrm{d}	heta}ight] + \alpha\,(\cos	heta + \Lambda\sin	heta)\,F = \hat\gamma^2\,(1+\Lambda^{2})\,F,\qquad F(\pm	heta_\mathrm{max}) = 0\] NameTypeUnitDescription sfloat-Magnetic shear. alphafloat-Normalised pressure gradient. theta_maxfloatradHalf-length of the extended-angle interval, positive. n_pointsint-Grid points on $[-	heta_\mathrm{max}, 	heta_\mathrm{max}]$, at least 101. Returns growth_rate_squaredfloat-$\hat\gamma^2 = \gamma^2 q^2R^2/v_A^2$ of the most unstable mode; positive is unstable. thetanp.ndarrayradExtended angle. Fnp.ndarray- The eigenfunction, even, normalised to $\max F = 1$ with $F(0) > 0$. Convention $\Lambda = s	heta - \alpha\sin	heta$ and the operator of s_alpha_ballooning_solution; the inertia term $(1+\Lambda^2)$ is $k_\perp^2$ along the line and the growth rate is in Alfvén units $v_A/(qR)$, the circular large-aspect-ratio normalisation. Second-order finite differences, a symmetric generalised eigenproblem, Dirichlet ends: for a stable surface the largest eigenvalue is near zero and negative (the discretised continuum), for an unstable one it is positive and the mode decays well inside the interval. The matrix is scaled by $M^{-1/2}$ to a symmetric tridiagonal one, so the cost is linear in n_points. Raises ValueError A non-positive theta_max or too few points. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · Validity · References Physical interpretation The mode balloons: largest at $	heta = 0$, the outboard midplane where the curvature is bad, and decaying over a few poloidal transits of the extended angle – the “ballooning” the name refers to. Assumptions As s_alpha_ballooning_stable; ideal MHD, incompressible, $n 	o \infty$. Validity The unstable mode decays over $\sim 1/\hat\gamma$ in $	heta$, so the Dirichlet box needs $	heta_\mathrm{max} \gg 1/\hat\gamma$; near a stability boundary $\hat\gamma 	o 0$ and the box stabilises the marginal mode. With the default $6\pi$ a verdict within about $0.015$ of the boundary in $\alpha$ is unreliable (at $s = 1$ the modes for $\alpha \in (0.61, 0.625)$ come out stable while s_alpha_ballooning_stable finds them unstable); use s_alpha_ballooning_stable for the verdict and this function for the mode structure and growth rate away from the boundary. Like that function it needs $s \gtrsim 0.05$ to resolve the envelope. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 396 (1978). J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Proc. R. Soc. A 365, 1 (1979). s_alpha_ballooning_solution Convention-sensitive source s_alpha_ballooning_solution(s, alpha, theta_max=25.132741228718345, step=0.02) The even solution $F(	heta)$ of the marginal $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation. \[ rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	heta}\left[(1+\Lambda^{2}) rac{\mathrm{d}F}{\mathrm{d}	heta}ight] + \alpha\,(\cos	heta + \Lambda\sin	heta)\,F = 0,\qquad F(0) = 1,\ F'(0) = 0\] NameTypeUnitDescription sfloat-Magnetic shear. alphafloat-Normalised pressure gradient. theta_maxfloatradEnd of the extended-angle interval. stepfloatradFixed fourth-order Runge-Kutta step. Raises ValueError theta_max or step is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The marginal ($\omega^2 = 0$) solution along the field line on the extended angle – not a localised eigenfunction: a stable $F$ grows without decaying. A zero crossing means a localised perturbation can release energy. Assumptions As s_alpha_ballooning_stable. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 396 (1978). s_alpha_ballooning_stable Convention-sensitive source s_alpha_ballooning_stable(s, alpha, theta_max=125.66370614359172, step=0.02) Ideal ballooning stability of the circular $s$-$\alpha$ model. \[ rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	heta}\left[(1+\Lambda^{2}) rac{\mathrm{d}F}{\mathrm{d}	heta}ight] + \alpha\,(\cos	heta + \Lambda\sin	heta)\,F = 0, \qquad \Lambda = s	heta - \alpha\sin	heta\] NameTypeUnitDescription sfloat or np.ndarray-Magnetic shear $r q’/q$. alphafloat or np.ndarray-Normalised pressure gradient $-2\mu_0 R q^{2} p’/B^{2}$. theta_maxfloatradExtent of the ballooning-angle integration. stepfloatradFixed fourth-order Runge-Kutta step. Returns —bool or np.ndarray-True where the marginal ballooning equation is stable, broadcast over s and alpha. Convention Connor-Hastie-Taylor normalisation: $\alpha > 0$ for pressure falling outwards (ballooning_alpha_from_p_B_R), $s > 0$ for $q$ rising outwards. Newcomb’s criterion on the even solution, $F(0) = 1$, $F’(0) = 0$: the point is unstable if $F$ crosses zero anywhere on $0 < 	heta \le 	heta_\mathrm{max}$. Raises ValueError theta_max or step is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · Validity · Numerical notes · References Physical interpretation $\alpha\cos	heta$ is the bad-curvature drive on the outboard side and $\Lambda$ the local shear that bends field lines against it. Raising $\alpha$ first destabilises (first stability boundary) and then, through the $-\alpha\sin	heta$ term that makes the local shear vanish on the outboard side and reverse elsewhere, restabilises (second stability). Assumptions Large aspect ratio, circular shifted flux surfaces, infinite toroidal mode number, marginal stability ($\omega^{2} = 0$). Validity $s \gtrsim 0.05$. Towards zero shear the solutions decay only algebraically and a finite theta_max resolves the boundary progressively worse; at $s \le 0$ the model is stable. Numerical notes A fixed-step integrator, vectorised over the broadcast inputs, so the result is deterministic and a whole $(s, \alpha)$ grid costs one pass. With the defaults, halving step does not move the boundary at the 1e-4 level; extending theta_max to $2560\pi$ moves $\alpha_1$ by about 0.012 at $s = 0.1$ and 0.002 at $s = 1$. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 396 (1978). J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.13. s_alpha_curvature_drive Convention-sensitive source s_alpha_curvature_drive(theta, s, alpha, theta0=0.0) Normal-curvature drive of the $s$-$\alpha$ ballooning equation along the extended angle. \[K(	heta) = \cos	heta + \Lambda\sin	heta,\qquad \Lambda = s(	heta - 	heta_0) - \alpha(\sin	heta - \sin	heta_0)\] NameTypeUnitDescription thetafloat or np.ndarrayradExtended ballooning angle, not restricted to one period. sfloat-Magnetic shear. alphafloat-Normalised pressure gradient. theta0floatradBallooning angle $	heta_0$ (radial-wavenumber parameter). Returns —float or np.ndarray-$K$; the drive $\alpha K F$ is destabilising where $K > 0$. Convention The coefficient of $\alpha F$ in the equation of s_alpha_ballooning_stable (there $	heta_0 = 0$). $\cos	heta$ is the normal curvature – bad (positive) on the outboard side – and $\Lambda\sin	heta$ the geodesic curvature weighted by the local shear. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Where the mode sits along the field line decides whether pressure drives it: it balloons where $K > 0$, on the outboard, bad-curvature side, and is stabilised by field-line bending elsewhere. $	heta_0$ slides the point of zero local shear along the line. Assumptions As s_alpha_ballooning_stable: large aspect ratio, circular shifted surfaces, infinite toroidal mode number. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 396 (1978). s_alpha_marginal_alpha Convention-sensitive source s_alpha_marginal_alpha(s, alpha_max=6.0, resolution=0.001) First and second ballooning stability boundaries of the $s$-$\alpha$ model. \[\alpha_1(s) = \min\{\alpha : 	ext{unstable}\}, \qquad \alpha_2(s) = \max\{\alpha : 	ext{unstable}\}\] NameTypeUnitDescription sfloat or np.ndarray-Magnetic shear $r q’/q$. alpha_maxfloat-Upper end of the searched $\alpha$ range. resolutionfloat-Bisection tolerance on each boundary. Returns alpha_firstfloat or np.ndarray-Lowest unstable $\alpha$: the first stability boundary; nan where no instability is found. alpha_secondfloat or np.ndarray-Highest unstable $\alpha$: the second stability boundary; nan where none is found or the unstable band reaches alpha_max. Convention The boundaries of s_alpha_ballooning_stable (same normalisation and Newcomb criterion). The unstable set at fixed $s$ is taken to be the single band $[\alpha_1, \alpha_2]$ it is in this model. Raises ValueError s is not finite, alpha_max is below 0.1 or resolution is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · Numerical notes · References Physical interpretation Below $\alpha_1$ the plasma is first-stable; above $\alpha_2$ it has reached second stability. $\alpha_1 \approx 0.6\,s$ at moderate shear, the line ballooning_stability_criterion uses. Assumptions As for s_alpha_ballooning_stable. Numerical notes A scan on a 0.05-spaced $\alpha$ grid brackets each boundary, then one vectorised bisection refines both to resolution. A band narrower than the scan spacing (very small $s$) can be missed. References J. W. Connor, R. J. Hastie and J. B. Taylor, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 396 (1978). J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.13. sawtooth_stability_criterion Empirical fitDeprecated source sawtooth_stability_criterion(q_0, beta_pol) Deprecated: heuristic margin against an unsourced $ eta_{p,crit} = 0.3\,(1 - q_0)$; no replacement. Porcelli et al. [1] trigger the crash on conditions in the internal-kink energy $\delta\hat W$, the fast-ion precession frequency, the ion diamagnetic frequency (Eqs. 13-15) and, through Eq. (15a), the shear $s_1$ at $q = 1$, with $ eta_{p1}$ defined inside the $q = 1$ surface (Eq. 12). None reduces to a threshold $0.3\,(1 - q_0)$ on the global $ eta_p$ (#350), so this has no drop-in replacement. Results are unchanged; a DeprecationWarning is emitted. \[\Delta =  eta_p -  eta_{p,crit}, \qquad  eta_{p,crit} = 0.3\,(1 - q_0)\] NameTypeUnitDescription q_0float-Safety factor on axis. beta_polfloat-Poloidal beta. Returns marginfloat-$ eta_p -  eta_{p,crit}$; positive means the threshold is exceeded. beta_pol_critfloat-The threshold. Validity · Limitations · References Validity Empirical fit. Modelled on the Porcelli trigger, in which the internal-kink threshold scales with the poloidal beta inside the $q=1$ surface and a critical value of order 0.3 [1]; the linear $(1 - q_0)$ dependence and the coefficient are VAFT heuristics without a recorded source. Limitations Uses the global $ eta_p$, not $ eta_{p,1}$ inside $q=1$; returns a negative threshold for $q_0 > 1$, where sawteeth do not occur. Tracked in #350. References F. Porcelli, D. Boucher and M. N. Rosenbluth, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 38 (1996) 2163, Sec. 3, Eqs. (12)-(15a). shear_alfven_frequency source shear_alfven_frequency(k_parallel, v_A) Frequency of the ideal shear Alfven wave in a uniform plasma. \[\omega^2 = k_\parallel^2v_A^2,\qquad \omega = |k_\parallel|\,v_A\] NameTypeUnitDescription k_parallelfloat or np.ndarray1/mWavenumber along $\mathbf B_0$, signed. v_Afloat or np.ndarraym/sAlfven speed $B_0/\sqrt{\mu_0ho}$ (v_alfven_from_B_n_mi), non-negative. Returns —float or np.ndarrayrad/s$\omega \ge 0$. Raises ValueError v_A is negative. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Field-line bending restored by magnetic tension: the displacement and $\delta\mathbf B_\perp = -\delta\mathbf v_\perp\,B_0/v_A$ (forward wave) are perpendicular to both $\mathbf B_0$ and $\mathbf k$, and $|\mathbf B|$ is unchanged to first order. $\omega$ depends on $k_\perp$ not at all, so energy travels along $\mathbf B_0$ only; in an inhomogeneous plasma this gives the Alfven continuum $\omega = k_\parallel(r)v_A(r)$. Assumptions Uniform ideal MHD plasma, linear, $\omega \ll \Omega_i$; no finite Larmor radius or electron inertia (kinetic and inertial Alfven waves). References J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), Sec. 10.2. H. Alfven, Nature 150, 405 (1942). slab_perturbed_flux Convention-sensitive source slab_perturbed_flux(x, y, shear, amplitude, k_y, parity='tearing') Helical flux of a sheared slab with a tearing- or twisting-parity perturbation. \[\Psi_T =  rac{B_s'}{2}x^2 + \psi_0\cos k_y y,\qquad \Psi_W =  rac{B_s'}{2}x^2 + \psi_1\,x\cos k_y y\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymDistance from the rational surface. yfloat or np.ndarraymBinormal coordinate. shearfloatT/m$B_s’ = dB_y/dx$ at the rational surface, non-zero. amplitudefloatT m or T$\psi_0$ (tearing) or $\psi_1$ (twisting); the units follow $\Psi$. k_yfloat1/mBinormal wavenumber $m/r_s$. paritystr-"tearing" (even $	ilde\psi$) or "twisting" (odd $	ilde\psi$). Returns —float or np.ndarrayT m$\Psi$; field lines lie on its contours. Convention $\mathbf B_\perp = \hat{\mathbf z}	imes
abla\Psi$ in the slab frame of sheared_slab_field (with $B_y = B_s’x$), so $\delta B_x = -\partial_y	ilde\psi$. Tearing parity has $	ilde\psi(-x) = 	ilde\psi(x)$ and $\delta B_x(0) 
e 0$; twisting parity has $	ilde\psi(-x) = -	ilde\psi(x)$ and $\delta B_x(0) = 0$. $\Psi_T/B_s’$ is island_pendulum_hamiltonian with $\xi = k_yy + \pi$ and full width $w = 4\sqrt{|\psi_0/B_s’|}$; the O-points sit where $\cos k_yy = -\mathrm{sgn}(\psi_0/B_s’)$. shear may be negative – the slab of local_slab_from_cylinder has $L_s < 0$ for positive shear. Raises ValueError shear is zero or parity is unknown. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Tearing parity reconnects flux across the rational surface and opens a magnetic island (O- and X-points, separatrix); its displacement $\xi_x = -	ilde\psi/(B_s’x)$ is odd in $x$. Twisting parity has no normal field on the rational surface ($k_\parallel = 0$ there), no reconnection, and an even displacement $\xi_x = -\psi_1\cos k_yy/B_s’$: the surfaces on both sides, and the rational surface with them, move together. Linear in the amplitude: contours of $\Psi_W$ close to $x = 0$ form thin cells of width $O(\psi_1/B_s’)$ that are an artefact of dropping the $O(\psi_1^2)$ term; $	frac12B_s’(x + \psi_1\cos k_yy/B_s’)^2$ completes it. Freidberg, Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy, Cambridge University Press (2007), Sec. 10.5 (Alfven waves). NRL Plasma Formulary (2019), p. 29.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/green/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.green: 16 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("green.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview This module provides functions for calculating various Green’s function integrals used in plasma physics calculations. SymbolMeaningUnit GGreen's function- Kcomplete elliptic integral of first kind- Ecomplete elliptic integral of second kind- Every flux these functions return is full weber, psi = mu0 G per ampere – the physical flux through the toroidal circle, which grows toward a positive current – not the per-radian g-file family. Hand such a flux to vaft.formula.equilibrium.vertical_magnetic_field_from_psi and the other field helpers with cocos=13 ($k = -1/2\pi$, the factor psi_per_radian=False gives vaft.formula.equilibrium.poloidal_field_factor). Their default is $2\pi$ too large, and cocos=11 has the right size but the opposite sign: IMAS flux grows away from a positive current (#354). Functions calculate_distanceEuclidean distance between $(r_1, z_1)$ and $(r_2, z_2)$ in the poloidal plane. complete_elliptic_integral_eComplete elliptic integral of the second kind $E(m)$. Convention complete_elliptic_integral_kComplete elliptic integral of the first kind $K(m)$. Convention elliptic_integralPolynomial approximations of $K$ and $E$ for a ring source and observer points. green_br_bzField of a unit-current ring, $(B_r, B_z)$ at observer points (legacy elliptic path). Convention green_br_bz_exact$(B_r, B_z)$ per unit ring current, exact elliptic integrals, broadcasting. Convention green_psi_exactPoloidal flux per unit ring current, exact elliptic integrals. Convention green_rPoloidal flux per unit ring current at observer points (legacy elliptic path). Convention greens_function_3dToroidal-angle-resolved variant of the $\sqrt{RR_0}\,K(m)$ kernel. greens_function_exactExact free-space axisymmetric Green’s function and its derivatives. Convention greens_integral_2dLine integral along $R$ of the 2-D kernel times a source density. greens_integral_3dLine integral along $R$ of the 3-D kernel times a source density. mutual_inductanceMutual inductance between two rectangular-cross-section ring coils. self_inductanceSelf-inductance of a rectangular-cross-section ring coil. trapz_integralTrapezoidal integral $\int y\,dx$, local copy for the Green kernels. No function matches. calculate_distance source calculate_distance(r1, r2, z1, z2) Euclidean distance between $(r_1, z_1)$ and $(r_2, z_2)$ in the poloidal plane. \[d = \sqrt{(r_2 - r_1)^2 + (z_2 - z_1)^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription r1float or np.ndarraymRadius of the first point(s). r2float or np.ndarraymRadius of the second point(s). z1float or np.ndarraymHeight of the first point(s). z2float or np.ndarraymHeight of the second point(s). Notes Notes A distance in the $(R, Z)$ half-plane, not the 3-D distance between points on two current loops. complete_elliptic_integral_e Convention-sensitive source complete_elliptic_integral_e(m) Complete elliptic integral of the second kind $E(m)$. \[E(m) = \int_0^{\pi/2}\sqrt{1 - m\sin^2\theta}\,d\theta\] NameTypeUnitDescription mfloat or np.ndarray-Parameter $m = k^2$, in $[0, 1]$. References References NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Sec. 19.2(ii), https://dlmf.nist.gov/19.2. M. Abramowitz and I. A. Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, Dover (1972), Sec. 17.3. complete_elliptic_integral_k Convention-sensitive source complete_elliptic_integral_k(m) Complete elliptic integral of the first kind $K(m)$. \[K(m) = \int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\theta}{\sqrt{1 - m\sin^2\theta}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription mfloat or np.ndarray-Parameter $m = k^2$, in $[0, 1)$. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$K(m)$. Convention Takes the parameter $m = k^2$, as scipy.special.ellipk does, not the modulus $k$; $K \to \infty$ logarithmically as $m \to 1$. References References NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Sec. 19.2(ii), https://dlmf.nist.gov/19.2. M. Abramowitz and I. A. Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, Dover (1972), Sec. 17.3. elliptic_integral source elliptic_integral(r_obs, z_obs, r_src, z_src) Polynomial approximations of $K$ and $E$ for a ring source and observer points. \[m = \frac{4r_{obs}r_{src}}{(r_{obs} + r_{src})^2 + (z_{obs} - z_{src})^2}, \qquad m_1 = 1 - m\] then the Hastings polynomials $K \approx \sum a_km_1^k + \ln(1/m_1)\sum b_km_1^k$ and $E \approx \sum c_km_1^k + \ln(1/m_1)\sum d_km_1^k$ to fourth order. References M. Abramowitz and I. A. Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, Dover (1972), Eqs. 17.3.34 and 17.3.36. C. Hastings, Approximations for Digital Computers, Princeton University Press (1955). green_br_bz Convention-sensitive source green_br_bz(r_obs, z_obs, r_src, z_src) Field of a unit-current ring, $(B_r, B_z)$ at observer points (legacy elliptic path). \[B_r = \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}\,\frac{z - z_0}{\sqrt{(r + r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}} \left[\frac{r^2 + r_0^2 + (z - z_0)^2}{(r - r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}E - K\right], \quad B_z = \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{(r + r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}} \left[K - \frac{r^2 - r_0^2 + (z - z_0)^2}{(r - r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}E\right]\] NameTypeUnitDescription r_obsnp.ndarraymRadius of the observation points. z_obsnp.ndarraymHeight of the observation points. r_srcfloatmRadius of the current ring. z_srcfloatmHeight of the current ring. Convention Right-handed $(r, \varphi, z)$ with the current flowing in $+\varphi$; $B_z$ is positive inside the ring. SI throughout; no $2\pi$ flux ambiguity arises for fields. Uses the approximate elliptic_integral; the exact, broadcasting counterpart is green_br_bz_exact. Limitations · References Limitations Divides by $(r - r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2$ and by $r_{obs}$ without guards, so a coincident point or an on-axis observer gives inf/nan (the callers’ shifted-evaluation scheme avoids exact coincidence). Tracked in #356. References W. R. Smythe, Static and Dynamic Electricity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill (1968), Sec. 7.10 (field of a circular loop). J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5. green_br_bz_exact Convention-sensitive source green_br_bz_exact(r_obs, z_obs, r_src, z_src) $(B_r, B_z)$ per unit ring current, exact elliptic integrals, broadcasting. \[B_r = -\frac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}\,\frac{\partial G}{\partial z}, \qquad B_z = +\frac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}\,\frac{\partial G}{\partial r}\] NameTypeUnitDescription r_obsarray-likemObservation major radius. z_obsarray-likemObservation height. r_srcarray-likemSource major radius. z_srcarray-likemSource height. Returns brnp.ndarrayT/ARadial field per ampere. bznp.ndarrayT/AVertical field per ampere. Convention Right-handed $(r, \varphi, z)$, current in $+\varphi$; consistent with green_psi_exact through $B_z = (1/r)\,\partial\psi/\partial r \times 1/2\pi$ for a full-weber $\psi$. Limitations · References Limitations Observation points on the geometric axis ($r_{obs} = 0$) return the analytic limits $B_r = 0$, $B_z = \mu_0 r_0^2/(2(r_0^2 + (z - z_0)^2)^{3/2})$; the coincident-point caveat of greens_function_exact applies. References W. R. Smythe, Static and Dynamic Electricity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill (1968), Sec. 7.10. green_psi_exact Convention-sensitive source green_psi_exact(r_obs, z_obs, r_src, z_src) Poloidal flux per unit ring current, exact elliptic integrals. \[\psi = \mu_0\,G(r, z; r_0, z_0)\] with $G$ from greens_function_exact. NameTypeUnitDescription r_obsarray-likemObservation major radius. z_obsarray-likemObservation height. r_srcarray-likemSource major radius. z_srcarray-likemSource height. Returns —np.ndarrayWb/AFlux per ampere, broadcast over observation and source arrays. Convention Full weber, the IMAS Data Dictionary storage (COCOS 11-18), same as green_r. The per-radian flux of an EFIT g-file or of vaft.formula.equilibrium.poloidal_field_factor with cocos=None is this divided by $2\pi$; mixing the two silently mis-scales fields by $2\pi$. Tracked in #354. References References J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5. green_r Convention-sensitive source green_r(r_obs, z_obs, r_src, z_src) Poloidal flux per unit ring current at observer points (legacy elliptic path). \[\psi = 2\mu_0\,\frac{\sqrt{r r_0}}{k}\left[\left(1 - \frac{k^2}{2}\right)K - E\right], \qquad k^2 = \frac{4rr_0}{(r + r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription r_obsnp.ndarraymRadius of the observation points. z_obsnp.ndarraymHeight of the observation points. r_srcfloatmRadius of the current ring. z_srcfloatmHeight of the current ring. Returns —np.ndarrayWb/AFlux per ampere at each observation point. Convention Full weber ($\psi = \mu_0 G$, identical to green_psi_exact up to the elliptic-integral approximation); divide by $2\pi$ before combining with the per-radian equilibrium helpers. Tracked in #354. Limitations · References Limitations Uses the Hastings polynomials of elliptic_integral; returns 0 on the axis ($r_{obs} = 0$ or $r_{src} = 0$) and clips $k^2$ into $[0, 1]$. References J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5, Eq. (5.37). greens_function_2d Convention-sensitive source greens_function_2d(R, Z, R0, Z0) Axisymmetric kernel $\sqrt{RR_0}\,K(m)$ between a field point and a ring source. \[G_{2D} = \sqrt{R R_0}\;K(m), \qquad m = \frac{4RR_0}{(R + R_0)^2 + (Z - Z_0)^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the field points. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the field points. R0floatmMajor radius of the ring source. Z0floatmHeight of the ring source. Returns —np.ndarraymKernel value at each field point. Convention This is the leading term of the ring-current flux function, not the flux Green’s function itself: the poloidal flux per unit current is $\mu_0\sqrt{RR_0}\,[(2 - m)K(m) - 2E(m)]/\sqrt{m}$ (greens_function_exact, green_psi_exact). Use those for any physical field; this kernel is kept for the legacy integrals below. Limitations · References Limitations Diverges logarithmically at the source point; no guard. References J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5 (vector potential of a circular loop). greens_function_3d source greens_function_3d(R, Z, phi, R0, Z0, phi0) Toroidal-angle-resolved variant of the $\sqrt{RR_0}\,K(m)$ kernel. \[G_{3D} = \sqrt{R R_0}\;K(m), \qquad m = \frac{4RR_0}{(R + R_0)^2 + (Z - Z_0)^2 + 4RR_0\sin^2\!\big(\tfrac{\varphi - \varphi_0}{2}\big)}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the field points. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the field points. phinp.ndarrayradToroidal angle of the field points. R0floatmMajor radius of the source. Z0floatmHeight of the source. phi0floatradToroidal angle of the source. Returns —np.ndarraymKernel value at each field point. Limitations · References Limitations Not the Biot-Savart kernel of a point source, and the difference is exact rather than vague. The chord between two points in a torus is \[d^2 = (R - R_0)^2 + (Z - Z_0)^2 + 4RR_0\sin^2\!\big(\tfrac{\varphi - \varphi_0}{2}\big),\] while the ring kernel’s denominator is $(R + R_0)^2 + (Z - Z_0)^2 = (R - R_0)^2 + (Z - Z_0)^2 + 4RR_0$. A point source therefore replaces the $4RR_0$ with $4RR_0\sin^2(\Delta\varphi/2)$; this expression adds the second term to the first, so the two coincide only at $\Delta\varphi = 0$, where the $\sin^2$ vanishes and the ring result is recovered. That $\Delta\varphi = 0$ reduction is the one property worth relying on. Away from it the expression decays with toroidal separation in a way that has no recorded derivation, so it should not be read as a field. Tracked in #356: it needs either a derivation or a replacement, and it has no production caller today. References J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5. greens_function_exact Convention-sensitive source greens_function_exact(r, z, r0, z0, mode='psi') Exact free-space axisymmetric Green’s function and its derivatives. \[G(r, z; r_0, z_0) = \frac{\sqrt{rr_0}}{k}\left[(2 - k^2)K(k^2) - 2E(k^2)\right], \qquad k^2 = m = \frac{4rr_0}{(r + r_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2}\] so that $\psi = \mu_0 I\,G$ is the poloidal flux of a ring current $I$; mode selects $G$, $\partial G/\partial r$, $\partial G/\partial z$, $\partial^2G/\partial r\partial z$, $\partial^2G/\partial r^2$, or the raw $K$ and $E$. NameTypeUnitDescription rarray-likemObservation major radius. zarray-likemObservation height. r0array-likemSource major radius. z0array-likemSource height. modestr, optionalstrOne of GREEN_EXACT_MODES; default "psi". Returns —np.ndarrayanyRequested quantity, broadcast over all four coordinates. $G$ is in m, its derivatives in m per m, $K$ and $E$ dimensionless. Convention Full weber: $\psi = \mu_0 G$ per ampere (same as green_r), and $B_z = +\mu_0/(2\pi r)\,\partial G/\partial r$, $B_r = -\mu_0/(2\pi r)\, \partial G/\partial z$. The equilibrium helpers assume flux per radian by default, so divide by $2\pi$ (or pass cocos) before feeding this flux to vaft.formula.equilibrium.vertical_magnetic_field_from_psi. Raises ValueError Unknown mode or coordinates giving $m$ outside $[0, 1]$. Limitations · Numerical notes · References Limitations Points with $rr_0 = 0$ return their analytic limits (0 for every mode except d2psi_dr2, whose on-axis limit is $\pi r_0^2/(r_0^2 + (z - z_0)^2)^{3/2}$). The elliptic parameter is clamped just below 1, so a coincident observer and source return finite numbers, but those are artifacts of the clamp, not physical limits (the ideal-filament self term diverges): handle genuinely coincident pairs yourself, e.g. with self_inductance or a shifted-evaluation scheme such as compute_br_bz_phi. Numerical notes scipy.special.ellipk/ellipe on the parameter $m$; every $1/k$, $1/m$ and $1/r$ is guarded and overwritten on axis. The d2psi_dr2 branch corrects a sign error in the legacy VFIT getGreenFunction.m case 7 ($-2(r + r_0)A$, from $d(1/D)/dr = -D’/D^2$) and is validated against finite differences of dpsi_dr. References J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999), Sec. 5.5, Eq. (5.37). Legacy VFIT getGreenFunction.m (modes 1-7), the reference algorithm. greens_integral_2d source greens_integral_2d(R, Z, R0, Z0, f) Line integral along $R$ of the 2-D kernel times a source density. \[I = \int G_{2D}(R, Z; R_0, Z_0)\,f(R)\,dR\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the samples, monotonic. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the samples. R0floatmMajor radius of the source. Z0floatmHeight of the source. fnp.ndarrayanySource density at the samples. Returns —floatanyIntegral in units of f times m^2. Limitations · Numerical notes Limitations Integrates along the single supplied R array (a line, not an area) with the kernel of greens_function_2d; not a flux or field. Numerical notes Trapezoidal rule. greens_integral_3d source greens_integral_3d(R, Z, phi, R0, Z0, phi0, f) Line integral along $R$ of the 3-D kernel times a source density. \[I = \int G_{3D}(R, Z, \varphi; R_0, Z_0, \varphi_0)\,f(R)\,dR\] NameTypeUnitDescription Rnp.ndarraymMajor radius of the samples, monotonic. Znp.ndarraymHeight of the samples. phinp.ndarrayradToroidal angle of the samples. R0floatmMajor radius of the source. Z0floatmHeight of the source. phi0floatradToroidal angle of the source. fnp.ndarrayanySource density at the samples. Returns —floatanyIntegral in units of f times m^2. Limitations · Numerical notes Limitations Same caveats as greens_integral_2d and greens_function_3d. Numerical notes Trapezoidal rule along R only. mutual_inductance source mutual_inductance(r1, z1, dr1, dz1, r2, z2, dr2, dz2, *, tilt1=0.0, tilt2=0.0, turns1=1.0, turns2=1.0, mu_r=1.0, n_div=5) Mutual inductance between two rectangular-cross-section ring coils. \[M = N_1N_2\,\mu_r\mu_0\,\big\langle G(r_i, z_i; r_j, z_j)\big\rangle_{i \in 1,\ j \in 2}\] the Neumann formula evaluated as the mean flux linkage between midpoint filaments laid over each cross-section. NameTypeUnitDescription r1floatmCentre radius of coil 1. z1floatmCentre height of coil 1. dr1floatmRadial width of coil 1; 0 degenerates to a filament. dz1floatmHeight of coil 1; 0 degenerates to a filament. r2floatmCentre radius of coil 2. z2floatmCentre height of coil 2. dr2floatmRadial width of coil 2. dz2floatmHeight of coil 2. tilt1float, optionalradTilt of cross-section 1 about its centre; default 0. tilt2float, optionalradTilt of cross-section 2; default 0. turns1float, optional-Turns of coil 1; default 1. turns2float, optional-Turns of coil 2; default 1. mu_rfloat, optional-Relative permeability of the medium, e.g. 1.04 for SUS304; default 1. n_divint, optional-Subdivision refinement; default 5. The cell size is half the pair’s characteristic scale over n_div. Returns —floatHMutual inductance. Assumptions · Numerical notes · References Assumptions Axisymmetric coils with uniform current density over the cross-section; the toroidal curvature correction $r \to r\,(1 + (\cos\theta\,\Delta r/r)^2/24)$ is applied to each cell. Numerical notes Midpoint rule over both cross-sections (reference: legacy VFIT getMutualInductanceCoil.m). The cell size uses the $z$-separation $\sqrt{(r_1 + r_2)^2 + (z_1 - z_2)^2}$; the legacy code used $z_1 + z_2$, which is not invariant under a rigid vertical translation. Legacy material codes are intentionally not reproduced: pass mu_r explicitly. References W. R. Smythe, Static and Dynamic Electricity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill (1968), Sec. 8.06 (mutual inductance of coaxial circles). Legacy VFIT getMutualInductanceCoil.m. self_inductance source self_inductance(r, dr, dz, *, tilt=0.0, turns=1.0, mu_r=1.0, n_div=5) Self-inductance of a rectangular-cross-section ring coil. \[L = \frac{N^2}{n^2}\left[\sum_{i \ne j}\mu_r\mu_0\,G(r_i, z_i; r_j, z_j) + \sum_i \mu_r\mu_0\,r_i\left(\ln\frac{8r_i}{s} - \frac{7}{4}\right)\right], \qquad s = \sqrt{\Delta r\,\Delta z/\pi}\] midpoint subdivision into $n$ cells with the analytic self-term of a circular filament of equivalent radius $s$ on the diagonal. NameTypeUnitDescription rfloatmCentre radius, positive. drfloatmRadial width, positive. dzfloatmHeight, positive. tiltfloat, optionalradTilt of the cross-section; default 0. turnsfloat, optional-Number of turns; default 1. mu_rfloat, optional-Relative permeability; default 1. n_divint, optional-Cells per centre radius; default 5. Returns —floatHSelf-inductance. Raises ValueError For non-positive r, dr or dz. Assumptions · Numerical notes · References Assumptions Uniform current density; the self-cell term is the low-frequency inductance of a thin ring of wire radius $s$ (internal inductance included, hence $7/4$ rather than 2). Numerical notes Reference: legacy VFIT getSelfInductanceCoil.m; nz is forced even. Convergence in n_div is first order because of the self-cell approximation. References W. R. Smythe, Static and Dynamic Electricity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill (1968), Sec. 8.10 (self-inductance of a circular ring). Legacy VFIT getSelfInductanceCoil.m. trapz_integral source trapz_integral(x, y) Trapezoidal integral $\int y\,dx$, local copy for the Green kernels. \[\int y\,dx \approx \sum_i \frac{y_i + y_{i+1}}{2}\,(x_{i+1} - x_i)\] NameTypeUnitDescription xnp.ndarrayanySample abscissae, monotonic. ynp.ndarrayanyIntegrand at the samples. Returns —floatanyIntegral over the sampled range, in units of y times x. Numerical notes Numerical notes Identical to vaft.formula.utils.trapz_integral (numpy.trapezoid via vaft.compat.trapz_compat); this copy is the one vaft.formula.trapz_integral resolves to, and it is kept because test_formula_lazy_namespace pins that shadowing. The reason it was written – that importing utils dragged in scikit-learn – is gone since #426.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/atomic/.title: Formula reference: atomic
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/atomic/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.atomic: 8 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("atomic.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview The equilibrium construction follows MIT-licensed work, Copyright (c) 2021 Francesco Sciortino. See the third-party notices in the project README. This module is the numerical layer of VAFT’s atomic package. It accepts SI electron densities, evaluates native ADF11 tables in log10 space, and returns charge-state fractions or cooling coefficients without depending on OMAS. Functions fractional_abundancesIonisation-equilibrium (coronal) fractional abundances from ACD and SCD tables. Convention hydrogenic_energy_levelBohr energy of level $n$ of a one-electron ion, with the reduced-mass correction. hydrogenic_transition_wavelengthVacuum wavelength of the $n_u \to n_l$ line of a one-electron ion (Rydberg formula). Convention impurity_fraction_from_effective_chargeImpurity-to-electron density ratio that produces a given effective charge. interpolate_adf11Interpolate every charge-state block of an ADF11 table at given $(n_e, T_e)$. Convention line_cooling_coefficientEquilibrium line-radiation cooling coefficient $L_{line}(n_e, T_e)$ of a species. Convention mean_charge_from_charge_state_densitiesMean charge of one element over its charge states. Convention z_eff_from_n_s_Z_sEffective charge of a mixture of ion species. Convention No function matches. fractional_abundances Convention-sensitive source fractional_abundances(ne_m3, te_eV, acd, scd) Ionisation-equilibrium (coronal) fractional abundances from ACD and SCD tables. \[\frac{f_{z+1}}{f_z} = \frac{S_z(n_e, T_e)}{\alpha_{z+1}(n_e, T_e)}, \qquad \tilde f_0 = 1, \quad \tilde f_z = \prod_{j=0}^{z-1}\frac{S_j}{\alpha_{j+1}}, \quad f_z = \frac{\tilde f_z}{\sum_k\tilde f_k}\] with $S_z$ the SCD effective ionisation and $\alpha_{z+1}$ the ACD effective recombination coefficients. NameTypeUnitDescription ne_m3array-likem^-3Electron density, finite and positive. te_eVarray-likeeVElectron temperature, finite and positive. acdADF11Data or path-liken/aEffective recombination table. scdADF11Data or path-liken/aEffective ionisation table. Returns —np.ndarray-Fractional abundances, summing to one over the last axis. That axis has n_rate_blocks + 1 charge states, neutral to fully stripped. Convention Effective (collisional-radiative, density-dependent) coefficients in the ADAS sense, evaluated in cm^-3 internally; the density cancels in the ratio, so the result is dimensionless. Raises ValueError Mismatched charge-state counts, wrong table class, or non-finite rates. Assumptions · Limitations · References Assumptions Steady state, no transport: the local balance of ionisation and recombination alone sets the charge-state distribution. Limitations Transport in a real edge or start-up plasma shifts the distribution toward lower charge states than coronal equilibrium predicts (the effect Aurora models with an impurity transport solve). References H. P. Summers, The ADAS User Manual, version 2.6 (2004), Sec. on ADF11 (ionisation balance). F. Sciortino et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 63 (2021) 112001, Sec. 2 (equilibrium construction; MIT-licensed, see the module docstring). hydrogenic_energy_level source hydrogenic_energy_level(n, Z=1, mass_number=None) Bohr energy of level $n$ of a one-electron ion, with the reduced-mass correction. \[E_n = -\frac{\mu}{m_e}\,\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\,R_\infty hc,\qquad R_\infty hc = \frac{m_ee^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2h^2}\approx 13.606\ \mathrm{eV}\] NameTypeUnitDescription nint or np.ndarray-Principal quantum number, at least 1. Zint, optional-Nuclear charge of the one-electron ion (1 for H I, 2 for He II). mass_numberint or None, optional-1, 2 or 3 for H, D, T (the reduced mass $\mu = m_eM/(m_e + M)$), only with Z = 1; None for an infinitely heavy nucleus. Returns —float or np.ndarrayeV$E_n$, negative, from the ionisation limit. Raises ValueError n below one, Z below one, an unknown mass_number, or a mass_number with Z > 1. Assumptions · References Assumptions Non-relativistic Bohr/Schroedinger levels of a one-electron ion: no fine structure, Lamb shift or hyperfine splitting (H-alpha’s fine structure spans about 0.016 nm). Not a stand-in for many-electron levels, which need atomic data (ADF04). References H. A. Bethe and E. E. Salpeter, Quantum Mechanics of One- and Two-Electron Atoms, Springer (1957), Sec. 2. hydrogenic_transition_wavelength Convention-sensitive source hydrogenic_transition_wavelength(n_upper, n_lower, Z=1, mass_number=None) Vacuum wavelength of the $n_u \to n_l$ line of a one-electron ion (Rydberg formula). \[\frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{\mu}{m_e}R_\infty Z^2\left(\frac{1}{n_l^2} - \frac{1}{n_u^2}\right),\qquad R_\infty = \frac{m_ee^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2h^3c}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_upperint or np.ndarray-Upper principal quantum number, above n_lower. n_lowerint-Lower principal quantum number, at least 1. Zint, optional-Nuclear charge of the one-electron ion. mass_numberint or None, optional-1, 2 or 3 for H, D, T; None for infinite nuclear mass. Returns —float or np.ndarraymVacuum wavelength. Convention Vacuum wavelength. Tabulated visible lines are usually quoted in air (H-alpha 656.28 nm air, 656.47 nm vacuum): the difference is the refractive index of air, about $2.8\times10^{-4}$. The series of the fusion-diagnostic names is Balmer: alpha is $3 \to 2$, beta $4 \to 2$. The isotope shift from the reduced mass (D-alpha about 0.18 nm below H-alpha) is what separates H and D lines. Raises ValueError n_upper <= n_lower or an argument of hydrogenic_energy_level is invalid. References References H. A. Bethe and E. E. Salpeter, Quantum Mechanics of One- and Two-Electron Atoms, Springer (1957), Sec. 2. impurity_fraction_from_effective_charge source impurity_fraction_from_effective_charge(z_eff, z_impurity) Impurity-to-electron density ratio that produces a given effective charge. \[\frac{n_I}{n_e} = \frac{Z_{\mathrm{eff}} - 1}{Z_I\,(Z_I - 1)}\] the inverse of z_eff_from_n_s_Z_s for one fully ionised impurity of charge $Z_I$ in a hydrogenic main ion. NameTypeUnitDescription z_efffloat or array-like-Effective charge, within $[1, Z_I]$. z_impurityfloat-Impurity charge $Z_I$, greater than one. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$n_I/n_e$, of the shape of z_eff; the main-ion fraction is $n_H/n_e = 1 - Z_I\,n_I/n_e$. Raises ValueError z_impurity not greater than one, or z_eff non-finite or outside $[1, Z_I]$, where no non-negative density pair exists. Assumptions · Limitations · See Also · References Assumptions Quasi-neutrality $n_e = n_H + Z_I n_I$ and exactly two ion species: a hydrogenic main ion ($Z = 1$, any isotope) and one impurity in a single charge state. Those two conditions and the definition $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} n_e = n_H + Z_I^2 n_I$ fix both fractions. Limitations One impurity only: a measured $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ does not determine a mixture, so the answer is the fraction of the named impurity that would alone account for it. At $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2$ that is $1/30$ for carbon but $1/5402$ for fully stripped tungsten. See Also z_eff_from_n_s_Z_s References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Ch. 2 (collisions, resistivity and the effective charge). interpolate_adf11 Convention-sensitive source interpolate_adf11(table, ne_m3, te_eV, *, multiply_density=False) Interpolate every charge-state block of an ADF11 table at given $(n_e, T_e)$. \[C_z(n_e, T_e) = 10^{\,\mathcal{I}_2[\log_{10}C_z]}\] where $\mathcal{I}2$ is bilinear interpolation on the table’s rectangular grid of $\log{10}n_e\,[\mathrm{cm^{-3}}]$ and $\log_{10}T_e\,[\mathrm{eV}]$. NameTypeUnitDescription tableADF11Datan/aParsed ADF11 table (acd, scd, plt, …). ne_m3array-likem^-3Electron density, finite and positive. te_eVarray-likeeVElectron temperature, finite and positive. multiply_densitybool, optionalboolMultiply by $n_e$ in cm^-3 to turn coefficients into rates; default False. Returns —np.ndarrayanyCoefficients in the table’s own unit, or rates with multiply_density. Shape broadcast(ne_m3, te_eV).shape + (n_blocks,); cm^3/s for ACD/SCD and W cm^3 for PLT, s^-1 when multiplied by density. Convention ADF11 stores densities in cm^-3 and rate coefficients in cm^3 s^-1; the SI input is converted to cm^-3 internally and the output is not converted back, so callers multiply by $10^{-6}$ for m^3 s^-1 (as line_cooling_coefficient does for W m^3). Raises ValueError Empty, non-finite or non-positive profiles. Validity · Limitations · Numerical notes · References Validity Inside the tabulated grid (typically $10^{8}$-$10^{15}$ cm^-3 and 1 eV-10 keV for iso-nuclear ADF11 files). Limitations Linear extrapolation in log space is retained outside the grid to match the established ADF11 calculation path; extrapolated coefficients are not physical and are not flagged. Numerical notes scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator with bounds_error=False, fill_value=None, one interpolator per charge-state block. References H. P. Summers, The ADAS User Manual, version 2.6 (2004), https://www.adas.ac.uk/manual.php, ADF11 format. F. Sciortino et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 63 (2021) 112001 (Aurora; the calculation path this follows). line_cooling_coefficient Convention-sensitive source line_cooling_coefficient(species, ne_m3, te_eV, *, acd=None, scd=None, plt=None, cache_dir=None) Equilibrium line-radiation cooling coefficient $L_{line}(n_e, T_e)$ of a species. \[L_{\mathrm{line}}(n_e, T_e) = 10^{-6}\sum_{q=0}^{Z-1} f_q(n_e, T_e)\, P^{\mathrm{PLT}}_q(n_e, T_e)\] the PLT coefficients weighted by the coronal abundances of fractional_abundances; the fully stripped state has no line radiation and is omitted. NameTypeUnitDescription speciesstrstrAtomic symbol with configured default ADF11 files, e.g. "C". ne_m3array-likem^-3Electron density, finite and positive. te_eVarray-likeeVElectron temperature, finite and positive. acdADF11Data or path-like or None, optionaln/aRecombination table; None resolves the configured file. scdADF11Data or path-like or None, optionaln/aIonisation table; None resolves the configured file. pltADF11Data or path-like or None, optionaln/aLine-power table; None resolves the configured file. cache_dirstr or path-like or None, optionaln/aOPEN-ADAS cache directory; downloads on a miss. Returns —np.ndarrayW m^3Cooling coefficient with the broadcast input shape. Multiply by $n_e n_Z$ for a power density. Convention ADF11 PLT is stored in W cm^3; the factor $10^{-6}$ converts to W m^3. Coronal equilibrium, no transport, no recombination/bremsstrahlung continuum (that is the separate PRB class). Raises KeyError Unconfigured species. ADASDataError Lookup, download or parsing failure. ValueError Invalid inputs or mismatched charge-state dimensions. References References H. P. Summers, The ADAS User Manual, version 2.6 (2004), ADF11 PLT class. D. E. Post et al., At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 20 (1977) 397 (coronal cooling curves). mean_charge_from_charge_state_densities Convention-sensitive source mean_charge_from_charge_state_densities(n_z, axis=-1) Mean charge of one element over its charge states. \[\langle Z\rangle = \sum_j j\,f_j = \frac{\sum_j j\,n_j}{\sum_j n_j}, \qquad f_j = \frac{n_j}{\sum_k n_k}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_zarray-likem^-3Density of each charge state along axis, ordered neutral first, so that index $j$ is charge $j$; finite and non-negative. axisint, optional-Axis that runs over the charge states. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Mean charge, with axis removed. Convention Index is charge, neutral first, the layout fractional_abundances returns – so its output can be passed straight in, and densities need not be normalised first because the fractions $f_j$ are formed here. Spectroscopic notation counts from one (C I is neutral carbon); pass charge, not ionisation stage, or every value comes out one high. Raises ValueError A non-finite or negative density, or a slice whose densities sum to zero, which has no charge distribution to average. See Also · References See Also fractional_abundances z_eff_from_n_s_Z_s References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 4.25 (impurity charge states). z_eff_from_n_s_Z_s Convention-sensitive source z_eff_from_n_s_Z_s(n_s, Z_s, n_e=None) Effective charge of a mixture of ion species. \[Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s Z_s^2}{n_e}, \qquad n_e = \sum_s n_s Z_s\ \text{when not given}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_sarray-likem^-3Density of each ion species or charge state, finite and non-negative; the last axis runs over species. Z_sarray-like-Charge of each, broadcastable against n_s, finite and non-negative n_efloat or array-like, optionalm^-3Electron density, finite and positive; default the quasi-neutral $\sum_s n_s Z_s$. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Effective charge, with the species axis removed. Convention Pass the electron density only when it is measured independently. The default makes the plasma quasi-neutral by construction, and then a pure hydrogenic plasma is exactly 1 and every impurity raises it. A measured $n_e$ that disagrees with $\sum_s n_s Z_s$ is taken as given and not reconciled, so a density error lands directly in $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$. A charge-resolved impurity is several species here, one per charge state: $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ weights $Z^2$, so collapsing an element of density $n_I$ onto its mean charge first underestimates it by exactly $n_I\,\mathrm{Var}(Z)/n_e$ – the quasi-neutral $n_e$ is unchanged, since it weights $Z$ only linearly. Raises ValueError A non-finite or negative density or charge, a non-positive electron density, or a quasi-neutral electron density of zero. See Also · References See Also mean_charge_from_charge_state_densities vaft.formula.equilibrium.spitzer_resistivity_from_T_e_Z_eff_ln_Lambda References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 4.25.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/statisti.title: Formula reference: statistics
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/statisti.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.statistics: 22 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("statistics.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview This module is the single source of truth for the mathematics used to judge how well a reconstruction reproduces its own inputs: residual magnitude, residual bias, residual structure, goodness of fit against declared uncertainties, and the rate at which an iterative solver approaches its answer. Every function here takes plain arrays or scalars and returns plain floats. Nothing in this module knows what an ODS, an EFIT run, a diagnostic channel or a validation policy is – deciding which physical arrays enter a formula belongs to the OMAS layer, and deciding what value is acceptable belongs to the validation layer. Keeping the mathematics separate means a definition can be tested against an analytic reference without constructing a tokamak. Non-finite samples are ignored rather than propagated, so a single dead channel does not erase a whole family’s statistic. A statistic that is undefined for the input given – too few samples, zero variance, a zero denominator – returns nan rather than raising, because these arise routinely from real diagnostics and every caller aggregates over many channels or slices. No numpy warning is emitted for an empty or all-non-finite input; the degenerate case is guarded explicitly. None of these statistics is a pass/fail rule on its own. Each is a diagnostic indicator whose interpretation depends on assumptions – stated per function – that the caller is responsible for defending.
