W_kinfloatJBulk kinetic energy. W_thfloatJThermal energy. Returns W_totalfloatJSum of the three energies. virial_ratiofloat-Ratio of material to magnetic energy. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The scalar virial theorem forbids a plasma confined by its own fields alone: a positive-definite $W_{\mathrm{mag}}$ must be balanced by external (coil) fields, and the ratio measures how far the material energy is from that balance. References V. D. Shafranov, in Reviews of Plasma Physics, Vol. 2, Consultants Bureau (1966), p. 103. J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), Sec. 3.6 (virial theorem). virial_thermal_energy Convention-sensitive source virial_thermal_energy(n, T, V) Thermal energy of a sampled plasma, $W_{th} = \tfrac{3}{2}\sum n T\,V$. \[W_{\mathrm{th}} = \int\frac{3}{2}\,n\,T\,dV\] NameTypeUnitDescription nnp.ndarraym^-3Number density at each sample. Tnp.ndarrayJTemperature at each sample, in energy units. Vfloatm^3Volume attributed to each sample. Returns —floatJThermal energy. Convention T must be in joules ($k_B T$); a temperature in eV needs the factor QE. One species only: sum electron and ion calls for the total. Assumptions · References Assumptions Equal-volume samples (V is the cell volume); three degrees of freedom. References V. D. Shafranov, in Reviews of Plasma Physics, Vol. 2, Consultants Bureau (1966), p. 103.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/.title: Process reference
/vaft/develop/reference/process/.body: vaft.process is the computation layer of VAFT. Almost every function in it takes plain NumPy arrays and scalars and returns arrays, tuples or dataclasses; it does not read or write ODS. The ODS-aware layer lives in vaft.omas (mainly vaft.omas.process_wrapper), which pulls geometry and signals out of an ODS, calls into vaft.process, and writes the results back. Rule of thumb: vaft.process is the math, vaft.omas.compute_* is the API you usually call. Every public processing function is documented under one contract, and these pages are generated from those docstrings by python -m vaft.process.catalog. Where a formula page answers what is this quantity and when is it valid, a process page answers how is this input turned into this output: the parameters and returns with their units, the processing steps in order, the defaults that change the result and what kind of value each is, the conventions assumed, the machine scope, the limitations, and the provenance of the method. Nothing here is written by hand, so the site and vaft.process.describe("<name>") always agree. import vaft.process as P print(P.describe("repair_clipped_interval")) # one routine, rendered P.search("vest.yaml") # every routine whose text mentions it P.list_processes(category="signal_processing") # imports only that submodule The discovery layer is loaded on first use only; import vaft.process.signal_processing never touches it. Categories The layer is being brought under the contract one submodule at a time (#252). A category gets a reference page when every function in it conforms; until then its count is shown and its page is absent. CategoryModuleFunctionsUnder contractContents profile vaft.process.profile 28 yes Kinetic profiles: from diagnostic points to a stored ``core_profiles`` slice. equilibrium vaft.process.equilibrium 77 yes Axisymmetric equilibrium: from a flux map to the quantities derived from it. camera_geometry vaft.process.camera_geometry 4 yes Pinhole camera projection math for the VEST FAST camera. signal_processing vaft.process.signal_processing 27 yes Conditioning of one waveform on a plain time axis. fluctuation vaft.process.fluctuation 8 yes Diagnostic-independent spectral analysis of scalar fluctuation time series. soft_x_rays vaft.process.soft_x_rays 10 yes VEST soft X-ray fluctuation and two-filter analysis routines. electromagnetics vaft.process.electromagnetics 10 yes Axisymmetric electromagnetic response: what a current does elsewhere, and how the vessel answers. numerical vaft.process.numerical 1 yes Numerical primitives on plain arrays. magnetics vaft.process.magnetics 16 yes Magnetic diagnostics: from a coil voltage to a current, a flux, or a mode number. perturbation vaft.process.perturbation 27 yes Resonant response at the rational surfaces: windows, reductions, ratios. statistical_analysis vaft.process.statistical_analysis 11 yes Log-linear regression of confinement time against engineering parameters. atomic vaft.process.atomic 5 yes Atomic-radiation processing on OMAS data structures. langmuir vaft.process.langmuir 8 yes Backend-independent VEST triple Langmuir probe physics. impa vaft.process.impa 14 yes Generic algorithms for the VEST Internal Magnetic Probe Array. onset vaft.process.onset 13 yes Onset and active-window primitives on plain arrays (issue #409). wall_modes vaft.process.wall_modes 22 yes Segment-wise eigenmode basis of a passive wall, with global coupling (vaft #473). coils_non_axisymmetric vaft.process.coils_non_axisymmetric 3 yes Kernels on non-axisymmetric coil sets: toroidal mode content and vacuum field. camera_fluctuation vaft.process.camera_fluctuation 7 yes Fluctuation analysis of FAST-camera image sequences. line_of_sight vaft.process.line_of_sight 3 yes Line integrals of a poloidal-plane field along diagnostic sightlines (issue #886). magnetic_island vaft.process.magnetic_island 4 yes An analytic magnetic island placed on an axisymmetric equilibrium (issue #886). field_line_topology vaft.process.field_line_topology 10 yes Relative heat-load proxies from field-line tracing products (issue #1099). ml vaft.process.ml 21 yes Backend-neutral machine-learning processing: data to published model (#669). transients vaft.process.transients 2 yes Measurements of a plasma-current transient on plain arrays. nbi vaft.process.nbi 1 yes Reduced neutral-beam attenuation along a prescribed 1-D path (vaft #1136). cocos vaft.process.cocos 6 yes Operational COCOS handling: consistency checking against Sauter Eq. 23. Machine-independent or VEST policy Every function’s Applicability section opens with one of two sentences, and each page badges it. Machine-independent means the caller supplies every machine-specific number – an acquisition rail, a chord length, a processing window – and the routine infers nothing about the hardware; the VEST values are read from vest.yaml by vaft.machine_mapping, never here. VEST-specific means the routine embeds a VEST constant, a VEST column name or a VEST acquisition-era rule, and its page says which and for what shot range. Where a default came from A default that changes the result is classified on its page as one of: physical constant, literature value, diagnostic calibration, empirical estimate, validated-workflow default, machine-specific setting, acquisition-era policy, legacy compatibility value, or numerical convenience. A legacy compatibility value is one that arrived with a ported routine and whose derivation is not recorded; the page says so rather than inventing one. Refreshing this snapshot From a checkout of the develop branch, run: python -m vaft.process.catalog --output docs/_data/process_catalog.yml The snapshot records the SHA-256 of every vaft/process/*.py source file, the private _equilibrium_parametric.py included; documentation validation compares them when VAFT_REGISTRY_SOURCE points to the corresponding source checkout. The same text is available offline as vaft.process.describe("<name>"), vaft.process.search("<text>") and vaft.process.list_processes(category="<category>").

/vaft/develop/reference/process/signal_p.title: Process reference: signal_processing
/vaft/develop/reference/process/signal_p.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.signal_processing: 27 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("signal_processing.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Everything here takes NumPy arrays and returns NumPy arrays. Nothing reads an ODS, nothing knows what the waveform is, and nothing embeds a VEST constant except where the function’s name says so (vest_*) and its Applicability section says why. The VEST source selection, calibration and processing windows that decide which waveform to condition, and with what numbers, live in vaft.machine_mapping and vest.yaml. Four kinds of operation: Filtering – smooth, butterworth_lowpass, butterworth_bandpass, detrend_moving_average, anti_alias_filter, vest_coil_current_noise_reduction. Baseline – define_baseline selects the quiet samples, subtract_baseline fits one of linear_baseline, quadratic_baseline, exp_baseline or a spline through them and removes it. Saturation repair – detect_clipped_samples, repair_clipped_interval. Timebase and activity – describe_time_grid, resample_to_time, detect_active_window, signal_on_offset, is_signal_active, infer_signal_orientation, line_average_density, and the legacy process_signal wrapper. SymbolMeaningUnit ttimes dtsample spacings f_ssample rate, ``1 / dt``Hz f_NNyquist frequency, ``f_s / 2``Hz f_cfilter cutoffHz xthe waveform, in whatever unit it hasany Two filtering conventions coexist and each function says which it uses. Causal (scipy.signal.lfilter) delays every feature by the filter’s group delay and is the convention of the validated VEST SXR viewer, where matched delay between channels matters more than zero phase. Zero-phase (scipy.signal.filtfilt, forward then backward) moves nothing in time and is mandatory wherever an onset time is read off the result. butterworth_lowpass defaults to causal, everything else to zero-phase. Functions VEST_CoilCurrentNoiseReductionDeprecated compatibility wrapper for the snake-case function. Deprecated anti_alias_filterZero-phase FIR low-pass applied on the source grid, ahead of a rate cut. Convention butterworth_bandpassButterworth band-pass filter along the last axis. Convention butterworth_lowpassButterworth low-pass filter along the last axis. Convention define_baselineSelect the baseline samples around a signal’s onset and optional offset. describe_time_gridMeasure a timebase’s spacing, uniformity and monotonicity. Convention detect_active_windowReturn the active time window that contains a signal’s main peak. detect_clipped_samplesReturn a boolean mask of samples sitting at an acquisition limit. detrend_moving_averageSubtract a centered moving-average trend along the last axis. Convention exp_baselineExponential model for baseline fitting: y = a * exp(b * x) + c. fir_filterLinear-phase FIR filter along the last axis. Convention fir_filter_coefficientsWindow-method FIR coefficients for a linear-phase filter. Convention infer_signal_orientationInfer the dominant sign of signal from its active region. Convention is_signal_activeDecide whether a trace carries a signal or is flat. line_average_densityReturn line-average electron density given an explicit chord length. Convention linear_baselineLinear model for baseline fitting: y = a * x + b. process_signalLegacy conditioning wrapper: crop, resample, then filter. Convention quadratic_baselineQuadratic model for baseline fitting: y = a * x^2 + b * x + c. repair_clipped_intervalReconstruct samples saturated at an acquisition limit by interpolation. resample_to_timeProject a signal onto target_time, low-passing first if that is a rate cut. Convention signal_on_offsetSmooth a waveform, then return the window in which it is above a threshold. Convention signal_onoffsetDeprecated compatibility wrapper for signal_on_offset. Deprecated smoothApply MATLAB-like moving-average smoothing with edge tapering. Convention subtract_baselineFit a baseline through the selected samples and subtract it everywhere. vest_coil_current_noise_reductionSuppress point spikes in coil current traces. Convention vfit_signal_start_endDeprecated compatibility wrapper for detect_active_window. Deprecated vfit_signal_startendDeprecated compatibility wrapper for detect_active_window. Deprecated No function matches. VEST_CoilCurrentNoiseReduction Deprecated source VEST_CoilCurrentNoiseReduction(data) Deprecated compatibility wrapper for the snake-case function. anti_alias_filter Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source anti_alias_filter(values, *, source_rate, cutoff_hz, stopband_hz=None, numtaps=None, axis=-1, nan_policy='segment', return_mask=False) Zero-phase FIR low-pass applied on the source grid, ahead of a rate cut. This is the half of a downsample that np.interp cannot do for you. Filtering after the rate has already been reduced is too late: whatever folded is now indistinguishable from real in-band signal. NameTypeUnitDescription valuesarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is axis. source_ratefloatHzSample rate of values. cutoff_hzfloatHzPassband edge, strictly inside (0, source_rate / 2). stopband_hzfloat or None, optionalHzFrequency by which the response must be down – for a downsample, the target Nyquist. Sets the transition band and so the tap count. numtapsint or None, optional-Override the designed tap count; forced odd. axisint, optional-The time axis of values. nan_policy{"segment", "error", "ignore"}, optional-"segment" filters each maximal finite run on its own; "error" refuses non-finite samples; "ignore" hands them to filtfilt, which smears them across the record. return_maskbool, optional-Also return which samples the filter actually covered. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe filtered waveform, same shape as values. —np.ndarray of bool-Only with return_mask=True: True where filtfilt ran over the sample, False for a sample left unfiltered (a short record or finite run) and for a non-finite sample under "segment"; same shape as values. Convention Zero-phase, and load-bearing: filterscope intensity feeds onset detection, where a causal filter would move the onset by the group delay. firwin filtfilt rather than a Butterworth or decimate’s Chebyshev, because it is the idiom the VEST mappers already use (machine_mapping/tf.py, machine_mapping/pf_active.py, process/magnetics.py). Raises ResamplingError cutoff_hz or stopband_hz outside their bands, or a non-finite sample under nan_policy="error". ValueError Unknown nan_policy. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Size the filter: numtaps ~ 3.3 * source_rate / (stopband - cutoff), the Hamming-window rule [1], measured against the target Nyquist – not the source Nyquist, which is ten times higher for a VEST fast channel and would size the filter at nine taps instead of the three hundred the job needs. Forced odd so the FIR is Type I with integer group delay. Design it with scipy.signal.firwin (Hamming window, low-pass). Apply scipy.signal.filtfilt to each finite run long enough for it; shorter runs are passed through with a RuntimeWarning. Defaults stopband_hz = 1.25 * cutoff_hz is a numerical convenience consistent with resample_to_time’s default 0.8-of-Nyquist cutoff: it puts the stopband exactly at the target Nyquist. nan_policy = "segment" is a validated-workflow default – one NaN must not blank a whole record. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations filtfilt needs 3 * numtaps + 1 samples; a record or finite run shorter than that is returned unfiltered rather than padded, and nothing is interpolated or invented in its place. One warning per call summarizes how many runs and samples were left unfiltered, so a caller can tell a single stray sample from most of the record; return_mask=True says which samples, so a caller can flag them rather than store them beside filtered values as if they were equivalent (#915). The filter assumes evenly spaced samples; on an irregular grid the design rate is a fiction, which resample_to_time refuses for you. Provenance Hamming-window FIR design rule, N ~ 3.3 f_s / Delta f, e.g. Oppenheim & Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, window method. vaft/machine_mapping/tf.py and pf_active.py, the mappers whose established filtering idiom this generalizes. butterworth_bandpass Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source butterworth_bandpass(data, low, high, fs, order=2, *, zero_phase=True) Butterworth band-pass filter along the last axis. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is the last. lowfloatHzLower band edge. highfloatHzUpper band edge, above low and below the Nyquist frequency. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Filter order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for forward-backward filtfilt; False for a causal lfilter. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe filtered waveform, same shape as data. Convention Zero-phase by default; see butterworth_lowpass for the causal alternative and when each is right. Raises ValueError The band edges do not satisfy 0 < low < high < fs / 2. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults order = 2 is a validated-workflow default shared with butterworth_lowpass. zero_phase = True is the opposite of the low-pass default because band-passed signals feed spectral and mode-number analysis, where phase across channels is the measurement. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations As butterworth_lowpass: a record too short for filtfilt raises from SciPy. butterworth_lowpass Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source butterworth_lowpass(data, cutoff, fs, order=2, *, zero_phase=False) Butterworth low-pass filter along the last axis. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is the last. cutofffloatHzCutoff frequency, strictly between 0 and the Nyquist frequency. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Filter order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for forward-backward filtfilt; False for a causal lfilter. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe filtered waveform, same shape as data. Convention Causal by default. With zero_phase=False every feature is delayed by the filter’s group delay, identically on every channel, which is what ratio and reference arithmetic between SXR channels needs. Pass zero_phase=True wherever a time is going to be read off the result – an onset, a peak – because a causal filter moves it. Raises ValueError cutoff is not inside (0, fs / 2). Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults order = 2 and zero_phase = False are validated-workflow defaults: the values the VEST SXR viewer uses [SXR], kept so that vaft.process.soft_x_rays reproduces it. Applicability Machine-independent. The defaults are VEST SXR practice but embed no VEST constant. Limitations filtfilt needs a record longer than three times the filter’s padding length and raises from SciPy otherwise; nothing here catches that. define_baseline Machine-independent source define_baseline(time, onset_time, onset_window, offset_time=None, offset_window=None) Select the baseline samples around a signal’s onset and optional offset. Converts onset_time (and offset_time) to indices with np.searchsorted and returns the onset_window samples immediately before the onset, plus the offset_window samples immediately after the offset when both are given. The result is what subtract_baseline fits through. NameTypeUnitDescription timenp.ndarraysSample times, sorted. onset_timefloatsTime at which the signal begins to deviate from baseline. onset_windowint-Number of samples before the onset to include. offset_timefloat or None, optionalsTime at which the signal returns to baseline. offset_windowint or None, optional-Number of samples after the offset to include; both offset arguments must be given for the offset region to be used. Returns —np.ndarray-Indices into time of the baseline samples, onset region first. Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Assumptions The signal is genuinely quiet in the selected windows. A window that reaches back into a previous pulse, or forward into pickup from a coil ramp, is fitted as if it were baseline. Applicability Machine-independent. The onset and offset times, and the window widths, are the caller’s; on VEST they come from the magnetics processing window in vest.yaml via vaft.process.magnetics. Limitations Windows are clipped to the record silently, so a window wider than the pre-onset record yields fewer samples than asked, with no warning. Provenance The legacy VEST EFIT magnetics chain [VFIT], where the baseline is taken before the discharge and after it and removed by a fit. describe_time_grid Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source describe_time_grid(time, *, rtol=0.001) Measure a timebase’s spacing, uniformity and monotonicity. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, flattened. rtolfloat, optional-Largest |dt_i - median(dt)| / median(dt) for which the grid is still reported uniform. Returns —TimeGridanyn, t0, the median dt, sample_rate, whether the grid is uniform within rtol and strictly_increasing, and the max_relative_jitter actually measured. Convention dt is the median spacing, robust to the single ragged interval a concatenated acquisition can leave behind. dt and sample_rate are nan for a single-sample grid, where neither is defined; an empty grid reports n = 0 and nan throughout. Defaults · Applicability Defaults rtol = 1e-3 is a numerical convenience sized to an acquisition-era fact: VEST shots after 42190 store their timebase as linspace(0, span, n), so a nominally 4e-6 s grid is really span / (n - 1) = 4.00016e-6 s. That is uniform for every purpose here and a tight tolerance would only reject it. Applicability Machine-independent. detect_active_window Machine-independent source detect_active_window(time, signal, threshold=0.01) Return the active time window that contains a signal’s main peak. Finds the largest sample and walks outward from it in both directions while the signal stays at or above threshold; the window is the time of the first and last sample reached. If the peak itself is below threshold the whole record is returned. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, one-dimensional. signalarray_likeanyThe waveform, one-dimensional, same length as time; already the physical quantity, not a raw digitizer voltage. thresholdfloat, optionalanyLevel at or above which a sample counts as active, in the units of signal. Returns —tuple of (float, float)s(start, end) times of the active window. Raises ValueError The inputs are not one-dimensional, differ in length, or are empty. Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults threshold = 0.01 is a legacy compatibility value from the donor vfit_signal_startend, which was applied to an H-alpha trace normalised to its own minimum. It is absolute, so a caller with a differently scaled signal must pass its own. Assumptions The signal has one dominant positive excursion and is at or above threshold throughout it. A dip below the threshold inside the pulse ends the window early. Applicability Machine-independent. VEST source selection and calibration belong in vaft.machine_mapping; the resulting physical signal is what is passed here. For a plasma onset with evidence and a verdict, use vaft.process.onset instead. Limitations The threshold is absolute, not relative to the peak, and the walk is not robust to noise: a single sample below threshold stops it. Provenance vfit_signal_startend, the function nested in Function/vest_Halpha_tstart_tend.m of the legacy VEST workflow [VFIT]; kept here under the deprecated name vfit_signal_start_end. detect_clipped_samples Machine-independent source detect_clipped_samples(data, *, clip_values, tolerance) Return a boolean mask of samples sitting at an acquisition limit. clip_values is a single signed level or a sequence of them, and the mask is their union: a sample is saturated when it lies within tolerance of any supplied level. Real acquisition hardware rails on both sides and rarely symmetrically – VEST’s diamagnetic Rogowski channel is a signed 16-bit ADC over +/-5 V, so its rails are exactly -5.0 and 5 * 32767 / 32768 [1]. Detecting every level in one pass is not a convenience. Where a waveform oscillates hard enough to hit both rails within a few samples, repairing one rail at a time would fit the reconstruction through samples still pinned at the other one. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform, raw or calibrated; the rails are in its units. clip_valuesfloat or sequence of floatanyThe acquisition limit or limits, signed, in the units of data. tolerancefloatanyHalf-width of the band around each limit inside which a sample counts as saturated. Returns —np.ndarray-Boolean mask, True where the sample is saturated; same shape as data. Raises SignalRepairError clip_values is empty or non-finite, or tolerance is not a positive finite width. Assumptions · Applicability · Provenance Assumptions Saturation shows as a sample at the rail, not as a distorted sample near it. A digitizer that soft-clips will not be detected by a narrow tolerance. Applicability Machine-independent. The caller supplies the rails and tolerance; this function infers nothing about the hardware. The VEST values are read from vest.yaml by vaft.machine_mapping, never here. Provenance vest.yaml, the diamagnetic_flux processing block, where the asymmetric 16-bit rails are derived; issue #285. detrend_moving_average Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source detrend_moving_average(data, window_samples) Subtract a centered moving-average trend along the last axis. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is the last. window_samplesint-Width of the trend window in samples; 1 or less removes nothing. Returns —np.ndarrayanydata minus its rolling mean, same shape. Convention The trend is a centred rolling mean with min_periods=1 semantics: the window at index i spans [i - w//2, i + (w-1)//2] clipped to the record, so edge windows shrink rather than yield NaN and the output has the input’s length. This is exactly pandas.Series.rolling(window, center=True, min_periods=1).mean(), the convention of the validated VEST SXR viewer [SXR], reimplemented with cumulative sums so that vaft.process.soft_x_rays does not need pandas for it. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A centred window is zero-phase but the shrinking edge windows bias the first and last w/2 samples toward the local level. The trend is a plain mean: one large excursion inside the window pulls the trend toward it and appears, inverted, in the neighbours. exp_baseline Machine-independent source exp_baseline(x, a, b, c) Exponential model for baseline fitting: y = a * exp(b * x) + c. NameTypeUnitDescription xarray_likeanyAbscissa, normally time. afloatanyAmplitude. bfloatanyRate; the sign decides growth or decay. cfloatanyOffset. Returns —np.ndarrayanya * exp(b * x) + c. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. A fit model for subtract_baseline. fir_filter Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source fir_filter(data, cutoff, fs, *, kind='lowpass', numtaps=None, window='hann', zero_phase=True) Linear-phase FIR filter along the last axis. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is the last. cutofffloat or sequence of floatHzBand edge, or the pair of edges for bandpass/bandstop. fsfloatHzSample rate. kindstr, optional-lowpass, highpass, bandpass or bandstop. numtapsint or None, optional-Filter length; None derives it from fs (fir_filter_coefficients). windowstr, optional-Window passed to scipy.signal.firwin. zero_phasebool, optional-True for forward-backward filtfilt; False for a causal lfilter that keeps the filter’s own group delay. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe filtered waveform, same shape as data. Convention An FIR filter of this design is already linear-phase, so a causal application shifts every frequency by the same (numtaps - 1) / 2 samples and the delay can be removed exactly – unlike an IIR filter, whose phase distortion is frequency-dependent and only filtfilt removes it. That is the reason to reach for FIR here rather than butterworth_bandpass: the cost is a longer impulse response and more arithmetic per sample. Raises ValueError As fir_filter_coefficients. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults zero_phase = True is a validated-workflow default matching butterworth_bandpass: a filtered fluctuation signal feeds spectral and mode-number analysis, where phase across channels is the measurement. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations filtfilt needs a record longer than roughly three times the tap count and raises from SciPy otherwise; a one-millisecond default response is long at a high sample rate. fir_filter_coefficients Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source fir_filter_coefficients(cutoff, fs, *, kind='lowpass', numtaps=None, window='hann') Window-method FIR coefficients for a linear-phase filter. NameTypeUnitDescription cutofffloat or sequence of floatHzBand edge, or the pair of edges for bandpass/bandstop. fsfloatHzSample rate. kindstr, optional-lowpass, highpass, bandpass or bandstop. numtapsint or None, optional-Filter length; None derives it from fs (see Defaults). windowstr, optional-Window passed to scipy.signal.firwin. Returns —np.ndarray-numtaps coefficients of a symmetric (Type I) FIR filter. Convention The length is always odd, so the filter is Type I: symmetric with an integer group delay of (numtaps - 1) / 2 samples, and with a response that is not forced to zero at the Nyquist frequency – which a Type II (even-length) filter would be, making a high-pass or band-stop unusable. Raises ValueError kind is not one of the four supported responses, the number of band edges does not match it, or an edge is outside 0 < f < fs / 2. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults numtaps = None and window = "hann" are validated-workflow defaults, taken from VEST’s fluctuation analysis. The length is an impulse response one millisecond long, int(fs * 1e-3) forced odd, which ties the transition width to the sample rate rather than to a fixed tap count. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The window method sets the transition width by the tap count alone; it does not meet a stated ripple specification the way an equiripple design would. infer_signal_orientation Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source infer_signal_orientation(signal, *, mask=None, active_fraction=0.1, min_samples=8, agreement=0.6) Infer the dominant sign of signal from its active region. The region is mask when given, otherwise the samples whose magnitude reaches active_fraction of the signal’s peak magnitude – so the long zero stretches before and after a discharge do not vote. The verdict is the sign of the region’s median, resolved only when at least agreement of the region shares it and the region holds at least min_samples finite samples; otherwise it is unresolved and the multiplier is +1 (canonical), never a guess. abs is never applied to the data and no sample is flipped on its own. NameTypeUnitDescription signalarray_likeanyThe waveform, one-dimensional; non-finite samples are ignored. maskarray_like of bool or None, optional-The region to vote over, instead of the magnitude rule. active_fractionfloat, optional-Fraction of the peak magnitude a sample must reach to be in the region min_samplesint, optional-Fewest finite samples the region may hold for a verdict. agreementfloat, optional-Smallest fraction of the region that must share the median’s sign. Returns —SignalOrientation-multiplier (+1 or -1 when resolved, else +1), the median statistic, the region’s count, and a reason when unresolved. Convention The multiplier is meant to be applied to the whole signal once, for display or for a sign-convention check. It never rectifies samples. Raises ValueError signal is not one-dimensional. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults active_fraction = 0.1, min_samples = 8 and agreement = 0.6 are empirical estimates fixed when #307 was implemented; #307 sets the rule (median of an active region, never abs, never per-sample) but records no derivation for the three numbers. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A signal that is genuinely bipolar over its active region – a Mirnov fluctuation, a flux loop through a reversal – is correctly left unresolved, which the caller must handle rather than assume. Provenance Issue #307, which established the rule and its defaults. is_signal_active Machine-independent source is_signal_active(data, var_ratio_thresh=0.01, change_ratio_thresh=0.01, verbose=False) Decide whether a trace carries a signal or is flat. Both tests are relative to the trace’s own level, so the verdict does not depend on the signal’s units or gain. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform; fewer than two samples is never active. var_ratio_threshfloat, optional-Threshold on the variance divided by the squared mean absolute level, the squared coefficient of variation. change_ratio_threshfloat, optional-Threshold on the mean absolute sample-to-sample change divided by the mean absolute level. verbosebool, optional-Print both ratios. Returns —bool-True unless both ratios fall below their thresholds. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults Both thresholds at 1e-2 are legacy compatibility values; no derivation is recorded. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A trace held at a non-zero level with noise far below that level is inactive, whatever the level. The converse is the caveat: the test is scale-free by design and has no absolute floor, so a zero-mean noise trace scores near 1 on both ratios and is reported active at any amplitude. A caller that knows a noise floor must apply it before asking. An identically zero trace is inactive. line_average_density Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source line_average_density(n_e_line, path_length_m) Return line-average electron density given an explicit chord length. NameTypeUnitDescription n_e_linearray_likem^-2Line-integrated electron density along the diagnostic chord. path_length_mfloatmLength of the chord through the plasma. Returns —np.ndarraym^-3Line-average electron density, n_e_line / path_length_m. Convention Line-integrated in, line-averaged out. An interferometer measures the former; the latter is what confinement scalings and Greenwald fractions want. No calibration or geometry is inferred here – the chord length is the caller’s. Raises ValueError path_length_m is not positive. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. The chord length of a VEST interferometer channel comes from vaft.machine_mapping. linear_baseline Machine-independent source linear_baseline(x, a, b) Linear model for baseline fitting: y = a * x + b. NameTypeUnitDescription xarray_likeanyAbscissa, normally time. afloatanySlope. bfloatanyIntercept. Returns —np.ndarrayanya * x + b. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. A fit model for subtract_baseline. process_signal VEST-specificConvention-sensitive source process_signal(time, data, options=None) Legacy conditioning wrapper: crop, resample, then filter. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, flattened. dataarray_likeanyThe waveform, flattened. optionsdict or None, optional-time_range (t_start, t_end) to crop to; resample with dt to write onto a uniform grid; filter_params with type ("lowpass", "highpass", "bandpass"), cutoff and order. Returns —tuple of (np.ndarray, np.ndarray)anyThe conditioned (time, data). Convention Zero-phase (filtfilt) for the shaping filter. The sample rate for filter design is taken from the first two samples, not the median. Raises ValueError A filter_params cutoff outside (0, f_s / 2), a malformed band-pass cutoff, or an unknown filter type. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Processing steps Crop to time_range. Resample onto arange(t[0], t[-1], dt) through resample_to_time, so a rate reduction anti-aliases on the input grid first. Apply a zero-phase Butterworth from filter_params. This is a shaping filter and its cutoff is interpreted against the output grid’s sample rate, not the input’s. Defaults dt = 4e-5 s is the VEST slow-DAQ spacing, a machine-specific setting. cutoff = 1000 Hz and order = 4 are legacy compatibility values whose origin is not recorded. Applicability VEST-specific. The defaults embed the VEST acquisition grid, and the option dictionary is the legacy call convention kept for existing workflows; new code should call resample_to_time and butterworth_lowpass directly. Limitations Kept for compatibility; its future is decided by the module-ownership audit tracked in #263. quadratic_baseline Machine-independent source quadratic_baseline(x, a, b, c) Quadratic model for baseline fitting: y = a * x^2 + b * x + c. NameTypeUnitDescription xarray_likeanyAbscissa, normally time. afloatanyQuadratic coefficient. bfloatanyLinear coefficient. cfloatanyConstant. Returns —np.ndarrayanya * x**2 + b * x + c. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. A fit model for subtract_baseline. repair_clipped_interval Machine-independent source repair_clipped_interval(time, data, *, clip_value, tolerance, min_support=4, return_mask=False) Reconstruct samples saturated at an acquisition limit by interpolation. Samples within tolerance of clip_value are treated as saturated and replaced by a cubic spline fitted to the remaining samples on the physical time axis. Every unsaturated sample is preserved exactly. clip_value may be a single signed level or a sequence of levels, in which case saturation is their union (see detect_clipped_samples). With return_mask=True the saturation mask is returned alongside the repaired waveform, so a caller can report which samples it reconstructed instead of handing downstream consumers an unmarked mixture. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, one-dimensional, same length as data. dataarray_likeanyThe waveform with saturated samples, one-dimensional. clip_valuefloat or sequence of floatanyThe acquisition limit or limits, signed, in the units of data. tolerancefloatanyHalf-width of the band around each limit inside which a sample counts as saturated. min_supportint, optional-Fewest unsaturated samples the spline may be fitted through. return_maskbool, optional-Also return the saturation mask. Returns —np.ndarray or tuple of (np.ndarray, np.ndarray)anyThe repaired waveform, and with return_mask=True also the boolean saturation mask. Raises SignalRepairError The inputs differ in shape or are not one-dimensional; any sample is non-finite; the whole waveform is saturated; fewer than min_support unsaturated samples remain; or the saturated interval reaches either end of the record, which would require extrapolation. Processing steps · Input semantics · Output semantics · Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Mask the saturated samples with detect_clipped_samples. Refuse if the mask covers everything, leaves fewer than min_support samples, or touches either end of the record. Fit scipy.interpolate.CubicSpline through the unsaturated samples against time. Evaluate it at the saturated instants and write those samples back. Input semantics Raw or calibrated – the rails must be expressed in the same units as data. Unrepaired: a waveform that has already been filtered has smeared its rails and cannot be repaired here. Output semantics Repaired. The reconstructed samples are interpolated, not measured; the mask says which they are. Defaults min_support = 4 is a numerical convenience: a cubic spline needs four points to be determined at all, and this is the floor, not a quality bar. Assumptions The waveform is smooth on the scale of the saturated interval, so a cubic through its neighbours is a defensible estimate of what was lost. A saturated interval that hides a genuine fast feature is reconstructed as if the feature were absent. Applicability Machine-independent. Callers supply the limit and tolerance. On VEST the PF6 supply clips near -5000 A and the repair is enabled per acquisition era in vest.yaml, because PF6’s gain flips sign at shot 38110 and before that a -5000 A sample is ordinary data [1]. Limitations Interpolation only: a saturated run at the start or end of the record is refused rather than extrapolated. Reconstructing more than a few samples in a row grows less defensible with every sample; there is no cap on that here, so the caller should look at the mask. Provenance vest.yaml, pf_active processing saturation_repair and the per-era policy comment; the donor vest_pf.m applied the -5000 A repair unconditionally. Issues #195 and #285. resample_to_time Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source resample_to_time(source_time, values, target_time, *, anti_alias='auto', cutoff_fraction=0.8, cutoff_hz=None, numtaps=None, min_ratio=1.05, extrapolate='clamp', nan_policy='segment', on_unsorted='error', axis=-1, return_filter_mask=False) Project a signal onto target_time, low-passing first if that is a rate cut. Use this instead of a bare np.interp anywhere a diagnostic is written onto a common time grid. Interpolation and downsampling look identical in source but are not the same operation: evaluating a signal at new instants is always fine, whereas reducing the sample rate discards the information needed to distinguish a high frequency from its alias, so the content above the new Nyquist has to be removed while it still can be. NameTypeUnitDescription source_timearray_likesSample times of values, flattened; must be strictly increasing under the default on_unsorted. valuesarray_likeanyThe waveform or a stack of them; the time axis is axis. target_timearray_likesInstants to evaluate at; need not be sorted. anti_aliasbool or "auto", optional-"auto" filters only for a genuine rate reduction; True always; False never. cutoff_fractionfloat, optional-Anti-alias cutoff as a fraction of the target Nyquist. cutoff_hzfloat or None, optionalHzExplicit cutoff, overriding cutoff_fraction. numtapsint or None, optional-Passed to anti_alias_filter. min_ratiofloat, optional-dt_target / dt_source at or below which "auto" does not filter. extrapolate{"clamp", "nan", "error"}, optional-What a target sample outside the source span gets. nan_policystr, optional-Passed to anti_alias_filter. on_unsorted{"error", "sort"}, optional-Refuse an unsorted source, or sort it and collapse duplicates. axisint, optional-The time axis of values. return_filter_maskbool, optional-Also return, on the source grid, which samples reached the target band-limited. Returns —np.ndarrayanyvalues on target_time; the time axis has len(target_time) samples. —np.ndarray of bool-Only with return_filter_mask=True (which requires on_unsorted="error"): per source sample, True if no filter was needed or anti_alias_filter covered it, False if a filter was needed but the sample was left unfiltered or is non-finite. It is a logical series: project it with anti_alias=False. Convention The cutoff is placed against the target grid’s spacing measured in time order, even when target_time is unsorted; the shuffled array would report a median dt tens of times too large and design a filter that eats the signal. An explicit cutoff_hz above the target Nyquist is honoured as a deliberate choice to keep more band and gets anti_alias_filter’s own transition instead. Raises ResamplingError Empty source; unsorted or duplicated source times under the default policy; a target outside the source span under extrapolate="error"; a forced filter whose cutoff exceeds the source Nyquist; or a filter requested on a non-uniform source grid. ValueError An option outside its allowed values. Processing steps · Output semantics · Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Validate options; sort and de-duplicate the source if asked. Measure both grids with describe_time_grid. Decide whether to filter: anti_alias as given, or under "auto" whether dt_target / dt_source > min_ratio. If filtering, refuse a non-uniform source, place the cutoff at cutoff_fraction of the target Nyquist (or cutoff_hz), put the stopband at the target Nyquist, and run anti_alias_filter on the source grid. np.interp onto target_time with the extrapolate policy. Output semantics Interpolated. When no filter runs, the result is bit-for-bit np.interp – deliberately, so equal-rate call sites can adopt this primitive without moving a stored value. When one does, the result is band-limited to the target Nyquist and then interpolated. Defaults anti_alias = "auto" and min_ratio = 1.05 are validated-workflow defaults: the safe thing by default, the unsafe thing by name. cutoff_fraction = 0.8 is a numerical convenience – firwin sits at -6 dB at its cutoff and needs a transition band, so a passband edge below Nyquist puts everything that can fold into the stopband. extrapolate = "clamp" matches np.interp. on_unsorted = "error" because np.interp returns silent nonsense for an unsorted x. Assumptions values is a band-limited physical signal. A validity mask or any other logical series is not, and must be resampled with anti_alias=False. Applicability Machine-independent. The motivating case is VEST, which acquires at FAST_DT = 4e-6 s and SLOW_DT = 4e-5 s while every processed grid in vest.yaml is 4e-5 s, so a fast channel written onto a policy grid is a 10x decimation [1]. Limitations A single-sample target has no Nyquist: "auto" interpolates with a warning and True raises unless cutoff_hz is given. A non-uniform source grid cannot be anti-aliased by a single-rate FIR and is refused; resample onto a uniform grid first, or pass anti_alias=False to accept a bare interpolation knowingly. Provenance vaft.database.raw FAST_DT / SLOW_DT, and the processed time grids declared in vaft/machine_mapping/vest.yaml. signal_on_offset Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source signal_on_offset(time, data, smooth_window=5, threshold=0.01, verbose=False) Smooth a waveform, then return the window in which it is above a threshold. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, one-dimensional. dataarray_likeanyThe waveform, one-dimensional, same length as time. smooth_windowint, optional-Savitzky-Golay window length in samples; must be odd and larger than the polynomial order, 3. thresholdfloat, optionalanyLevel at or above which the smoothed signal counts as active, in the units of data. verbosebool, optional-Print the threshold. Returns —tuple of (float, float)s(onset, offset) times. Convention Zero-phase: a Savitzky-Golay filter is a centred polynomial fit and moves nothing in time, so the returned onset is not delayed by the smoothing. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Processing steps Smooth with scipy.signal.savgol_filter(data, smooth_window, 3). Hand the smoothed waveform to detect_active_window. Defaults smooth_window = 5 and the cubic polynomial are legacy compatibility values from the ported workflow, unrecorded beyond that. threshold = 0.01 is inherited from detect_active_window. Applicability Machine-independent. Callers in vaft.omas.general and vaft.database pass threshold=0.05 for VEST H-alpha; the default is not a VEST policy. For a plasma onset with evidence and a verdict, use vaft.process.onset. Limitations Those of detect_active_window: an absolute threshold and a walk that stops at the first sample below it. signal_onoffset Deprecated source signal_onoffset(time, data, smooth_window=5, threshold=0.01, verbose=False) Deprecated compatibility wrapper for signal_on_offset. smooth Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source smooth(array, span) Apply MATLAB-like moving-average smoothing with edge tapering. A centred moving average of odd width span. At each end the window shrinks symmetrically – widths 1, 3, 5, … – so the output has the input’s length and no sample is padded, which is what MATLAB’s smooth does and what the ported VEST workflows expect. NameTypeUnitDescription arrayarray_likeanyThe waveform, one-dimensional. spanint-Window width in samples; an even value is reduced by one, and a value wider than the record is clipped to it. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe smoothed waveform, same length as array. Convention Zero-phase: the window is centred, so features are not shifted in time. Edge samples are averaged over progressively narrower windows rather than over a padded record, which biases the ends less than reflection padding would but leaves them noisier than the interior. Raises ValueError array is not one-dimensional. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance MATLAB smooth(y, span) with the default 'moving' method; ported from the legacy VEST workflow [VFIT] with its semantics preserved so that results match the donor sample for sample. subtract_baseline Machine-independent source subtract_baseline(time, signal, baseline_indices, fitting_opt='linear') Fit a baseline through the selected samples and subtract it everywhere. NameTypeUnitDescription timenp.ndarraysSample times. signalnp.ndarrayanyThe waveform, same length as time. baseline_indicesnp.ndarray-Indices of the samples the baseline is fitted through, normally from define_baseline. fitting_opt{"linear", "quadratic", "spline", "exp"}, optional-The baseline model. Returns correctednp.ndarrayanysignal minus the fitted baseline. baselinenp.ndarrayanyThe fitted baseline evaluated on the whole time axis. Raises ValueError Unknown fitting_opt. Processing steps · Output semantics · Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Take time and signal at baseline_indices. Fit the chosen model through them: scipy.optimize.curve_fit for the parametric models, scipy.interpolate.UnivariateSpline(s=0) – an interpolating spline – for "spline". Evaluate the model on the full time axis and subtract. Output semantics Baseline-subtracted. The second return is the baseline itself, so the caller can plot or store what was removed. Defaults fitting_opt = "linear" is a legacy compatibility value: the donor workflow removed a linear drift, which is the right model for an integrator’s offset. The exponential fit uses maxfev = 10000, a numerical convenience. Assumptions The samples at baseline_indices contain no signal. The parametric models assume the drift has that form over the whole record, including the pulse, where it is extrapolated rather than measured. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations "spline" interpolates the baseline samples exactly, so noise in them is reproduced in the baseline; with the onset and offset regions far apart it is a straight line between them in practice. "exp" can fail to converge and raises from SciPy. Nothing checks that baseline_indices is non-empty. Provenance The legacy VEST EFIT magnetics chain [VFIT], where an integrated probe signal’s drift is removed by a fit through the pre- and post-discharge windows. vest_coil_current_noise_reduction VEST-specificConvention-sensitive source vest_coil_current_noise_reduction(data) Suppress point spikes in coil current traces. Walks the record and, wherever a sample’s magnitude exceeds the mean of its two neighbours’ magnitudes by more than a fixed margin, replaces it with the previous sample. A port of the donor routine, kept sample for sample so that the legacy PF-current preprocessing reproduces. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeACoil current, one-dimensional; records shorter than three samples are returned unchanged. Returns —np.ndarrayAThe de-spiked current, same length. Convention Causal: a spike is replaced by its predecessor, so a genuine step is delayed by one sample at its leading edge. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps For each interior sample (the first two and the last are never touched), compute |x[i]| - |(x[i+1] + x[i-1]) / 2|. Where that exceeds 0.001, overwrite x[i] with the already processed x[i-1]. Defaults The 0.001 margin is a legacy compatibility value from the donor VEST_CoilCurrentNoiseReduction.m [1]. It is absolute, in the units of data, and its derivation is not recorded. On a trace in amperes it flags any excursion above a milliamp, so in practice every spike; on a trace in kiloamperes it would let real noise through. Applicability VEST-specific. Written for the VEST PF coil current traces as digitized by the legacy DAQ; the margin has no meaning for another machine’s units or noise floor. Limitations Only a single-sample spike is caught: two consecutive bad samples pass, because the second is compared against the first. Sign is ignored in the test but preserved in the replacement. Provenance Function/VEST_CoilCurrentNoiseReduction.m in the legacy VEST workflow [VFIT]; loop bounds and margin preserved. vfit_signal_start_end Deprecated source vfit_signal_start_end(time, data, threshold=0.01) Deprecated compatibility wrapper for detect_active_window. vfit_signal_startend Deprecated source vfit_signal_startend(time, data, threshold=0.01) Deprecated compatibility wrapper for detect_active_window.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/numerica.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.numerical: 1 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("numerical.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview One function so far. Anything that is a physics formula belongs in vaft.formula; anything that knows about a diagnostic belongs in a diagnostic module. This is for the operations that are neither. SymbolMeaningUnit ttimes xthe sampled quantityany Functions time_derivativeTime derivative of a sampled quantity on a non-uniform time axis. Convention No function matches. time_derivative Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source time_derivative(time, data) Time derivative of a sampled quantity on a non-uniform time axis. A weighted central difference: at each interior point the forward and backward differences are averaged with weights proportional to the opposite interval, so the closer neighbour counts more. On a uniform grid this reduces to the ordinary central difference; the ends use a one-sided difference. NameTypeUnitDescription timenp.ndarraysSample times; spacing may vary. datanp.ndarrayanyThe sampled quantity, same shape as time. Returns —np.ndarrayany/sd(data)/dt at each sample, same shape as data. Convention The weighting is the simple interval-weighted average of the two one-sided differences, not the second-order non-uniform stencil; it is what was written and is kept so that results do not move. Raises ValueError The arrays differ in shape, or hold fewer than two samples. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations Processing steps First sample: forward difference. Last sample: backward difference. Interior sample i: with h_b = t[i] - t[i-1] and h_f = t[i+1] - t[i], the derivative is (h_f * backward + h_b * forward) / (h_b + h_f). A zero interval on either side falls back to the difference across the other; zero on both sides yields 0. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A zero time interval produces a 0 derivative silently rather than an error, so a duplicated timestamp hides as a flat spot. The scheme is first-order accurate on a non-uniform grid and amplifies sample noise as any finite difference does; smooth or filter first if the derivative is to be read quantitatively. The loop over interior points is pure Python and slow on long records.

Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("statistical_analysis.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview The workflow behind the confinement-scaling study: take a table of shots with their engineering parameters and energy confinement time, take natural logarithms, fit ln tau_E = c0 + sum_i c_i ln p_i by ordinary least squares, and read the scaling exponents off the coefficients. Everything operates on pandas DataFrames whose columns are named by the caller; nothing here knows which columns exist except through the eng_params list it is handed. Two functions are not statistics and are here for historical reasons: generate_core_profiles_history_dataframe builds the input table by running a workflow script, and confinement_time_histogram draws one. Both are documented as they are; their home is decided by #263. SymbolMeaningUnit tau_Eenergy confinement times p_ian engineering parameterany c_ithe scaling exponent of ``p_i``- alphasignificance level- Functions analyze_significanceFlag which scaling exponents are statistically significant. compute_metricsGoodness-of-fit metrics of the regression in original units. Convention confinement_time_histogramPlot histograms of the scaling parameters in an m x n grid. filter_dataframeDrop shots with unrealistic loss power and rectify the toroidal field sign. Convention generate_core_profiles_history_dataframeBuild the scaling table by running the core-profiles history workflow. get_correlation_matrixPearson correlation matrix of the log-transformed regressors and target. get_individual_correlationsPearson correlation of each log regressor with the log target. get_residualsResiduals of the log-space fit. load_data_from_excelLoad a confinement-scaling table from an Excel file. log_transformTake natural logarithms of the engineering parameters and the target. Convention perform_ols_regressionFit the log-linear scaling by ordinary least squares. Convention No function matches. analyze_significance Machine-independent source analyze_significance(results, alpha=0.05) Flag which scaling exponents are statistically significant. NameTypeUnitDescription resultsRegressionResults-A fitted regression. alphafloat, optional-Significance level; a coefficient with p < alpha is significant Returns —dict of str to bool-Parameter name to whether its exponent is significant; a parameter absent from the fit is False. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations Defaults alpha = 0.05 is the conventional literature value, no more. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A p-value from a small sample with correlated regressors overstates significance; see get_correlation_matrix before trusting it. compute_metrics Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source compute_metrics(results, df, target_param='tauE_s') Goodness-of-fit metrics of the regression in original units. NameTypeUnitDescription resultsRegressionResults-A fitted regression. dfpd.DataFrame-The original table the regression was fitted from. target_paramstr, optional-Column name of the confinement time. Returns —dict of str to float-R2, RMSE, MAE, Mean_Relative_Error_% and Median_Relative_Error_%. Convention Metrics are in the original units, so R2 here is not the rsquared of the log fit on the results object; the two differ and both are reported deliberately. RMSE and MAE carry the target’s unit, seconds for tauE_s, and are returned as plain floats. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations Processing steps Exponentiate the fitted log values to get predicted confinement times. Select the actual values at the rows the fit used. Compute the metrics with sklearn.metrics and NumPy. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations When the fitted values carry no index the actual values are truncated to the shorter length, which silently misaligns rows if any were dropped. confinement_time_histogram Machine-independent source confinement_time_histogram(df, eng_params=None, m=None, n=None, figsize=None, bins=30, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', **kwargs) Plot histograms of the scaling parameters in an m x n grid. Returns —matplotlib.figure.Figure-The figure, as vaft.plot.history.confinement_time_histogram returns it. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Rendering lives in vaft.plot.history.confinement_time_histogram (issue #63); this is a compatibility shim that keeps the old call site and pulls Matplotlib in on call. Convention Bt_T is made positive regardless of the field direction actually run, so the fit sees magnitude only. Any sign convention on the field is discarded here. Defaults The 3 MW ceiling is a hard-coded empirical cut from the study; its derivation is not recorded. It is not a parameter. Applicability VEST-specific. The ceiling and the column names are the VEST study’s. Returns —pd.DataFrame-One row per shot with the engineering parameters and tauE_s. Raises ImportError The workflow script cannot be found or loaded. ValueError The script returned nothing. Returns —pd.DataFrame-The correlation matrix over the available ln_ columns; empty when fewer than two exist. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Pairwise-complete, as DataFrame.corr is; rows are not dropped consistently across pairs. get_individual_correlations Machine-independent source get_individual_correlations(log_df, eng_params, target_param='tauE_s') Pearson correlation of each log regressor with the log target. NameTypeUnitDescription log_dfpd.DataFrame-Output of log_transform. eng_paramslist of str-Column names of the engineering parameters. target_paramstr, optional-Column name of the confinement time. Returns —dict of str to float-Parameter name to its correlation with the target; NaN when the column is missing or fewer than two complete rows exist. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. get_residuals Machine-independent source get_residuals(results) Residuals of the log-space fit. NameTypeUnitDescription resultsRegressionResults-A fitted regression. Returns —pd.Series-ln(actual) - ln(fitted) per row used in the fit. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. load_data_from_excel Machine-independent source load_data_from_excel(filepath) Load a confinement-scaling table from an Excel file. NameTypeUnitDescription filepathstr-Path to the .xlsx file; one row per shot, columns as the study named them. Returns —pd.DataFrame-The table as read, untouched. Raises Exception Whatever pandas.read_excel raises, after logging it. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. The tables under workflow/automatic_pipeline_3_data_summary/ are VEST, but nothing here depends on that. Provenance The study notebook [NB]. log_transform Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source log_transform(df, eng_params, target_param='tauE_s') Take natural logarithms of the engineering parameters and the target. NameTypeUnitDescription dfpd.DataFrame-The scaling table. eng_paramslist of str-Column names of the engineering parameters. target_paramstr, optional-Column name of the confinement time. Returns —pd.DataFrame-Columns ln_<name> for each parameter and the target, same index as df; a missing column becomes all-NaN with a warning. Convention Natural logarithm, so the fitted coefficients are the exponents of a power law directly. A value that is not strictly positive has no logarithm and becomes NaN, to be dropped by perform_ols_regression. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. perform_ols_regression Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source perform_ols_regression(df, eng_params, target_param='tauE_s', dropna=True) Fit the log-linear scaling by ordinary least squares. NameTypeUnitDescription dfpd.DataFrame-The scaling table, in original units. eng_paramslist of str-Column names of the engineering parameters to regress on. target_paramstr, optional-Column name of the confinement time. dropnabool, optional-Drop rows with any NaN among the regressors or the target. Returns —RegressionResults-The fitted statsmodels model with the log table, the parameter list and the target name; get_exponents() reads the scaling exponents off it. Convention The fit is in log space, so the coefficients are exponents and the residuals are relative errors. Metrics in original units come from compute_metrics, which exponentiates the fitted values. Raises ValueError No rows remain after dropping NaN. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps log_transform the table. Select the ln_ regressors and the ln_ target. Drop rows with NaN, if dropna. Add an intercept column and fit statsmodels.api.OLS. Defaults dropna = True is a validated-workflow default; statsmodels would otherwise raise on NaN. Applicability Machine-independent.
