/vaft/develop/reference/process/cocos/.title: Process reference: cocos
/vaft/develop/reference/process/cocos/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.cocos: 6 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("cocos.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview vaft.data.cocos declares what each convention and each external code is. This module answers whether a given equilibrium is actually consistent with the convention it claims, which is the check that catches a mislabelled file before its signs propagate into derived quantities. Sauter & Medvedev 2013 Eq. 23 gives six relations that any equilibrium in a given COCOS must satisfy, in terms of the signs of the plasma current and the vacuum toroidal field: =============== ===================================== quantity required sign =============== ===================================== F sigma_B0 Phi_tor sigma_B0 psi_edge - sigma_Ip * sigma_Bp psi_axis dp/dpsi -sigma_Ip * sigma_Bp j_phi sigma_Ip q sigma_Ip * sigma_B0 * sigma_rhotheta =============== ===================================== The q relation is reported as a warning rather than an error: Sauter Sect. IV notes that codes frequently emit abs(q), so a mismatch there is common and is not on its own evidence of a wrong index. Only four of the six are checkable against vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData as it stands: it carries no toroidal current density and no toroidal flux, so j_phi and Phi_tor are always reported as unverifiable. They are listed here because they are part of Eq. 23 and become checkable if those fields are ever added, not because they are being tested today. Functions cocos_consistency_signsObserved sign of each Sauter Eq. 23 quantity, or None where not determinable. Convention cocos_field_scalesThe two sign multipliers that carry an equilibrium from one COCOS to another. Convention identify_conventionCandidate COCOS indices for an equilibrium, from its observable signs. Convention identify_flux_exponentDecide whether psi is stored in weber or weber per radian, from Ampere’s law. Convention identify_flux_exponent_from_qDecide weber versus weber per radian by rebuilding q on closed contours. Convention validate_cocosCheck an equilibrium against the Sauter Eq. 23 relations for one COCOS index. Convention No function matches. cocos_consistency_signs Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source cocos_consistency_signs(equilibrium) Observed sign of each Sauter Eq. 23 quantity, or None where not determinable. Reads signs off the equilibrium as it stands. Nothing is compared against a convention here and nothing is converted; validate_cocos does the comparison and vaft.process.equilibrium.convert_cocos is the only transform in the package. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-The equilibrium to inspect. Missing fields yield None for the relations that need them rather than an error. Returns —dict of str to int or None-Keys f, q, j_phi, phi_tor, dpsi, pprime; each +1, -1, or None when the field is absent or all-zero. Convention Signs only, in whatever convention the equilibrium is already in; this function neither assumes nor imposes a COCOS. j_phi and phi_tor are always None today because vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData carries neither a toroidal current density nor a toroidal flux; they are reported so that Eq. 23 is represented in full, not because they are tested. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps f, q, j_phi and phi_tor: the sign of the profile’s median, with a deadband so a numerically-zero profile reports None. dpsi: the sign of psi_boundary - psi_axis. pprime: the stored pprime profile’s sign when the equilibrium carries one, which for a GEQDSK or an ODS it essentially always does. Only when it does not is the bulk slope (p_edge - p_axis)/(psi_edge - psi_axis) used instead, taken on a profile reordered axis-to-edge so the direction is known. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A bulk slope is the sign of the overall trend, not of every point: a non-monotonic pressure profile still reports one sign. Because the stored pprime takes precedence, the fallback rarely runs in practice; that the two paths can disagree for a hand-built equilibrium is tracked in #605. Provenance Sauter and Medvedev, Tokamak Coordinate Conventions: COCOS, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184, 293 (2013), Eq. 23, which defines the six sign relations this function measures. The preference for a bulk pressure slope over a pointwise derivative is that paper’s own recommendation. cocos_field_scales Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source cocos_field_scales(source, target) The two sign multipliers that carry an equilibrium from one COCOS to another. NameTypeUnitDescription sourceint-The index the equilibrium is in. targetint-The index it is wanted in. Returns —tuple of int-(psi_scale, field_scale), each +1 or -1. psi_scale multiplies the poloidal flux – psi on the grid and the axis and boundary values with it – and field_scale multiplies the toroidal field and the poloidal current function F. Convention From Sauter Eq. 12, B_pol = sigma_Bp sigma_RphiZ grad(psi) x grad(phi) / (2 pi)**e_Bp: the sign psi carries relative to the physical poloidal field is the product sigma_Bp * sigma_RphiZ, so the flux flips when that product differs between the two conventions. The toroidal field’s direction follows sigma_RphiZ alone, so F and B_t flip when the handedness of (R, phi, Z) differs. This is a sign conversion, not a unit conversion. e_Bp differs between the 1-8 and 11-18 families by a factor of 2 pi on psi, and nothing here applies it: a caller crossing the families has to scale the flux itself, and identify_flux_exponent is what tells it which family a file is in. Raises ValueError Either index is not one of the eighteen COCOS indices. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Look up both conventions’ sigma_Bp and sigma_RphiZ. The flux multiplier is the product of the two sigma_Bp sigma_RphiZ products; the field multiplier is the product of the two sigma_RphiZ. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Says nothing about sigma_rhothetaphi, which sets the poloidal angle’s direction. Two conventions differing only in that give (+1, +1) here and still disagree about the sign of theta – a caller relabelling a poloidal angle needs the third sigma, not these two. Provenance O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. 12 and Table I. Two conversions measured on real runs, both reproduced by this rule: a COCOS 5 g-file into FLARE’s COCOS 3 needs (-1, +1), and a COCOS 2 CHEASE equilibrium needs (+1, -1). identify_convention Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source identify_convention(equilibrium, *, clockwise_phi=None) Candidate COCOS indices for an equilibrium, from its observable signs. Narrows rather than decides: the return is every index consistent with what the data shows, which is often more than one. A caller that needs a single index supplies the missing fact instead of guessing. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry bt0, ip, q and psi_1d; without them the candidate set is empty. clockwise_phibool, optional-Whether the machine’s toroidal angle runs clockwise seen from above. A fact about the machine, not about the data; without it both the odd and the even index of each pair are returned. Returns —tuple of int-The candidate COCOS indices in increasing order, empty when the required fields are missing or the sign identification fails. Convention Returns indices in the standard 1 to 18 numbering; 9 and 10 do not exist. The sign family and the storage family are identified by different evidence, signs for the first and an Ampere loop integral for the second, and either can be inconclusive on its own. What each index means is declared in vaft.data.cocos, not here. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Reorder psi_1d and q axis-to-edge when the stored profile runs the other way. Get the sign family from omas.identify_cocos, which reads it off the signs of ip, bt0, q and the psi gradient. Narrow to 1-8 or 11-18 using identify_flux_exponent, falling back to identify_flux_exponent_from_q when that one had no inputs to measure, and keeping the full set when neither answers. Applicability Machine-independent. clockwise_phi is where a machine’s own geometry enters. Limitations The axis-to-edge reorder exists because identify_cocos reads the psi gradient at the first node, so a boundary-first profile would invert the poloidal-flux sign silently. When both flux-exponent rungs abstain the result spans both storage families, and a caller that then converts must not assume the candidates share one. The contour-q rung is deliberately not consulted when the Ampere rung ran and rejected both families: that is a file whose ip and psi map disagree, and reporting a confident index for it would hide the disagreement rather than resolve it. Any exception from the underlying identification is reported as no candidates rather than raised. Provenance Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for the index numbering and the sign relations the identification rests on. omas.identify_cocos supplies the sign family; its flux-exponent argument is deliberately not used, see identify_flux_exponent. The contour-q fallback is hsyun_GPEC library/geqdsk_cocos.py::flux_normalization_diagnostic, ported in identify_flux_exponent_from_q. identify_flux_exponent Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source identify_flux_exponent(equilibrium) Decide whether psi is stored in weber or weber per radian, from Ampere’s law. The loop integral of the poloidal field around the last closed flux surface equals mu0*|Ip|. Computing that field from psi as if it were weber per radian gives a ratio of 1 when the assumption holds and 2*pi when psi is really in weber, so the two answers are a factor 2*pi apart and the test is decisive rather than a threshold on a continuum. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry ip, a closed lcfs, and a psi map on its r and z grid; anything missing yields (None, None). Returns —tuple of (int or None, float or None)-(e_Bp, ratio). e_Bp is 0 for a weber-per-radian psi (COCOS 1-8) and 1 for a weber psi (COCOS 11-18), or None when the inputs are unavailable or the ratio lands near neither answer. ratio is the measured loop integral over mu0*|Ip|. Convention Decides which storage family psi is in; it does not rescale psi and does not say which of the eight sign orientations applies. e_Bp is Sauter’s flux exponent: 0 means the 2*pi is not carried in psi, 1 means it is. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Close the LCFS contour and compute the poloidal field on it with vaft.process.equilibrium.poloidal_field_at_boundary in the weber-per-radian form; only the magnitude matters. Integrate it along the contour by the trapezoidal rule. Divide by mu0*|Ip|. Accept 0 or 1 if the ratio is within FLUX_EXPONENT_TOLERANCE of 1 or 2*pi; otherwise abstain. Defaults FLUX_EXPONENT_TOLERANCE is 0.15, a numerical convenience rather than a physical threshold: a correct equilibrium lands within about half a percent, the residual being LCFS discretization, so the band is roughly thirty times the observed error while leaving the two acceptance windows far apart, at 0.85 to 1.15 against 5.34 to 7.23. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Abstains rather than picking the nearer of two wrong answers. A ratio near neither value is evidence the input is broken, a truncated LCFS or an ip that disagrees with the psi map, not evidence of a convention. Needs a 2-D psi map and an LCFS, so a profiles-only equilibrium cannot be classified. Provenance Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for e_Bp and the storage families. Replaces the a argument of omas.identify_cocos, which is not usable here: it evaluates pi*B0*(a[i]-a[0])**2/(psi[i]-psi[0]) at the node adjacent to the axis, where the minor radius goes as sqrt(psi), so a linear reconstruction underestimates it and the estimate depends on its square. On the packaged VEST sample that picks the wrong family on a margin of 0.22 against 1.67, where this loop integral separates 1.004 from 6.31. identify_flux_exponent_from_q Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source identify_flux_exponent_from_q(equilibrium, *, levels=None) Decide weber versus weber per radian by rebuilding q on closed contours. The second, independent answer to the question identify_flux_exponent asks. The safety factor of a closed surface is q = |F|/(2*pi) * contour_integral(dl / (R |grad psi|)) when psi is in weber per radian, and 2*pi times that when psi is in weber, so comparing both reconstructions against the q profile the file already carries separates the two families. It needs q and F; it needs neither ip nor a boundary outline, which is exactly what identify_flux_exponent cannot do without. On the three real equilibria this was measured on the two agree; where they differ is that this one still answers when the current record is zero or the boundary outline is missing. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry r, z, psi, psi_axis, psi_boundary, psi_1d, q and f; anything missing is an abstention, not an error. levelsarray_like, optional-Normalized flux levels to trace, defaulting to CONTOUR_Q_LEVELS Returns —ContourQNormalization-exponent 0 for weber per radian and 1 for weber, or None with a reason when the measurement does not support either. Convention Decides Sauter’s flux exponent e_Bp – whether the 2*pi is carried inside psi – and nothing else. It does not rescale psi, does not identify a sign orientation, and does not distinguish the eight indices within a family. q and F are compared by magnitude, because codes routinely emit abs(q) and the sign question belongs to validate_cocos. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Trace each requested level with vaft.process.equilibrium.extract_flux_surface_contours and keep the longest closed contour that encloses the magnetic axis; a level whose contours are all open or all off-axis contributes nothing. On each kept contour evaluate |grad psi| = R * B_p with vaft.process.equilibrium.poloidal_field_at_boundary in its weber-per-radian form and integrate dl / (R |grad psi|) by the midpoint rule. Form the two candidate safety factors, |F|/(2*pi) times that integral and 2*pi times the first, and take each one’s |ln(q_model / q_stored)| against the stored |q| interpolated to the level. Take the median of each across the surfaces and accept the smaller one, but only when it is itself within CONTOUR_Q_LOG_TOLERANCE. Defaults CONTOUR_Q_LEVELS and CONTOUR_Q_MIN_SURFACES are legacy compatibility values, carried over from geqdsk_cocos.flux_normalization_diagnostic so the two agree surface for surface. CONTOUR_Q_LOG_TOLERANCE is a numerical convenience: the Ampere rung’s 15% band made symmetric in the ratio, so a model q 1.16 times too large and one 1.16 times too small are equally far out. A plain relative error is not symmetric and accepted the second while rejecting the first. Applicability Machine-independent. Needs a 2-D psi map with closed interior surfaces, so a profiles-only equilibrium cannot be classified. Limitations Abstains rather than picking the nearer of two wrong answers. A q profile that disagrees with its own psi map – a rescaled psi, a q taken from a different solve – makes both hypotheses wrong, and this reports that rather than a family. Marching squares resolves a contour only to the grid cell, so the log-ratio has a floor set by the grid: it was 1e-5 to 4e-4 on 129-by-129 and 513-by-513 reconstructions, against a losing log-ratio of ln(2*pi) = 1.8379. Provenance hsyun_GPEC library/geqdsk_cocos.py::flux_normalization_diagnostic on branch codex/gpec-flare-cocos-handshake, which is the method and the levels. Its acceptance rule was relative only – the winner had to beat the loser threefold, with no bar on the winner’s own agreement – and that accepts a decisive-looking wrong answer: measured on a real g-file with psi scaled by one half, the winning hypothesis is off by a factor of 2.00 and the separation is still 3.65, so the legacy returns “weber per radian, decisive” for a hypothesis its own measurement misses by a factor of two. The bar in step 4 is what rejects it (D-04), and it makes the threefold rule unreachable: the two hypotheses sit exactly ln(2*pi) apart, so a winner inside the band leaves a ratio of at least twelve. The separation is reported, not applied. Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for e_Bp and the storage families. validate_cocos Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source validate_cocos(equilibrium, cocos=None, *, sigma_ip=None, sigma_b0=None) Check an equilibrium against the Sauter Eq. 23 relations for one COCOS index. The check that catches a mislabelled file before its signs propagate into derived quantities. Never raises on an inconsistency: it returns a report and lets the caller decide whether a mismatch is fatal. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-The equilibrium to check. cocosint, optional-The convention to check against, 1 to 18. Defaults to the index recorded on the equilibrium’s own convention. sigma_ipint, optional-Sign of the plasma current, +1 or -1. Defaults to the sign of the equilibrium’s ip. sigma_b0int, optional-Sign of the vacuum toroidal field. Defaults to the sign of bt0. Returns —ValidationReport-One issue per violated relation, plus at most one cocos_unverifiable warning covering every relation whose inputs were missing. An empty report means every checkable relation held. Convention Checks consistency with a convention; it does not identify one and does not convert. A mismatch on q is reported at warning severity rather than error, because codes commonly emit abs(q) and a sign disagreement there is not on its own evidence of a wrong index. Every other relation is an error. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Resolve the target index and the two reference signs from the arguments, falling back to the equilibrium’s own convention and field signs. Measure the observed signs with cocos_consistency_signs. Compare each against the sign Eq. 23 requires for that index, collecting the mismatches. Collapse every unverifiable relation into a single warning rather than one issue each. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Only four of Eq. 23’s six relations are checkable against vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData as it stands; j_phi and phi_tor have no field to read and are always unverifiable. A passing report therefore means “consistent as far as the stored fields can say”, not “the index is correct”. Provenance Sauter and Medvedev (2013), Eq. 23 for the relations and Sect. IV for the rule that a q sign mismatch is a warning, not a rejection.

All process categories Overview The chain, and where each step’s state changes:: measured diagnostic points (R, Z, value) -> equilibrium-mapped coordinates: psi_norm, rho_pol_norm = sqrt(psi_norm), rho_tor_norm from the equilibrium's own Phi(psi) [MappedPositions] -> coordinate-selected profile points (default rho_tor_norm) -> fitted callable in that coordinate [FittedProfile] -> equilibrium-grid profile, stored on grid.rho_tor_norm / psi / rho_pol_norm with the fit's provenance beside it [core_profiles] Everything here is machine-independent. The radial coordinate to fit in, the statistical Ti/Te ratio for a Thomson-only slice, and their provenance are arguments; on VEST the pipeline (vaft.code.efit.build_kinetic_core_profiles) resolves them from vest.yaml through vaft.machine_mapping.core_profiles.vest_core_profiles_policy. This module holds no VEST number (issue #420). A fit is a function of exactly one of them and carries which; core_profiles evaluates it on the equilibrium grid expressed in that coordinate. Parameter names that still say rho (rho_points, the deprecated mapped_rho_position) predate the choice and mean “the fit coordinate”. Any equilibrium record with a gridded flux map: an analytic Solov’ev or Guazzotto-Freidberg geometry, a GEQDSK, an ODS slice through vaft.process.equilibrium.as_equilibrium. Limitations Without an lcfs outline only the flux threshold is used, which can admit exterior points where the flux turns over near coils. A flux function is constant on flux surfaces by construction; the projection adds no poloidal variation. Provenance VAFT issue #1045: the explicit f(psi_N) -> f(R, Z) mapping. project_plasma_state Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source project_plasma_state(state, equilibrium, quantity='p_total', *, outside='nan') Project one quantity of an analytic plasma state onto an equilibrium’s (R, Z) grid. NameTypeUnitDescription stateAnalyticPlasmaState-From compose_plasma_state or a preset. equilibriumEquilibriumData-The geometry to project onto; it is read, never changed. quantitystr, optional-Any quantity evaluate_plasma_state accepts. outsidestr, optional-"nan" or "edge", as in project_flux_function. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe quantity on the grid, shape (r.size, z.size), in the unit of vaft.data.ANALYTIC_STATE_UNITS. Convention Evaluated exactly from the state’s analytic definition at each point’s psi_norm, not interpolated from the state’s sampling grid. The profile keeps its 1-D definition whatever geometry it is projected onto. Raises ValueError As for project_flux_function and evaluate_plasma_state. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The projected pressure is not the equilibrium’s own pressure: the state was prescribed, and the geometry was solved for different sources. Making them agree is a new equilibrium solve (CHEASE refinement, #123). Provenance VAFT issue #1045: 2-D projection of a prescribed plasma state. spec_from_plasma_state Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source spec_from_plasma_state(state, *, main_ion='H', label=None) The generator spec that reproduces a #1045 analytic plasma state on any equilibrium. NameTypeUnitDescription stateAnalyticPlasmaState-From a preset (vaft.process.profile.analytic_hmode_state, …) or vaft.process.profile.compose_plasma_state. main_ionstr, optional-Hydrogenic main-ion label, "H", "D" or "T"; the state itself does not name one. labelstr, optional-Label of the spec; the state’s label when omitted. Returns —SyntheticKineticSpec-pressure_constraint="kinetic", the state’s three channels as unnormalized vaft.data.analytic_plasma_state.AnalyticProfile shapes, T_i as an independent profile, the state’s composition, and its psi_norm grid when that runs from 0 to 1. Convention The channels stay in psi_norm exactly as the state defines them, so the generator evaluates the same analytic functions: a preset is the Level 1 special case of the generator with no normalization and no pressure constraint. The impurity is the element whose nuclear charge equals state.impurity_charge (carbon for the default 6). Raises SyntheticProfileError The state’s impurity charge matches no species of vaft.data.ION_SPECIES, or the main ion is not hydrogenic. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VAFT issue #1045, whose presets become special cases of the #122 generator’s inputs. strip_electron_only_pressure Machine-independent source strip_electron_only_pressure(ods) Drop slice-total pressure from every core_profiles slice with no ion temperature. Each leaf in TOTAL_PRESSURE_LEAVES is a sum over species, so none of them is meaningful on a slice that never measured an ion. A slice carrying ion.0.temperature is a real kinetic one and keeps its pressure; the rest are stripped in place. Assuming a Ti/Te ratio is a legitimate thing to do – it is what the electron-efit lineage exists for – but the assumption has to be declared by whoever makes it, rather than reaching a product whose consumers read it as measured. NameTypeUnitDescription odsomas.ODSn/aMutated in place. An ODS with no core_profiles is left alone. Returns —Nonen/aThe ODS is edited in place. Assumptions · Applicability Assumptions Presence of ion.0.temperature marks a slice whose ion temperature was measured rather than assumed. The builders uphold that by refusing to write an ion block from a Ti/Te fallback. Applicability Machine-independent. The rule follows from what the IMAS leaves mean, not from any VEST diagnostic. write_synthetic_core_profiles Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source write_synthetic_core_profiles(result, ods=None, *, time=None, time_tolerance=1e-06) Store a successful synthetic kinetic state as one core_profiles.profiles_1d slice. NameTypeUnitDescription resultSyntheticKineticProfiles-From generate_synthetic_kinetic_profiles; must have status "success". odsODS, optional-Mutated in place; a new ODS when omitted. timefloat, optionalsSlice time; the result’s time when omitted. time_tolerancefloat, optionalsAn existing slice within this of time is replaced. Returns —ODS-The ODS with the slice written. Convention grid.rho_pol_norm always; grid.rho_tor_norm only when it was derived from the equilibrium’s q; grid.psi in Wb, COCOS 11, only when the source convention fixes it – a coordinate that is not known is left out, never substituted. grid.volume in m^3. Electrons and each ion carry density, density_thermal, temperature and pressure_thermal; ion 0 is the main ion, ion 1 the impurity, with z_ion, element[0].z_n and element[0].a. The slice also carries zeff, pressure_thermal, pressure_ion_total and t_i_average. code.parameters is a JSON object keyed by slice time, which survives an IMAS round trip as a string. Raises SyntheticProfileError A result whose status is not "success" (status carried over), or no time on either the result or the call. ValueError ods already holds a core_profiles IDS from another producer – any slice, code.name or code.parameters this writer did not write, e.g. vaft.process.profile.core_profiles_from_eq or the measured-fit vaft.process.profile.core_profiles. Input semantics · Output semantics · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Input semantics Synthetic: a generated, validated kinetic state. Output semantics Stored: the same arrays in standard core_profiles paths, labelled synthetic and assumption-driven in ids_properties.comment and code.parameters. Assumptions One producer per IDS. ids_properties and code belong to the whole core_profiles IDS, so a synthetic slice beside a measured or legacy one would carry, or impose, the wrong label. The writer therefore writes only into an ODS whose core_profiles is empty or was written by itself (code.name is this generator and code.parameters its JSON); there it appends a slice, or replaces the slice at the same time whole. There is deliberately no opt-in to mix producers: store synthetic profiles in their own ODS. The measured-fit and legacy writers refuse an IDS written here for the same reason. Every array is checked finite before anything is written. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations No rotation, fast particles or radiation; nothing in equilibrium is touched. Provenance IMAS Data Dictionary core_profiles (COCOS 11), the paths written. VAFT issue #122: synthetic profiles never labelled as measured or transport-predicted.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/atomic/.title: Process reference: atomic
/vaft/develop/reference/process/atomic/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.atomic: 5 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("atomic.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview This module owns profile selection, time alignment, impurity-density fallback and volume integration. Numerical atomic physics remains in vaft.formula.atomic and ADF11 file access in vaft.data.open_adas. Which impurity species to include and what fraction to assume for them is machine policy, resolved by the pipeline (vaft.omas.formula_wrapper.compute_power_balance from vest.yaml on VEST) and passed in; this module holds no such number (issue #420). SymbolMeaningUnit n_eelectron densitym^-3 n_impimpurity densitym^-3 T_eelectron temperatureeV L_Zline-radiation cooling coefficient of species ZW m^3 epsilonline emissivity, n_e n_imp L_ZW/m^3 P_lineradiated line power, int epsilon dVW Vcumulative enclosed plasma volumem^3 rho_tor_normnormalized toroidal-flux radius- Functions compute_line_radiation_power_seriesLine-radiation power for matched equilibrium slices, from the stored kinetic profiles. Convention compute_time_match_atolAn absolute time-matching tolerance adapted to the native time spacing. find_time_match_indexIndex of the time closest to target_time, within the adaptive tolerance. integrate_emissivity_profileIntegrate an emissivity profile to a total radiated power. Convention normalize_atomic_symbolNormalize an element or ion label to a supported atomic symbol. No function matches. compute_line_radiation_power_series Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source compute_line_radiation_power_series(ods, eq_indices, eq_times, volume_series, line_radiation_species=None, impurity_fractions=None, Z_eff=None, *, return_assumptions=False) Line-radiation power for matched equilibrium slices, from the stored kinetic profiles. For each species and time slice the local emissivity is epsilon = n_e n_imp L_Z(n_e, T_e) and the power P = int epsilon dV. NameTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries core_profiles.profiles_1d and equilibrium.time_slice. eq_indiceslist of int-Equilibrium slice indices to evaluate. eq_timesarray_likesTime of each of those slices. volume_seriesarray_likem^3Total plasma volume of each slice, for the integration fallback. line_radiation_specieslist of str, optional-Species to include; None for every species that has a configured fraction or an ion density profile in the ODS. impurity_fractionsdict of str to float, optional-n_imp / n_e per species, used when the ODS carries no profile for it; None means no assumption. Z_efffloat, optional-Effective charge, used only to infer a single species’ fraction when nothing else is known. return_assumptionsbool, optional-Also return what each species’ density was taken from. Returns —np.ndarray or tuple of (np.ndarray, dict)WNon-negative line-radiation power per eq_indices entry, and with return_assumptions a dict of species, per-species impurity_source (profile, configured, inferred_from_zeff or none), the impurity_fraction used, and z_eff. Convention The radial coordinate is rho_tor_norm throughout: the core_profiles grid and the equilibrium profiles_1d both carry it and are interpolated against each other in it. n_i for the impurity is fraction * n_e where a fraction is used; Z_eff inference assumes hydrogenic main ions, n_imp/n_e = (Z_eff - 1)/(Z(Z - 1)). Raises ValueError Mismatched eq_times / volume_series lengths, non-finite times, an unrecognized species label, or a negative or non-finite fraction. Processing steps · Input semantics · Output semantics · Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Match each equilibrium time to a core_profiles slice (find_time_match_index); an unmatched slice radiates nothing. Interpolate n_e, T_e from the slice’s rho_tor_norm onto the equilibrium’s rho_tor_norm (constant edge extrapolation). For each species, take n_imp / n_e from, in order: the slice’s own ion density profile; impurity_fractions; a single-species inference from Z_eff; else zero with one warning per species. L_Z from the ADAS tables [FORMULA]; epsilon = L_Z n_e n_imp. integrate_emissivity_profile per species, summed; clipped at zero. Input semantics Stored kinetic profiles (fitted or synthetic) on their core_profiles grid, plus the equilibrium grid and volume. Output semantics Synthetic: a modelled diagnostic-like quantity, not a measurement. Defaults impurity_fractions = None and line_radiation_species = None mean no assumption. The VEST carbon and oxygen fractions that used to be this function’s defaults are machine-specific settings, each an assumed value in vest.yaml resolved by the pipeline. Z_eff = None disables the single-species inference, a numerical convenience. Assumptions Coronal equilibrium for L_Z; one impurity species at a time with no mutual dilution; the core_profiles slice at the matched time describes the equilibrium slice. Applicability Machine-independent. Species and fractions arrive as arguments. Limitations Every failure mode – no core_profiles, no matching time, no n_e or T_e, ADAS data unavailable, no fraction known – yields zero for that slice or species with a logged warning rather than an error, to keep an offline power balance running; the returned assumptions are how a caller can tell. A core_profiles slice stored on rho_pol_norm only (no equilibrium at its time) has no rho_tor_norm and is skipped. Provenance ADAS tables [ADAS] through the cooling-coefficient kernel [FORMULA]. compute_time_match_atol Machine-independent source compute_time_match_atol(time_array, base_atol=1e-06) An absolute time-matching tolerance adapted to the native time spacing. max(base_atol, 0.25 * min(diff(unique_finite_times))), which absorbs floating-point drift in a time coordinate without ever matching an adjacent physical slice. NameTypeUnitDescription time_arraynp.ndarraysThe time coordinate to be matched against. base_atolfloat, optionalsFloor on the tolerance. Returns —floatsThe tolerance; base_atol when fewer than two distinct finite times exist. Raises ValueError base_atol non-finite or negative. Defaults · Applicability Defaults base_atol = 1e-6 s and the factor 0.25 are numerical conveniences: a quarter of the smallest spacing can never reach the neighbouring slice. Applicability Machine-independent. find_time_match_index Machine-independent source find_time_match_index(time_array, target_time) Index of the time closest to target_time, within the adaptive tolerance. NameTypeUnitDescription time_arraynp.ndarraysThe time coordinate. target_timefloatsThe time to match. Returns —int or None-Index of the closest time within compute_time_match_atol; None for an empty array, a non-finite target, or no candidate within tolerance. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. integrate_emissivity_profile Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source integrate_emissivity_profile(emissivity_profile, volume_profile, total_volume) Integrate an emissivity profile to a total radiated power. NameTypeUnitDescription emissivity_profilenp.ndarrayW/m^3Local emissivity on the radial grid. volume_profilenp.ndarray or Nonem^3Cumulative enclosed volume on the same grid, or None. total_volumefloatm^3Total plasma volume, for the fallback. Returns —floatWP = int epsilon dV, or the fallback, or 0. Convention volume_profile is the cumulative enclosed volume V(rho), so dV is its difference; it is not a shell volume. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations Processing steps If volume_profile is given, matches the emissivity’s shape and has at least two finite points spanning a non-zero volume: trapezoidal integration of epsilon against V, in volume order. Else, if total_volume is finite and positive: nanmean(epsilon) * total_volume. Else 0. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The two fallbacks are silent: a volume profile of the wrong length drops to the mean-times-volume estimate, and a missing volume to zero, with no warning from this function. normalize_atomic_symbol Machine-independent source normalize_atomic_symbol(label) Normalize an element or ion label to a supported atomic symbol. Full English names and charge-decorated labels are accepted – carbon6+ gives C, neon gives Ne. NameTypeUnitDescription labelstr, bytes or None-The label as found in an ODS ion.label or a species list. Returns —str or None-The symbol, or None for an unrecognized label so the caller decides whether absence is fatal. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Only the elements in the module’s table are recognized (H through W, the common tokamak species); isotopes D and T map to their own symbols.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/equilibr.title: Process reference: equilibrium
/vaft/develop/reference/process/equilibr.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.equilibrium: 77 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("equilibrium.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Physics only. Nothing here reads or writes an ODS: every function takes arrays and returns arrays or plain records, so the same code serves a GEQDSK, an ODS slice and an analytic model. The adapters that turn those into one record, and the parametric models fitted to them, live in _equilibrium_parametric and are re-exported through this module, which is their stable import location. What the module does, in the order a flux map is usually consumed:: psi(R, Z) on a grid -> radial coordinates: psi_norm, and the toroidal radius through q -> flux surfaces: contours, their shape, their averages -> fields: the poloidal field from psi, the toroidal field from F -> global scalars: diamagnetism, the Shafranov integrals, force balance SymbolMeaningUnit psipoloidal fluxWb/rad psi_norm(psi - psi_axis)/(psi_boundary - psi_axis)- Fpoloidal current function, R*B_phiT m B_ppoloidal field magnitudeT qsafety factor- kSauter Eq. 20 prefactor carrying sign and 2*pi- Flux is per radian unless a function says otherwise. The poloidal field from psi carries a factor k = sigma_RphiZ * sigma_Bp / (2*pi)**e_Bp [1], which folds the orientation sign and the 2pi normalization together. A function that forms a field from psi takes a COCOS index, and with none it uses the historical weber-per-radian form. Getting this wrong scales the field by 2pi and the poloidal beta by its square, plausibly and silently. A function that takes a precomputed field instead inherits whatever convention produced it and cannot check it. Three radial coordinates, never interchangeable. rho_tor_norm equals sqrt(psi_norm), which is rho_pol_norm, only for a flat safety factor. derive_radial_coordinates returns all three with an explicit record of which is unavailable and why. Flux maps are indexed (R, Z), matching the IMAS two-dimensional profile layout. Boundary contours run counter-clockwise, because the Shafranov outward normal is only outward then. Functions as_equilibriumAdapt a GEQDSK, ODS, IMAS handle, or native model to one equilibrium record. Convention calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_fieldContour-length average of the poloidal field around a closed boundary. Convention calculate_diamagnetismDiamagnetism from its volume-integral definition. Convention calculate_q_profile_from_psiCalculate the safety factor profile q(psi) from a 2D poloidal flux map and F(psi). Convention calculate_reconstructed_diamagnetic_fluxDiamagnetic flux reconstructed from the equilibrium’s own toroidal field. Convention check_equilibrium_requirementsWhether an equilibrium carries what a named algorithm needs to run. Convention compare_contoursHow far apart two closed contours are, point to curve. Convention computed_diamagnetism_from_phiEFIT-style diamagnetism from an already-computed diamagnetic flux. Convention connection_length_mapConnection length of the field line through each of many starting points. Convention contour_shape_parametersShape parameters of one closed flux-surface contour. Convention contour_shaping_observablesModel-independent shaping observables of one closed contour: indentation and asymmetry. Convention convert_cocosConvert an equilibrium between two explicitly known COCOS conventions. Convention current_centroidTotal toroidal current and its centroid, from a gridded current density. Convention current_covarianceSecond central moment tensor of a gridded current density. Convention current_momentOne moment integral (R - R_0)**p (Z - Z_0)**q J_phi dA of a gridded current density. Convention derive_boundary_representationClassify the plasma boundary and derive its geometric diagnostics. Convention derive_current_momentsReduce an equilibrium’s toroidal current density to its low-order moments. Convention derive_global_descriptorsGlobal scalar descriptors of one equilibrium, each with its derivation record. Convention derive_radial_coordinatesThe three normalized radial coordinates, each with its derivation record. Convention efit_virial_volume_integralsEFIT-style weighted volume integrals for the virial closures. Convention ejiri_mirror_geometryEjiri mirror-confinement proxy for one magnetic snapshot. Convention equilibrium_field_on_grid(B_R, B_Z, B_phi) on the whole (R, Z) grid, each (nR, nZ). Convention evaluate_fourier_surfacePoints on a Fourier-represented flux surface at given arc-length angles. Convention evaluate_guazzotto_freidbergNormalized flux and its analytic derivatives of a Guazzotto-Freidberg equilibrium. Convention evaluate_millerPoints on a Miller-parameterized flux surface at given poloidal angles. Convention evaluate_mxh_chebyshevFlux-surface points of an MXH-Chebyshev representation. Convention evaluate_solovevEvaluate an analytic Solov’ev equilibrium on a set of points. Convention extract_flux_surface_contoursIso-flux contours at requested normalized levels, by marching squares. Convention find_rational_surfacesWhere a toroidal mode resonates: the surfaces with q = m / n. find_stationary_pointsLocate the O-points and saddles of psi to sub-grid accuracy. Convention fit_fourier_surfaceRepresent one closed flux-surface contour as a truncated Fourier series. Convention fit_fourier_surface_sequenceRepresent a sequence of internal flux surfaces as Fourier series. Convention fit_miller_sequenceFit Miller parameters across a sequence of flux surfaces, with radial derivatives. Convention fit_miller_surfaceFit the Miller shape parameters to one closed flux-surface contour. Convention fit_mxh_chebyshevRepresent an equilibrium’s flux surfaces by MXH shapes with Chebyshev radial profiles. Convention fit_solovevRepresent an equilibrium by the Solov’ev solution closest to its flux map. Convention flux_surface_quantitiesFlux-surface averages and shape parameters on each normalized flux level. Convention fractional_cell_weights_from_boundaryFractional area of each grid cell that lies inside the plasma boundary. Convention grad_shafranov_operatorThe Grad-Shafranov elliptic operator on a rectangular grid. Convention grad_shafranov_residualHow far an equilibrium is from satisfying its own force balance, surface by surface. Convention grad_shafranov_residual_modesProject the Grad-Shafranov residual onto poloidal harmonics on nested flux surfaces. Convention guazzotto_freidberg_parametersThe dimensionless plasma parameters of Section 6 for a Guazzotto-Freidberg equilibrium. Convention guazzotto_freidberg_to_equilibriumExport a Guazzotto-Freidberg equilibrium as a gridded record in physical units. Convention integrate_romero_closureIntegrate Romero’s first-order closure from a boundary-voltage history. Convention lab_to_straight_field_lineRelabel a geometric poloidal angle into the straight-field-line one. Convention make_equilibrium_field_interpolatorBuild a callable giving the full magnetic field anywhere on one time slice. Convention make_vacuum_field_interpolatorBuild a callable giving the vacuum magnetic field anywhere on one grid. Convention miller_surfacesA family of Miller surfaces for a shape scan. Convention parallel_current_from_toroidalConvert a shell toroidal driven current to the IMAS parallel current. Convention plasma_cell_weightsFraction of each grid cell that is plasma, from the boundary outline when there is one. Convention poloidal_field_at_boundaryPoloidal field on a boundary contour, from the flux map by bicubic spline. Convention prepare_boundary_for_shafranovCondition a boundary contour into the form the Shafranov integrals require. Convention psi_to_radialInboard and outboard major radius of each flux value, along the axis row. Convention psi_to_rhoNormalized toroidal-flux radius at one poloidal flux value, by integrating q. Convention psi_to_rzMap a flux-surface profile onto the two-dimensional grid through psi. Convention r_at_z_extremumMajor radius where a contour reaches its highest or lowest point. Convention radial_to_psiPoloidal flux at a major radius on the midplane row of the flux map. Convention resistive_layer_atResistivity and mass density at flux surfaces someone else located. resistive_layer_parametersResistivity and mass density at each rational surface of a toroidal mode. rho_to_psiPoloidal flux at one normalized toroidal-flux radius, by root finding. Convention romero_flux_balanceRomero’s exact voltage and volt-second balance over a sampled discharge. Convention scale_boundary_conformalScale a closed boundary about a centre, giving a contour conformal to it. Convention shafranov_integralsThe three Shafranov boundary integrals and the virial coefficient. Convention solovev_exampleBuild a shaped analytic Solov’ev equilibrium in a chosen boundary topology. Convention solovev_shape_constraintsThe Cerfon-Freidberg boundary conditions for a shaped, possibly diverted, plasma. Convention solovev_to_equilibriumExport an analytic Solov’ev model as a gridded equilibrium record. Convention solovev_xpoint_constraintsThe three conditions that make a point an X-point on the boundary flux surface. solve_guazzotto_freidbergSolve the Guazzotto-Freidberg analytic equilibrium for a shape and a beta parameter. Convention solve_solovev_constraintsSolve for the Solov’ev coefficients that satisfy a set of geometric constraints. Convention straight_field_line_angle_on_gridThe PEST straight-field-line angle on every node of a flux map. Convention straight_field_line_mapThe PEST straight-field-line poloidal angle of a flux map, built once. Convention straight_field_line_tablesPer-surface tables taking the geometric poloidal angle to the code’s own. Convention trace_field_lineTrace one magnetic field line through the equilibrium field. Convention validate_equilibriumDeprecated compatibility wrapper for check_equilibrium_requirements. Deprecated virial_alpha_conformal_annulusVirial closure coefficient from a thin annulus conformal to the LCFS. Convention virial_alpha_thin_annulusVirial closure coefficient in the thin-annulus limit, from the boundary field. Convention volume_averageVolume average of a gridded quantity over the confined region. Convention No function matches. as_equilibrium Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source as_equilibrium(source, *, time_index=0, profile_index=0, convention=None) Adapt a GEQDSK, ODS, IMAS handle, or native model to one equilibrium record. The single entry point every algorithm here goes through, so that they operate on one normalized shape regardless of where the equilibrium came from. NameTypeUnitDescription sourceEquilibriumData, ODS, GEQDSK, IMAS equilibrium IDS, path or mapping-A record is returned as is, or converted when a convention is asserted; a path or path-like is read as a GEQDSK; an object exposing an OMAS export is exported first; a native IDS root is wrapped. time_indexint, optional-Which time slice to take from a multi-slice source. profile_indexint, optional-Which 2-D profile grid to take from a slice carrying more than one. conventionint, optional-A COCOS index the caller asserts for source, 1 to 18. When given it always wins over identification, and the result is converted to it. Returns —EquilibriumData-The normalized record, with its convention set from the assertion when one was made and from identification otherwise. Convention Normalizes shape, not convention: the returned record is not converted to any internal standard unless convention asks for it, so its psi may be in weber or weber per radian and only convention.psi_per_radian says which. A record built without a convention reports neither, and downstream field calculations then fall back to the historical per-radian form. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A GEQDSK is identified as a two-dimensional grid by the presence of its characteristic keys, so a mapping that happens to carry them is treated as one. Only the requested time slice and profile grid are read; everything else in a multi-slice source is discarded. Provenance The per-source adapters below preserve each format’s own layout conventions; see vaft.process.cocos.identify_convention for how the convention is inferred when the caller does not assert one. calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_field Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_field(R_bdry, Z_bdry, B_p_bdry) Contour-length average of the poloidal field around a closed boundary. NameTypeUnitDescription R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the contour points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the contour points. B_p_bdryarray_likeTPoloidal field magnitude at those points. Returns —floatTThe average poloidal field, the contour integral of the field over the contour length. Convention Weighted by arc length, not by point count, so an unevenly sampled contour still gives the physical average. The midpoint rule is used between consecutive points, and the contour is treated as closed. This is the normalizing field that the poloidal beta and the diamagnetism are taken against, so it must come from the same convention as the field that produced it. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Midpoint rule on the given points, so a coarsely sampled contour underweights regions of high curvature. Takes the field magnitudes as given and cannot check they were computed in a consistent convention. Provenance The definition used with shafranov_integrals and calculate_diamagnetism as their reference field. calculate_diamagnetism Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source calculate_diamagnetism(R_grid, Z_grid, psi_RZ, psi_axis, psi_lcfs, psiN_1d, f_1d, f_vac_val, B_pa, V_p=None, weights=None) Diamagnetism from its volume-integral definition. NameTypeUnitDescription R_gridarray_likemMajor-radius grid axis. Z_gridarray_likemHeight grid axis. psi_RZarray_likeWb/radPoloidal flux on the grid, indexed (R, Z). psi_axisfloatWb/radPoloidal flux on the magnetic axis. psi_lcfsfloatWb/radPoloidal flux at the last closed flux surface. psiN_1darray_like-Normalized poloidal flux the poloidal-current profile is given on. f_1darray_likeT mPoloidal current function F = R*B_phi on that abscissa. f_vac_valfloatT mThe same function at the boundary, standing in for the vacuum field B_pafloatTBoundary-average poloidal field, the normalizing scale, strictly positive V_pfloat, optionalm^3Plasma volume. Computed from the same grid and mask when not given weightsarray_like, optional-Fraction of each cell inside the plasma, from plasma_cell_weights; replaces the normalized-flux mask when given. Returns —float-The diamagnetism, positive for a diamagnetic plasma and negative for a paramagnetic one. Convention mu_i = (1/(B_pa^2 * V)) * integral (B_tv^2 - B_t^2) dV, with the toroidal fields taken as the poloidal current function over the major radius and the axisymmetric volume element. Positive means the plasma reduced the toroidal field. A result of the unexpected sign usually means the vacuum proxy was taken on axis rather than at the boundary, or that the poloidal current profile’s sign convention disagrees with the equilibrium it came from. Raises ValueError The boundary-average poloidal field is not positive. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The same per-cell boundary mask as volume_average, so the boundary is resolved only to the grid. The vacuum field is a single boundary value rather than a profile.
