Applicability Machine-independent. The wall polygon is where a machine’s own geometry enters, and it is supplied by the caller. Limitations Fixed step, so accuracy is set by the step alone and there is no error control; a line near a separatrix, where the pitch changes fastest, is the least accurate. Terminating on the coordinate bounds is a safety net against extrapolating far outside the equilibrium grid, not a physical condition. Provenance The field-line equations in toroidal-angle form; the field itself comes from make_equilibrium_field_interpolator. validate_equilibrium Deprecated source validate_equilibrium(equilibrium, *, required_for='general') Deprecated compatibility wrapper for check_equilibrium_requirements. virial_alpha_conformal_annulus Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source virial_alpha_conformal_annulus(R_grid, Z_grid, B_R_grid, B_Z_grid, R_bdry, Z_bdry, thickness=0.1, samples_per_axis=5) Virial closure coefficient from a thin annulus conformal to the LCFS. alpha_2 = 2 * sum(R Bz^2 w dA) / sum(R Bp^2 w dA) over an annulus bounded by the boundary and a copy of it scaled by 1 - thickness. Obtains the closure coefficient without the volume integral over the plasma interior, which a reconstruction that fixes the boundary but not the internal field cannot supply. NameTypeUnitDescription R_gridarray_likemMajor-radius grid, as an axis or a mesh. Z_gridarray_likemHeight grid, as an axis or a mesh. B_R_gridarray_likeTMajor-radius field component on that grid. B_Z_gridarray_likeTVertical field component on that grid. R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the boundary points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the boundary points. thicknessfloat, optional-Annulus width as a fraction of the distance from the centre to the boundary, not an absolute length; default 0.1. samples_per_axisint, optional-Sub-samples per cell axis in the area-fraction weighting; default 5. Returns —dict-alpha the closure coefficient, NaN unless valid; valid whether the annulus could be integrated; reason why not, or None; n_cells the summed annulus weight. Convention alpha = 2 <R Bz^2> / <R Bp^2>, 1 for a symmetric circular cross-section and 2 in the infinitely elongated limit. Only squares of the field enter, so the sign convention the components arrive in does not matter. Processing steps · Defaults · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Orient the boundary counter-clockwise, build the inner contour with scale_boundary_conformal, take the annulus weight map as the difference of two fractional_cell_weights_from_boundary maps so that cells cut by either contour carry their area fraction, reject an annulus too small or too narrow for the grid, then integrate over the cells that survive a shared finite-field mask. Defaults thickness=0.1 is a validated workflow default: near the accuracy optimum on analytic Solov’ev equilibria and still thousands of cells on a reconstruction-sized grid. samples_per_axis=5 is a numerical convenience matching fractional_cell_weights_from_boundary, and it sets how thin an annulus can be resolved. Assumptions The annulus is built by geometric conformal scaling, not as a psi_N band: a psi_N band would reintroduce the dependence on reconstructed interior flux that this estimate exists to avoid. Applicability Machine-independent. Any boundary with a poloidal-field map covering it. Limitations Abstains – NaN with a reason – rather than returning a number when the boundary leaves the grid, when the annulus holds fewer than MIN_ANNULUS_CELLS, or when it is narrower than MIN_ANNULUS_WIDTH_SUBSAMPLES sub-samples at its narrowest point, in which case the integral would report the grid phase rather than the field. Cells whose field is only partly finite are dropped from both integrals together, since dropping one from the denominator alone would bias alpha up. As thickness -> 0 this tends to virial_alpha_thin_annulus, whose accuracy against the true alpha is slightly worse – a finite annulus samples some interior, and that helps. Provenance M. W. Bongard et al., Phys. Plasmas 23 (2016), the low-aspect-ratio virial closure and its annulus estimate of alpha. Measured against analytic Solov’ev equilibria in test/test_virial_alpha_approximations.py. virial_alpha_thin_annulus Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source virial_alpha_thin_annulus(R_bdry, Z_bdry, B_R_bdry, B_Z_bdry, center=None, mode='conformal', n_points=512) Virial closure coefficient in the thin-annulus limit, from the boundary field. The exact thickness -> 0 limit of virial_alpha_conformal_annulus, evaluating 2 * closed_integral(R Bz^2 w dl) / closed_integral(R Bp^2 w dl). Needs only the field on the LCFS, so unlike the volume integral it asks nothing of the plasma interior. NameTypeUnitDescription R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the boundary points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the boundary points. B_R_bdryarray_likeTMajor-radius field component at those points. B_Z_bdryarray_likeTVertical field component at those points. centertuple of float, optionalmCentre the conformal annulus shrinks towards. The boundary’s bounding-box centre when not given. modestr, optional-"conformal" (default) weights each segment by the support function, the limit of a conformally scaled annulus; "uniform" weights every segment equally, the limit of a uniform-offset annulus. n_pointsint, optional-Segments in the arc-length resampling; default 512. Returns —float-The closure coefficient, or NaN when the contour is degenerate or folds over the centre. Convention alpha = 2 <R Bz^2> / <R Bp^2>, which is 1 for a symmetric circular cross-section and 2 in the infinitely elongated limit. Only squares of the field enter, so the result does not depend on the sign convention the components arrive in. Raises ValueError mode is neither "conformal" nor "uniform", or the boundary and field arrays differ in length. Processing steps · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Drop non-finite points, close the contour, remove zero-length segments, orient counter-clockwise so the normal (dZ, -dR)/dl points outward, resample to n_points by arc length, then take the segment-midpoint quadrature through vaft.formula.equilibrium.virial_alpha_from_R_Bz_Bp_dl. Assumptions mode="conformal" assumes the boundary is star-shaped about center, so that shrinking it about that point sweeps a simple annulus. A conformal annulus has local width t * (x - c).n, so its area element is t * (x - c).n * dl and the constant t cancels; that support function is the weight. Weighting uniformly instead is a different region and on a VEST-like boundary a ~5% different answer, so the two modes are not interchangeable. Applicability Machine-independent. Any closed boundary with its poloidal field, from a reconstruction or an analytic equilibrium. Limitations Returns NaN rather than a number when more than MAX_NONCONVEX_ARC_FRACTION of the arc length has negative support: the conformal annulus folds over itself there, and an unclamped negative weight would subtract from both integrals. mode="uniform" makes no such assumption and still answers. How closely the limit matches a finite annulus is a property of the equilibrium, not of this quadrature. Provenance M. W. Bongard et al., Phys. Plasmas 23 (2016), the low-aspect-ratio virial closure and its annulus estimate of alpha. Measured against analytic Solov’ev equilibria in test/test_virial_alpha_approximations.py. volume_average Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source volume_average(f_RZ, psiN_RZ, R, Z, weights=None) Volume average of a gridded quantity over the confined region. NameTypeUnitDescription f_RZarray_likeanyThe quantity on the grid, in whatever unit it has. psiN_RZarray_like-Normalized poloidal flux on the same grid, used only as the mask. Rarray_likemMajor-radius axis, or the full mesh. Zarray_likemHeight axis, or the full mesh. weightsarray_like, optional-Fraction of each cell inside the plasma, from plasma_cell_weights; replaces the normalized-flux mask when given. Returns favgfloatanyThe volume-weighted average of f_RZ inside the boundary. volumefloatm^3The volume the average was taken over. Convention The volume element is the axisymmetric 2*pi*R dR dZ, so cells at large major radius weigh proportionally more; this is a torus average, not a cross-sectional one. Accepts either one-dimensional axes or a full mesh. Pass weights whenever the slice has a boundary outline. Without them the plasma is every cell with normalized flux between zero and one and a positive major radius – a flux threshold, not a containment test. Outside the plasma psi is not monotonic and turns over by the coils, so the threshold admits exterior cells: on the packaged VEST samples the flux-mask volume is 1.7 to 18 times the plasma’s, and a volume-averaged pressure comes out 40-50 % low. With plasma_cell_weights from the outline both match the contour-traced reference to 0.1 % and 1 %. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Cell areas come from a gradient of the axes, so the outermost cells are one-sided and a strongly non-uniform grid is approximated. The flux mask is a per-cell test with no sub-cell weighting; weights carry each boundary cell’s area fraction instead. Provenance The axisymmetric volume element, and the same normalized-flux mask psi_to_rz applies.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/soft_x_r.title: Process reference: soft_x_rays
/vaft/develop/reference/process/soft_x_r.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.soft_x_rays: 10 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("soft_x_rays.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Ported from the validated VEST SXR Viewer analysis tool (vest_sxr_viewer.py v5, module-level science functions; provenance: the 2026 VEST SXR thesis presentation). The 455xx SXR campaign acquires both digitizers – 22577 at the 4 o’clock port (toroidal 0 deg) and 17592 at the 12 o’clock port (120 deg) – at 125 MHz / 128 = 976562.5 Hz starting at the 285 ms trigger. Every routine here takes plain arrays (time in seconds, data shaped (n_channels, n_samples)); nothing reads a CSV or an ODS except the explicit ODS pairing helper. Vacuum-shot PF-noise removal is a standalone optional step (sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference): no other routine applies it, so the main processing path is always baseline -> window -> filter on exactly the data the caller supplied. Generic spectral analysis (PSD, spectral index, spectrogram) is not here – use vaft.process.fluctuation on any prepared channel. The forward direction is here too: synthetic_island_soft_x_rays turns a prescribed magnetic island on an equilibrium into chord signals (issue #886), through vaft.process.magnetic_island and vaft.process.line_of_sight. It is machine-independent; VEST chords come from vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.sxr_sightlines. Functions hilbert_instantaneous_phaseInstantaneous phase and envelope of a band-limited signal at one time. Convention load_te_ratio_calibrationLoad a ratio-to-temperature table and build its interpolator. Convention rank_toroidal_mode_numbersRank candidate toroidal mode numbers from phases measured at two locations. Convention sxr_band_signalsBaseline, window and band-pass chord signals into named frequency bands. Convention sxr_baseline_correctionZero each channel against the quiet tail after the plasma. Convention sxr_cwt_spectrogramContinuous-wavelet magnitude scalogram of one trace. Convention sxr_electron_temperatureElectron temperature from the two-filter signal ratio, chord by chord. Convention sxr_subtract_vacuum_referenceSubtract a low-passed vacuum shot to remove poloidal-field pickup. Convention sxr_te_pairs_from_odsPair the two filters’ channels of one array by the chord they view. Convention synthetic_island_soft_x_raysLine-integrated soft-X-ray signals of a rotating island on an equilibrium. No function matches. hilbert_instantaneous_phase Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source hilbert_instantaneous_phase(signal, time, t_eval) Instantaneous phase and envelope of a band-limited signal at one time. NameTypeUnitDescription signalarray_likeVA band-passed, roughly monochromatic trace. timearray_likesIts time base. t_evalfloatsTime at which to report the phase. Returns —tuple-The phase in degrees and the envelope in volts at the nearest sample, that sample’s index, and the full phase and envelope series. Convention Phase comes from the analytic signal and is wrapped to the principal branch, so it runs within a full turn and jumps rather than accumulating. The sample nearest the requested time is used; no interpolation. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Meaningful only for a band-passed input. The analytic signal of a broadband trace has a phase that does not correspond to any single mode, so filter first with sxr_band_signals. The Hilbert transform is also poorly behaved at the record edges, so a time near either end is unreliable. Provenance The analytic-signal phase estimate used by the validated VEST SXR viewer’s mode analysis. load_te_ratio_calibration Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source load_te_ratio_calibration(path=None) Load a ratio-to-temperature table and build its interpolator. NameTypeUnitDescription pathstr or path-like, optional-Calibration table with te and ratio columns. Defaults to the packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium table. Returns —tuple-The interpolator mapping ratio to temperature, the temperature column in electron-volts, and the ratio column, dimensionless. Convention The interpolator extrapolates rather than clipping, so a ratio outside the table returns an extrapolated temperature, not the nearest tabulated one. A caller that needs out-of-range samples rejected must test the ratio itself. Column names are matched case-insensitively after stripping. Raises ValueError The table lacks either column, or holds fewer than two valid points. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults The packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium table is a diagnostic calibration, shipped with the package and described in the data directory’s own notes. Applicability Machine-independent. The table is an argument; only the packaged default is the VEST filter pair, and a different filter combination supplies its own. Limitations Non-finite rows are dropped silently. The two-filter method assumes a thermal spectrum, so the temperature it returns is meaningless for a non-thermal one. Provenance The packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium ratio calibration, vaft/data/legacy/sxr_te_ratio_be_al.csv. rank_toroidal_mode_numbers Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source rank_toroidal_mode_numbers(theta_a_deg, phase_a_deg, theta_b_deg, phase_b_deg, n_max) Rank candidate toroidal mode numbers from phases measured at two locations. NameTypeUnitDescription theta_a_degfloatdegToroidal angle of the first observation point. phase_a_degfloatdegMeasured phase there. theta_b_degfloatdegToroidal angle of the second point. phase_b_degfloatdegMeasured phase there. n_maxint-Largest magnitude of mode number to consider. Returns —tuple of ToroidalModeCandidatedegEvery candidate with its anchor offset and wrapped residual, best first Convention For each candidate the wrapped phase-versus-angle line is anchored exactly at the first point and scored by the wrapped residual at the second. Zero is excluded, since it carries no toroidal structure. Candidates sort by absolute residual, then by absolute mode number, and a positive mode number wins a remaining tie over its negative counterpart, which is a tie-break, not physics. Raises ValueError The two points share a toroidal angle, so no mode number can be inferred. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. The port angles are arguments; the VEST pair used in practice is a worked example, not a built-in. Limitations Two points cannot resolve aliasing. A candidate and one differing by 360/|dtheta| produce identical residuals; for the VEST ports at zero and 120 degrees that period is three. Every degenerate candidate is returned with an equal residual and none is physically privileged; choosing among them needs independent information such as frequency scaling, mode structure, or a third port. The phases must come from the same band and the same filtering convention, or the residual compares two different quantities. Provenance The two-point toroidal mode-number estimate of the validated VEST SXR viewer, and its documented aliasing degeneracy. sxr_band_signals Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sxr_band_signals(time, data, *, baseline_start, bands, fs, order=2, time_range=None, channels=None, dead_channels=(), zero_phase=True) Baseline, window and band-pass chord signals into named frequency bands. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples), or one trace. baseline_startfloat or NonesStart of the quiet tail, or None when the data is already corrected bandsmapping of str to sequence of floatHzNamed (f_low, f_high) pairs; the names are the caller’s. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Butterworth order for every band. time_rangesequence of float, optionalsAnalysis window as (t_min, t_max). channelssequence of int, optional-Row indices to process; all rows when omitted. dead_channelssequence of int, optional-Rows whose band output is forced to zero. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. Returns —SXRBandResultVThe windowed time base, the raw windowed signals, one array per band, and the channel indices selected. Convention The band-pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), so no feature moves in time. That matters because the phase read off this output by hilbert_instantaneous_phase feeds a toroidal mode number. Pass zero_phase=False if causal filtering is explicitly required. A dead channel’s band output is zeroed but its raw trace is kept, so it stays visible in a raw map instead of disappearing. Raises ValueError The time range selects no samples. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Baseline-correct, unless the caller says the data already is. Restrict to the analysis window. Select the requested channels. Band-pass each into every named band, substituting zeros for dead channels. Defaults order = 2 is a numerical convenience. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Vacuum-reference correction is not applied; run sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference first when it is wanted. Band edges are passed straight to the filter, so a band reaching the Nyquist frequency raises from SciPy rather than being clipped. Filtering is applied directly to the windowed segment (preserving legacy viewer parity); under zero_phase=True, boundary transients occur at both edges of time_range extending over the filter settling time. Windows shorter than the filter padding length (3 * (2 * order + 1) samples, 15 for order 2) raise from SciPy under zero_phase=True. Provenance The validated VEST SXR viewer’s band decomposition. sxr_baseline_correction Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sxr_baseline_correction(time, data, baseline_start) Zero each channel against the quiet tail after the plasma. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples), or one trace. baseline_startfloatsTime from which the record is taken to be quiet. Returns —np.ndarrayVThe signals with each channel’s own zero level removed. Convention The zero level is per channel, not shared, because the detectors have different dark levels. The mean of the tail is used, not a fitted trend, so a drift through the shot survives. Raises ValueError The time base and the sample axis disagree in length. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults When no sample lies at or beyond baseline_start the last 1000 samples are used instead. That fallback is a validated-workflow default carried from the VEST SXR viewer. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Assumes the tail is genuinely quiet. A record that ends while the plasma is still radiating has its baseline biased by that signal, and the fallback makes that silent rather than an error. Provenance The validated VEST SXR viewer, whose baseline convention and last-1000-sample fallback this reproduces. sxr_cwt_spectrogram Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sxr_cwt_spectrogram(signal, fs, f0, f1, n_freq) Continuous-wavelet magnitude scalogram of one trace. NameTypeUnitDescription signalarray_likeVThe trace. fsfloatHzSample rate. f0floatHzLowest frequency of the scalogram. f1floatHzHighest frequency. n_freqint-Number of frequencies between them. Returns —tuple of np.ndarray-The frequency axis, ascending, and the magnitude as (n_freq, n_samples). Convention Frequencies are returned ascending, which reverses the underlying library’s own descending order, and the magnitude rows are reversed to match. A wavelet transform trades frequency resolution for time resolution as frequency rises, unlike the fixed-window short-time transform. Raises ImportError The optional wavelet package is not installed. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults Single-threaded execution is a numerical convenience, keeping the call deterministic and avoiding a thread pool inside a per-channel loop. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Needs an optional package that is not a VAFT dependency. The short-time transform in vaft.process.fluctuation.compute_spectrogram covers the default time-frequency need without it. The input is cast to single precision by that library. Provenance The optional fcwt continuous-wavelet implementation; the alternative path is vaft.process.fluctuation. sxr_electron_temperature Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sxr_electron_temperature(time, data, pairs, *, calibration, baseline_start, fs, lowpass_cutoff=50000.0, al_gain=1.07, al_threshold=0.1, detrend_window=400, order=2, zero_phase=True, time_range=None) Electron temperature from the two-filter signal ratio, chord by chord. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples). pairssequence of sequence of int-(beryllium_index, aluminium_index) pairs, one per chord. calibrationcallable-Maps a signal ratio to a temperature; see load_te_ratio_calibration. baseline_startfloat or NonesStart of the quiet tail, or None when already corrected. fsfloatHzSample rate. lowpass_cutofffloat, optionalHzConditioning low-pass cut-off. al_gainfloat, optional-Relative sensitivity of the aluminium channel. al_thresholdfloat, optionalVConditioned aluminium level below which a sample is invalid. detrend_windowint, optional-Width of the centred rolling trend, in samples. orderint, optional-Butterworth order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. time_rangesequence of float, optionalsAnalysis window as (t_min, t_max). Returns —SXRTemperatureResult-The windowed time base, the temperature per chord in electron-volts, and its percentage deviation from the rolling trend. Convention The low pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), matching the convention of sxr_band_signals and preserving exact temporal alignment with other diagnostics and fast MHD events. Pass zero_phase=False to reproduce legacy causal filtering behavior with filter group delay. The relative fluctuation is a percentage of the rolling trend, and the trend is centred, so it uses samples on both sides. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Baseline-correct, unless the caller says the data already is. Restrict to the analysis window. Low-pass both channels of each pair. Scale the aluminium channel by its relative sensitivity. Take the ratio and map it through the calibration. Subtract a centred rolling trend to get the relative fluctuation. Invalidate samples whose conditioned aluminium level is at or below the threshold. Defaults The 50 kHz cut-off, the 1.07 aluminium gain, the 0.10 V threshold and the 400-sample trend window are validated-workflow defaults, the settings of the validated VEST viewer. order = 2 is a numerical convenience. Applicability Machine-independent. The defaults are VEST viewer practice and the calibration is supplied by the caller. Limitations The two-filter method assumes a thermal spectrum. Invalid samples are NaN rather than removed, so a caller must honour them. Vacuum-reference correction is not applied here. Provenance The validated VEST SXR viewer, whose conditioning settings, validity threshold and detrending this reproduces. sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference(data, reference_data, *, cutoff, fs, order=2, zero_phase=True) Subtract a low-passed vacuum shot to remove poloidal-field pickup. An optional step. Nothing else in this module calls it, so the main path is always baseline, then window, then filter, on exactly the data the caller supplied. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeVPlasma-shot signals as (n_channels, n_samples). reference_dataarray_likeVVacuum-shot signals with the same channel count. cutofffloatHzLow-pass cut-off applied to the reference. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Butterworth order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. Returns —np.ndarrayVThe plasma signals with the pickup removed, truncated to the shorter record. Convention Pickup from the poloidal field coil ramps appears identically in a vacuum shot, so low-passing that record and subtracting it channel-wise removes the common drive while leaving plasma fluctuations untouched. The low pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), preserving exact temporal alignment with the un-delayed plasma shot. Pass zero_phase=False to reproduce legacy causal filtering behavior. Both inputs should already be baseline-corrected. Raises ValueError The two inputs have different channel counts. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults order = 2 is a numerical convenience matching the rest of the module’s conditioning. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Assumes the vacuum shot reproduces the plasma shot’s coil programme. Records are truncated to the shorter of the two rather than aligned in time, so two records with different start triggers are subtracted misaligned. The reference is truncated to length n before filtering, so both leading and trailing edges are subject to filter boundary transients. Inputs shorter than the filter padding length (3 * (order + 1) samples for low-pass) raise from SciPy under zero_phase=True. Provenance The validated VEST SXR viewer’s optional PF-noise removal step. sxr_te_pairs_from_ods VEST-specificConvention-sensitive source sxr_te_pairs_from_ods(ods, array) Pair the two filters’ channels of one array by the chord they view. NameTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries soft_x_rays.channel with the identifiers the VEST mapper writes. arraystr-Which array to pair within. Returns —tuple of tuple of int-One (beryllium_index, aluminium_index) pair per shared chord, ordered by chord number. Convention Channel identifiers are {daq}:{array}:{filter}:{chord}, written by the VEST digitizer mapper. Pairing on the chord number rather than on position in the channel list is what absorbs a per-block wiring reversal: the two filter blocks need not be ordered the same way. Returns index pairs, not data, so it changes no measurement. Raises ValueError No chord in that array carries both filters. Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Applicability VEST-specific. Depends on the identifier grammar and the filter names written by vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.soft_x_rays_from_digitizer_csv; another machine’s mapper would need its own pairing rule. Limitations A channel whose identifier does not split into four parts, or whose chord is not an integer, is skipped silently, so a mis-mapped channel is absent from the result rather than reported. Provenance vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.soft_x_rays_from_digitizer_csv, which writes the identifiers this parses. synthetic_island_soft_x_rays Machine-independent source synthetic_island_soft_x_rays(equilibrium, island, sightlines, *, time=0.0, emissivity_profile=None, model='flatten', domain=None, amplitude=1.0, smoothing=0.1, hard_mask=False, keep_fields=True) Line-integrated soft-X-ray signals of a rotating island on an equilibrium. NameTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData or source-The axisymmetric equilibrium, the only source of plasma geometry; anything vaft.process.equilibrium.as_equilibrium accepts. islandMagneticIslandSpec-Mode numbers, outboard-midplane full width, phase and rotation. sightlinesSightlines-The chords, each in the poloidal plane at its own toroidal angle. timefloat or array_like, optionalsTimes at which to evaluate the island phase. emissivity_profilecallable or tuple of array_like, optionalemissivity unitAxisymmetric background epsilon_0(psi_N). modelstr, optional-"flatten" or "island", as in vaft.process.magnetic_island.island_emissivity. domaintuple of array_like, optionalm(R, Z) of a closed polygon, normally the limiter, that clips every chord. amplitudefloat, optional- or emissivity unitIsland amplitude A. smoothingfloat, optional-Width of the island mask edge in helical-flux units. hard_maskbool, optional-Use a binary island mask. keep_fieldsbool, optional-Keep the emissivity fields on the result; False keeps only the brightness, for a long time series where the (time, plane, R, Z) arrays would dominate memory. Returns —SyntheticSXRResultemissivity unit times mTime, the chord planes’ toroidal angles, the emissivity and its island part on the equilibrium grid per time and plane, and the chord brightness per time and channel. Raises ValueError The island cannot be placed on the equilibrium, or the emissivity model or profile is invalid. Processing steps · Input semantics · Output semantics · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Build the island topology once, which fixes the resonant surface, the straight-field-line angle and the displacement. Group the chords by toroidal angle and build one path-length operator per plane, clipped to the domain. For every time and plane, rephase the island, form the emissivity, and integrate it along that plane’s chords. Input semantics A prescribed island on a reconstructed or analytic equilibrium, and chord geometry from the machine mapping; no measured signal enters. Output semantics Synthetic chord brightness in the emissivity’s unit times metres, before any detector, filter or etendue response, comparable to measured signals only up to a per-channel calibration. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A forward model only: no inversion, no noise, pencil-beam chords. Each chord is assumed to lie in one poloidal plane. The island rotates rigidly at a fixed width. Provenance Le, T. X. K. et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 68, 065003 (2026), a rotating-island SXR forward model of the same scope. Dreval, M. B. et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 63, 065006 (2021) and 65, 035001 (2023), for SXR forward modelling of MHD modes. Jang, J. Y. et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 93, 093506 (2022), the VEST SXR arrays.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/langmuir.title: Process reference: langmuir
/vaft/develop/reference/process/langmuir.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.langmuir: 8 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("langmuir.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview This module is machine-independent: raw VEST field selection, shot-era bias voltage/tip geometry, and ODS population belong in vaft.machine_mapping.langmuir_probes. Callers here pass already-selected physical signals (or raw counts plus explicit calibration factors) and get back electron temperature/density. Functions calibrate_currentConvert a raw probe current record to amperes. calibrate_voltageConvert a raw probe voltage record to physical volts. electron_densityElectron density from the ion saturation current and the solved temperature. Convention median_filter_signalMedian-filter a waveform along its only axis. Convention probe_surface_areaCollection area of a cylindrical probe tip. The second pair’s voltage is a scalar broadcast over the record, since it is a fixed bias rather than a measurement. Raises ValueError The two time bases do not agree. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Verify that the voltage and current time bases agree, and refuse if not. Remove the leading-sample baseline from both records. Optionally median-filter both. Calibrate to volts and amperes. Solve the triple-probe relation for the temperature. Compute the density, and combine the two validity masks. Defaults The gain, divisor and baseline length are machine-specific VEST values mirrored from vest.yaml. median_kernel is deliberately unset: issue #152 does not record the kernel the original workflow used, so no filtering is applied rather than a guessed width. The time tolerances are numerical conveniences. Applicability Machine-independent. The chain is generic; the calibration, baseline and geometry arguments carry VEST defaults that another machine overrides. Limitations Inherits every assumption of the two inference steps. The returned mask is the conjunction of the temperature and density masks, so a sample invalid in either is invalid in the result. Provenance Issue #152, the port of the VEST triple-probe workflow that this chain reproduces, including the decisions it left unresolved. remove_offset Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source remove_offset(data, *, n_baseline_samples=500) Subtract a signal’s pre-plasma baseline, taken as its leading samples. NameTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform, in whatever unit it has. n_baseline_samplesint, optional-How many leading samples make up the baseline. Returns —np.ndarrayanyThe waveform with its baseline mean removed. Convention The mean of the leading window, not a fitted trend, so a baseline that drifts during the shot is not removed. Raises ValueError The record is shorter than the requested baseline. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults n_baseline_samples = 500 is an acquisition-era value carried from the VEST probe digitizer settings, where the leading samples precede the discharge. It is a sample count, not a duration, so it means a different interval on a different sample rate. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Assumes the leading window is signal-free. A probe already collecting current at the start of the record has its baseline biased by that current. Provenance vest.yaml langmuir_probes processing, which carries the VEST sample count this default mirrors. solve_electron_temperature Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source solve_electron_temperature(vd2, vd3, *, te_bounds=(0.1, 500.0), rtol=1e-06) Solve the classical triple-probe relation for the electron temperature. NameTypeUnitDescription vd2array_likeVVoltage difference between the first probe pair. vd3array_likeVVoltage difference between the second pair, same shape. te_boundstuple of float, optionaleVBracket the root is searched in. rtolfloat, optional-Relative tolerance of the root finder. Returns tenp.ndarrayeVElectron temperature per sample, NaN where no root was found. solver_oknp.ndarray-True where a root was found inside the bracket. Convention Solves (1 - exp(-Vd2/Te)) / (1 - exp(-Vd3/Te)) = 1/2, the theoretical triple-probe relation, sample by sample by bracketed root finding. The one half on the right is the definition of the technique, not a tunable. Raises ValueError The two voltage arrays do not have the same shape. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults The bracket and the tolerance are numerical conveniences: the bracket spans the range a probe measurement can plausibly occupy, and the tolerance is far below the scatter of the voltages that feed it. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations A sample with no root inside the bracket yields NaN and a false flag rather than a substituted value, so a caller must honour the mask. The relation assumes a Maxwellian electron distribution, equal collecting areas on the three tips, and a thin sheath. The implemented relation is the theoretically correct one. The MATLAB expression quoted by issue #152 parses as a different equation, a 1 - a/b transcription of (1-a)/b, and no reference data was available to arbitrate; this deliberately does not reproduce that apparent transcription error. Provenance The classical triple-probe relation; the transcription discrepancy is recorded in issue #152.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/camera_g.title: Process reference: camera_geometry
/vaft/develop/reference/process/camera_g.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.camera_geometry: 4 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("camera_geometry.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Pure array-in/array-out functions (no ODS, no file I/O) mirroring the style of vaft.process.equilibrium. Reproduces the forward/virtual-camera projection used by the VEST_Fast Camera_Diagnostics repository’s camera_geometry.ipynb (see that repo’s CALIBRATION.md): a standard OpenCV pinhole model with Brown-Conrady radial/tangential distortion, cv2.projectPoints, applied directly with a shot’s calibrated (rvec, tvec) pose onto the ORIGINAL (distorted) camera frame. Per that notebook’s own documented finding (cell 50), the recovered pose is the true physical camera attitude regardless of which click-point convention was used to solve for it, so no undistortion or newOrigin handling is needed at projection time – one formula for every calibrated shot. World points are in centimeters throughout, matching the packaged calibration convention: (X, Y, Z)_cm = (R_m * cos(theta), R_m * sin(theta), Z_m) * 100. Functions project_pointsProject world points into camera pixels, flagging the ones the model cannot be trusted for. Convention sweep_toroidalSweep poloidal points through toroidal angles into world points. Convention toroidal_ringSweep one poloidal point into a full toroidal ring. Convention trajectory_world_pointsConvert a matched trajectory of cylindrical coordinates into world points. Convention No function matches. project_points Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source project_points(world_xyz_cm, rvec, tvec, camera_matrix, dist_coeffs, *, max_normalized_radius=1.3) Project world points into camera pixels, flagging the ones the model cannot be trusted for. NameTypeUnitDescription world_xyz_cmarray_likecmWorld points as (N, 3), in the machine frame. rvecarray_likeradRotation vector of the calibrated camera pose, Rodrigues form. tvecarray_likecmTranslation vector of that pose. camera_matrixarray_like-Intrinsic matrix, 3x3. dist_coeffsarray_like-Brown-Conrady radial and tangential distortion coefficients. max_normalized_radiusfloat, optional-Largest normalized image-plane radius still considered inside the model’s fitted range. Returns pixel_uvnp.ndarray-Pixel positions as (N, 2) in column-then-row order. valid_masknp.ndarray-True where the projection can be trusted. Convention Pixels are returned column first, then row, which is the opposite of the row-then-column order an image array is indexed with. World points are in centimetres, matching the packaged calibration, while every other geometry argument in this package is in metres; the sweep helpers here do that conversion. The pose is applied directly to the original distorted frame. Per the source notebook’s own finding, the recovered pose is the true physical camera attitude whichever click-point convention solved for it, so no undistortion step is needed and one formula serves every calibrated shot. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults max_normalized_radius = 1.3 is a validated-workflow default, the same guard the source notebook applies in its own projection routine. Applicability Machine-independent. Standard OpenCV pinhole geometry; the calibration that makes it a VEST camera is supplied by the caller. Limitations Two kinds of point are excluded rather than projected. A point behind the camera has non-positive depth and no meaningful pixel. A point far off the optical axis lies outside the angular range the distortion polynomial was fitted over, where that polynomial can turn non-monotonic and place the point at a wildly wrong pixel rather than smoothly off-frame; the mask catches that case, which is why it is a validity test and not a crop. Requires OpenCV, imported at call time. Provenance The VEST FAST camera diagnostics repository’s camera_geometry.ipynb and its CALIBRATION.md; this reproduces that notebook’s projection, including the depth and field-of-view guard from its own routine. sweep_toroidal Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source sweep_toroidal(r_m, z_m, theta_rad) Sweep poloidal points through toroidal angles into world points. NameTypeUnitDescription r_marray_likemMajor radius of each poloidal point. z_marray_likemHeight of each poloidal point, same shape as r_m. theta_radarray_likeradToroidal angles to sweep through. Returns —np.ndarraycmWorld points as (len(theta) * len(r), 3), one row per angle and point combination. Convention X = R cos(theta), Y = R sin(theta), Z = Z, then converted from metres to centimetres because the packaged calibration is in centimetres. Rows vary fastest over the poloidal points and slowest over the angles. This is an outer product: every point is swept through every angle, giving a surface. trajectory_world_points pairs them element-wise instead, for a single ordered path. Confusing the two produces an array of the wrong length rather than an error. Raises ValueError The two poloidal arrays do not have the same shape. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance Reproduces the source notebook’s torus sweep; see project_points for the repository and calibration reference. toroidal_ring Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source toroidal_ring(r_m, z_m, theta_rad) Sweep one poloidal point into a full toroidal ring. NameTypeUnitDescription r_mfloatmMajor radius of the point. z_mfloatmHeight of the point. theta_radarray_likeradToroidal angles making up the ring. Returns —np.ndarraycmWorld points as (len(theta), 3). Convention The single-point case of sweep_toroidal, with the same axis definitions and the same conversion from metres to centimetres. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance sweep_toroidal, which this delegates to. trajectory_world_points Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source trajectory_world_points(r_m, z_m, phi_rad) Convert a matched trajectory of cylindrical coordinates into world points. NameTypeUnitDescription r_marray_likemMajor radius along the trajectory. z_marray_likemHeight along the trajectory, same shape. phi_radarray_likeradToroidal angle at each point, same shape. Returns —np.ndarraycmWorld points as (N, 3), one row per trajectory point. Convention Element-wise pairing, one angle per point, for an ordered path such as a traced field line. sweep_toroidal takes the outer product instead and gives a surface. Same axis definitions and the same conversion to centimetres. Raises ValueError The three arrays do not all have the same shape. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance The world-frame convention of the source notebook; see project_points.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/impa/.title: Process reference: impa
/vaft/develop/reference/process/impa/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.impa: 14 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("impa.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview The array is an insertable midplane probe carrying, at each of eight radial positions, a toroidal-field Hall sensor and a vertical-field sensor. The radial-field sensors are retired: the original design used them only to confirm the probe sat at the midplane, where the radial field is negligible. The two sets play different roles [1]: the Hall channels establish where the array is. The toroidal field goes as one over the major radius, so measuring it against the known coil current gives each sensor’s radius, and the fitted spacing against the rigid as-built pitch gives the probe’s incident angle. they also establish how each vertical sensor is aligned. On an interval driven by the toroidal field alone the true vertical field is negligible, so whatever the vertical sensor reads there is crosstalk, and its ratio to the measured toroidal field is that sensor’s misalignment. the vertical sensors, once corrected for that crosstalk, carry the physics measurement: the toroidal current density from the radial gradient of the vertical field at the midplane. Every routine here works on plain arrays, so the machine-specific parts – raw field codes, shot-era geometry and thresholds – stay in vaft.machine_mapping.impa and vest.yaml. SymbolMeaningUnit B_measfield a probe actually measuresT Btvacuum toroidal field at a radius, mu0 N I / (2 pi R)T Bzvertical field, after compensationT alphaprobe coupling to the toroidal field, sin of its tilt- betaper-probe offsetT kappathe observable ratio alpha / R1/m R0major radius of the innermost channelm I_TFtoroidal field coil currentA The measurement model. Each probe sees a mixture of the local poloidal field and the toroidal field:: B_meas_i(t) = alpha_i * Bt(R_i, t) + Bz_i(t) * sqrt(1 - alpha_i**2) + beta_i Inverting it gives the compensated internal field:: Bz_i = (B_meas_i - alpha_i * Bt(R_i)) / sqrt(1 - alpha_i**2) Sign. VAFT takes the coil current as the raw field times -3e4, as vaft.machine_mapping.tf already does, together with a Hall gain of -2/15 T/V. That is the “Data gain” on the array’s own wiring datasheet, the authoritative hardware configuration, and it matches neither legacy script exactly [2]. All three pairings give the same ratio of measured to toroidal field up to an overall sign, so the fits here are sign-agnostic: they detect the working polarity from the data rather than assuming a positive coupling, and only the magnitude of the coupling carries physical meaning. The shipped default carries that sign since #681 closed #624. The datasheet leaves the vertical sensors’ own volts-to-tesla gain unspecified, so those waveforms stay in native volts throughout; see ImpaCrosstalkFit for what that means for the crosstalk angle. Geometry and coupling are degenerate. During a toroidal-field-only interval that field is the only driver, so a probe measures alpha_i * mu0 * N * I_TF / (2 * pi * R_i) and only the ratio kappa_i = alpha_i / R_i is observable. Assuming unit coupling yields the radial position, which is the legacy method; a known radius yields the coupling instead. The two cannot be recovered together from that data alone. Geometry is per shot. The array is insertable and its radial position is set per shot, so self-calibration from the shot’s own clean window is the primary geometry source, not a fallback, and comparing fitted positions between shots is meaningless because the probe really did move. A configured radius in vest.yaml applies only to an era where the array was surveyed or left fixed, and then takes precedence. A reference shot taken with the array in the same position can supply the calibration for another, which is the legacy two-shot arrangement; the single-shot path never requires it. Functions find_tf_calibration_windowFind the interval where the toroidal field alone drives the probes. Convention fit_impa_crosstalkFit the toroidal-field bleed into each vertical sensor. Convention fit_impa_geometrySelf-calibrate the array’s radial position from the toroidal-field profile. Convention fit_impa_tf_couplingFit each probe’s coupling to the toroidal field, at known radii. Convention grade_impa_qualityGrade whether an array’s measurements can be trusted, and say why not. Convention impa_calibrate_signalsFilter, scale and baseline raw probe records into field units. Convention impa_lowpassZero-phase low pass reproducing the legacy filter design. Convention legacy_impa_compensationFaithful port of the legacy compensation script, at one time sample. Convention legacy_impa_positionFaithful port of the legacy position script, at one time sample. Convention process_impaRun the whole array chain for one shot, from raw records to a graded result. Convention remove_bz_crosstalkSubtract a vertical sensor’s toroidal crosstalk. Convention remove_tf_pickupRecover the vertical field by removing a probe’s toroidal pickup. Convention toroidal_fieldVacuum toroidal field at a radius, from the coil current. Convention validate_impaDeprecated compatibility wrapper for grade_impa_quality. Deprecated No function matches. find_tf_calibration_window Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source find_tf_calibration_window(time, i_tf, ip=None, pf_currents=None, *, criteria=None, b_measured=None) Find the interval where the toroidal field alone drives the probes. Calibration needs a stretch of the same shot in which the coil is energised and nothing else is: no plasma current, no poloidal field. That interval is what makes the geometry and coupling fits meaningful, so this reports why it chose the one it did. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times. i_tfarray_likeAToroidal field coil current. iparray_like, optionalAPlasma current, used to exclude the discharge. pf_currentsarray_like, optionalAPoloidal field coil currents as (n_coils, n_samples). criteriaTfWindowCriteria, optional-Thresholds the interval must satisfy. b_measuredarray_like, optionalTConditioned probe records, used to require finite channels. Returns —tuple-The chosen TfCalibrationWindow with its metrics, and a tuple of reason strings recording what was applied and why. Convention The chosen interval is the best-conditioned one, meaning the widest spread in coil current, rather than the longest. A long interval at nearly constant current constrains the fit poorly however many samples it holds, because the fit is a regression against that current. Both an absolute floor and a fraction of the shot’s own peak are applied, because a shot can be energised weakly overall while still having a usable interval, and a fixed floor alone would either reject it or admit noise on a strong shot. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Validate the time axis. Require the coil current above an absolute floor and above a fraction of the shot’s own peak. Exclude samples where the plasma current or any poloidal coil exceeds its limit, on median-filtered traces. Require every probe channel finite. Group what survives into contiguous runs and drop the too-short ones. Choose among the survivors by conditioning, not length. Defaults The thresholds are hard-coded: an absolute current floor, a fraction of peak, plasma and poloidal current limits, a minimum duration and a dynamic-range floor. The fraction of peak is a validated-workflow value distinguishing the reference shots from a weakly energised one; the rest have no recorded derivation. The median-filter width is an acquisition-era value, one millisecond at the array’s own rate. One configured threshold, the relative noise limit, is read by nothing at all, which is tracked in #625. Applicability Machine-independent. The thresholds arrive as an argument. Limitations Reasons are returned rather than raised, so a caller must read them: a window can be chosen and still be poor. Without the optional currents the corresponding exclusions simply do not happen, and an interval containing plasma can be selected. Provenance vest.yaml impa.calibration_window, which carries the VEST thresholds and the evidence for the fraction-of-peak value. fit_impa_crosstalk Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source fit_impa_crosstalk(b_toroidal, b_z_raw, window, *, max_angle_deg=30.0, bz_gain=None) Fit the toroidal-field bleed into each vertical sensor. On an interval driven by the toroidal field alone the true vertical field is negligible, so whatever a vertical sensor reads there is crosstalk. Its ratio to the measured toroidal field is that sensor’s misalignment. NameTypeUnitDescription b_toroidalarray_likeTToroidal field at each sensor. b_z_rawarray_likeVRaw vertical-sensor records, in native units. windowTfCalibrationWindow-The toroidal-field-only interval. max_angle_degfloat, optionaldegLargest misalignment still treated as physical. bz_gainfloat, optionalT/VVolts-to-tesla gain for the vertical sensors, if known. Returns —ImpaCrosstalkFit-Per-sensor slope, offset and goodness of fit; the misalignment angle only when a gain was supplied. Convention The slope is volts per tesla, not a dimensionless projection, because the wiring datasheet leaves the vertical sensors’ gain unspecified and those waveforms stay in volts. Without a gain the angle cannot be formed and is returned as NaN rather than silently wrong. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults The maximum angle is hard-coded with no recorded derivation. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Rests on the vertical field being negligible over the window, which is what makes the window selection load-bearing. A linear fit only: a sensor responding non-linearly keeps a residual. Provenance Yang et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 85, 11D809 (2014), for the alignment role of the two sensor sets; vest.yaml impa.crosstalk for the configured thresholds. fit_impa_geometry Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source fit_impa_geometry(b_measured, i_tf, window, *, pitch=0.05, z=0.0, turns=24, r0_initial=0.4, r_bounds=(0.1, 0.9), fit_pitch=False) Self-calibrate the array’s radial position from the toroidal-field profile. NameTypeUnitDescription b_measuredarray_likeTConditioned probe records as (n_channels, n_samples). i_tfarray_likeAToroidal field coil current. windowTfCalibrationWindow-The interval to fit over. pitchfloat, optionalmAs-built spacing between channels. zfloat, optionalmHeight of the array. turnsint, optional-Coil turns. r0_initialfloat, optionalmStarting guess for the innermost channel’s radius. r_boundstuple of float, optionalmBounds on that radius. fit_pitchbool, optional-Whether to fit the spacing as well as the position. Returns —ImpaGeometryFit-The fitted radii, the spacing, the incident angle and the residual statistics. Convention This is the half of the degeneracy that assuming unit coupling resolves, which is the legacy method: a rigid array of known spacing is slid along the one-over-radius profile until it matches. The other half is fit_impa_tf_coupling. The coupling sign is detected, not assumed. The measured sign follows the configured Hall gain’s polarity, which this function has no reason to know. An incident angle of zero is a purely radial insertion in the midplane. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Keep the channels finite across the window. Detect the working polarity from the data. Solve a bounded least squares for the innermost radius, and the spacing when asked. Form the residual and its normalized form. Recover the incident angle from the ratio of fitted to as-built spacing. Defaults The spacing is machine-specific, the array’s rigid as-built value. The starting guess and the radial bounds are machine-specific too, spanning the vessel. turns = 24 is the VEST coil. Applicability Machine-independent. Every machine number is an argument. Limitations Assumes the array is rigid and the coupling uniform, so a fitted position is meaningful only where the residual is small; the reference shots sit at 9 to 12 percent and the rejected ones at 34 to 35. Positions are not comparable between shots, because the array is insertable and really is repositioned. Provenance The vest_impa_position model: uniform channel spacing and unit coupling, reproduced faithfully by legacy_impa_position. fit_impa_tf_coupling Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source fit_impa_tf_coupling(b_measured, i_tf, r, window, *, turns=24, tilt_bounds_deg=(-10.0, 10.0)) Fit each probe’s coupling to the toroidal field, at known radii. NameTypeUnitDescription b_measuredarray_likeTConditioned probe records as (n_channels, n_samples). i_tfarray_likeAToroidal field coil current. rarray_likemMajor radius of each probe. windowTfCalibrationWindow-The interval to regress over. turnsint, optional-Coil turns. tilt_bounds_degtuple of float, optionaldegBounds on the probe tilt. Returns —ImpaCouplingFit-Per-channel coupling and offset with their residual statistics. Convention Regresses the measured field on the modelled toroidal field at the known radius, giving the coupling as slope and the offset as intercept. This is the half of the degeneracy that a known radius resolves; see fit_impa_geometry for the other half. Only the magnitude of the coupling carries meaning, since its sign follows the calibration polarity. Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Defaults turns = 24 is machine-specific. The tilt bounds are a legacy compatibility value from a model that assumed a near-vertical probe, and they saturate on an array that faces the toroidal field, which is the reference condition here. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Needs the radii, which on this array are usually themselves fitted, so the two must not be circular. The tilt bounds saturating is a signal that the model does not fit the array, not a result to use. /vaft/develop/reference/process/magnetic.title: Process reference: magnetics
/vaft/develop/reference/process/magnetic.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.magnetics: 16 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("magnetics.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Three groups, with different provenance and different applicability. Sensor geometry is pure arithmetic on a layout: where the array’s centre is and what poloidal angle each sensor sits at. The legacy VEST equilibrium chain is the ported workflow that turns raw magnetic diagnostic records into the currents and fluxes an equilibrium reconstruction consumes. Its functions are named vest_*, are VEST-specific, and carry shot-era acquisition policy: which samples the output window covers, and which samples the baseline is fitted over, both depend on the shot number. Those policies live in vest.yaml and reach these functions through a configuration record. Mode analysis conditions Mirnov coil signals and extracts a toroidal mode number, either from the cross-spectral phase of a pair or from a wrapped-phase fit across an array. SymbolMeaningUnit Vcoil terminal voltageV Phipoloidal flux through a loopWb B_ppoloidal field at a probeT I_pplasma currentA ntoroidal mode number- ffrequencyHz Integration carries Faraday’s minus sign, applied before the baseline is removed. A flux loop’s flux is the negative time integral of its voltage, and a poloidal probe’s field likewise; the constant of integration is absorbed into the fitted baseline rather than chosen separately. Flux is stored per radian, which the ODS mapper multiplies back by two pi. The two generic integrating routines hedge their sign and the VEST ones state it. flux_loop_flux and b_field_pol_probe_field say the minus applies “if that is the convention”, because they take whatever a caller hands them; the vest_* functions know their own diagnostics and assert it. That difference is deliberate and is preserved rather than harmonized. Plasma-current polarity is inferred from the data, not asserted. rogowski_coil_ip flips the sign when the negative excursion dominates, which is the one place in the module where a convention is decided by the signal rather than declared. Toroidal mode numbers adhere to standard right-handed cylindrical coordinates. Coordinates (R, phi, Z) are oriented such that phi increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above. A positive toroidal mode number (n > 0) denotes a perturbation propagating in the positive phi direction (co-current / toroidal direction). Across toroidally separated sensors, the signal phase varies as theta(phi) = theta_0 - n * phi (negative phase slope d(theta)/d(phi) = -n). For two coils separated by toroidal angle Delta_phi = phase_geometry > 0, the cross-spectral phase of the downstream coil relative to the upstream coil is Delta_theta = -n * Delta_phi, so the mode number is n = -Delta_theta / Delta_phi. Both toroidal_mode_analysis and toroidal_phase_fit_at_time share this convention. Functions b_field_pol_probe_fieldPoloidal field from raw probe records, filtered before integration. Convention flux_loop_fluxPoloidal flux from raw flux-loop records, with a two-sided baseline. Convention magnetics_sensor_centreGeometric centre of a magnetic sensor layout. Convention magnetics_sensor_poloidal_anglePoloidal angle of each sensor about the layout centre. Convention mirnov_preprocess_signalCondition a Mirnov coil signal for mode analysis. Convention mirnov_spectrogramSliding-window amplitude spectrogram of a Mirnov signal. Convention rogowski_coil_ipPlasma current from a Rogowski coil, compensated by a flux-loop reference. Convention toroidal_mode_analysisToroidal mode number from the cross-spectral phase of two coils. Convention toroidal_phase_fit_at_timeToroidal mode numbers from a wrapped-phase fit across an array, at one time. Convention vest_b_field_pol_probe_legacyPoloidal field at a VEST probe, from its raw record. Convention vest_equilibrium_magnetics_detailedProcess every magnetic channel of one VEST shot onto the output window. Convention vest_equilibrium_magnetics_signalsThe processed magnetics of one VEST shot, as the three-array legacy view. Convention vest_flux_loop_flux_from_voltagePoloidal flux through a VEST flux loop, from its calibrated voltage. Convention vest_flux_loop_legacyPoloidal flux through a VEST flux loop, from its raw record. Convention vest_flux_loop_voltageCalibrated flux-loop terminal voltage, before integration. Convention vest_magnetics_time_windowThe output time window a VEST shot’s magnetics are resampled onto. Returns —tuple of np.ndarray-The field per probe in tesla, together with the intermediate stages the caller may want to inspect. The leading minus is Faraday’s, applied as the caller’s system defines it rather than asserted; see this module’s conventions. Filtering before integration matters: integrating first would accumulate the noise the filter is there to remove. Fit and subtract the two-sided baseline per column. Defaults The onset, offset and window lengths are machine-specific VEST values. Applicability Machine-independent. Every machine number is an argument. Limitations Assumes the record is quiet either side of the baseline window. This is the routine the fluctuation module points at as the canonical path from pickup voltage to field, and a spectrum taken before this step is a derivative spectrum, not a field one. Provenance The legacy VEST probe chain, kept here in a machine-independent form; vaft.process.fluctuation for why the integration must precede a spectral index. flux_loop_flux Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source flux_loop_flux(time, raw, gain, baseline_onset=0.27, baseline_offset=0.28, baseline_type='linear', baseline_onset_window=500, baseline_offset_window=100) Poloidal flux from raw flux-loop records, with a two-sided baseline.
