The orbit scales behind them are transit_frequency, deeply_trapped_bounce_frequency, trapped_particle_effective_collision_frequency and banana_width in vaft.formula.neoclassical. vaft.formula.ntv holds the exact, convention-bearing relations: ntv_precession_frequency, whose zero is the superbanana-plateau resonance. $\omega_E$ is the $E	imes B$ frequency omega_exb, never the toroidal rotation, and both $\omega_E$ and $\omega_B$ are measured along the plasma current; nonambipolar_torque_density, the torque on the plasma: the $\mathbf J	imes\mathbf B$ of the return current that cancels the non-ambipolar flux. Ion loss in a co-current plasma drives counter-current rotation. The size of the flux needs a drift-kinetic code (vaft.code), and Shaing’s connected formula is not implemented, so the NTV regime diagram shows slopes only. vaft.diagram.neoclassical_collisionality(epsilon=0.1) vaft.diagram.ntv_collisionality() vaft.diagram.ntv_precession_regimes(omega_magnetic=1.0)     Diagram Concept nbi_particle_lifecycle Injection, ionisation, fast-ion birth, confinement, slowing down, heating and drive, then thermalisation. Each loss branches at its own stage: shine-through while neutral, prompt orbit loss after ionisation, delayed loss after confinement nbi_neutral_attenuation Survival $e^{-	au}$ and birth density $\alpha S$ along a path through a parabolic plasma (an illustrative $\alpha$). Births are drawn at equal probability steps, and the shine-through is marked at the exit Diagram Concept o_mode_cutoff Evanescent below $\omega_{pe}$, propagating above; the cutoff $P = 0$ does not depend on $B$ x_mode_dispersion Evanescent below $\omega_L$, propagating to the upper-hybrid pole, evanescent to $\omega_R$, then propagating. Poles are masked cma_diagram Cutoffs (solid) and resonances (dashed) of a cold electron plasma in the CMA plane profile_propagation $n_O^2$ and $n_X^2$ along $R$, with strips where each mode propagates (propagation_regime), for an example tokamak (not a device) at the on-axis electron cyclotron frequency: O cutoffs, L and R cutoffs, the upper-hybrid layer behind the R cutoff, and the ECR   Diagram Concept     neoclassical_collisionality $D/D_\mathrm{plateau}$ against $\hat
u$: asymptotes $\hat
u/\epsilon^{3/2}$, 1 and $\hat
u$ meeting at the formula’s boundaries. Orderings, not phase boundaries     ntv_collisionality Non-resonant ($1/
u$, then $
u$–$\sqrt
u$) and resonant ($1/
u$, superbanana plateau, superbanana $
u$) branches, with Shaing’s exponents. Schematic breakpoints     ntv_precession_regimes $
u_\mathrm{eff}$ against $\omega_E/\omega_B$: the resonance $\omega_d = 0$ and the ordering $
u_\mathrm{eff} = \omega_d $ from ntv_precession_frequency. A schematic resonant band holds the superbanana plateau and $
u$ regimes Wall conditioning Baking, glow-discharge cleaning and boronization, each drawn as a transition of the wall state $S^{(0)}\mathrm{wall} 	o S^{(1)}\mathrm{wall}$ (WALL_STATE_CHANGE in the module), not only as “cleaning”. The diagrams are reduced and semantic, and share one vessel with an inlet port, a pump port and a wall-surface primitive: baking is thermal desorption only: no glow, anode, ion bombardment or coating; the glow discharges share one apparatus template: gas feed, glow, anode, the wall as cathode, and ions accelerated across the cathode sheath onto the whole wall. H$_2$/D$_2$ is reactive cleaning, with volatile O/C products that match the feed isotope. He is ion-induced release of retained H/D, drawn with its own arrow style; boronization names a “B-containing precursor” unless one is passed, and leaves a B-rich layer. Species are examples. No temperature, precursor, pressure or thickness is built in. A temperature (in K or °C) or a thickness is drawn only when the caller passes it together with its source. The sequence ends in plasma operation; how the conditioned wall responds then is the plasma-wall interaction section. vaft.diagram.wall_conditioning_baking() # temperature=, temperature_unit="K"|"degC", temperature_source= vaft.diagram.wall_conditioning_gdc("D2") # "H2", "D2" or "He" vaft.diagram.wall_conditioning_boronization(precursor="B$_2$H$_6$") vaft.diagram.wall_conditioning_sequence(("baking", "D2_gdc", "He_gdc", "boronization"))     Diagram Concept wall_conditioning_baking External heat drives adsorbed water and gases off the wall into the pump wall_conditioning_gdc One glow-discharge template. H$_2$/D$_2$: O and C leave as volatile products. He: He$^+$ bombardment releases retained H/D wall_conditioning_boronization A B-containing precursor in a deposition plasma leaves a B-rich surface layer, a change of surface state rather than cleaning wall_conditioning_sequence The single stages in the caller’s order, each arrow a wall-state transition, ending in plasma operation. The order is not a recommended procedure SOL blobs and filaments A blob is a localized positive density (pressure) perturbation in the scrape-off layer, and a hole is a negative one. The filament is the field-aligned structure whose perpendicular cross-section is the blob. How a blob moves: curvature and $
abla B$ drift ions and electrons apart; the density monopole becomes a charge dipole, $+$ above and $-$ below; the dipole’s $E$ field drives an $E	imes B$ drift outward on the low-field side, down $
abla B$ (a hole moves inward). How fast it moves depends on where the polarization current closes: along the field to the sheaths (sheath-connected, $v \propto \delta^{-2}$); across the field by ion inertia (inertial or resistive-ballooning, $v \propto \delta^{1/2}$); with resistivity and X-point fanning, in between. vaft.formula.sol holds the prescribed filament state blob_density_perturbation (a blob, or a hole below the background), the reference size $\delta_* = ho_s^{4/5}L_\parallel^{2/5}/R^{1/5}$, the reference velocity $v_$, the collisionality $\Lambda$, both limits, the interpolation, and the four regime scalings. All follow D’Ippolito, Myra and Zweben (2011), with a Gaussian of radius $\delta$. The $O(1)$ prefactors in Krasheninnikov (2001) and Theiler et al. (2011) belong to their own size definitions. The NSTX parameters of Myra et al. (2006) give $\hat a \approx 1.3$, as in their Fig. 1, and $v_ \approx 3$ km/s from their symbolic Eq. (3); their text quotes $v_* \sim 2$ km/s. Cold ions throughout: $c_s = (T_e/m_i)^{1/2}$. vaft.diagram.blob_polarization() # the mechanism: dipole, E, E x B; perturbation="hole" reverses it vaft.diagram.blob_current_closure(regime="sheath") # or "inertial": where the current closes vaft.diagram.blob_velocity_scaling() # v/v* against delta/delta*: both limits and Eq. (9) vaft.diagram.blob_regimes(epsilon_x=0.1) # Lambda against Theta = delta_hat^{5/2}: RB, RX, C_i, C_s         Integrated modeling: knowledge basis, realization, abstraction A single “analytic / numerical / empirical / data-driven” list mixes three independent questions. These diagrams keep them apart (#1085): Knowledge basis: where does the model’s knowledge come from, from first-principles to data-driven? Computational realization: how is the model evaluated, from analytical to fully numerical? Physical abstraction: at what description level is the system represented, from particle orbits to static equilibrium? The diagrams then combine the three axes into one space and connect models by typed couplings. They show location and character, not ranking: neither end of an axis is better. vaft.diagram.knowledge_basis() vaft.diagram.computational_realization() vaft.diagram.physical_abstraction() vaft.diagram.integrated_modeling_space() # "fusion", "tearing" vaft.diagram.integrated_modeling_process() Diagram Concept knowledge_basis Mechanistic/first-principles, semi-empirical/closure, empirical, data-driven. Physics-informed models (physical constraints with fitted or learned parts) are a bridge over the axis, not one point on it computational_realization Analytical, semi-analytical, reduced numerical, fully numerical. Learned surrogates are not a rung: they are placed by knowledge basis and role physical_abstraction Particle/orbit, kinetic, moment/fluid, MHD, equilibrium/static. Each arrow names its reduction: ensemble average, velocity moments + closure, single fluid at low frequency, stationary force balance integrated_modeling_space Knowledge basis across, realization up. The physical abstraction is shown by the fill colour of each model and repeated in its border pattern, so it survives grayscale. Conceptual and heuristic models (physical picture, cartoon, scaling argument, toy model) are an explanatory layer beside the space, not a fourth axis integrated_modeling_process Experiment, measurement, processing, inverse model (parameter inference), physical state, forward and data-driven models, prediction, and validation/control, with the eight coupling types of the legend Semi-empirical is a knowledge basis: a physical form with fitted coefficients. Semi-analytical is a computational realization: an asymptotic expansion, a Green-function reduction or a quadrature of a closed form. The words look alike but belong to different axes. Positions are semantic, not layout. Models with the same knowledge basis share an x and are separated in y. A learned model is not a realization rung. A surrogate takes the y of the model it emulates and is linked to it; a model that emulates nothing, such as a classifier, sits at the rung of its evaluation. The "fusion" overlay places familiar codes, from Solov’ev, EFIT and CHEASE to TGLF, TRANSP and ASCOT5, with an empirical confinement scaling, a neural-operator surrogate of TGLF and an event classifier. These placements are illustrative, not a classification: EFIT is an inverse model: it solves the Grad–Shafranov equation numerically inside a fit to measurements. TRANSP is mainly used interpretively, so it is also an inverse model. DCON integrates the Newcomb ODE, which is a reduced numerical method. TGLF is gyro-Landau-fluid approximating gyrokinetics, with a saturation rule fitted to nonlinear gyrokinetic runs, so it sits at semi-empirical/closure. The "tearing" variant follows one phenomenon from an island picture in the explanatory layer, through the Rutherford equation, to a nonlinear resistive-MHD simulation. The coupling types are data flow, closure, parameter inference/calibration, surrogate replacement, residual correction, validation/benchmarking, feedback/control and iterative coupling. A coupling is a label on an edge. The data-driven model’s three uses are alternatives: a closure inside the forward model, or a surrogate replacement of it, or a residual correction of its prediction (the hybrid mode). Validation compares the prediction with the processed measurement, and control acts on the experiment. The vocabulary and the example placements are data in vaft.diagram._modeling_schema: the axis stations, ModelDescriptor, ModelCoupling and the coupling types. They are kept apart from the drawing so that documentation and provenance tooling can reuse them. They are not a stable public API yet. Using the committed assets The reference SVGs live in docs/assets/diagrams/ and are the artifacts to embed anywhere: Documentation pages: ![island]({{ '/assets/diagrams/magnetic_island_poloidal.svg' | relative_url }}). The README, notebooks and slides: link or copy the SVG. It is self-contained, with glyphs stored as paths and no external fonts or images. They do not ship in the wheel. An installed package builds any diagram from its packaged TikZ template. Regenerating and checking python -m vaft.diagram.build # re-render diagrams whose TikZ source changed python -m vaft.diagram.build --check # verify the committed assets; needs no TeX manifest.json, stored next to the SVGs, records the SHA-256 of the generated TikZ document each SVG was rendered from, together with the SHA-256 of the SVG itself. --check rebuilds the TikZ in pure Python and fails in four cases: an asset is stale, an asset was edited by hand, an asset is missing, or an asset is orphaned. CI runs it on every pull request. Freshness is judged on the source and not on SVG bytes, because two dvisvgm releases write different but equally correct SVG for the same picture. Rendering needs latex and dvisvgm, which TeX Live and MacTeX provide. The generated .tex, PDF, PNG and LaTeX by-products are never committed.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/particle.title: Formula reference: particle
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/particle.body:
Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.particle: 13 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("particle.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview This module provides the gyration and guiding-centre drift relations of a charged particle, and a Boris integrator of the full Lorentz-force orbit against which the drift relations can be checked. SymbolMeaningUnit qparticle charge, signedC mparticle masskg Bmagnetic field (vector or magnitude)T Eelectric fieldV/m v_perpspeed perpendicular to Bm/s v_parspeed parallel to Bm/s omega_csigned gyrofrequency qB/mrad/s rhoLarmor radiusm R_cradius-of-curvature vector of the field linem Functions boris_orbitCharged-particle orbit from the Lorentz force, by the Boris scheme. Convention bounce_harmonic_detuningFrequency mismatch of a trapped orbit with a toroidal-$n$ perturbation at bounce harmonic $\ell$. Convention canonical_toroidal_momentumCanonical toroidal angular momentum of a particle in an axisymmetric field. Convention curvature_drift_velocityCurvature drift velocity of the guiding centre. Convention exb_drift_velocityE-cross-B drift velocity of the guiding centre. Convention grad_b_drift_velocityGrad-B drift velocity of the guiding centre. Convention guiding_center_toroidal_momentumCanonical toroidal momentum of a guiding centre, flux plus mechanical parts. Convention gyration_offsetPosition of a gyrating particle relative to its guiding centre. Convention gyrofrequencySigned gyrofrequency of a charged particle. Convention larmor_radiusLarmor (gyro) radius of a charged particle. Convention magnetic_momentMagnetic moment of a gyrating particle, the first adiabatic invariant. Convention parallel_speed_from_muParallel speed where the field is $B$, from energy and magnetic-moment conservation. Convention psi_per_radian_from_cocosThe guiding-centre $\psi = RA_\phi$ from a flux stored in a COCOS convention. Convention No function matches. boris_orbit Convention-sensitive source boris_orbit(q, m, x0, v0, E_field, B_field, dt, n_steps) Charged-particle orbit from the Lorentz force, by the Boris scheme. \[m\, rac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{v}}{\mathrm{d}t} = q\,(\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{v}	imes\mathbf{B}), \qquad  rac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mathbf{v}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCParticle charge, signed. mfloatkgParticle mass. x0array_likemInitial position. v0array_likem/sInitial velocity. E_fieldcallableV/mE_field(x) returning the electric field at position x. B_fieldcallableTB_field(x) returning the magnetic field at position x. dtfloatsTime step. n_stepsint-Number of steps. Returns positionsnp.ndarraymPositions, shape (n_steps + 1, 3), the first being x0. velocitiesnp.ndarraym/svelocities[i + 1] is the velocity over the step from positions[i] to positions[i + 1]; velocities[0] is v0. Shape (n_steps + 1, 3). Convention Non-relativistic leapfrog: velocities live at the half steps between positions (half electric kick, magnetic rotation, half kick, then the position advance). v0 is taken as the velocity half a step before x0. Right-handed Cartesian components. Raises ValueError m, dt or n_steps is not positive, or a vector is not a 3-vector. Physical interpretation · Numerical notes · References Physical interpretation The full orbit the drift formulas average: integrated in a uniform or slowly varying field, its guiding centre moves at exb_drift_velocity, grad_b_drift_velocity and curvature_drift_velocity. Numerical notes The magnetic rotation is exact in angle up to the $	an(\omega_c\Delta t /2)$ phase error, so with $E = 0$ the kinetic energy is conserved to round-off for any step; the scheme is volume-preserving and has no secular energy drift. Keep $|\omega_c|\Delta t \lesssim 0.1$ for an accurate gyrophase. Fixed step, so the output is deterministic. References J. P. Boris, Proc. 4th Conf. Numer. Sim. Plasmas, NRL (1970), 3. C. K. Birdsall and A. B. Langdon, Plasma Physics via Computer Simulation, McGraw-Hill (1985), Sec. 4-4. H. Qin et al., Phys. Plasmas 20, 084503 (2013). bounce_harmonic_detuning Convention-sensitive source bounce_harmonic_detuning(omega_b, omega_exb, omega_magnetic=0.0, *, l=1, n=1) Frequency mismatch of a trapped orbit with a toroidal-$n$ perturbation at bounce harmonic $\ell$. \[\Delta\omega_\mathrm{BH} = \ell\,\omega_b - n\,\omega_E - n\,\omega_B\] NameTypeUnitDescription omega_bfloat or np.ndarrayrad/sBounce frequency of the trapped orbit. omega_exbfloat or np.ndarrayrad/sToroidal $E	imes B$ precession frequency. omega_magneticfloat or np.ndarrayrad/sToroidal magnetic (grad-B and curvature) precession frequency. lint-Bounce harmonic, any integer including 0. nint-Toroidal mode number of the perturbation. Returns —float or np.ndarrayrad/s$\Delta\omega_\mathrm{BH}$; zero at the resonance. Convention The temporal resonance of Park, Boozer and Menard: a static perturbation $\propto e^{in\phi}$ seen by an orbit precessing toroidally at $\omega_E + \omega_B$ and bouncing at $\omega_b$. $\ell = 0$ is the precession resonance. It is not the spatial resonance $m = nq$ of a field line; the two are separate conditions. Raises ValueError l or n is not an integer. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Where it vanishes the orbit sees a stationary phase of the perturbation each bounce, so the change of $P_\phi$ adds up secularly instead of averaging out – the orbit-level origin of non-resonant transport and NTV, which themselves need the kinetic response of the whole distribution. References J.-K. Park, A. H. Boozer and J. E. Menard, Phys. Rev. Lett. 102 (2009) 065002. canonical_toroidal_momentum Convention-sensitive source canonical_toroidal_momentum(q, m, R, v_phi, A_phi) Canonical toroidal angular momentum of a particle in an axisymmetric field. \[P_\phi = m R v_\phi + q R A_\phi\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCSigned particle charge. mfloatkgParticle mass. Rfloat or np.ndarraymMajor radius of the particle. v_phifloat or np.ndarraym/sPhysical toroidal velocity component $\hat{ oldsymbol\phi}\cdot\mathbf v$. A_phifloat or np.ndarrayT mPhysical toroidal component of the vector potential. Returns —float or np.ndarraykg m^2/s$P_\phi = \partial\mathcal L/\partial\dot\phi$. Convention Cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ right-handed, $\phi$ counter-clockwise seen from above (the IMAS $\phi$). v_phi and A_phi are physical components; $RA_\phi$ is the covariant one, which equals the poloidal flux per radian $\psi$ (see guiding_center_toroidal_momentum). The full particle form: it includes the gyration in $v_\phi$. Raises ValueError m is not positive or R is negative. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The momentum conjugate to $\phi$. Where $\partial\mathcal L/\partial\phi = 0$ (axisymmetry) it is exactly conserved, which ties the particle’s toroidal velocity to its flux-surface position. Assumptions The Lagrangian $\mathcal L = 	frac12 mv^2 + q\mathbf A\cdot\mathbf v - q\Phi$; conservation needs axisymmetry, $\partial\mathcal L/\partial\phi = 0$. References R. B. White, The Theory of Toroidally Confined Plasmas, 3rd ed., Imperial College Press (2014), Ch. 3. curvature_drift_velocity Convention-sensitive source curvature_drift_velocity(q, m, v_par, B, R_c) Curvature drift velocity of the guiding centre. \[\mathbf{v}_R =  rac{m v_\parallel^{2}}{qB^{2}}\,  rac{\mathbf{R}_c	imes\mathbf{B}}{R_c^{2}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCParticle charge, signed. mfloatkgParticle mass. v_parfloat or np.ndarraym/sSpeed along the magnetic field. Barray_likeTMagnetic field, last axis the three Cartesian components. R_carray_likemRadius-of-curvature vector, from the centre of curvature to the field line. Returns —np.ndarraym/sDrift velocity. Convention $\mathbf{R}_c$ points outward, from the centre of curvature to the line, as in Chen. Charge-signed like the grad-B drift. In a vacuum field $
abla	imes\mathbf{B} = 0$ the two drifts add in the same direction. Raises ValueError An input is not a 3-vector, q is zero, or B or R_c vanishes. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The centrifugal force of streaming along a curved line, $m v_\parallel^2 / R_c$, acts like any other perpendicular force $\mathbf{F}$ and drives $\mathbf{F}	imes\mathbf{B}/(qB^2)$. Assumptions $ho \ll R_c$. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.3.2. exb_drift_velocity Convention-sensitive source exb_drift_velocity(E, B) E-cross-B drift velocity of the guiding centre. \[\mathbf{v}_E =  rac{\mathbf{E}	imes\mathbf{B}}{B^{2}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Earray_likeV/mElectric field, last axis the three Cartesian components. Barray_likeTMagnetic field, last axis the three Cartesian components. Returns —np.ndarraym/sDrift velocity, same shape as the broadcast inputs. Convention Right-handed Cartesian components. The drift is independent of charge and mass, so ions and electrons move together and no current flows. Raises ValueError An input is not a 3-vector, or B vanishes. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Over each gyration the particle gains energy on one side of its orbit and loses it on the other, so its radius changes around the orbit and the guiding centre steps sideways – perpendicular to both fields. Assumptions $E_\perp \ll cB$ (non-relativistic drift); uniform fields over a Larmor radius and slow in time compared with the gyroperiod. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.2.2. grad_b_drift_velocity Convention-sensitive source grad_b_drift_velocity(q, m, v_perp, B, grad_B) Grad-B drift velocity of the guiding centre. \[\mathbf{v}_{
abla B} =  rac{m v_\perp^{2}}{2qB}\,  rac{\mathbf{B}	imes
abla B}{B^{2}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCParticle charge, signed. mfloatkgParticle mass. v_perpfloat or np.ndarraym/sSpeed perpendicular to the magnetic field. Barray_likeTMagnetic field, last axis the three Cartesian components. grad_Barray_likeT/m Gradient of the field magnitude $ \mathbf{B} $. Returns —np.ndarraym/sDrift velocity. Convention Charge-signed: ions and electrons drift in opposite directions, which is what makes this drift carry current. Raises ValueError An input is not a 3-vector, q is zero, or B vanishes. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The orbit is tighter where the field is stronger, so the guiding centre walks perpendicular to both $\mathbf{B}$ and its gradient. Assumptions $ho \ll B/|
abla B|$; the drift is the first-order average over a gyration. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.3.1. guiding_center_toroidal_momentum Convention-sensitive source guiding_center_toroidal_momentum(q, m, v_par, R, b_phi, psi_per_radian) Canonical toroidal momentum of a guiding centre, flux plus mechanical parts. \[P_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}} = q\psi + m v_\parallel R\, b_\phi\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCSigned particle charge. mfloatkgParticle mass. v_parfloat or np.ndarraym/sSigned parallel velocity, positive along $\mathbf B$. Rfloat or np.ndarraymMajor radius of the guiding centre. b_phifloat or np.ndarray-Toroidal component of the unit vector $\mathbf b = \mathbf B/B$. psi_per_radianfloat or np.ndarrayWb/radPoloidal flux per radian at the guiding centre, $\psi = RA_\phi$. Returns —float or np.ndarraykg m^2/s$P_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}}$. Convention $\psi$ is per radian and is the covariant $RA_\phi$ with the IMAS $\phi$: its sign follows the plasma current’s direction in $\phi$, largest on the axis for a current along $+\phi$. A stored COCOS flux is converted by psi_per_radian_from_cocos – $-\psi/(2\pi)$ for COCOS 11 (IMAS DD3), $+\psi/(2\pi)$ for COCOS 17; used as stored it gives the flux term the wrong sign or a $2\pi$ error. $b_\phi v_\parallel$ is the toroidal velocity of the guiding centre; $mRb_\phi v_\parallel = mIv_\parallel/B$ with $I = RB_\phi$. Raises ValueError m is not positive or R is negative. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Conserved in axisymmetry, so a change of $v_\parallel$ along the orbit is paid for by a change of $\psi$: $\Delta\psi = -(m/q)\Delta(v_\parallel Rb_\phi)$. That is the finite orbit width – the global view of what the grad-B and curvature drifts do locally. Assumptions Lowest-order guiding-centre theory: the gyration averaged out, drift velocity small against $v_\parallel$ in the mechanical term. References R. B. White, The Theory of Toroidally Confined Plasmas, 3rd ed., Imperial College Press (2014), Ch. 3. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.12. gyration_offset Convention-sensitive source gyration_offset(q, m, B, v) Position of a gyrating particle relative to its guiding centre. \[ oldsymbol{ho} =  rac{m}{qB^{2}}\,\mathbf{B}	imes\mathbf{v}_\perp\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloatCParticle charge, signed. mfloatkgParticle mass. Barray_likeTMagnetic field, last axis the three Cartesian components. varray_likem/sVelocity in the guiding-centre frame; only its part perpendicular to B enters. Returns —np.ndarraymVector from the guiding centre to the particle. Convention Guiding centre = position minus this vector. Its magnitude is larmor_radius and its sense follows the charge: for $\mathbf{B} = \hat z$ and $\mathbf{v} = \hat x$, an ion sits a Larmor radius along $+\hat y$ from its guiding centre, an electron along $-\hat y$. Raises ValueError An input is not a 3-vector, q is zero, m is not positive, or B vanishes. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The Lorentz force $q\mathbf{v}	imes\mathbf{B}$ points from the particle to the centre of its orbit; this is minus that direction times the Larmor radius. Assumptions Uniform field over the orbit; v measured in the frame moving with any drift. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.2. gyrofrequency Convention-sensitive source gyrofrequency(q, m, B) Signed gyrofrequency of a charged particle. \[\omega_c =  rac{qB}{m}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloat or np.ndarrayCParticle charge, signed. mfloat or np.ndarraykgParticle mass. Bfloat or np.ndarrayTMagnetic-field magnitude. Returns —float or np.ndarrayrad/sGyrofrequency, positive for positive charge. Convention Signed: $\omega_c > 0$ for an ion, $< 0$ for an electron. An ion gyrates in the left-handed sense about $\mathbf{B}$ (clockwise seen with $\mathbf{B}$ pointing at the viewer), an electron in the right-handed sense; the sign carries that. Use abs for the frequency alone. Raises ValueError m is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The rate at which the Lorentz force turns the perpendicular velocity: the fastest time scale of magnetised motion, and the reason drifts are slow by comparison. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.2. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 2.2. larmor_radius Convention-sensitive source larmor_radius(q, m, v_perp, B) Larmor (gyro) radius of a charged particle. \[ho =  rac{m\,v_\perp}{|q|\,B}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloat or np.ndarrayCParticle charge; only its magnitude enters. mfloat or np.ndarraykgParticle mass. v_perpfloat or np.ndarraym/sSpeed perpendicular to the magnetic field. Bfloat or np.ndarrayTMagnetic-field magnitude. Returns —float or np.ndarraymRadius of the gyro-orbit. Convention Always positive: the gyration sense is in gyrofrequency. $v_\perp$ is the speed in the guiding-centre frame, i.e. after removing any drift. Raises ValueError q or B is zero. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The scale below which a particle does not follow field lines; drift approximations need it small against the field’s gradient length. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.2. magnetic_moment Convention-sensitive source magnetic_moment(m, v_perp, B) Magnetic moment of a gyrating particle, the first adiabatic invariant. \[\mu =  rac{m v_\perp^2}{2B}\] NameTypeUnitDescription mfloatkgParticle mass. v_perpfloat or np.ndarraym/sSpeed perpendicular to $\mathbf B$. Bfloat or np.ndarrayTField strength at the guiding centre. Returns —float or np.ndarrayJ/T$\mu$, non-negative. Convention Independent of the charge sign; v_perp enters squared, so its sign is irrelevant. With $E = 	frac12 mv_\parallel^2 + \mu B$ in a static field it gives the mirror relation of parallel_speed_from_mu. Raises ValueError m or B is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The gyro-orbit’s magnetic dipole moment, equivalently its gyro-action $J_\perp = (2m/|q|)\mu$ up to a constant: the invariant of the fastest motion, which is why $v_\perp^2$ tracks $B$ along a field line. Assumptions Conserved only under the adiabatic ordering: the field changes little over a gyro-period and a Larmor radius. It is defined for any inputs; its conservation is not implied. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.3.3. parallel_speed_from_mu Convention-sensitive source parallel_speed_from_mu(v, pitch_ref, B_ref, B) Parallel speed where the field is $B$, from energy and magnetic-moment conservation. \[ rac{v_\parallel}{v} = \pm\sqrt{1 - \left(1 - \xi_\mathrm{ref}^2ight) rac{B}{B_\mathrm{ref}}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription vfloatm/sSpeed, conserved. pitch_reffloat-Pitch $\xi = v_\parallel/v$ where the field is B_ref, in $[-1, 1]$. B_reffloatTField strength at the reference point. Bfloat or np.ndarrayTField strength along the orbit. Returns —float or np.ndarraym/s $ v_\parallel $, NaN where the particle cannot reach (it is reflected before $B$). Convention Magnitude only: the sign is the direction of travel, which the caller tracks. $\mu = mv_\perp^2/(2B)$ and $E = mv^2/2$ are the invariants; a static field, no electric potential. Raises ValueError pitch_ref lies outside $[-1, 1]$ or a field is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · See Also · References Physical interpretation The magnetic mirror: $v_\parallel$ falls as the particle moves into stronger field and vanishes where $B = B_\mathrm{ref}/(1 - \xi_\mathrm{ref}^2)$, the bounce point of a trapped particle. Assumptions Adiabatic motion: $\mu$ conserved, field varying slowly over a gyro-orbit. See Also vaft.diagram.trapped_and_passing_orbits : the canonical diagram of this relation. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Sec. 2.3.3. psi_per_radian_from_cocos Convention-sensitive source psi_per_radian_from_cocos(psi, cocos) The guiding-centre $\psi = RA_\phi$ from a flux stored in a COCOS convention. \[\psi_{RA_\phi} = -\,\sigma_{Bp}\,\sigma_{R\phi Z}\, rac{\psi_\mathrm{COCOS}}{(2\pi)^{e_{Bp}}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription psifloat or np.ndarrayWb or Wb/radPoloidal flux as the COCOS convention stores it. cocosint-The COCOS index, 1-8 or 11-18. Returns —float or np.ndarrayWb/rad$RA_\phi$ with the IMAS $\phi$, the flux per radian that guiding_center_toroidal_momentum takes. Convention $\mathbf B_\mathrm{pol} = 
abla(RA_\phi)	imes
abla\phi$ with $\phi$ counter-clockwise from above, so $RA_\phi$ is largest on the axis for a current along $+\phi$. Sauter’s COCOS flux has $d\psi/dho$ of sign $\sigma_{Ip}\sigma_{Bp}$ and its own $\phi$ orientation $\sigma_{R\phi Z}$, hence the factor: $-1/(2\pi)$ for COCOS 11 (IMAS DD3), $+1/(2\pi)$ for COCOS 17 (DD4), $-1$ for COCOS 1. $e_{Bp} = 1$ for 11-18 (whole-turn flux in Wb). Raises ValueError cocos is not one of the sixteen indices. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Only this signed, per-radian flux makes $q\psi + mv_\parallel Rb_\phi$ a conserved quantity; a COCOS flux used as stored gives the flux term the wrong sign or a $2\pi$ error. References O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. 8 and Table I.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/transfor.title: Formula reference: transformer
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/transfor.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.transformer: 8 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("transformer.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview Romero’s reduction of Poynting’s theorem to three voltages – the boundary loop voltage $V_B$, the resistive voltage $V_R$ and the voltage $V_C$ at the current-weighted “equilibrium” flux surface – closes the plasma current and the internal inductance exactly, with no assumption about the current profile. This module holds those identities and the definitions they rest on. It owns no time derivative and no integral over time: $V_C = -\dot\psi_C$, the volt-second budget and any closure for $V_C$ belong to the process layer. SymbolMeaningUnit I_pplasma currentA L_idimensional internal inductance, 2 W_int / I_p^2H psipoloidal flux through the toroidal circle, fullWb psi_Bpsi at the plasma boundaryWb psi_Ccurrent-weighted flux average, int psi j dS / I_pWb V_Bboundary loop voltage, -d psi_B / dtV V_Cvoltage at the equilibrium surface, -d psi_C / dtV V_Rresistive voltage, R_p (I_p - I_ni)V R_pplasma resistanceOhm I_ninon-inductively driven currentA Romero’s signs throughout. $\psi$ is the full flux through the toroidal circle through a point, in weber and not per radian, and every voltage is $V = -\dot\psi$ (Lenz). In this convention $\psi_C - \psi_B = L_i I_p$ has the sign of $I_p$, and a positive $V_B$ sustains a positive $I_p$ – the same sense as the loop voltage of vaft.formula.startup.plasma_current_derivative_lumped_from_V_loop_R_p_I_p_L_p. An equilibrium stored in another COCOS must be brought to it first; the one function here that reads a flux refuses a result whose sign says it was not. This is not the convention of vaft.formula.equilibrium.loop_voltage_from_total_flux, which is Ejima’s $+2\pi\,\dot\psi_b$ on a per-radian flux: the two differ in sign and by $2\pi$ in normalisation (#354). Feeding that function’s output in as $V_B$ turns a ramp-up into a ramp-down. Functions current_weighted_flux_from_psi_j_dSCurrent-weighted average of the poloidal flux over the plasma cross-section. Convention equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_RVoltage at the equilibrium flux surface, inferred from the inductance history. Convention equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_RVoltage at the equilibrium flux surface, inferred from the current history. Convention internal_inductance_from_psi_C_psi_B_I_pDimensional internal inductance from the equilibrium and boundary fluxes. Convention internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_CRate of change of the internal inductance, Romero’s exact balance. Convention plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_RRate of change of the plasma current, Romero’s exact balance. Convention resistive_voltage_from_R_p_I_p_I_niResistive voltage of the plasma, net of non-inductive current drive. Convention romero_closure_rates_from_I_p_L_i_V_CB_V_B_V_R_k_tauState rates of Romero’s first-order current-diffusion closure. Empirical Convention No function matches. current_weighted_flux_from_psi_j_dS Convention-sensitive source current_weighted_flux_from_psi_j_dS(psi_Wb, j_phi_A_m2, dS_m2) Current-weighted average of the poloidal flux over the plasma cross-section. \[\psi_C = \frac{\int_\Omega \psi\,j_\phi\,dS}{\int_\Omega j_\phi\,dS}\] NameTypeUnitDescription psi_Wbarray_likeWbPoloidal flux at each cell inside the boundary, full flux in Romero’s sign, finite. j_phi_A_m2array_likeA m^-2Toroidal current density at the same cells, finite. dS_m2array_likem^2Poloidal cross-section area of each cell, finite and non-negative; broadcast against the other two. Returns —floatWb$\psi_C$. Convention The cells must be the plasma, not the grid. Cells outside the boundary carry vessel or coil current in a free-boundary solution and would pull $\psi_C$ toward the wall; mask them out, or pass $dS = 0$ for them. The quadrature is the plain cell sum – the caller chooses the cells, which is the one approximation this makes. $V_C = -\dot\psi_C$ is the voltage the other functions here take; the time derivative is the process layer’s. Raises ValueError A non-finite input, a negative cell area, arrays that do not broadcast, or a net enclosed current of zero. See Also · References See Also internal_inductance_from_psi_C_psi_B_I_p References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eq. (34). equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_R Convention-sensitive source equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_R(I_p_A, dL_i_dt_H_s, V_R_V) Voltage at the equilibrium flux surface, inferred from the inductance history. \[V_C^{(L)} = V_R - \frac{I_p}{2}\,\dot L_i\] NameTypeUnitDescription I_p_Afloat or np.ndarrayAPlasma current, finite. dL_i_dt_H_sfloat or np.ndarrayH/sRate of change of the internal inductance, finite. V_R_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage, finite. Returns —float or np.ndarrayV$V_C$. Convention Romero’s eq. (39) solved for $V_C$. This and equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_R read the same $V_C$ off two different measured histories, and a third route is $-\dot\psi_C$ from the equilibria; their disagreement is #781’s first validation target, and it lands on whichever input is worst – usually $R_p$, which enters both. Raises ValueError A non-finite input. See Also · References See Also equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_R current_weighted_flux_from_psi_j_dS References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eq. (39). equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_R Convention-sensitive source equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_R(L_i_H, dI_p_dt_A_s, V_B_V, V_R_V) Voltage at the equilibrium flux surface, inferred from the current history. \[V_C^{(I)} = L_i\,\dot I_p - V_B + 2V_R\] NameTypeUnitDescription L_i_Hfloat or np.ndarrayHDimensional internal inductance, finite and non-negative. dI_p_dt_A_sfloat or np.ndarrayA/sRate of change of the plasma current, finite. V_B_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVBoundary loop voltage, finite. V_R_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage, finite. Returns —float or np.ndarrayV$V_C$. Convention Romero’s eq. (40) solved for $V_C$; see equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_R for the other route and what their difference measures. Raises ValueError A non-finite input or a negative internal inductance. See Also · References See Also equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_R References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eq. (40). internal_inductance_from_psi_C_psi_B_I_p Convention-sensitive source internal_inductance_from_psi_C_psi_B_I_p(psi_C_Wb, psi_B_Wb, I_p_A) Dimensional internal inductance from the equilibrium and boundary fluxes. \[L_i = \frac{\psi_C - \psi_B}{I_p}\] NameTypeUnitDescription psi_C_Wbfloat or np.ndarrayWbCurrent-weighted flux average, Romero’s sign, finite. psi_B_Wbfloat or np.ndarrayWbBoundary flux, same convention, finite. I_p_Afloat or np.ndarrayAPlasma current, finite and non-zero. Returns —float or np.ndarrayHInternal inductance. Convention Exact, and a sign check on the flux convention. With $W_{p,\mathrm{int}} = \tfrac12(\psi_C - \psi_B) I_p$ this is $2W_{p,\mathrm{int}}/I_p^2$, the same $L_i$ as vaft.formula.equilibrium.internal_inductance_from_W_int_Ip, so it is positive for any current profile. A negative value is therefore not a physical answer but an inverted $\psi$ – a COCOS whose flux grows outward for positive current – and is refused rather than returned. A per-radian flux is $2\pi$ too small and passes that check: convert it before calling. Raises ValueError A non-finite input, a zero current, or a negative result – which means the flux is in a convention opposite to Romero’s. See Also · References See Also current_weighted_flux_from_psi_j_dS References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eqs. (35)-(36). internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C Convention-sensitive source internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C(I_p_A, V_R_V, V_C_V) Rate of change of the internal inductance, Romero’s exact balance. \[\dot L_i = \frac{2\,(V_R - V_C)}{I_p}\] NameTypeUnitDescription I_p_Afloat or np.ndarrayAPlasma current, finite and non-zero. V_R_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage, finite. V_C_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVVoltage at the equilibrium flux surface, finite. Returns —float or np.ndarrayH/s$\mathrm{d}L_i/\mathrm{d}t$. Convention Romero’s signs, as in the module docstring. Exact: no current-profile model enters. $L_i$ is steady exactly when $V_C = V_R$, and the full steady state is $V_C = V_R = V_B$, a flat loop-voltage profile. Raises ValueError A non-finite input or a zero plasma current. See Also · References See Also plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_R equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_I_p_dL_i_V_R References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eq. (39). plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_R Convention-sensitive source plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_R(L_i_H, V_B_V, V_C_V, V_R_V) Rate of change of the plasma current, Romero’s exact balance. \[\dot I_p = \frac{V_B + V_C - 2V_R}{L_i}\] NameTypeUnitDescription L_i_Hfloat or np.ndarrayHDimensional internal inductance, finite and positive. V_B_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVBoundary loop voltage, finite. V_C_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVVoltage at the equilibrium flux surface, finite. V_R_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage, finite. Returns —float or np.ndarrayA/s$\mathrm{d}I_p/\mathrm{d}t$. Convention Romero’s signs. Together with internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C it gives $L_i\dot I_p + \tfrac12 I_p\dot L_i = V_B - V_R$, the energy balance of the internal field, without assuming how $L_i$ evolves. Only the internal inductance appears: the external one and the coils are inside $V_B$. Raises ValueError A non-finite input or a non-positive internal inductance. See Also · References See Also internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C equilibrium_surface_voltage_from_L_i_dI_p_V_B_V_R References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eq. (40). resistive_voltage_from_R_p_I_p_I_ni Convention-sensitive source resistive_voltage_from_R_p_I_p_I_ni(R_p_ohm, I_p_A, I_ni_A) Resistive voltage of the plasma, net of non-inductive current drive. \[V_R = R_p\,(I_p - \hat I)\] NameTypeUnitDescription R_p_ohmfloat or np.ndarrayOhmPlasma resistance, finite and non-negative. I_p_Afloat or np.ndarrayAPlasma current, finite. I_ni_Afloat or np.ndarrayANon-inductively driven current, finite; 0 asserts a purely Ohmic plasma. Returns —float or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage. Convention I_ni_A has no default on purpose. $\hat I = 0$ is a statement that nothing but the transformer drives current, true of a pure-Ohmic VEST discharge and false with EC, NBI or helicity injection; a caller must make it. $R_p$ and $\hat I$ are Romero’s resistance-weighted definitions, $\int\eta j^2 dS/I_p^2$ and $\int\eta j\hat j dS/\int\eta j^2 dS\cdot I_p$, which are what make $I_p V_R$ the dissipated power; a Spitzer ring resistance is an estimate of the first. Raises ValueError A non-finite input or a negative resistance. See Also · References See Also vaft.formula.startup.plasma_resistance_uniform_ellipse_from_eta_R0_a_kappa References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eqs. (17)-(21). romero_closure_rates_from_I_p_L_i_V_CB_V_B_V_R_k_tau Empirical fitConvention-sensitive source romero_closure_rates_from_I_p_L_i_V_CB_V_B_V_R_k_tau(I_p_A, L_i_H, V_CB_V, V_B_V, V_R_V, k, tau_s) State rates of Romero’s first-order current-diffusion closure. \[L_i\,\dot I_p = 2(V_B - V_R) + V,\qquad I_p\,\dot L_i = 2(V_R - V_B) - 2V,\qquad \dot V \simeq -\frac{V}{\tau} + \frac{k}{\tau}(V_R - V_B)\] with $V = V_C - V_B$: the two exact identities of plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_R and internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C rewritten in $V$, and a first-order relaxation of $V$ that closes them. NameTypeUnitDescription I_p_Afloat or np.ndarrayAPlasma current, finite and non-zero. L_i_Hfloat or np.ndarrayHDimensional internal inductance, finite and positive. V_CB_Vfloat or np.ndarrayV$V = V_C - V_B$, the equilibrium-surface voltage relative to the boundary, finite. V_B_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVBoundary loop voltage, finite. V_R_Vfloat or np.ndarrayVResistive voltage, finite. kfloat or np.ndarray-Closure gain, finite. tau_sfloat or np.ndarraysClosure time constant, finite and positive. Returns dI_p_dtfloat or np.ndarrayA/sRate of change of the plasma current. dL_i_dtfloat or np.ndarrayH/sRate of change of the internal inductance. dV_CB_dtfloat or np.ndarrayV/sRate of change of $V_C - V_B$. Convention Romero’s signs, as in the module docstring. The first two rates are exact; only $\dot V$ is modelled. The fixed point is $V = 0$ and $V_R = V_B$ – a flat loop-voltage profile – for any $k \ne 1$ and $\tau$: there $L_i$ and $I_p$ are both steady. Raises ValueError A non-finite input, a zero current, a non-positive internal inductance or a non-positive time constant. Validity · Limitations · See Also · References Validity Empirical fit. Eq. (41) is a first-order approximation of current diffusion, and $k$ and $\tau$ are identified per device and regime by fitting the model to measured histories (Romero’s JET fits); nothing here supplies them. With $k = 0$ the relative voltage simply decays as $e^{-t/\tau}$. Limitations One radial mode: a current profile that relaxes on two time scales, or a sawtoothing core, is outside it. $V_R$ is an input, so an $R_p$ that depends on the evolving profile must be updated by the caller. See Also plasma_current_rate_from_L_i_V_B_V_C_V_R internal_inductance_rate_from_I_p_V_R_V_C References J. A. Romero and JET-EFDA contributors, Nucl. Fusion 50 (2010) 115002, eqs. (41)-(45).

/vaft/develop/reference/process/ml/.title: Process reference: ml
/vaft/develop/reference/process/ml/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.ml: 21 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("ml.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview Training is a VAFT processing stage like any other. This package owns the whole path – dataset construction, group-aware splitting, windowing, training, evaluation, threshold calibration, artifact packaging, export, resolution of published versions and inference – while trained weights are distributed through the separate VEST-Tokamak/vaft-nn registry. Importing it loads NumPy only. Frameworks are backends chosen by name in a ModelSpec and imported on first use: "numpy" (ridge, PCA autoencoder, k-NN distance – no dependency), "sklearn" (one-class SVM, stored as ONNX) and "torch" (MLP, autoencoder, and any architecture task code registers), the last two installed with pip install 'vaft[ml]'. No public signature takes or returns a framework object. Published models come from VEST-Tokamak/vaft-nn, an external dependency configured with $VAFT_NN_HOME like the external codes’ $XHOME. A split assigns groups – the independent scientific unit, a shot or a simulation case – to partitions, and is made before windowing or augmentation; it then applies unchanged to every derived dataset. Normalisation moments come from the train partition only. Every inference result carries the immutable identity of the model that produced it: exact version and manifest SHA-256, never only a stage alias. Functions build_datasetAssemble a fingerprinted dataset from arrays. calibrate_thresholdSet a decision threshold on a per-sample model output from one partition. dataset_fingerprintSHA-256 content fingerprint of a dataset. evaluate_modelStandard ML metrics of a model on one partition, overall and per group. export_modelExport the network to an inference format and prove it agrees. fetch_modelDownload a published model’s release assets into the cache, verified. load_datasetLoad a dataset written by save_dataset, verifying its fingerprint. load_modelResolve a published model and load it, ready for predict. load_model_artifactLoad an artifact directory, verifying every file against its manifest. load_model_bundleLoad a bundle directory, verifying every file and member manifest. predictRun a model on new data and stamp the result with its exact identity. register_architectureMake a task-defined network available to a backend by name. register_augmentationMake a train-time augmentation available by name. register_lossMake a task-defined training loss available by name. resolve_modelResolve a published model to one exact, hash-verified local version. Convention save_datasetMaterialise a dataset on disk so training can run elsewhere. save_model_artifactWrite a model as an immutable, hash-pinned artifact directory. save_model_bundleWrite a multi-model bundle as one immutable, hash-pinned release. split_groupsAssign independent groups to train/validation/test partitions. train_modelTrain a model on the train partition and package it with its provenance. Convention window_datasetCut sliding windows that never cross a group boundary. No function matches. build_dataset Machine-independent source build_dataset(inputs, groups, *, spec, targets=None, sample_meta=None, feature_spec=None, available=None) Assemble a fingerprinted dataset from arrays. The generic entry point for every ML task: an engineered-feature table (pass feature_spec), a waveform or image tensor, or paired input-target supervision (pass targets). NameTypeUnitDescription inputsarray_likeanySamples along the first axis, shape (n, *input_shape). groupsarray_like-Independent unit of each sample (shot number, simulation case), shape (n,). specDatasetSpec-Name, task, group key and column names of the dataset. targetsarray_like or None, optionalanyPaired targets, shape (n, *target_shape); None for an unsupervised dataset. sample_metamapping of str to array_like or None, optionalanyPer-sample arrays that travel with every subset, such as window times. feature_specFeatureSpec or None, optional-Column schema of a 2-D engineered-feature table; returns a FeatureDataset when given. availablearray_like of bool or None, optional-Per-sample availability: False where the inputs do not exist (a diagnostic absent for that shot). Such samples may hold non-finite inputs; they are stored as zeros and excluded from training, calibration and evaluation, and predict reports them as unavailable. None means every sample is available. Returns —DatasetArtifact-The dataset with its fingerprint filled in. Raises ModelContractError On mismatched lengths, a non-finite input in an available sample, or a feature table whose width differs from feature_spec. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Available inputs must be finite: imputation is a scientific choice (train-partition medians, a flag, a drop) that belongs to the caller. Unavailability is per sample, not per feature: a two-stage model whose second stage lacks a diagnostic builds that stage’s dataset with its own available. calibrate_threshold Machine-independent source calibrate_threshold(model, dataset, split, *, partition='validation', output='score', quantile=0.99, name=None, mask=None, population=None) Set a decision threshold on a per-sample model output from one partition. The second half of a two-stage detector: a score is only an event candidate once a threshold, fixed on data the network did not train on, has been applied. Attach the result with model.with_calibration(result); predict then reports <name>_exceeds for every sample. NameTypeUnitDescription modelModelArtifact-Trained or loaded model. datasetDatasetArtifact-Data with the model’s input shape. splitSplit-Group assignment selecting the partition. partitionstr, optional-Partition the quantile is taken over. outputstr, optional-Per-sample scalar output to threshold. quantilefloat, optional-Quantile of that output on the partition, in (0, 1). namestr or None, optional-Calibration name; output when None. maskarray_like of bool or None, optional-Further restricts the population within the partition – a second stage calibrated only on the first stage’s candidates. populationstr or None, optional-Description of mask stored with the result, e.g. "stage1_exceeds". Returns —CalibrationResultanyThreshold with the partition, population, quantile, sample count and groups it was set on. Raises ModelContractError When the output is not a per-sample scalar, the population is empty, quantile is outside (0, 1), mask is given without a population description, the dataset’s columns differ from the model’s, or the partition holds groups the model was fitted on – a model scores its own training samples in-sample (a k-NN against themselves), so that threshold would be too low; use TrainingResult.train_scores for a training-population statistic. Defaults · Applicability Defaults quantile = 0.99 is numerical convenience; a detector’s quantile is a task decision (the VEST IRE prototype used 0.85-0.90). Applicability Machine-independent. dataset_fingerprint Machine-independent source dataset_fingerprint(dataset) SHA-256 content fingerprint of a dataset. Two datasets share a fingerprint only when their spec, feature schema, inputs, targets, groups and per-sample metadata are identical in value, dtype and shape. A model records this fingerprint as part of its identity, so “which data trained it” is answerable from the artifact alone. NameTypeUnitDescription datasetDatasetArtifact-The dataset to fingerprint; its own fingerprint field is ignored. Returns —str-64-character lowercase hex digest. Processing steps · Applicability Processing steps Hash the canonical JSON of the spec (and the feature spec, if any). Hash inputs, targets, string group labels, the availability mask (when one is set) and each sample_meta array in sorted key order, each prefixed by its name, dtype and shape. Applicability Machine-independent. evaluate_model Machine-independent source evaluate_model(model, dataset, split, partition='test', *, metrics=None) Standard ML metrics of a model on one partition, overall and per group. This is training evaluation. Whether a model is scientifically valid – campaign robustness, negative controls, cross-diagnostic timing – is a task-specific verdict for vaft.validation, not a number here. NameTypeUnitDescription modelModelArtifact-Trained or loaded model. datasetDatasetArtifact-Data with the model’s input shape. splitSplit-Group assignment selecting the partition. partitionstr, optional-Partition to evaluate. metricscallable or None, optional-Task metrics, metrics(outputs, subset) returning a mapping of names to floats, where outputs are the model outputs and subset the DatasetArtifact of the evaluated samples; evaluated overall and per group, and merged into the built-in metrics. Returns —EvaluationResultanyAggregate and per-group metrics over the available samples: mse, rmse, mae and r2 in target units for a supervised model; score_mean, score_median, score_p95 (normalised units for an autoencoder, the detector’s own for a score model) and, for an autoencoder, reconstruction_mse in input units. Raises ModelContractError When the partition holds groups the model was fitted on (other than evaluating the training partition itself, which reports training metrics), or the dataset’s columns differ from the model’s. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. export_model Machine-independent source export_model(model, directory, *, format='onnx') Export the network to an inference format and prove it agrees. The training artifact and the deployment artifact need not be the same thing: a model trained in PyTorch can be served by ONNX Runtime. The export is accepted only after the exported graph reproduces the source model on a probe batch. NameTypeUnitDescription modelModelArtifact-Trained or loaded model. directorystr or path-like-Output directory; must not exist or be empty. formatstr, optional-Target format; "onnx" is the only one implemented. Returns —dict-Export record written to export.json: format, opset, parity difference and tolerance, runtimes, and the source model identity. Raises ModelContractError When the backend cannot export to format or the parity check fails. BackendUnavailableError When the exporter or runtime is not installed. Output semantics · Applicability · Provenance Output semantics The exported graph maps normalised inputs to normalised outputs; normalization.npz is written beside it and must be applied around it, exactly as predict does. A sklearn one-class SVM’s graph returns scores, the estimator’s decision function; the model’s score is its negative. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, section 12: training and inference artifacts are separate, with numerical validation between them. fetch_model Machine-independent source fetch_model(name, *, version=None, stage=None, registry=None, cache=None, env=None) Download a published model’s release assets into the cache, verified. The registry checkout says which files a version is (their hashes); the GitHub Release holds the bytes. This copies the bytes into the cache and accepts them only if they are exactly the files the registry pins. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Registry model name. versionstr or None, optional-Exact version; give this or stage. stagestr or None, optional-Lifecycle alias, resolved to an exact version first. registrystr or path-like or None, optional-vaft-nn checkout; $VAFT_NN_HOME when None. cachestr or path-like or None, optional-Artifact cache root; $VAFT_NN_CACHE, else the platform cache directory. envmapping or None, optional-Environment to read the variables from; os.environ when None. Returns —ModelIdentity-The identity resolve_model returns for the fetched version. Raises ModelResolutionError When gh is missing or cannot read the release, or a downloaded file is missing or differs from the registry manifest; the cache is then left as it was. Processing steps · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Resolve the exact version and its manifest from the registry. Download the release <name>-v<version> (or the tag the registry records) with gh release download into a temporary directory inside the cache root; the repository is the registry checkout’s GitHub origin. Verify every file the registry manifest lists, then replace <cache>/<name>/<version> with the verified directory. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Needs the GitHub CLI logged in to an account that can read the private repository; VAFT reads no token itself. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, sections 10 and 13: weights are release artifacts outside git history, verified against the registry on resolution. load_dataset Machine-independent source load_dataset(directory) Load a dataset written by save_dataset, verifying its fingerprint. NameTypeUnitDescription directorystr or path-like-Directory holding arrays.npz and dataset.json. Returns —DatasetArtifact-The dataset, a FeatureDataset when one was saved. Raises ModelContractError When the files are missing or the recomputed fingerprint differs from the recorded one – the arrays changed after they were saved. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. load_model Machine-independent source load_model(name, *, version=None, stage=None, registry=None, cache=None, env=None, fetch=False) Resolve a published model and load it, ready for predict. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Registry model name. versionstr or None, optional-Exact version; give this or stage. stagestr or None, optional-Lifecycle alias such as "production". registrystr or path-like or None, optional-vaft-nn checkout; $VAFT_NN_HOME when None. cachestr or path-like or None, optional-Artifact cache root; $VAFT_NN_CACHE, else the platform cache directory. envmapping or None, optional-Environment to read the variables from. fetchbool, optional-On a cache miss or mismatch, run fetch_model and retry. Returns —ModelArtifact or ModelBundle-The model (or bundle of models), carrying the identity resolve_model returned. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. load_model_artifact Machine-independent source load_model_artifact(directory, *, manifest=None, verify=True) Load an artifact directory, verifying every file against its manifest. NameTypeUnitDescription directorystr or path-like-Directory holding the weights and normalisation files. manifeststr or path-like or None, optional-Manifest to trust; directory/manifest.json when None. The resolver passes the registry’s reviewed copy here, so a tampered cache cannot vouch for itself. verifybool, optional-Check the SHA-256 and size of every file before loading. Returns —ModelArtifact-The model with an identity naming the directory, version and manifest hash. Raises ModelResolutionError When the manifest is missing or a file is missing or differs. ModelContractError When the manifest’s schema version is not one this VAFT reads. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, section 13: resolution verifies identity, version and artifact hash. load_model_bundle Machine-independent source load_model_bundle(directory, *, manifest=None, verify=True) Load a bundle directory, verifying every file and member manifest. NameTypeUnitDescription directorystr or path-like-Directory holding the bundle’s files. manifeststr or path-like or None, optional-Bundle manifest to trust; directory/manifest.json when None. The resolver passes the registry’s reviewed copy. verifybool, optional-Check every file’s SHA-256 and size first. Returns —ModelBundle-The members, each with an identity naming the bundle, and the composition record. Raises ModelResolutionError When a file is missing or differs, or a member manifest differs from the hash the bundle pins. ModelContractError When the manifest is not a bundle manifest this VAFT reads. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. predict Machine-independent source predict(model, data) Run a model on new data and stamp the result with its exact identity. Accepts a dataset (checked against the model’s feature schema) or a bare array. The result records the model’s immutable identity – name, exact version, manifest and weight hashes – never an alias such as production, so a stored result keeps meaning what it meant when it was produced. NameTypeUnitDescription modelModelArtifact-Trained, loaded or resolved model. dataDatasetArtifact or array_likeanyInputs of shape (n, *model.input_shape). Returns —InferenceResultanyOutputs aligned with the samples (prediction; reconstruction and a per-sample score; or score alone; plus <name>_exceeds for every calibration and, for a dataset with an availability mask, available), the model identity, and the groups and per-sample metadata of a dataset input. Raises ModelContractError When the input shape, or a dataset’s column names, differ from the model’s. Output semantics · Applicability Output semantics prediction and reconstruction are in the units of the targets and inputs; an autoencoder’s score is the mean squared reconstruction error in the model’s normalised units, and a score model’s is the detector’s own anomaly measure (larger is more anomalous). An unavailable sample has NaN outputs and exceeds no threshold: missing data is not “no anomaly”. A score or an exceedance is a model output, not a physical event: an IRE-like candidate, never a reconnection onset (#669 section 16). Applicability Machine-independent. register_architecture Machine-independent source register_architecture(name, factory, *, kind, backend='torch') Make a task-defined network available to a backend by name. Task code (the SXR reconstruction transformer, a sequence model) defines its network next to its science and registers it here; a ModelSpec then selects it with architecture=name. The factory is called only when a model is built, so registering imports no ML framework. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Architecture name a ModelSpec refers to. factorycallable-factory(spec, input_shape, output_shape) returning a network that maps a batch of shape (n, *input_shape) to (n, *output_shape) without flattening it first. kind{"supervised", "reconstruction", "score"}-What the network learns. backendstr, optional-Backend the factory builds for; only "torch" accepts registrations. Returns —None-The architecture is registered for this process. Raises ModelContractError On an unknown kind, a backend that does not accept registrations, a name that shadows a built-in, or a second registration of one name with a different factory. Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The registry is per process. A published model records its architecture’s name, not its code; loading it needs the same task module imported, and the code version is traced through the VAFT revision in the manifest. register_augmentation Machine-independent source register_augmentation(name, function) Make a train-time augmentation available by name. Selected with TrainingConfig(augmentation=name). It is applied to the train partition only, once per epoch, after the group split – so an augmented copy of a sample can never reach validation or test. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Augmentation name. functioncallable-function(inputs, targets, rng) returning (inputs, targets) of the same shapes, in physical (un-normalised) units; targets is None for an unsupervised model and rng is a seeded numpy.random.Generator. Returns —None-The augmentation is registered for this process. Raises ModelContractError On a name already registered with a different function. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. register_loss Machine-independent source register_loss(name, factory) Make a task-defined training loss available by name. Selected with ModelSpec(hyperparameters={"loss": name}). The factory receives the model spec and the train-partition normalisation, so a physics loss – a line-of-sight residual through a projector acting on emissivity in physical units – can undo the normalisation the network works in. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Loss name. factorycallable-factory(spec, normalization) returning loss(prediction, target, inputs), a differentiable scalar in the backend’s tensor type. prediction, target and inputs are normalised and keep their sample shapes; normalization maps input_mean, input_std and, for a supervised model, target_mean and target_std to NumPy arrays that broadcast against one sample. Returns —None-The loss is registered for this process. Raises ModelContractError On a name that is already registered with a different factory, or that shadows the built-in "mse". Applicability · Limitations Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations Only the iterative torch backend trains with a loss; the closed-form and scikit-learn backends refuse a loss hyperparameter. resolve_model Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source resolve_model(name, *, version=None, stage=None, registry=None, cache=None, env=None) Resolve a published model to one exact, hash-verified local version. NameTypeUnitDescription namestr-Registry model name, e.g. "ire_ae_vaft_v1". versionstr or None, optional-Exact version; give this or stage. stagestr or None, optional-Lifecycle alias such as "production", resolved to an exact version before anything is loaded. registrystr or path-like or None, optional-vaft-nn checkout; $VAFT_NN_HOME when None. cachestr or path-like or None, optional-Artifact cache root; $VAFT_NN_CACHE, else the platform cache directory. envmapping or None, optional-Environment to read the two variables from; os.environ when None. Returns —ModelIdentity-Name, exact version, manifest SHA-256, requested stage, lifecycle status and the verified artifact directory (source). Convention A stage alias is mutable and a version is not. The returned identity always carries the exact version and manifest hash; stage only records what was asked for. Raises ModelResolutionError When the registry, model, version, stage, manifest or a cached file is missing, or a hash differs from the one the registry pins. ModelContractError When both or neither of version and stage are given. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Read models/<name>/releases.yaml from the registry. Map stage to its version, or take version; refuse a stage that points at a deprecated version. Check the registry manifest’s SHA-256 against the pinned one. Check every file the manifest lists in <cache>/<name>/<version>/ for presence, size and SHA-256. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, sections 9 and 13: lifecycle aliases resolve to immutable artifacts, and resolution verifies the hash. save_dataset Machine-independent source save_dataset(dataset, directory) Materialise a dataset on disk so training can run elsewhere. Building a corpus-scale dataset (reading thousands of shots) and training on it are separate steps, often on separate machines; this is the hand-off. NameTypeUnitDescription datasetDatasetArtifact-Fingerprinted dataset from build_dataset. directorystr or path-like-Target directory; must not exist or be empty. Returns —str-The dataset fingerprint, which load_dataset re-checks. Raises ModelContractError When the dataset has no fingerprint, the directory is not empty, or an array has dtype object. Applicability Applicability Machine-independent. save_model_artifact Machine-independent source save_model_artifact(model, directory, *, version, model_card=None, applicability=None) Write a model as an immutable, hash-pinned artifact directory. The directory is what gets attached to a vaft-nn release; its manifest.json is what gets committed to the registry. NameTypeUnitDescription modelModelArtifact-Trained model; model.name must be lower_snake_case. directorystr or path-like-Target directory; must not exist or be empty. versionstr-Semantic version of this artifact, e.g. "0.1.0". model_cardmapping or None, optional-Intended use, training population, validation evidence and known limits, stored in the manifest. applicabilitymapping or None, optional-The input domain the model was trained and validated on (parameter ranges, shot ranges, diagnostics), stored in the manifest. Returns —ModelArtifact-The same model carrying its saved identity: version, manifest SHA-256 and weight SHA-256. Raises ModelContractError On an invalid name or version, or a non-empty target directory. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Write the backend weights and the normalisation moments. Hash each file and write manifest.json (sorted keys, two-space indent) pinning every hash and size. Hash the manifest; that hash is the artifact’s identity. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, sections 10-11: the vaft-nn release layout and manifest contract. save_model_bundle Machine-independent source save_model_bundle(bundle, directory, *, version, model_card=None, applicability=None) Write a multi-model bundle as one immutable, hash-pinned release. NameTypeUnitDescription bundleModelBundle-Members by role and the composition record. directorystr or path-like-Target directory; must not exist or be empty. versionstr-Semantic version shared by the bundle and every member. model_cardmapping or None, optional-Intended use, population, validation evidence and limits. applicabilitymapping or None, optional-Input domain the bundle was trained and validated on. Returns —ModelBundle-The bundle carrying its saved identity; every member carries its own identity and the bundle’s. Raises ModelContractError On an invalid bundle or member name or version, or a non-empty directory. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Write each member as an ordinary artifact whose file names are prefixed by its role. Write manifest.json with kind: "bundle", every file’s SHA-256 and size, each member manifest’s SHA-256 and the composition record. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#973, section 24: one logical model release may contain two fitted stage artifacts. split_groups Machine-independent source split_groups(groups, spec=None) Assign independent groups to train/validation/test partitions. Splits the groups – never the samples – so correlated samples of one shot or one simulation case can never sit on both sides of a holdout. Do this on the record-level data, before any windowing or augmentation; the returned Split then applies unchanged to everything derived. NameTypeUnitDescription groupsarray_like or DatasetArtifact-Group label of every sample, or a dataset whose groups are used. specSplitSpec or None, optional-Partition fractions (of groups), seed and pinned groups; None uses 70/15/15 with seed 0. Returns —Split-Group-to-partition assignment. Raises ModelContractError When a pinned group is absent, or when there are fewer groups than partitions with a positive fraction. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Take the unique groups as strings, sorted, so the result depends on the set of groups and the seed only – not on sample order. Assign the groups spec.fixed pins. With method="permutation", permute the remaining groups with numpy.random.default_rng(seed) and cut the permutation at the cumulative fractions, rounding so every partition with a positive fraction receives at least one group. With method="hash", map each group to u = int(sha256("seed:group")) / 2**256 in [0, 1) and place it in the partition whose cumulative-fraction interval holds u; no partition is guaranteed a group. Defaults The 70/15/15 fractions are numerical convenience, the same shares the VEST IRE prototype used [ire]. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance S. Kaufman, S. Rosset, C. Perlich, O. Stitelman, “Leakage in data mining: formulation, detection, and avoidance”, ACM TKDD 6, 15 (2012). VEST IRE two-stage anomaly-detection notebook (v4), shot-level split; reviewed in issue #669 section 15A. train_model Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source train_model(dataset, split, model_spec, config=None, *, name=None, train_mask=None, train_mask_record=None) Train a model on the train partition and package it with its provenance. The one training entry point for every backend and architecture. What comes back is a ModelArtifact, not a framework object: its trained state is opaque bytes and everything that identifies it – data, split, configuration, software – travels with it. NameTypeUnitDescription datasetDatasetArtifact-Fingerprinted training data from build_dataset. splitSplit-Group assignment from split_groups, made before any windowing. model_specModelSpec-Backend, architecture, task and hyperparameters. configTrainingConfig or None, optional-Optimisation, normalisation and augmentation settings; None uses the defaults. namestr or None, optional-Model name used when publishing; model_spec.task when None. train_maskarray_like of bool or None, optional-Per-sample mask further restricting the fitted samples within the train partition – training-set cleaning; None keeps them all. train_mask_recordmapping or None, optional-How train_mask was made (method, threshold, source model), stored in the provenance next to the kept and removed counts. Returns —TrainingResult-The artifact, the per-epoch history, the split, the epoch whose weights were kept, the fitted sample indices and, for a score model that can leave a sample out (k-NN), the leave-self-out training scores. Convention Normalisation is a z-score, (x - mean) / std, with a constant element given std = 1; the reconstruction score of an autoencoder is measured in these normalised units. A score model’s score is larger for more anomalous samples. Raises ModelContractError When the dataset has no fingerprint, a group is missing from the split, no sample is left to fit, a supervised architecture has no targets, or a named augmentation or loss is not registered. BackendUnavailableError When the backend’s framework is not installed. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Select the fitted samples: train partition, available, and train_mask; select the available validation samples. Compute input (and target) normalisation moments on the fitted samples only, per element or pooled over config.normalize_axes. Fit the backend on the normalised arrays; a reconstruction architecture learns to reproduce its input. A registered augmentation is applied to the fitted samples only, once per epoch. The validation loss drives early stopping and the best epoch’s weights are kept. Record dataset fingerprint and spec, split groups, the train-mask record, model spec, configuration, software revision and runtimes, and the loss history. Defaults The TrainingConfig defaults (Adam, learning rate 1e-3, batch 64, patience 10, per-element normalisation) are numerical convenience, not tuned for any task. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance VEST-Tokamak/vaft#669, sections 6 and 7: training as a VAFT processing stage, dataset provenance as part of model identity. window_dataset Machine-independent source window_dataset(dataset, window, step, *, target_mode=None) Cut sliding windows that never cross a group boundary. Turns a record-level dataset – samples in time order, one row per time point – into a window dataset for a sequence model or a feature extractor. NameTypeUnitDescription datasetDatasetArtifact-Record-level samples in time order within each group. windowint-Samples per window. stepint-Samples between consecutive window starts. target_mode{"window", "last", "none"} or None, optional-What each window’s target is: the target rows over the window, the target at its last sample, or none; None is "window" for a dataset with targets and "none" otherwise. Returns —DatasetArtifact-Inputs of shape (n_windows, window, *input_shape); groups repeated per window; sample_meta carries each window’s window_start and window_stop source indices and, for every per-sample array of the source, its value at the window’s first sample. Raises ModelContractError When window or step is not a positive integer, or a target mode asks for targets the dataset does not have. Processing steps · Input semantics · Output semantics · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Find the maximal contiguous runs of one group label. Within each run, start a window every step samples while a full window fits; a shorter tail is dropped. Recompute the fingerprint of the result. Input semantics One row per sample time, grouped and time-ordered within each group. Output semantics One row per window. The group of every window is the group of all of its samples, so a Split made on the source applies unchanged. A window is available only when every sample in it is. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance S. Kaufman et al., “Leakage in data mining”, ACM TKDD 6, 15 (2012): windows from one unit on both sides of a holdout leak.

/vaft/develop/reference/process/transien.title: Process reference: transients
/vaft/develop/reference/process/transien.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.transients: 2 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("transients.<name>") prints.
