All process categories Overview A current quench and the brief rise of current that can precede it are the two features of a plasma-current record a transient-event analysis starts from. Everything here measures them – times, rates, amplitudes – on a (time, current) pair and knows nothing about the machine that produced it. SymbolMeaningUnit ttimes I_pplasma current, as storedA I_refreference current the fractions are taken ofA t_80, t_20last 80 % and first 20 % crossings of the quenchs dI/dtrate of change of the current magnitudeA/s Numbers, not names. A quench found here is a fall of the current magnitude through two fractions of a reference; a spike is a short positive excursion above the local trend. Neither is called an internal reconnection event or a disruption: that is a classification, and it needs evidence – the magnetic fluctuation, the radiation, the position – that a current record alone does not carry. The sign of the stored current is removed. Every quantity is measured on polarity * I_p, where polarity is the sign of the current at its largest magnitude, and the polarity is returned, so a machine that stores a negative current gets the same numbers as one that stores a positive one. Absence is an answer. A record with no quench, or no spike above its own noise, returns a result whose measured fields are None and whose reason says why, never the record bounds or its loudest noise sample. Functions current_quenchTime a current quench between 80 % and 20 % of a reference current, and its fastest fall. Convention current_spikeMeasure a short positive rise of the current magnitude above its trend, before a quench. Convention No function matches. current_quench Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source current_quench(time, ip, *, window=None, reference_current=None, smoothing_s=None) Time a current quench between 80 % and 20 % of a reference current, and its fastest fall. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesStrictly increasing sample times. iparray_likeAPlasma current, either sign. windowsequence of float, optionals(start, stop) the search is restricted to. reference_currentfloat, optionalACurrent the fractions are taken of; default the largest magnitude in the window. smoothing_sfloat, optionalsWidth of a quadratic Savitzky-Golay window the rate is taken with; None takes centred differences of the record as it is. Returns —CurrentQuench-The reference current in amperes, the 80 % and 20 % crossing times, their separation and its extrapolation to a full quench in seconds, the most negative rate of change of the current magnitude in amperes per second and when it occurred, the polarity, and reason when nothing was measured. Convention Measured on the magnitude. didt_min is the most negative rate of the polarity-corrected current, so a falling current reads negative whichever sign the machine stores. The rate is searched between the two crossings only, so the sharp fall at the end of a spike before the 80 % crossing is not mistaken for the quench rate. extrapolated_quench_time is duration_80_20 / 0.6, the ITPA convention for the time a linear quench would take from 100 % to zero. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Restrict to the window and flip the record to positive polarity. Take the reference current, and the time of the largest magnitude. Find the first sample after that time below 20 % of the reference, and the last sample before it at or above 80 %; interpolate both crossings. With no sample at or above 80 % in between – a reference_current above the peak divided by 0.8 – stop with a reason. Differentiate the magnitude – centred differences, or a quadratic Savitzky-Golay derivative over smoothing_s – and take its minimum between the two crossings. Defaults The 80 % and 20 % fractions are the conventional ITPA disruption-database values. With no reference_current the largest magnitude in the window is used, a numerical convenience. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations The default reference is the largest magnitude, so a spike on the flat top raises it and moves both crossings slightly earlier; pass reference_current to use a plateau value instead. Only the first fall through 20 % after the largest magnitude is timed. A spike inside the quench still contributes the fall that ends it, which can be several times the mean quench rate; time_didt_min says where the minimum was, and current_spike with before= set past it measures the spike. The raw derivative of a noisy record is dominated by the noise; smoothing_s exists for that, and assumes uniform sampling (it uses the median step). Provenance A. Savitzky and M. J. E. Golay, Anal. Chem. 36 (1964) 1627, as implemented by scipy.signal.savgol_filter: the smoothed rate. current_spike Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source current_spike(time, ip, *, before=None, lookback_s=0.002, trend_s=0.0005, n_sigma=5.0) Measure a short positive rise of the current magnitude above its trend, before a quench. NameTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesStrictly increasing sample times. iparray_likeAPlasma current, either sign. beforefloat, optionalsEnd of the search; default the quench’s 80 % crossing from current_quench. lookback_sfloat, optionalsLength of the search window ending at before. trend_sfloat, optionalsWidth of the centred median filter that defines the trend. n_sigmafloat, optional-Robust standard deviations of the residual a spike must exceed. Returns —CurrentSpike-The time of the largest excursion in seconds, its height above the trend in amperes and as a fraction of the trend current, the trend current and the noise’s robust sigma in amperes, the search end, the polarity, and reason when nothing qualified. Convention Positive on the magnitude. A spike is a rise of the polarity-corrected current, so on a machine that stores a negative current it is a more negative excursion of the stored value. Its amplitude is reported positive. Processing steps · Defaults · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Flip the record to positive polarity. Take before as given, or the 80 % crossing of the quench; with neither, stop with a reason. Median-filter the magnitude over trend_s and subtract it: an excursion shorter than half that width survives in the residual, the trend does not. Within [before - lookback_s, before] take the largest residual above the residual’s median, and the noise as the robust sigma of the first differences over the same samples divided by the square root of two. Accept it only above n_sigma robust sigmas. Defaults lookback_s = 2 ms and trend_s = 0.5 ms are empirical, a numerical convenience sized for sub-millisecond excursions on a current that changes over milliseconds, as in a small tokamak; a longer discharge wants both scaled. n_sigma = 5 is a numerical convenience that keeps the largest of a few hundred Gaussian residual samples below the threshold. Applicability Machine-independent. Limitations One spike: the largest excursion in the window. An excursion longer than half of trend_s is absorbed into the trend and not reported. Pickup from a coil switching at the same time looks identical in a current record; nothing here can tell them apart. Provenance

/vaft/develop/reference/process/field_li.title: Process reference: field_line_topology
/vaft/develop/reference/process/field_li.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.process.field_line_topology: 10 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.process.describe("field_line_topology.<name>") prints. All process categories Overview A field-line tracer answers where does a line launched here go, and how far does it travel before it hits something. Turning that into a picture of where the heat lands needs a model, and the model here is deliberately a crude one: an upstream channel width in normalized flux, the projection of the field onto the target, and a parallel-loss weight. It models no cross-field transport, no radiation, no detachment, no sheath, and no self-consistent scrape-off layer. So the result is relative and has no heat-flux units. It says which part of a target is hit harder than which other part, and how the targets compare with each other. It does not say how many watts. Nothing here reads a file. The arrays come from vaft.data.flare_products, and the IDS stand-ins they are written into are in vaft.machine_mapping.field_line_topology. SymbolMeaningUnit Aarea of one target surface elementm^2 psi_Nnormalized poloidal flux, 1 on the separatrix- psi_N,minthe deepest flux surface a traced line reached- lambda_psiupstream channel width, in psi_N- alphaangle between the field line and the target surfacedeg L_cconnection length of a field line, reduced over its two w_psiupstream channel weight exp(-max(psi_N,min - psi_sep, 0)/lambda_psi)- w_Lparallel-loss weight, inverse or exponential in L_c/L_0- qthe proxy, w_psi |sin alpha| w_L- The proxy is a surface density, and the cell areas are what integrates it. q stands in for the heat flux arriving per unit target area, so the incident total on a target is sum(q A) – and the areas enter there and nowhere else. The donor implementation instead multiplied q by 1/A, a “hit density” borrowed from FLARE’s own strike-density task. That factor belongs there and not here: a strike density counts lines launched elsewhere and landing on a cell, whereas a footprint grid launches exactly one line from every node, so 1/A carries no strike information at all. It is the Jacobian of the launch lattice – on a grid uniform in toroidal angle and distance along the target it is exactly proportional to 1/R – and carrying it makes the per-target total proportional to the node count the caller chose. See footprint_incident_total. A missing incidence column is not an incidence of ninety degrees. FLARE writes alphaS only when the tracing task was asked for it, and the committed reference footprint does not have it. Omitting the factor is a legitimate choice; making it silently is not, so footprint_heat_load_proxy takes the angles as a required argument whose None is the explicit opt-out, and records which it was. A tracer reports two directions, and reducing them is part of the model. The shortest connection length and the total are different quantities, and the donor used the shortest while calling the result Lc. So footprint_heat_load_proxy takes both directions and reduces them itself, by the rule FootprintProxyModel.connection_length_reduction names – a caller cannot hand it an already-reduced array and have the wrong reduction labelled with a model that did not produce it. The flux is always the deepest incursion, the smaller of the two, because that is the surface the upstream channel weight is asking about; the model’s describe() says so, so the choice reaches the IDS provenance too. Functions connection_length_weightParallel-loss weight from a field line’s connection length. Convention footprint_heat_load_proxyA relative heat-load proxy over a divertor target’s footprint grid. Convention footprint_incident_totalThe proxy integrated over one target. Convention footprint_proxy_modelOne named footprint proxy model. incidence_factorThe projection of a field line onto the surface it strikes. Convention reduce_traced_directionsReduce a quantity traced in both directions to one value per line. Convention target_incident_fractionsEach target’s share of the proxy incident on all of them. Convention toroidal_surface_cell_areasArea of every quadrilateral cell of a surface mesh in (R, z, phi). Convention toroidal_surface_node_areasArea each node of a surface mesh represents, as a dual cell. Convention upstream_flux_weightExponential upstream heat-channel weight in normalized flux. Convention No function matches. connection_length_weight Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source connection_length_weight(length, *, scale, form) Parallel-loss weight from a field line’s connection length. NameTypeUnitDescription lengtharray_likemConnection length per line; negative entries are treated as zero, and non-finite ones are given zero weight. scalefloatmThe length the weight is measured against; must be positive. formstrn/a"inverse" for 1 / (1 + L / L_0), "exponential" for exp(-L / L_0), "none" for a flat one. Returns —ndarray-Weights in [0, 1]. Convention A longer line is weighted less: the length stands in for how much of the flux tube’s content was lost on the way. The two forms are empirical and disagree by construction – the inverse one keeps a long line at a small but finite weight, the exponential one takes it to zero – so which is used is part of the model, never a default. Raises ValueError scale is not positive, or form is not one of CONNECTION_LENGTH_FORMS. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance the donor’s connection_length_weight, whose "exp_loss" is this "exponential". footprint_heat_load_proxy Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source footprint_heat_load_proxy(*, min_psi_norm_backward, min_psi_norm_forward, connection_length_backward, connection_length_forward, area, incidence_angle_deg, model) A relative heat-load proxy over a divertor target’s footprint grid. NameTypeUnitDescription min_psi_norm_backwardarray_like-Deepest normalized flux each line reached tracing one way. min_psi_norm_forwardarray_like-The same tracing the other way; the two are reduced to the deeper incursion, which is the surface the channel weight asks about. connection_length_backwardarray_likemLength each line ran before it stopped, one way. connection_length_forwardarray_likemThe same the other way; the two are reduced by FootprintProxyModel.connection_length_reduction, so the shortest and the total cannot be confused for one another. areaarray_likem^2Surface area each sample represents, from toroidal_surface_node_areas or toroidal_surface_cell_areas; carried through so an integral needs nothing else. incidence_angle_degarray_like or NonedegAngle between each line and the target, as FLARE’s alphaS reports it. None is the explicit opt-out, recorded on the result – there is no implicit one. modelFootprintProxyModeln/aA named preset; see footprint_proxy_model. Required, because every coefficient in it is a modelling choice. Returns —FootprintProxy-The proxy and its three factors, all on the caller’s grid. Convention The proxy is a density and area is only its measure – it is not a factor. Multiplying by 1/area, as the donor did, imposes the launch lattice’s own Jacobian on the map and makes the per-target total scale with the node count; see this module’s Conventions. Both directions are required rather than one reduced array, because the reduction is part of the model and a pre-reduced input would let the wrong one be labelled with a model that did not produce it. Raises ValueError The arrays disagree in shape. Processing steps · Output semantics · Assumptions · Applicability · Limitations · Provenance Processing steps Reduce each line’s two traced directions: the flux to the deeper incursion, the length by the model’s own rule. w_psi from upstream_flux_weight. |sin alpha| from incidence_factor, or ones when the caller opted out – and the opt-out is recorded either way. w_L from connection_length_weight. Their product, which is the proxy. Output semantics A relative surface density, in no unit. Only ratios within one run and between targets of the same run mean anything; two runs are comparable only if they used the same model and the same tracing limits. Assumptions One traced line per grid sample, launched from the target – which is how FLARE’s equi2d_footprint_grid builds a footprint grid. A product whose lines were launched upstream and counted where they land is a strike density and is a different quantity. Applicability Machine-independent. Any target whose footprint was sampled by field-line tracing; the model’s coefficients are not. Limitations No cross-field transport, radiation, detachment, sheath physics or self-consistent scrape-off layer. The result has no heat-flux units and must not be converted into any. Provenance the donor’s compute_heat_flux_proxy. footprint_incident_total Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source footprint_incident_total(proxy) The proxy integrated over one target. NameTypeUnitDescription proxyFootprintProxy-As footprint_heat_load_proxy returns it. Returns —float-sum(density * area), in the proxy’s own relative scale. Convention This is a Riemann sum over the sample areas, so it converges as the grid is refined – which is the property a fraction between targets needs, and the one the legacy’s extra 1/area factor destroyed. With it the sum reduces to sum(w), which grows roughly with the number of samples the caller chose to trace rather than settling on the target’s own value. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Non-finite samples are skipped rather than propagated: a line the tracer could not follow contributes nothing, and one NaN would otherwise erase the target. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance the donor’s summarize_heat_flux_proxy, whose integral column is this same sum – taken over a density that carried an extra 1/area factor, which is what reduced it to the bare sum of the weights. footprint_proxy_model Machine-independent source footprint_proxy_model(name) One named footprint proxy model. NameTypeUnitDescription namestrn/aA key of FOOTPRINT_PROXY_MODELS. Returns —FootprintProxyModeln/aThe preset, which is frozen and safe to share. Raises KeyError No model carries that name; the message lists the ones that do. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance the donor’s FootprintProxyConfig, whose field defaults these presets carry as named values. incidence_factor Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source incidence_factor(angle_deg) The projection of a field line onto the surface it strikes. NameTypeUnitDescription angle_degarray_likedegAngle between the field line and the target surface, as FLARE’s alphaS reports it. Returns —ndarray-|sin alpha|, in [0, 1]. Convention The angle is measured from the surface, not from its normal, so a grazing line has a small angle and a small factor. That is FLARE’s own definition: alphaS = asin(|b.n| / |b|), which makes |sin alpha| the projection exactly rather than an approximation of it. A line that never struck the boundary is written as zero by the tracer and so receives zero weight, which is the right answer for a different reason – it deposits nothing because it does not arrive. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance FLARE/src/fortran/tasks/fieldline_connection.f90:158. the donor’s incidence_factor, which returned ones when the column was absent; see footprint_heat_load_proxy. reduce_traced_directions Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source reduce_traced_directions(backward, forward, *, how) Reduce a quantity traced in both directions to one value per line. NameTypeUnitDescription backwardarray_likeanyThe value the tracer reported going one way. forwardarray_likeanyThe value it reported going the other. howstrn/a"shortest" takes the smaller magnitude, "total" the sum, "deepest" the smaller signed value. Returns —ndarrayanyOne value per line, in the inputs’ own unit. Convention "shortest" compares magnitudes, because a tracer may report a backward length as negative; "deepest" compares signed values, because a flux label that ran further inward is genuinely smaller. Non-finite entries propagate rather than being skipped: a direction the tracer could not follow leaves the reduction undefined, and that is the honest answer for that line. Raises ValueError The arrays disagree in shape, or how is none of the three. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance FLARE/src/fortran/tasks/fieldline_connection.f90:90-96, whose own Lc = Lc_bwd + Lc_fwd, Lcs = min(Lc_bwd, Lc_fwd) and minPsiN = min(minPsiN_bwd, minPsiN_fwd) are these three reductions. FLARE’s arclengths are non-negative, so its plain min and the magnitude comparison here agree on its own output. target_incident_fractions Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source target_incident_fractions(totals) Each target’s share of the proxy incident on all of them. NameTypeUnitDescription totalsmapping of str to float-Per-target integrals, from footprint_incident_total; each must be finite and not negative. Returns —dict of str to float-The same keys, each divided by the sum over all of them, so the values add to one. Convention The denominator is the total over the targets in this mapping, so the fraction says what it says only if that set is every target the run covered. A fraction over a subset is a fraction of the subset. Raises ValueError totals is empty, an entry is negative or not finite, or they sum to zero – in which case there is no share to take, and returning equal shares would invent one. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance The IMAS stand-in decided on vaft#1099 (2026-09-21): the proxy integrated over each target, divided by the total over all targets, written to divertors.divertor[].target[].power_incident_fraction because it is dimensionless and so is the proxy. toroidal_surface_cell_areas Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source toroidal_surface_cell_areas(r, z, phi_deg) Area of every quadrilateral cell of a surface mesh in (R, z, phi). NameTypeUnitDescription rarray_likemNode major radius, shape (n_v, n_u). zarray_likemNode height, same shape. phi_degarray_likedegNode toroidal angle, same shape. Returns —ndarraym^2Cell areas, shape (n_v - 1, n_u - 1). Convention Node order is [i_v, i_u], the order FLARE’s own mesh files lay their values out in – see vaft.data.flare_products.FlareMesh.node_shape. Cell [j, i] is bounded by nodes [j, i], [j, i+1], [j+1, i+1] and [j+1, i]. Raises ValueError The three arrays disagree in shape, or the mesh is not two dimensional with at least two nodes on each axis. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps The nodes are placed in Cartesian space, and each cell is split along the diagonal from [j, i+1] to [j+1, i] into two triangles whose areas are summed. No small-angle expansion is taken, so the result is exact for a flat quadrilateral. A cell that is not flat has two diagonals that give slightly different answers, and this is the one FLARE splits along – which is why the two agree to parts in a trillion rather than merely closely. Applicability Machine-independent. Any surface described by node positions in cylindrical coordinates; nothing here is specific to a divertor target. Provenance moose/src/fortran/geometry/hypermesh3d.f90:563, the same two-triangle construction FLARE uses for the area column of its strike-density product. toroidal_surface_node_areas Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source toroidal_surface_node_areas(r, z, phi_deg) Area each node of a surface mesh represents, as a dual cell. NameTypeUnitDescription rarray_likemNode major radius, shape (n_v, n_u). zarray_likemNode height, same shape. phi_degarray_likedegNode toroidal angle, same shape. Returns —ndarraym^2Node areas, shape (n_v, n_u), summing to the total surface area Convention Node order is [i_v, i_u], as toroidal_surface_cell_areas. Raises ValueError As toroidal_surface_cell_areas. Processing steps · Applicability · Provenance Processing steps Each cell’s area is split equally between its four corners. A corner node therefore receives a quarter of one cell, an edge node a quarter of two, and an interior node a quarter of four – so the node areas sum to the surface area exactly, which is what makes an integral over them the same integral whether the values sit on nodes or on cells. Applicability Machine-independent. Provenance The donor’s footprint_cell_areas built the same quantity from midpoint axis widths and R dphi ds, which assumes the second axis is parameterized by its own arc length. This form reads the arc from the node positions instead, so a target curve whose parameter is not arc length is measured rather than assumed. upstream_flux_weight Machine-independentConvention-sensitive source upstream_flux_weight(psi_norm, *, separatrix_flux, decay_width, clip_inside=True) Exponential upstream heat-channel weight in normalized flux. NameTypeUnitDescription psi_normarray_like-The flux label each field line is weighted by – for a connection product, the deepest normalized flux it reached. separatrix_fluxfloat-Where the channel starts, normally 1. decay_widthfloat-e-folding width of the channel, in the same normalized flux; must be positive. clip_insidebool, optionaln/aWhether a line that reached inside separatrix_flux is given the full weight rather than one growing exponentially. True clips Returns —ndarray-Weights in (0, 1] when clipped, unbounded above otherwise. Convention psi_norm increases outward, so a line that stayed further out is weighted less. With clip_inside false the weight grows without bound inside the separatrix, which is the model being read outside the region it describes; it is offered because a caller comparing against the unclipped legacy form needs it, not because it is ever the better choice. Raises ValueError decay_width is not positive. Applicability · Provenance Applicability Machine-independent. The channel is an upstream scrape-off-layer width, so the weight is meaningful only for lines that reach the plasma edge. Provenance the donor’s upstream_psi_weight.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/geometry.title: Formula reference: geometry
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/geometry.body:
Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.geometry: 12 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("geometry.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview Also the canonical slab field configurations: a Harris current sheet and an X-point, in the same slab frame. The reductions plasma theory uses between a real torus and an analytic model, kept apart along two independent axes: the geometry (slab, cylindrical, toroidal) and the ordering (local versus global; large aspect ratio $\epsilon = a/R_0 \ll 1$). A slab can carry $q$, $\hat s$, $R_0$ or a $1/R_0$ curvature inherited from a torus and still be a slab; large aspect ratio is an ordering, not a geometry. The guide page Geometric approximations sets out what each representation retains and neglects. SymbolMeaningUnit x, y, zslab coordinates -- radial, binormal, parallelm rminor radius of the cylinderm thetapoloidal anglerad R0major radius the torus is straightened atm qsafety factor- s_hatmagnetic shear r q'/q- L_sshear length of a sheared slab, signedm m, npoloidal and toroidal mode numbers- k_y, k_zslab wavenumbers1/m k_parparallel wavenumber k.B/B1/m acurrent-sheet half-thicknessm Perturbations are $e^{i(m	heta - n\phi)}$ as in vaft.formula.stability.helical_phase: both mode numbers positive, the helicity in the minus sign; $q$ is a magnitude and $\hat s$ keeps the sign of $d|q|/dr$, so reversed shear flips the sign of $L_s$. A sheared slab is $\mathbf B = B_0(\hat{\mathbf z} + (x/L_s)\hat{\mathbf y})$ with $z$ along the field at $x = 0$. The local slab of a cylinder at $r_0$ is that field-aligned frame: $z$ along $\mathbf B(r_0)$, $y$ the binormal in the surface, $x = r - r_0$. There the harmonic has $k_y = m/r_0$ and $k_z = (m - nq_0)/(q_0R_0)$, zero on a rational surface; along the straightened torus ($z = R_0\phi$) it would be $-n/R_0$ instead. Positive shear makes $L_s = -q_0R_0/\hat s$ negative in that frame. Functions cylindrical_parallel_wavenumberParallel wavenumber of an $m/n$ harmonic on a cylindrical surface of safety factor $q$. Convention cylindrical_poloidal_fieldPoloidal field of a straight current column by Ampère’s law. Convention cylindrical_safety_factor_from_r_BSafety factor of a straight cylinder standing in for a torus. Convention harris_sheet_current_densityCurrent density of a Harris current sheet, from Ampere’s law. Convention harris_sheet_fieldReconnecting field of a Harris current sheet. Convention local_slab_from_cylinderThe field-aligned sheared slab of a cylinder at $r_0$: $(k_y, L_s, k_z)$ of an $m/n$ harmonic. Convention peaked_current_safety_factorCylindrical $q$ profile of the peaked current $j \propto (1 - x^2)^
u$. Convention shear_length_from_q_R0_sMagnitude of the shear length a torus or cylinder gives its local slab. Convention sheared_slab_fieldMagnetic field of the sheared slab at radial position $x$. Convention sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumberParallel wavenumber across a sheared slab, to first order in $x/L_s$. Convention slab_parallel_wavenumberComponent of a wavevector along the magnetic field. Convention x_point_fluxFlux function of a current-free magnetic X-point. Convention No function matches. cylindrical_parallel_wavenumber Convention-sensitive source cylindrical_parallel_wavenumber(m_pol, n_tor, q, R0) Parallel wavenumber of an $m/n$ harmonic on a cylindrical surface of safety factor $q$. \[k_\parallel =  rac{m - nq}{qR_0}\] NameTypeUnitDescription m_polint-Poloidal mode number. n_torint-Toroidal mode number. qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor of the surface. R0floatmMajor radius the cylinder is straightened at. Returns —float or np.ndarray1/m$k_\parallel$; zero exactly where $q = m/n$. Convention The harmonic is $e^{i(m	heta - n\phi)}$ (helical_phase) with $z = R_0\phi$, and $B \simeq B_z$ ($B_	heta \ll B_z$). $q$ is the positive magnitude, as the mode numbers are: a negative $q$ from a COCOS sign never reaches $m/n$. With $q$ rising outward, $k_\parallel$ falls through zero at the rational surface. Raises ValueError A mode number is not positive, or q is zero. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The resonance condition in wave-number form: the perturbation is constant along field lines where $q(r_s) = m/n$, and a rational surface is the place $k_\parallel = 0$. Assumptions Cylinder, large aspect ratio: $B_	heta/B_z = r/(qR_0) \ll 1$. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.4. cylindrical_poloidal_field Convention-sensitive source cylindrical_poloidal_field(r, I_enclosed) Poloidal field of a straight current column by Ampère’s law. \[B_	heta(r) =  rac{\mu_0 I(r)}{2\pi r}\] NameTypeUnitDescription rfloat or np.ndarraymMinor radius, positive. I_enclosedfloat or np.ndarrayAAxial current inside radius $r$. Returns —float or np.ndarrayT$B_	heta$. Convention $B_	heta$ has the sign of the enclosed current along $+z$, right-handed about it. Exact for a cylindrically symmetric current distribution. Raises ValueError r is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Only the current inside $r$ sets the field at $r$: a centrally peaked current makes $B_	heta$ rise fast and then fall as $1/r$, which is what shapes $q(r)$. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.3. cylindrical_safety_factor_from_r_B Convention-sensitive source cylindrical_safety_factor_from_r_B(r, B_theta, B_z, R0) Safety factor of a straight cylinder standing in for a torus. \[q(r) =  rac{r B_z}{R_0 B_	heta}\] NameTypeUnitDescription rfloat or np.ndarraymMinor radius. B_thetafloat or np.ndarrayTPoloidal (azimuthal) field at $r$. B_zfloat or np.ndarrayTAxial field, the stand-in for $B_\phi$. R0floatmMajor radius the torus is straightened at; the cylinder has length $2\pi R_0$. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$q(r)$. Convention $z = R_0\phi$ and $B_z \leftrightarrow B_\phi$: the field-line pitch $d\phi/d	heta$ of the torus becomes $dz/(R_0 d	heta)$. Signs follow the fields; take magnitudes for the usual positive $q$. Raises ValueError B_theta is zero somewhere. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Toroidal transits per poloidal transit. It is the leading $O(1)$ limit of the toroidal $q$ under $\epsilon = a/R_0 \ll 1$: no $1/R$ variation, no shaping, no Shafranov shift. Assumptions A periodic cylinder; a screw pinch has the same $q$ with $R_0$ set by the imposed period. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.3. J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), Ch. 11 (screw pinch). harris_sheet_current_density Convention-sensitive source harris_sheet_current_density(x, B0, a) Current density of a Harris current sheet, from Ampere’s law. \[J_z(x) =  rac{1}{\mu_0} rac{dB_y}{dx} =  rac{B_0}{\mu_0 a}\,\mathrm{sech}^2 rac{x}{a}\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymDistance from the sheet centre, along its normal. B0floatTAsymptotic reconnecting field, signed. afloatmSheet half-thickness, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayA/m^2$J_z$. Convention Right-handed $(x, y, z)$ with $\mu_0\mathbf J = 
abla	imes\mathbf B$, so $\mu_0J_z = \partial_xB_y$: $B_0 > 0$ ($B_y$ along $+y$ above the sheet) gives current along $+z$. The sheet carries $2B_0/\mu_0$ per unit length in $y$. Raises ValueError a is not positive and finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The field reversal of harris_sheet_field and a localized current are the same object: the current is confined to $|x| \lesssim a$, where the field changes sign. Assumptions As harris_sheet_field; displacement current neglected. References E. G. Harris, Nuovo Cimento 23, 115 (1962). D. Biskamp, Magnetic Reconnection in Plasmas, Cambridge University Press (2000), Sec. 3.1. harris_sheet_field Convention-sensitive source harris_sheet_field(x, B0, a) Reconnecting field of a Harris current sheet. \[B_y(x) = B_0	anh rac{x}{a}\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymDistance from the sheet centre, along its normal. B0floatTAsymptotic reconnecting field, signed. afloatmSheet half-thickness, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayT$B_y$. Convention Slab frame of sheared_slab_field: $x$ the sheet normal, $y$ the reconnecting direction, $z$ the current (and guide-field) direction; $B_y(-x) = -B_y(x)$. A guide field $B_g\hat{\mathbf z}$ adds without changing $J_z$ (harris_sheet_current_density). Raises ValueError a is not positive and finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The field reverses across a layer of thickness $\sim 2a$; for $|x| \ll a$ it is the sheared slab with $B_y’ = B_0/a$ and no guide field. In the original Harris equilibrium the magnetic pressure is balanced by a plasma pressure $\propto \mathrm{sech}^2(x/a)$. Assumptions One-dimensional, $\partial_y = \partial_z = 0$; the profile, not the kinetic (drifting-Maxwellian) closure that makes it an exact Vlasov equilibrium. References E. G. Harris, Nuovo Cimento 23, 115 (1962). D. Biskamp, Magnetic Reconnection in Plasmas, Cambridge University Press (2000), Sec. 3.1. local_slab_from_cylinder Convention-sensitive source local_slab_from_cylinder(m_pol, n_tor, r_0, R0, q_0, s_hat) The field-aligned sheared slab of a cylinder at $r_0$: $(k_y, L_s, k_z)$ of an $m/n$ harmonic. \[k_y =  rac{m}{r_0},\qquad L_s = - rac{q_0 R_0}{\hat s},\qquad k_z =  rac{m - nq_0}{q_0R_0}\] NameTypeUnitDescription m_polint-Poloidal mode number. n_torint-Toroidal mode number. r_0floatmRadius of the reference surface. R0floatmMajor radius. q_0float-Safety factor at $r_0$, a positive magnitude. s_hatfloat-Magnetic shear at $r_0$. Returns k_yfloat1/mBinormal wavenumber $m/r_0$. L_sfloatmSigned shear length of the local slab. k_zfloat1/mWavenumber along the field at $r_0$; zero when $q_0 = m/n$. Convention $x = r - r_0$; $z$ along $\mathbf B(r_0)$ and $y$ the binormal in the surface, the frame of sheared_slab_field, so sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumber(x, *local_slab_from_cylinder(...)) is the cylinder’s $k_\parallel$ to first order in $x$. The harmonic is $e^{i(m	heta - n\phi)}$; its wavenumber along the straightened torus ($z = R_0\phi$) would be $-n/R_0$, which is not this $k_z$. With $\hat s > 0$ the field line, followed in $z$, drifts to $-y$ faster on the outer surfaces, which makes $L_s$ negative in this frame. Raises ValueError A mode number is not positive, r_0, R0 or q_0 is not positive, or s_hat is zero. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The bridge from global mode numbers to local wavenumbers: on a rational surface $q_0 = m/n$ gives $k_z = 0$, and the shear becomes $k_\parallel’ = k_y/L_s = -k_y\hat s/(q_0R_0)$. Assumptions Locality $|x| \ll r_0$ with $q \simeq q_0 + q_0’x$; large aspect ratio ($B_	heta \ll B_z$). The same slab follows from a toroidal equilibrium by a local expansion, without the cylinder in between. References H. P. Furth, J. Killeen and M. N. Rosenbluth, Phys. Fluids 6 (1963) 459. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 6.8. peaked_current_safety_factor Convention-sensitive source peaked_current_safety_factor(x, q_a, nu) Cylindrical $q$ profile of the peaked current $j \propto (1 - x^2)^
u$. \[q(x) =  rac{q_a\,x^2}{1 - (1 - x^2)^{
u + 1}},\qquad q(0) =  rac{q_a}{
u + 1}\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarray-Normalised minor radius $r/a$, in $[0, 1]$. q_afloat-Edge safety factor $q(a)$. nufloat-Current peaking exponent, non-negative; $
u = 0$ is a flat current. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$q(x)$, rising from $q_a/(
u + 1)$ on axis to $q_a$ at the edge. Convention The enclosed current is $I(x) = I_a[1 - (1 - x^2)^{
u+1}]$; with cylindrical_poloidal_field and cylindrical_safety_factor_from_r_B this is $q = rB_z/(R_0B_	heta)$. The axis value is the limit $x 	o 0$. Raises ValueError x lies outside $[0, 1]$, q_a is not positive or nu is negative. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The more peaked the current (larger $
u$), the lower $q$ on axis and the stronger the shear outside: $q_a/q_0 = 
u + 1$ is fixed by the peaking alone. Assumptions Cylinder, large aspect ratio, the standard model profile; not a reconstructed equilibrium. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.3 and 6.8 (the profile used for tearing and kink examples). shear_length_from_q_R0_s Convention-sensitive source shear_length_from_q_R0_s(q, R0, s_hat) Magnitude of the shear length a torus or cylinder gives its local slab. \[L_s =  rac{q R_0}{|\hat s|}\] NameTypeUnitDescription qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor at the reference surface. R0floatmMajor radius. s_hatfloat or np.ndarray-Magnetic shear $\hat s = (r/q)\,dq/dr$, for example shear_from_r_q. Returns —float or np.ndarraym $ L_s $, the distance across the surfaces at which the field tilts by $B_y/B_z = 1$ in the local slab. Convention Unsigned: magnitudes of $q$ and $\hat s$, whatever sign a COCOS gives them. The sign a slab needs depends on how its $y$ is oriented, see local_slab_from_cylinder for VAFT’s. Raises ValueError s_hat is zero. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Short $L_s$ means strong shear: a mode stays field-aligned over a thinner layer. Local turbulence and drift-wave models keep this tokamak coefficient while discarding the rest of the geometry. Assumptions Large aspect ratio and a locality $ x \ll r$ around the surface. References W. Horton, Rev. Mod. Phys. 71 (1999) 735, Sec. II. sheared_slab_field Convention-sensitive source sheared_slab_field(x, B0, L_s) Magnetic field of the sheared slab at radial position $x$. \[\mathbf B = B_0\left(\hat{\mathbf z} +  rac{x}{L_s}\,\hat{\mathbf y}ight)\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymDistance from the reference surface. B0floatTField along $z$, the field direction at $x = 0$. L_sfloatmSigned shear length. Returns —np.ndarrayT$(B_x, B_y, B_z)$, last axis of length 3. Convention $x$ radial, $y$ binormal, $z$ along the field at $x = 0$. The sign of L_s is the sign of the field-line tilt $dB_y/dx$; the slab reached from a positive-shear cylinder by local_slab_from_cylinder has $L_s < 0$. Raises ValueError L_s is zero or not finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The field direction rotates with $x$ while its magnitude stays $B_0$ to first order: magnetic shear without curvature. It is the local model of the region around a rational surface. Assumptions $|x| \ll |L_s|$, so $|\mathbf B| \simeq B_0$; no curvature, no equilibrium gradient in the field strength. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 8.3. sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumber Convention-sensitive source sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumber(x, k_y, L_s, k_z=0.0) Parallel wavenumber across a sheared slab, to first order in $x/L_s$. \[k_\parallel(x) = k_z + k_y\, rac{x}{L_s}\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymDistance from the reference surface. k_yfloat1/mBinormal wavenumber. L_sfloatmSigned shear length, as in sheared_slab_field. k_zfloat1/mWavenumber along the field at $x = 0$; zero when $x = 0$ is the resonant surface. Returns —float or np.ndarray1/m$k_\parallel$. Convention The field of sheared_slab_field; slab_parallel_wavenumber of that field to first order. With $k_z = 0$ the resonance $k_\parallel = 0$ is at $x = 0$ and $k_\parallel’ = k_y/L_s$. Raises ValueError L_s is zero or not finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation A perturbation is field-aligned only on one surface; away from it, $|k_\parallel|$ grows linearly, which is what localises tearing layers, drift waves and ballooning-type modes around rational surfaces. Assumptions $ x \ll L_s $, dropping the $O(x^2/L_s^2)$ change of $ \mathbf B $. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 8.3. slab_parallel_wavenumber Convention-sensitive source slab_parallel_wavenumber(k, B) Component of a wavevector along the magnetic field. \[k_\parallel =  rac{\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|}\] NameTypeUnitDescription karray_like1/mWavevector $(k_x, k_y, k_z)$, last axis of length 3. Barray_likeTMagnetic field at the same point, last axis of length 3. Returns —float or np.ndarray1/mParallel wavenumber, signed along $\mathbf B$. Convention Signed: positive when $\mathbf k$ has a component along $\mathbf B$. In a straight slab $\mathbf B = B_0\hat{\mathbf z}$ it is $k_z$; neither curvature nor shear enters unless the field carries them. Raises ValueError A vector is not 3-dimensional or $ \mathbf B = 0$. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation How fast a perturbation varies along field lines. Electrons stream along $\mathbf B$, so modes with $k_\parallel 	o 0$ – flute-like, field-aligned – are the ones that escape parallel damping. References F. F. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion, 3rd ed., Springer (2016), Ch. 4. x_point_flux Convention-sensitive source x_point_flux(x, y, B_prime) Flux function of a current-free magnetic X-point. \[\psi(x, y) =  rac{B'}{2}\left(x^2 - y^2ight),\qquad \mathbf B_\perp = \hat{\mathbf z}	imes
abla\psi = B'\,(y, x)\] NameTypeUnitDescription xfloat or np.ndarraymCoordinate along the inflow (sheet normal) direction. yfloat or np.ndarraymCoordinate along the outflow direction. B_primefloatT/mField gradient $B’$, non-zero. Returns —float or np.ndarrayT m$\psi$; in-plane field lines lie on its contours. Convention The same $\mathbf B_\perp = \hat{\mathbf z}	imes
abla\psi$ as slab_perturbed_flux: along the inflow axis $B_y = B’x$ reverses across $x = 0$ as in a current sheet, along the outflow axis $B_x = B’y$. The separatrices are $y = \pm x$, the contour $\psi = 0$ through the X-point. Raises ValueError B_prime is zero or not finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The lowest-order field about a null: four branches meeting at the X-point, $
abla^2\psi = 0$ so no current. A current along $z$ at the null changes the separatrix angle away from $90^\circ$ (collapse towards a sheet). Near each X-point of a tearing island the flux of slab_perturbed_flux has this saddle form. Assumptions Two-dimensional, $\partial_z = 0$; expansion to second order about the null, valid for $|x|, |y|$ small against the scale of the surrounding field. References E. R. Priest and T. G. Forbes, Magnetic Reconnection, Cambridge University Press (2000), Sec. 2.1.

/vaft/develop/reference/geometric-approx.title: Geometric approximations
/vaft/develop/reference/geometric-approx.body: Analytic tokamak theory seldom works in the real torus. It works in a slab, a cylinder or an expanded torus, and it carries a few coefficients over from the real equilibrium. This page sets out those reductions using the literature’s names. The formulas are in vaft.formula.geometry. The toroidal parent geometry itself (flux surfaces, the Shafranov shift, shaping, $q$ as a winding number, and $\theta$ versus $\theta^*$) is drawn in the tokamak-geometry section of Scientific diagrams. How VAFT keeps coordinates, projections, representations, derived quantities and solver conventions of one real equilibrium apart is on Equilibrium representations. Two axes, not one hierarchy Geometry says what space the model lives in: slab, cylindrical or toroidal. Ordering says which scales are assumed small: local ($|x| \ll r$), large aspect ratio ($\epsilon = a/R_0 \ll 1$) or neither (global). The two are independent. A slab may carry $q$, $\hat s$, $R_0$ or a $1/R_0$ curvature inherited from a torus and still be a slab. Large aspect ratio is an ordering, not a geometry: some large-aspect-ratio theories stay toroidal. Representation Geometry Typical ordering Retained Neglected or parameterized straight slab slab local local gradients, wave propagation curvature, magnetic shear sheared slab slab local local gradients, magnetic shear, resonance global geometry; curvature unless added curved slab slab local shear plus a prescribed curvature, e.g. $1/R_0$ global toroidal geometry cylindrical tokamak cylindrical large aspect ratio, leading order radial structure, current profile, $q(r)$, rational surfaces toroidicity, shaping large-aspect-ratio torus toroidal $\epsilon \ll 1$ selected $O(\epsilon)$ toroidal corrections higher orders in $\epsilon$ general axisymmetric torus toroidal global shaping, curvature, toroidal coupling nothing geometric Conventions used throughout Perturbations are $e^{i(m\theta - n\phi)}$, as in vaft.formula.helical_phase. Both mode numbers are positive and the helicity is in the minus sign. $q$ is a magnitude, whatever sign a COCOS gives it. $\hat s$ keeps the sign of $d|q|/dr$: reversed shear ($\hat s < 0$) flips the sign of $L_s$. A torus is straightened at $R_0$ with $z = R_0\phi$ and $B_z \leftrightarrow B_\phi$. Along that $z$, the harmonic has wavenumber $-n/R_0$. A sheared slab is $\mathbf B = B_0(\hat{\mathbf z} + (x/L_s)\hat{\mathbf y})$, with $z$ along the field at $x = 0$ and $y$ the binormal in the surface. This field-aligned $z$ is not the straightened-torus $z = R_0\phi$. The local slab of a surface $r_0$ is that frame, with $x = r - r_0$. There the harmonic has: $k_y = m/r_0$; $k_z = (m - nq_0)/(q_0R_0)$, which is zero on a rational surface; $L_s$, which is signed: positive shear gives $L_s = -q_0R_0/\hat s < 0$. local_slab_from_cylinder returns $(k_y, L_s, k_z)$ in the order sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumber takes them. shear_length_from_q_R0_s returns the magnitude $qR_0/|\hat s|$. Straight slab Coordinates: $(x, y, z)$: radial, binormal, along $\mathbf B$. Field: $\mathbf B = B_0\hat{\mathbf z}$, uniform. Ordering: local. Gradients are taken over a region small against every equilibrium scale. Formula: $\tilde f \propto e^{i(k_xx + k_yy + k_zz)}$, and $k_\parallel = \mathbf k\cdot\mathbf B/B = k_z$ (slab_parallel_wavenumber). Keeps: wave propagation and local density or temperature gradients. Drops: magnetic curvature and magnetic shear, unless they are added separately. Used for: drift waves, and local dispersion relations before shear or curvature enter. Sheared slab Field: $\mathbf B = B_0(\hat{\mathbf z} + (x/L_s)\hat{\mathbf y})$ (sheared_slab_field), or equivalently $B_y(x) \simeq B_y’x$ near a resonant surface. Shear: $\hat s = (r/q)\,dq/dr$ (vaft.formula.shear_from_r_q). Under the local, large-aspect-ratio ordering, $|L_s| = qR_0/|\hat s|$ (shear_length_from_q_R0_s). Formula: $k_\parallel(x) \simeq k_z + k_y x/L_s$ (sheared_slab_parallel_wavenumber). The perturbation is field-aligned on one surface and $|k_\parallel|$ grows linearly away from it. Keeps: the resonance and its localisation. Drops: global geometry, and curvature unless it is added. Used for: the inner layer of tearing modes (FKR, Rutherford), drift waves with shear, and the local limits of gyrokinetics. Related configurations in the same frame: the reversing field of a Harris current sheet, $B_y = B_0\tanh(x/a)$ (harris_sheet_field, harris_sheet_current_density), whose centre is a sheared slab with $B_y’ = B_0/a$ and no guide field, and the current-free X-point $\psi = B’(x^2 - y^2)/2$ (x_point_flux). These configurations, not geometries, are drawn in the field-configuration section of the diagrams guide. Curved slab Curved slab is a family of local models, not one model. VAFT fixes no closure here: the curvature coefficient is whatever a particular model inherits from its parent torus. Coordinates and field: those of the straight or sheared slab. Curvature: toroidal curvature is added as a parameter, either an effective curvature $\boldsymbol\kappa = \mathbf b\cdot\nabla\mathbf b$ (typically $|\kappa| \simeq 1/R_0$ pointing to the major axis), or an effective gravity $g \sim v_{th}^2/R_0$. Ordering: local. The curvature is a constant coefficient over the region. Keeps: the interchange drive (the pressure gradient against the curvature) and the $\nabla B$ and curvature drifts. Drops: the poloidal variation of curvature (good and bad curvature sides), the geometry of the real flux surfaces, and toroidal mode coupling. Next more realistic model: a local toroidal (flux-tube) model, where $\kappa$ varies along the field line. Used for: interchange and Rayleigh–Taylor analogues, resistive-g modes, and reduced edge and SOL turbulence. Cylinder, screw pinch, cylindrical tokamak Coordinates: $(r, \theta, z)$. Field: $\mathbf B = B_\theta(r)\hat{\boldsymbol\theta} + B_z(r)\hat{\mathbf z}$. Safety factor: $q(r) = rB_z/(R_0B_\theta)$ (cylindrical_safety_factor_from_r_B). Resonance: $k_\parallel = (m - nq)/(qR_0)$ (cylindrical_parallel_wavenumber), so $k_\parallel = 0 \Leftrightarrow q(r_s) = m/n$. The three are related but not synonyms: A straight cylinder is only the coordinate system. A screw pinch is a cylindrical equilibrium with both $B_\theta(r)$ and $B_z(r)$, so its field lines are helices. Pure $\theta$- and $z$-pinches are its limits. A cylindrical (straight) tokamak is a screw pinch that is periodic in $z$ with length $2\pi R_0$ and has $B_z \gg B_\theta$, both taken from a torus. Keeps: radial structure, the current profile, $q(r)$ and rational surfaces. Drops: $1/R$ variation of $B_\phi$, toroidal curvature, inboard/outboard asymmetry, the Shafranov shift, toroidal coupling of harmonics, and shaping. The helical field lines are still curved, which is what drives Suydam interchange. Used for: Newcomb’s equation, the internal kink, the outer tearing problem and $\Delta’$. Large-aspect-ratio ordering For a circular torus $R = R_0 + r\cos\theta$, so \[\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{R_0}\left[1 - \frac{r}{R_0}\cos\theta + O(\epsilon^2)\right],\qquad B_\phi = B_0\frac{R_0}{R} = B_0\left[1 - \frac{r}{R_0}\cos\theta + O(\epsilon^2)\right].\] The second expression is vaft.formula.vacuum_toroidal_field. Worked $O(\epsilon)$ example: toroidal coupling. Any factor of $1/R$ multiplying a harmonic $e^{im\theta}$ creates sidebands: \[\frac{e^{im\theta}}{R} = \frac{1}{R_0}\left[e^{im\theta} - \frac{\epsilon}{2}\left(e^{i(m+1)\theta} + e^{i(m-1)\theta}\right)\right] + O(\epsilon^2),\qquad \epsilon = r/R_0 .\] So in a torus an $m/n$ perturbation drags along $(m \pm 1)/n$ components of relative size $\epsilon/2$. In a cylinder it cannot. The expansion is used in two different ways: Large-aspect-ratio toroidal model. It keeps selected $O(\epsilon)$ terms: curvature; inboard/outboard asymmetry; coupling of $m$ to $m \pm 1$. It is still toroidal. It keeps the $O(\epsilon)$ curvature and $1/R$ terms and drops $O(\epsilon^2)$. The Shafranov shift enters at $O(\epsilon(\beta_p + l_i/2))$ relative to $a$. Shaping is outside the circular expansion used here, although shaped large-aspect-ratio models exist (for example Miller local equilibria). Typical uses are the $s$–$\alpha$ ballooning model, toroidal Alfvén gaps and neoclassical trapping. Cylindrical tokamak limit. It keeps only $O(1)$: $R \simeq R_0$, and the toroidal direction is straightened as $z = R_0\phi$. The cylindrical tokamak is the leading-order limit of the large-aspect-ratio expansion. It is not the same thing as large aspect ratio. Local sheared-slab reduction Near a surface $r_0$, with $x = r - r_0$ and $|x| \ll r_0$, expand $q \simeq q_0 + q_0’x$ and take the field-aligned frame: $z$ along $\mathbf B(r_0)$, $y$ the binormal. The harmonic $e^{i(m\theta - n\phi)}$ has there \[k_y = \frac{m}{r_0},\qquad L_s = -\frac{q_0R_0}{\hat s},\qquad k_z = \frac{m - nq_0}{q_0R_0}\] (local_slab_from_cylinder). Along the straightened torus the same harmonic has $-n/R_0$; along the field it has $k_z$. On a rational surface $q_0 = m/n$, so the resonance $q(r_s) = m/n$ becomes $k_\parallel(0) = k_z = 0$ and the shear becomes $k_\parallel’ = k_y/L_s = -k_y\hat s/(q_0R_0)$. The test suite checks that this slab reproduces the cylinder’s $k_\parallel$ to first order in $x$. A local slab does not need a cylinder as an intermediate step. It can be expanded from a toroidal equilibrium directly. What defines it is locality relative to the equilibrium scale, not large aspect ratio. Turbulence and interchange models often keep toroidal coefficients in a slab, such as $|L_s| \simeq qR_0/|\hat s|$ and, in curved slabs, $\kappa \simeq 1/R_0$. The same field line in each geometry Toroidal Cylindrical Sheared slab Where these lead cylinder / screw pinch -> Newcomb equation, internal kink, outer tearing (Delta') cylinder -> sheared slab -> resistive inner layer: FKR, Rutherford, modified Rutherford straight / sheared / curved slab -> drift waves, interchange, reduced edge turbulence, local gyrokinetics The tearing diagrams (rational_surface, delta_prime, tearing_layer_matching) start from the cylinder and sheared slab described here. The current-sheet, X-point, reconnection and MHD-wave diagrams (current_sheet, x_point, magnetic_reconnection, shear_alfven_wave, mhd_wave_family) use the slab frame of this page. See Scientific diagrams. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Ch. 3, 6 and 8. J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), Ch. 9 and 11. H. P. Furth, J. Killeen and M. N. Rosenbluth, Phys. Fluids 6 (1963) 459. W. Horton, Rev. Mod. Phys. 71 (1999) 735.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/disrupti.title: Formula reference: disruption
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/disrupti.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.disruption: 11 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("disruption.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview The semi-analytic middle layer between detecting a disruption in the data (vaft.process.transients) and simulating one (DREAM-like kinetic or integrated codes): transparent reference models whose assumptions are easy to state. The chain they describe is:: thermal quench (T_e drops) -> resistivity rises -> current quench (L/R) -> induced E_par -> runaway seed (Dreicer) -> avalanche -> RE current Resistivity is spitzer_resistivity_from_T_e_Z_eff_ln_Lambda, the plasma resistance, inductance and L/R time are the startup lumped-circuit relations; they are reused here, not restated. SymbolMeaningUnit n_eelectron densitym^-3 T_eelectron temperatureeV Eparallel electric field, magnitudeV/m E_cConnor-Hastie critical fieldV/m E_DDreicer fieldV/m Z_effeffective ion charge- ln_LambdaCoulomb logarithm (relativistic for E_c, thermal for E_D) [-] L_pplasma self-inductanceH I_pplasma currentA R0major radiusm p_ccritical momentum, in units of m_e c- SI throughout, temperatures in eV. Fields are magnitudes along the current; the induced field has the sign that opposes the current’s decay, so a falling current drives electrons that carry it. Every Coulomb logarithm is an explicit argument – the relativistic one ($\approx 15$-$20$) belongs in $E_c$ and the avalanche rate, the thermal one in $E_D$ and the Dreicer rate; no default is hidden (#1188). Functions avalanche_efolds_from_current_dropNumber of avalanche e-folds a current quench provides, $E \gg E_c$. avalanche_growth_rateRosenbluth–Putvinski avalanche (secondary) growth rate of the runaway density. Convention connor_hastie_critical_fieldConnor–Hastie critical field below which no electron runs away. current_quench_currentExponential (L/R) current quench of the plasma current. dreicer_fieldDreicer field: the drag on a thermal electron. Convention dreicer_generation_rateDreicer (primary) runaway generation rate, Connor–Hastie asymptotic form. Convention inductive_parallel_electric_fieldParallel electric field a changing plasma current induces in the plasma. Convention relativistic_collision_timeCollision time of a relativistic electron, $\tau_c = m_ec/(eE_c)$. runaway_critical_momentumCritical momentum above which an electron runs away, in units of $m_ec$. runaway_current_from_densityCurrent carried by runaway electrons moving at the speed of light. thermal_quench_temperaturePrescribed exponential thermal quench of the electron temperature. No function matches. avalanche_efolds_from_current_drop source avalanche_efolds_from_current_drop(delta_I_p, L_p, R0, Z_eff, ln_Lambda) Number of avalanche e-folds a current quench provides, $E \gg E_c$. \[N = \int\gamma_\mathrm{av}\,dt \simeq \frac{e\,L_p\,\Delta I_p}{2\pi R_0\,m_ec\,\ln\Lambda} \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{3(Z_\mathrm{eff} + 5)}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription delta_I_pfloat or np.ndarrayACurrent lost in the quench, non-negative. L_pfloatHPlasma self-inductance, positive. R0floatmMajor radius, positive. Z_efffloat-Effective ion charge, positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Relativistic Coulomb logarithm, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Number of e-folds; the seed is multiplied by $e^N$. Raises ValueError delta_I_p is negative or another argument is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation $\int E\,dt = L_p\Delta I_p/(2\pi R_0)$ by inductive_parallel_electric_field, and $E_c\tau_c = m_ec/e$, so the $E_c$ dependence cancels: the gain depends on the current and the inductance, not the density. With $L_p \approx \mu_0R_0(\ln(8R_0/a) - 2 + l_i/2)$ this is the familiar $N \propto I_p/(I_A\ln\Lambda)$, $I_A = 4\pi\varepsilon_0m_ec^3/e \approx 17$ kA: a few MA gives tens of e-folds. Assumptions $E \gg E_c$ throughout (the $-1$ in $E/E_c - 1$ dropped), so this is an upper estimate; no runaway current feeding back on $E$; no vessel coupling. References M. N. Rosenbluth and S. V. Putvinski, Nucl. Fusion 37 (1997) 1355. avalanche_growth_rate Convention-sensitive source avalanche_growth_rate(E, E_c, Z_eff, ln_Lambda) Rosenbluth–Putvinski avalanche (secondary) growth rate of the runaway density. \[\gamma_\mathrm{av} = \frac{E/E_c - 1}{\tau_c\ln\Lambda}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{3(Z_\mathrm{eff} + 5)}},\qquad \tau_c = \frac{m_ec}{eE_c},\qquad \frac{dn_\mathrm{RE}}{dt} = \gamma_\mathrm{av}\,n_\mathrm{RE}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Efloat or np.ndarrayV/mParallel electric field, magnitude. E_cfloatV/mCritical field, positive. Z_efffloat-Effective ion charge, positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Relativistic Coulomb logarithm, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarray1/s$\gamma_\mathrm{av}$; zero where $E \le E_c$. Convention $\tau_c$ is derived from $E_c$ (relativistic_collision_time), so the two cannot be passed inconsistently. Raises ValueError E_c, Z_eff or ln_Lambda is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Close collisions of existing runaways knock thermal electrons above $p_c$: exponential growth from any seed, independent of $T_e$. Over a whole current quench it multiplies a seed by avalanche_efolds_from_current_drop e-folds – a few per MA, so a handful at 1 MA but tens at reactor currents, where a tiny seed can end up carrying most of the current. Assumptions The $E \gg E_c$ asymptote of Rosenbluth & Putvinski for a classical, fully ionised plasma: not valid with high-$Z$ impurities or partial screening, which raise the rate, nor with radiation losses. The rate is clipped at zero below $E_c$. References M. N. Rosenbluth and S. V. Putvinski, Nucl. Fusion 37 (1997) 1355. connor_hastie_critical_field source connor_hastie_critical_field(n_e, ln_Lambda) Connor–Hastie critical field below which no electron runs away. \[E_c = \frac{n_e e^3\ln\Lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2 m_e c^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_efloat or np.ndarraym^-3Electron density (free plus bound for a partially ionised plasma), positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Relativistic Coulomb logarithm, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayV/m$E_c$. Raises ValueError n_e or ln_Lambda is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The minimum of the collisional drag on an electron, reached at relativistic speed: below $E_c$ even the fastest electrons slow down. It is the threshold of the avalanche; synchrotron and bremsstrahlung losses and partial screening raise the effective threshold above it. References J. W. Connor and R. J. Hastie, Nucl. Fusion 15 (1975) 415. current_quench_current source current_quench_current(t, I_0, tau_CQ) Exponential (L/R) current quench of the plasma current. \[I_p(t) = I_0\,e^{-t/\tau_\mathrm{CQ}},\quad t \ge 0,\qquad \tau_\mathrm{CQ} = L_p/R_p\] NameTypeUnitDescription tfloat or np.ndarraysTime from the start of the current quench. I_0floatACurrent at the start. tau_CQfloatsL/R time, positive (lr_time_from_L_R). Returns —float or np.ndarrayA$I_p(t)$; $I_0$ for $t < 0$. Raises ValueError tau_CQ is not positive. Assumptions · References Assumptions Constant $L_p$ and $R_p$ – a cold, fixed-temperature plasma with no runaway current and no coupling to the vessel. With $R_p$ rising as the plasma cools, or runaways taking over the current, the decay is not a single exponential; the linear-decay fit used for CQ rates is another reduction. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 7.10. dreicer_field Convention-sensitive source dreicer_field(n_e, T_e, ln_Lambda) Dreicer field: the drag on a thermal electron. \[E_D = \frac{n_e e^3\ln\Lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2 T_e} = E_c\,\frac{m_ec^2}{T_e}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_efloat or np.ndarraym^-3Electron density, positive. T_efloat or np.ndarrayeVElectron temperature, positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Thermal Coulomb logarithm, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayV/m$E_D$. Convention $T_e$ enters as an energy $eT_e$; some texts put $T_e/m_e$ as $v_{te}^2$ with $v_{te} = \sqrt{2T_e/m_e}$, which changes the prefactor by two. This is the form of Connor & Hastie, consistent with $E_D/E_c = m_ec^2/T_e$. Raises ValueError An argument is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation A field $E \gtrsim E_D$ accelerates the bulk; well below it only the tail beyond the critical velocity runs away, at the exponentially small Dreicer rate. Which seed matters depends on the case: the rate is negligible below a few per cent of $E_D$, but a fast current quench can reach $E/E_D \approx 0.01$-$0.02$ at a few eV, where it is not. References H. Dreicer, Phys. Rev. 115 (1959) 238. J. W. Connor and R. J. Hastie, Nucl. Fusion 15 (1975) 415. dreicer_generation_rate Convention-sensitive source dreicer_generation_rate(n_e, T_e, E, Z_eff, ln_Lambda, *, prefactor) Dreicer (primary) runaway generation rate, Connor–Hastie asymptotic form. \[\frac{dn_\mathrm{RE}}{dt} = C\,n_e\nu_{ee}\left(\frac{E_D}{E}\right)^{\frac{3(1+Z)}{16}} \exp\left(-\frac{E_D}{4E} - \sqrt{\frac{(1+Z)E_D}{E}}\right),\qquad \nu_{ee} = \frac{n_ee^4\ln\Lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2m_e^2v_{te}^3}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_efloat or np.ndarraym^-3Electron density, positive. T_efloat or np.ndarrayeVElectron temperature, positive. Efloat or np.ndarrayV/mParallel electric field, magnitude. Z_efffloat-Effective ion charge, positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Thermal Coulomb logarithm, positive. prefactorfloat-The order-unity $C$ of the asymptotic formula, required: fits to kinetic solutions put it between about 0.3 and 1, so there is no canonical default. Returns —float or np.ndarraym^-3 s^-1Primary generation rate; zero where $E \le 0$. Convention $v_{te} = \sqrt{2eT_e/m_e}$; $E_D$ is dreicer_field. The prefactor is an explicit argument because published fits differ by a factor of a few. Raises ValueError A density, temperature, Z_eff or ln_Lambda is not positive. Assumptions · References Assumptions Steady state, $E \ll E_D$ (the asymptotic regime), non-relativistic thermal electrons – the relativistic correction factor $\exp[-(T_e/m_ec^2)(E_D^2/8E^2 + \ldots)]$ of Connor & Hastie is dropped – a classical fully ionised plasma (no partial screening), no hot tail; unreliable above $E/E_D \approx 0.1$. References J. W. Connor and R. J. Hastie, Nucl. Fusion 15 (1975) 415, Eq. (62). L. Hesslow et al., Nucl. Fusion 59 (2019) 084004, Eq. (4) (the form written here). inductive_parallel_electric_field Convention-sensitive source inductive_parallel_electric_field(L_p, dI_p_dt, R0) Parallel electric field a changing plasma current induces in the plasma. \[E_\parallel = -\frac{L_p}{2\pi R_0}\,\frac{dI_p}{dt}\] NameTypeUnitDescription L_pfloatHPlasma self-inductance, positive. dI_p_dtfloat or np.ndarrayA/sRate of change of the plasma current. R0floatmMajor radius, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayV/m$E_\parallel$, positive along the current when it decays. Convention Signed along the current: a decaying current ($dI_p/dt < 0$) gives $E_\parallel > 0$, the field that keeps pushing the current-carrying electrons. The flux linked with the vessel and coils is ignored, so this is the upper estimate an isolated plasma would see. Raises ValueError L_p or R0 is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation The magnetic energy $\tfrac12 L_pI_p^2$ cannot vanish instantly: a fast current quench turns it into a loop voltage $L_p|dI_p/dt|$, which spread over the circumference $2\pi R_0$ is the field that can exceed $E_c$ by orders of magnitude. Assumptions Uniform field over the cross-section; lumped (0-D) inductance. References J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 7.10. relativistic_collision_time source relativistic_collision_time(n_e, ln_Lambda) Collision time of a relativistic electron, $\tau_c = m_ec/(eE_c)$. \[\tau_c = \frac{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2m_e^2c^3}{n_ee^4\ln\Lambda}\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_efloat or np.ndarraym^-3Electron density, positive. ln_Lambdafloat-Relativistic Coulomb logarithm, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrays$\tau_c$. Raises ValueError An argument is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation The time the critical field takes to give an electron momentum $m_ec$; the avalanche grows on $\tau_c\ln\Lambda$. References M. N. Rosenbluth and S. V. Putvinski, Nucl. Fusion 37 (1997) 1355. runaway_critical_momentum source runaway_critical_momentum(E, E_c) Critical momentum above which an electron runs away, in units of $m_ec$. \[p_c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{E/E_c - 1}},\qquad E > E_c\] NameTypeUnitDescription Efloat or np.ndarrayV/mParallel electric field, magnitude. E_cfloat or np.ndarrayV/mCritical field (connor_hastie_critical_field), positive. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$p_c$; inf where $E \le E_c$. Raises ValueError E_c is not positive. Assumptions · References Assumptions A test electron moving along the field with the relativistic drag $\propto 1 + 1/p^2$; pitch-angle scattering (the $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ factor) and radiation raise $p_c$. References B. N. Breizman et al., Nucl. Fusion 59 (2019) 083001, Sec. 2. runaway_current_from_density source runaway_current_from_density(n_RE, area) Current carried by runaway electrons moving at the speed of light. \[I_\mathrm{RE} = e\,c\,n_\mathrm{RE}\,A\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_REfloat or np.ndarraym^-3Runaway-electron density, non-negative. areafloatm^2Poloidal cross-section they occupy, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayA$I_\mathrm{RE}$. Raises ValueError n_RE is negative or area is not positive. Assumptions · References Assumptions Every runaway moves along $\mathbf B$ at $v \simeq c$, uniform over the area; pitch-angle spread lowers the parallel velocity somewhat. References B. N. Breizman et al., Nucl. Fusion 59 (2019) 083001, Sec. 1. thermal_quench_temperature source thermal_quench_temperature(t, T_0, T_final, tau_TQ) Prescribed exponential thermal quench of the electron temperature. \[T_e(t) = T_\mathrm{f} + (T_0 - T_\mathrm{f})\,e^{-t/\tau_\mathrm{TQ}},\quad t \ge 0;\qquad T_e = T_0,\ t < 0\] NameTypeUnitDescription tfloat or np.ndarraysTime from the start of the quench. T_0floateVPre-disruption temperature. T_finalfloateVPost-quench temperature, positive and below T_0. tau_TQfloatsQuench e-folding time, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrayeV$T_e(t)$. Raises ValueError A temperature or tau_TQ is not positive, or T_final > T_0. Assumptions · References Assumptions A prescribed shape, not a transport or radiation calculation: real quenches are often two-stage (a fast conductive drop after stochastisation, then radiative cooling to a few eV) and not exponential. References T. C. Hender et al., Nucl. Fusion 47 (2007) S128, Sec. 3.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/pwi/.title: Formula reference: pwi
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/pwi/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.pwi: 4 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("pwi.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview The small, exactly defined relations the plasma-wall vocabulary rests on – not response data. Reflection and sputtering coefficients depend on projectile, target, energy, angle and surface state, and come from tables or codes (TRIM/SDTrimSP, Eckstein fits); nothing here supplies them. What is here keeps the concepts apart: particle versus energy reflection, reflection versus recycling versus retention, the projectile versus the target species. SymbolMeaningUnit m_1projectile masskg or u m_2target-atom masskg or u R_Nparticle reflection coefficient- R_Eenergy reflection coefficient- E_ssurface binding energy of the targeteV Gammaparticle flux densitym^-2 s^-1 Masses enter only as ratios, so any consistent unit works. Coefficients are per incident particle (R_N) or per unit incident energy (R_E), for one projectile-target pair, energy and angle. Functions binary_collision_energy_transfer_factorLargest fraction of a projectile’s energy one elastic collision can give a target atom. mean_reflected_energy_fractionMean energy of a reflected particle, as a fraction of the incident energy. Convention recycling_coefficientRecycling coefficient: particles returned to the plasma per incident particle. Convention sputtering_threshold_bohdanskyPhysical-sputtering threshold energy, Bohdansky’s empirical fit. Convention No function matches. binary_collision_energy_transfer_factor source binary_collision_energy_transfer_factor(m_1, m_2) Largest fraction of a projectile’s energy one elastic collision can give a target atom. \[\gamma = \frac{4m_1m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription m_1float or np.ndarraykg or uProjectile mass, positive. m_2float or np.ndarraykg or uTarget-atom mass, positive, same unit. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$\gamma \in (0, 1]$, one for equal masses. Raises ValueError A mass is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation A head-on elastic collision transfers $\gamma E$. A light projectile (D on W: $\gamma \approx 0.043$) cannot give a heavy target atom much energy in one collision, which is why light ions sputter heavy targets only well above the surface binding energy – the origin of the high sputtering threshold of tungsten under hydrogen. Assumptions Two-body elastic collision, target initially at rest; exact kinematics. References W. Eckstein, Computer Simulation of Ion-Solid Interactions, Springer (1991), Ch. 2. mean_reflected_energy_fraction Convention-sensitive source mean_reflected_energy_fraction(R_N, R_E) Mean energy of a reflected particle, as a fraction of the incident energy. \[\frac{\langle E_\mathrm{refl}\rangle}{E_\mathrm{in}} = \frac{R_E}{R_N}\] NameTypeUnitDescription R_Nfloat or np.ndarray-Particle reflection coefficient, in (0, 1]. R_Efloat or np.ndarray-Energy reflection coefficient, in [0, R_N]. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$\langle E_\mathrm{refl}\rangle/E_\mathrm{in}$. Convention $R_N$ counts reflected particles per incident particle, $R_E$ reflected energy per incident energy; they are different quantities with different data, and $R_E \le R_N$ because a reflected particle leaves with at most its incident energy. Raises ValueError R_N outside (0, 1] or R_E outside [0, R_N]. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Particle balance and energy balance are not the same bookkeeping: a surface may return most particles ($R_N$ large) while keeping most of their energy ($R_E/R_N$ small), and it is $R_E$, not $R_N$, that enters the power the wall absorbs. References W. Eckstein, Computer Simulation of Ion-Solid Interactions, Springer (1991), Ch. 8. recycling_coefficient Convention-sensitive source recycling_coefficient(Gamma_reflected, Gamma_reemitted, Gamma_incident) Recycling coefficient: particles returned to the plasma per incident particle. \[R = \frac{\Gamma_\mathrm{refl} + \Gamma_\mathrm{re\text{-}em}}{\Gamma_\mathrm{in}},\qquad 1 - R = \frac{\Gamma_\mathrm{retained}}{\Gamma_\mathrm{in}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription Gamma_reflectedfloat or np.ndarraym^-2 s^-1Promptly reflected flux (fast atoms), non-negative. Gamma_reemittedfloat or np.ndarraym^-2 s^-1Flux re-emitted after implantation (thermal atoms and molecules, counted as atoms), non-negative. Gamma_incidentfloat or np.ndarraym^-2 s^-1Incident ion plus atom flux, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$R$; below one while the wall retains, above one while it releases a previous inventory. Convention Counts atoms: a re-emitted D$_2$ molecule is two. Reflection is the prompt part only; recycling includes the delayed re-emission; retention is what neither returns. $R$ is not bounded by one: an outgassing wall returns more than it receives. Raises ValueError A returned flux is negative or Gamma_incident is not positive. References References P. C. Stangeby, The Plasma Boundary of Magnetic Fusion Devices, IOP (2000), Ch. 3. sputtering_threshold_bohdansky Convention-sensitive source sputtering_threshold_bohdansky(E_s, m_1, m_2) Physical-sputtering threshold energy, Bohdansky’s empirical fit. \[E_\mathrm{th} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{E_s}{\gamma(1 - \gamma)}, & m_1/m_2 \le 0.2 \\[1ex] 8E_s\left(\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}\right)^{2/5}, & m_1/m_2 > 0.2 \end{cases},\qquad \gamma = \frac{4m_1m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2}\] NameTypeUnitDescription E_sfloat or np.ndarrayeVSurface binding energy of the target (usually its sublimation energy), supplied by the caller, positive. m_1float or np.ndarraykg or uProjectile mass, positive. m_2float or np.ndarraykg or uTarget-atom mass, positive, same unit. Returns —float or np.ndarrayeVThreshold incident energy, normal incidence. Convention A named empirical model (Bohdansky 1984), not a table: $E_s$ is an input and no material data are built in. Fits of Eckstein and others differ by tens of per cent near threshold; use tabulated thresholds for quantitative work. The two branches do not join exactly: at $m_1/m_2 = 0.2$ the light branch gives $4.05E_s$ and the heavy one $4.20E_s$, a 4 % step. Raises ValueError A mass or E_s is not positive. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation A light projectile cannot sputter by a forward cascade: it is backscattered by a deeper target atom, keeping $(1 - \gamma)E$, and on its way out strikes a surface atom from below, giving it up to $\gamma(1 - \gamma)E$ (binary_collision_energy_transfer_factor for $\gamma$). That must exceed $E_s$: hence $E_s/\gamma(1 - \gamma)$, far above $E_s$ for D on W. References J. Bohdansky, J. Roth and H. L. Bay, J. Appl. Phys. 51 (1980) 2861; J. Bohdansky, Nucl. Instrum. Methods B 2 (1984) 587.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/ripple/.title: Formula reference: ripple
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/ripple/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.ripple: 6 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("ripple.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview Two kinds of relation live here and stay apart: the field – the smooth $1/R$ variation (vaft.formula.vacuum_toroidal_field) plus an $N_\mathrm{TF}$-periodic ripple – and the orbit consequences a trapped particle feels in it: local ripple wells, the ripple-trapped pitch range and the Goldston–White–Boozer stochasticity threshold. All are the standard large-aspect-ratio, small-ripple estimates; none replaces a 3-D field map or orbit following. SymbolMeaningUnit B0field at the magnetic axisT epsiloninverse aspect ratio of the surface, r/R0- thetapoloidal angle from the outboard midplanerad phitoroidal anglerad deltaripple amplitude (Bmax - Bmin)/(Bmax + Bmin)- n_tfnumber of toroidal-field coils- qsafety factor- dq_drradial derivative of q in physical minor radius1/m rhoLarmor radius of the particlem $B = B_0(1 - \epsilon\cos\theta)[1 - \delta\cos(N_\mathrm{TF}\phi + \phi_0)]$, so $\delta$ is the local amplitude of ripple_amplitude exactly (the additive $B_0[1 - \epsilon\cos\theta - \delta\cos(\ldots)]$ agrees to first order). The ripple is a minimum where $N_\mathrm{TF}\phi + \phi_0 = 0$, i.e. between coils for $\phi_0 = 0$ when a coil sits at $\phi = \pi/N_\mathrm{TF}$. $\delta$ is the local amplitude on the surface, not the machine’s maximum. Functions gwb_stochastic_thresholdGoldston–White–Boozer ripple above which banana-tip motion is stochastic. Convention gwb_stochasticity_parameterRipple over its GWB threshold: stochastic banana tips where it exceeds 1. Convention ripple_amplitudeRipple amplitude from the extreme field strengths along the toroidal angle. Convention ripple_trapping_pitch Largest pitch $ v_\parallel/v $ trapped in a ripple well of depth $\delta$. Convention ripple_well_parameterWhether ripple makes local wells along a field line: $\alpha^* < 1$. Convention toroidal_ripple_fieldField strength on a flux surface with toroidicity and TF-coil ripple. Convention No function matches. gwb_stochastic_threshold Convention-sensitive source gwb_stochastic_threshold(epsilon, q, dq_dr, rho, n_tf) Goldston–White–Boozer ripple above which banana-tip motion is stochastic. \[\delta_\mathrm{GWB} = \left(\frac{\epsilon}{\pi N_\mathrm{TF}\,q}\right)^{3/2}\frac{1}{\rho\,q'}\] NameTypeUnitDescription epsilonfloat or np.ndarray-Inverse aspect ratio $r/R_0$ of the surface. qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor, a positive magnitude. dq_drfloat or np.ndarray1/m$dq/dr$ in the physical minor radius, positive magnitude. rhofloat or np.ndarraymLarmor radius $v/\Omega$ with the full speed and the field at the surface, e.g. larmor_radius(q, m, v, B). n_tfint-Number of TF coils. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Threshold ripple $\delta_\mathrm{GWB}$. Convention The ITER Physics Basis form of the GWB criterion: $\rho$ is the gyroradius with the total speed, $q’ = dq/dr$ in metres of minor radius, and the coefficient is exactly the one written (no hidden $O(1)$ factor). Other papers fold factors of order unity into $\rho$ (toroidal vs total field, $v$ vs $v_\perp$); compare thresholds only within one convention. Raises ValueError n_tf is not a positive integer, or q, dq_dr or rho is not positive.
