Physical interpretation · Assumptions · Validity · See Also · References Physical interpretation Each bounce the ripple kicks the banana tip radially by an amount $\propto\delta$; when the kick shifts the tip’s toroidal precession phase by more than about a radian between bounces, successive kicks decorrelate and the tips random-walk out. Larger $\rho$ (faster particles), stronger shear $q’$ and higher $q$ lower the threshold; $\epsilon$ alone raises it, and outer surfaces still go stochastic first because $\delta$ and $q$ grow outward much faster. Assumptions Large aspect ratio, deeply trapped particles, a single $N_\mathrm{TF}$ harmonic, no collisions; an order-of-magnitude threshold, not a loss rate. Validity Orbit-following comparisons find stochastic losses near this threshold to within a factor of order one; use it to flag regimes, not to predict losses. See Also vaft.diagram.stochastic_ripple_orbit : the canonical diagram of this relation. References R. J. Goldston, R. B. White and A. H. Boozer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 47 (1981) 647. ITER Physics Expert Groups, Nucl. Fusion 39 (1999) 2471, Ch. 5. gwb_stochasticity_parameter Convention-sensitive source gwb_stochasticity_parameter(delta, epsilon, q, dq_dr, rho, n_tf) Ripple over its GWB threshold: stochastic banana tips where it exceeds 1. \[S_\mathrm{GWB} = \frac{\delta}{\delta_\mathrm{GWB}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription deltafloat or np.ndarray-Ripple amplitude on the surface. epsilonfloat or np.ndarray-Inverse aspect ratio $r/R_0$. qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor. dq_drfloat or np.ndarray1/m$dq/dr$ in physical minor radius. rhofloat or np.ndarraymLarmor radius, as in gwb_stochastic_threshold. n_tfint-Number of TF coils. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$S_\mathrm{GWB}$. Convention The threshold of gwb_stochastic_threshold with its stated $\rho$ and $q’$ conventions. Raises ValueError As gwb_stochastic_threshold, or delta is negative. Physical interpretation · See Also · References Physical interpretation A regime flag: $S_\mathrm{GWB} > 1$ marks where trapped fast particles of that gyroradius lose their orbits to ripple stochasticity. See Also vaft.diagram.stochastic_ripple_orbit : the canonical diagram of this relation. References R. J. Goldston, R. B. White and A. H. Boozer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 47 (1981) 647. ripple_amplitude Convention-sensitive source ripple_amplitude(B_max, B_min) Ripple amplitude from the extreme field strengths along the toroidal angle. \[\delta = \frac{B_\mathrm{max} - B_\mathrm{min}}{B_\mathrm{max} + B_\mathrm{min}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription B_maxfloat or np.ndarrayT Largest $ B $ along $\phi$ at fixed $(R, Z)$, under a coil. B_minfloat or np.ndarrayT Smallest $ B $ along $\phi$ at the same $(R, Z)$, between coils. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$\delta$, in $[0, 1)$. Convention The half peak-to-peak variation over the mean, so that toroidal_ripple_field has $B_\mathrm{max,min} = \bar B(1 \pm \delta)$. Some machines quote the full peak-to-peak $(B_\mathrm{max} - B_\mathrm{min})/\bar B = 2\delta$. Raises ValueError A field is not positive, or B_min exceeds B_max. Physical interpretation · See Also · References Physical interpretation How deep the toroidal corrugation is at one point; it rises steeply with $R$ towards the coil legs. See Also vaft.diagram.toroidal_field_ripple : the canonical diagram of this relation. References ITER Physics Expert Groups, Nucl. Fusion 39 (1999) 2471, Ch. 5 (ripple definition). ripple_trapping_pitch Convention-sensitive source ripple_trapping_pitch(delta) Largest pitch $ v_\parallel/v $ trapped in a ripple well of depth $\delta$. \[\left|\frac{v_\parallel}{v}\right|_\mathrm{trap} = \sqrt{\frac{2\delta}{1 + \delta}} \simeq \sqrt{2\delta}\] NameTypeUnitDescription deltafloat or np.ndarray-Ripple amplitude, in $[0, 1)$. Returns —float or np.ndarray-Pitch $\xi = v_\parallel/v$ at the well bottom below which a particle cannot climb over the next ripple maximum. Convention Measured at the well bottom $B = \bar B(1 - \delta)$, with the barrier $\bar B(1 + \delta)$; conservation of $\mu$ and energy gives $\xi^2 < 1 - B_\mathrm{min}/B_\mathrm{max}$. Ignores the $1/R$ tilt of the well, which only makes wells shallower (see ripple_well_parameter). Raises ValueError delta lies outside $[0, 1)$. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation Only nearly perpendicular particles – a pitch cone of half-width $\sim\sqrt{2\delta}$, a few per cent – are ripple-trapped; they then drift vertically out of the plasma unless collisions or the well’s end detrap them. Assumptions A well of full depth $2\delta$; $\mu$ and energy conserved. References P. N. Yushmanov, Rev. Plasma Phys. 16 (1990) 117, Sec. 2. ripple_well_parameter Convention-sensitive source ripple_well_parameter(epsilon, theta, q, delta, n_tf) Whether ripple makes local wells along a field line: $\alpha^* < 1$. \[\alpha^* = \frac{\epsilon\,|\sin\theta|}{N_\mathrm{TF}\,q\,\delta}\] NameTypeUnitDescription epsilonfloat or np.ndarray-Inverse aspect ratio of the surface. thetafloat or np.ndarrayradPoloidal angle from the outboard midplane. qfloat or np.ndarray-Safety factor, a positive magnitude. deltafloat or np.ndarray-Ripple amplitude on the surface. n_tfint-Number of TF coils. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$\alpha^*$; ripple wells exist where it is below 1. Convention Along a field line $\phi = q\theta$, so the ripple term of toroidal_ripple_field oscillates with $dB/d\theta \sim N_\mathrm{TF}q\delta B_0$ while the toroidal term’s slope is $\epsilon B_0\sin\theta$; $\alpha^*$ is their ratio. It is zero at the midplanes, where wells always form for any ripple. Raises ValueError n_tf is not a positive integer, or q or delta is not positive. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · See Also · References Physical interpretation Where the fine ripple modulation is steeper than the smooth $1/R$ slope, the field along the line has local minima that can trap particles with small $v_\parallel$ – ripple trapping. Assumptions Large aspect ratio, circular surfaces, $\phi = q\theta$ along the line; a local criterion, not a 3-D field analysis. It is first order in $\epsilon$: for the multiplicative toroidal_ripple_field the ripple slope carries a factor $1 - \epsilon\cos\theta$, and wells form where $\alpha^* < 1 - \epsilon\cos\theta$. See Also vaft.diagram.ripple_well_formation : the canonical diagram of this relation. References P. N. Yushmanov, Rev. Plasma Phys. 16 (1990) 117, Sec. 2. toroidal_ripple_field Convention-sensitive source toroidal_ripple_field(B0, epsilon, theta, delta, n_tf, phi, phase=0.0) Field strength on a flux surface with toroidicity and TF-coil ripple. \[B = B_0\left(1 - \epsilon\cos\theta\right)\left[1 - \delta\cos(N_\mathrm{TF}\phi + \phi_0)\right]\] NameTypeUnitDescription B0floatTField at the magnetic axis. epsilonfloat or np.ndarray-Inverse aspect ratio $r/R_0$ of the surface. thetafloat or np.ndarrayradPoloidal angle from the outboard midplane. deltafloat or np.ndarray-Ripple amplitude on the surface. n_tfint-Number of TF coils. phifloat or np.ndarrayradToroidal angle. phasefloatradToroidal phase $\phi_0$ of the ripple. Returns —float or np.ndarrayT $ B $. Convention $\theta = 0$ outboard, so the $1/R$ term makes the outboard midplane the field minimum; the ripple factor is a minimum where $N_\mathrm{TF}\phi + \phi_0 = 0$. Multiplicative, so $\delta$ is the local ripple_amplitude at every $\theta$; to first order it equals the additive $B_0[1 - \epsilon\cos\theta - \delta\cos(\ldots)]$. With $\delta = 0$ it is the first-order expansion of vacuum_toroidal_field. Raises ValueError n_tf is not a positive integer, or delta or epsilon is negative. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · See Also · References Physical interpretation The smooth $1/R$ mirror that traps bananas, corrugated $N_\mathrm{TF}$ times around the torus by the gaps between discrete coils. Assumptions Large aspect ratio ($\epsilon \ll 1$), small ripple ($\delta \ll \epsilon$ typically), a single $N_\mathrm{TF}$ harmonic; $\delta$ is taken as given on the surface (it grows steeply towards the outboard edge). See Also vaft.diagram.toroidal_field_ripple : the canonical diagram of this relation. References P. N. Yushmanov, Rev. Plasma Phys. 16 (1990) 117, Sec. 1.

/vaft/develop/reference/formula/vde/.title: Formula reference: vde
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/vde/.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.vde: 6 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("vde.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview Generic, model-neutral reference quantities for a VDE – how fast the plasma moves, how fast a conducting wall lets it, and how much and how unevenly the current returns through the wall as halo current. None of them is a VDE model: the hot-VDE edge-current loss, the cold-VDE equilibrium-branch loss and analytic halo-current models are named literature models that belong in their own functions once one is selected (#1042). The disruption chain these couple to – thermal and current quench, runaways – is vaft.formula.disruption; the plain circuit time $L/R$ of a wall element is lr_time_from_L_R. SymbolMeaningUnit ttimes Zvertical position of the current centroidm Z0reference vertical positionm sigmawall electrical conductivityS/m dwall thicknessm bwall minor radiusm mpoloidal mode number of the wall eddy pattern- I_halohalo currentA I_p0pre-disruption plasma currentA Growth rates are local: $\gamma = d\ln|Z - Z_0|/dt$ on whatever interval the caller passes, with no claim that the whole event is exponential. Halo fractions use the peak halo current over the pre-disruption plasma current, the ITER Physics Basis convention. Functions halo_current_fractionHalo-current fraction: peak poloidal halo current over the pre-disruption plasma current. Convention thin_wall_timeResistive time of a thin cylindrical wall, $\tau_w = \mu_0\sigma db$. Convention toroidal_peaking_factorToroidal peaking factor of the halo current: maximum over the toroidal mean. Convention vde_growth_rate Local growth rate of a vertical displacement, $d\ln Z - Z_0 /dt$. Convention vertical_velocityVertical velocity of the current centroid, $dZ/dt$. wall_mode_decay_timeDecay time of a thin wall’s poloidal-harmonic-$m$ eddy current. No function matches. halo_current_fraction Convention-sensitive source halo_current_fraction(I_halo_peak, I_p0) Halo-current fraction: peak poloidal halo current over the pre-disruption plasma current. \[f_\mathrm{halo} = \frac{I_\mathrm{halo}^\mathrm{peak}}{I_{p,0}}\] NameTypeUnitDescription I_halo_peakfloat or np.ndarrayAPeak (toroidally integrated, poloidal) halo current, non-negative. I_p0floatAPlasma current before the disruption, non-zero. Returns —float or np.ndarray-$f_\mathrm{halo}$. Convention Magnitudes; the ITER Physics Basis convention. A characterisation metric, not a halo-current model: it says nothing of the current path, the toroidal asymmetry (toroidal_peaking_factor) or the forces. Raises ValueError I_halo_peak is negative or I_p0 is zero. References References T. C. Hender et al., Nucl. Fusion 47 (2007) S128. thin_wall_time Convention-sensitive source thin_wall_time(sigma, d, b) Resistive time of a thin cylindrical wall, $\tau_w = \mu_0\sigma db$. \[\tau_w = \mu_0\,\sigma\,d\,b\] NameTypeUnitDescription sigmafloat or np.ndarrayS/mWall conductivity, positive. dfloat or np.ndarraymWall thickness, positive and much less than b. bfloat or np.ndarraymWall minor radius, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrays$\tau_w$. Convention The thin-wall time of the resistive-wall-mode literature (Freidberg). The eddy pattern of a poloidal harmonic $m$ decays in $\tau_w/(2m)$ (wall_mode_decay_time); the vertical ($m = 1$) displacement sees $\tau_w/2$ as its eddy time – its growth time is that divided by the stability margin, not equal to it. Some resistive-wall-mode papers call $\mu_0\sigma db/2$ “$\tau_w$”: the definition here is explicit. A real vessel with ports, gaps and several shells has a spectrum of times; its circuit elements’ $L/R$ are lr_time_from_L_R. Raises ValueError An argument is not positive. Assumptions · References Assumptions Axisymmetric, continuous cylindrical shell, $d \ll b$ (thin wall), uniform conductivity. References J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), the resistive-wall chapter. toroidal_peaking_factor Convention-sensitive source toroidal_peaking_factor(j_halo_phi) Toroidal peaking factor of the halo current: maximum over the toroidal mean. \[\mathrm{TPF} = \frac{\max_\phi j_\mathrm{halo}}{\langle j_\mathrm{halo}\rangle_\phi}\] NameTypeUnitDescription j_halo_phinp.ndarrayA or A/m^2Halo current (or current density) at toroidal positions spaced uniformly around the machine, last axis toroidal, non-negative. Returns —float or np.ndarray-TPF, at least one; one for an axisymmetric halo. Convention The samples must be uniform in $\phi$ for the mean to be the toroidal average; with a few discrete sensors TPF is a lower bound on the true peak. The product $f_\mathrm{halo}\cdot\mathrm{TPF}$ is the usual design-load figure. Raises ValueError Fewer than two toroidal samples, a negative sample, or a zero mean. References References T. C. Hender et al., Nucl. Fusion 47 (2007) S128. vde_growth_rate Convention-sensitive source vde_growth_rate(t, Z, Z0) Local growth rate of a vertical displacement, $d\ln Z - Z_0 /dt$. \[\gamma_\mathrm{VDE}(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\ln|\Delta Z|,\qquad \Delta Z = Z - Z_0\] NameTypeUnitDescription tnp.ndarraysTime, increasing. Znp.ndarraymVertical centroid position on t. Z0floatmReference position the displacement is measured from. Returns —np.ndarray1/s$\gamma_\mathrm{VDE}$ on t; NaN where $\Delta Z = 0$ and at its neighbouring samples, which the central difference reaches. Convention A local characterisation: constant only over an interval where the motion really is exponential ($\Delta Z = \Delta Z_0e^{\gamma t}$). A VDE is in general not one exponential – wall-limited growth, then an accelerating cold-VDE drift as the current decays, then wall contact. Raises ValueError t is not increasing or differs in length from Z. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation With a conducting wall the growth is slowed from the Alfvenic ideal rate to a rate set by the wall eddy time (wall_mode_decay_time, $m = 1$) divided by the stability margin; $1/\gamma$ read off a measured displacement says which regime an interval is in. References T. C. Hender et al., Nucl. Fusion 47 (2007) S128. vertical_velocity source vertical_velocity(t, Z) Vertical velocity of the current centroid, $dZ/dt$. \[v_Z = \frac{dZ}{dt}\] NameTypeUnitDescription tnp.ndarraysTime, increasing. Znp.ndarraymVertical centroid position on t. Returns —np.ndarraym/s$v_Z$ on t. Raises ValueError t is not increasing or differs in length from Z. Numerical notes · References Numerical notes Second-order central differences (numpy.gradient), one-sided at the ends; smooth or window a noisy $Z$ first. References T. C. Hender et al., Nucl. Fusion 47 (2007) S128. wall_mode_decay_time source wall_mode_decay_time(tau_w, m) Decay time of a thin wall’s poloidal-harmonic-$m$ eddy current. \[\tau_m = \frac{\tau_w}{2m}\] NameTypeUnitDescription tau_wfloat or np.ndarraysThin-wall time (thin_wall_time), positive. mint-Poloidal harmonic, positive. Returns —float or np.ndarrays$\tau_m$. Raises ValueError tau_w is not positive or m is not a positive integer. Physical interpretation · References Physical interpretation Higher harmonics have shorter current paths per unit flux and decay faster; a vertical displacement is the $m = 1$ pattern. References J. P. Freidberg, Ideal MHD, Cambridge University Press (2014), the resistive-wall chapter.

/vaft/develop/reference/plot/.title: Plot reference
/vaft/develop/reference/plot/.body: Generated from vaft.plot.registry by python -m vaft.plot.docs_catalog: 155 registered plots over 41 subjects, plus 21 other plotting functions. Each entry is a record of vaft.plot.available_plots(); nothing on this page is written by hand. A plot’s identity is subject / view / quantity: the subject is what it shows physically, the view is the kind of figure (time, profile, field, …), and the quantity picks one of several when a subject has more than one. From data, draw a plot with its vaft.omas.plot_<name> adapter; the renderer vaft.plot.<name> takes the typed view model instead. How the shared keywords behave is explained on Experimental interpretation and in the vaft.plot API. Each picture is drawn from one of the packaged sample shots by the plot’s own adapter, with python -m vaft.plot.docs_thumbnails, and committed; the caption names the shot. A plot no packaged sample can draw shows why instead, and a picture drawn before its renderer or sample last changed is marked stale until it is re-rendered. import vaft ods = vaft.omas.sample_ods() /vaft/develop/reference/diagram/.title: Diagram gallery
/vaft/develop/reference/diagram/.body: Generated from vaft.diagram.build.CANONICAL and docs/assets/diagrams/manifest.json by python -m vaft.diagram.docs_catalog: 126 builders, 156 committed SVGs. Nothing on this page is written by hand. Each picture is the committed SVG rendered from the builder’s TikZ source; the caption is the exact call that produced it, so vaft.diagram.<call>.save("x.svg") reproduces it. What the diagrams mean, and the conventions they share, is explained on Scientific diagrams. python -m vaft.diagram.build --check verifies that every SVG here still matches its source. Index Magnetic-island schematic: one physical model, three projections magnetic_islandSchematic of an $m/n$ magnetic island in one of three projections. Stability and operational-space diagrams: textbook 2-D projections peeling_ballooningSchematic edge-stability (peeling-ballooning) diagram. s_alpha_ballooningFirst and second ballooning stability in the circular $s$-$\alpha$ model. hugillHugill diagram: $1/q_\mathrm{cyl}$ against the Murakami parameter $\bar n R/B$. troyonTroyon diagram: toroidal beta against the normalised current $I_p/(aB_T)$. Single-particle motion diagrams: gyration and guiding-centre drifts exb_driftE-cross-B drift of an ion and an electron in uniform crossed fields. curvature_driftAn ion spiralling along a curved field line and drifting off it. magnetization_currentGyrating ions in a bounded region: interior currents cancel, the edge carries one. toroidal_driftWhy a purely toroidal field cannot confine a plasma. Tearing physics upstream of the island: rational surface, Delta-prime, layer matching rational_surfaceWhere a helical perturbation resonates: the rational surface $q(r_s) = m/n$. delta_primeWhat $\Delta’$ measures: the slope jump of the outer solution across $r_s$. tearing_layer_matchingWhy tearing theory splits the plasma into ideal outer regions and a thin inner layer. 3-D perturbation harmonics: what a complex Fourier coefficient means normal_field_component$\delta B_n = \delta\mathbf B\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}$: the part of a perturbation that crosses a surface. complex_harmonicOne harmonic as a complex coefficient $\hat b = b_R + i\,b_I = A\,e^{i\alpha}$. toroidal_harmonic_phaseThe toroidal mode number is the rate at which the phase winds around the torus. harmonic_real_space_projectionFrom a complex coefficient to the real field it stands for, $\mathrm{Re}[\hat b\,e^{i(m\theta - n\phi)}]$. complex_field_superpositionExternal and plasma-response fields add as complex numbers. Collision processes in fusion plasmas: a classification diagram collision_processesCollision processes in fusion plasmas: Coulomb, atomic and nuclear. Geometric approximations: which geometry, which ordering, and how modes map geometry_ordering_mapGeometry and ordering are two axes, not one hierarchy. field_line_geometryThe same field-line structure in toroidal, cylindrical and local sheared-slab geometry. mode_number_mapping$(m, n) \to (k_y, k_z)$: the rational surface is where $k_\parallel = 0$. Tokamak toroidal geometry and flux coordinates tokamak_torusThe tokamak torus: major radius $R_0$, minor radius $a$, toroidal $\phi$ and poloidal $\theta$. flux_surfacesNested circular flux surfaces, concentric or Shafranov-shifted. shaping_familyElongation $\kappa$ and triangularity $\delta$ on one boundary family. hfs_lfs_field$B_\phi \propto 1/R$: the high-field side is inboard, the low-field side outboard. safety_factor_winding$q$ is the number of toroidal turns a field line makes per poloidal turn. flux_coordinatesFlux coordinates $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ on a shaped cross-section. poloidal_angle_comparisonThe geometric poloidal angle and the straight-field-line angle $\theta^*$ are different coordinates. unwrapped_flux_surfaceOn an unwrapped flux surface a field line is straight in $(\theta^, \phi)$: $d\phi/d\theta^ = q$. field_line_pitchA field line on a toroidal surface and its field $\mathbf B = B_\phi\hat{\boldsymbol\phi} + B_\theta\hat{\boldsymbol\theta}$. Toroidicity and TF ripple, one concept per diagram trapped_and_passing_orbitsThe $1/R$ mirror: passing orbits go round, trapped ones bounce as bananas. toroidal_field_ripple$N_\mathrm{TF}$ discrete coils corrugate $B(\phi)$ around the smooth $1/R$ field. ripple_well_formationAlong a field line the ripple makes local wells where $\alpha^* < 1$. stochastic_ripple_orbitRipple kicks at successive banana tips decorrelate above the GWB threshold. Guiding-centre invariants and toroidal symmetry guiding_center_invariantsGyration, bounce and toroidal drift, and the invariant each carries. canonical_toroidal_momentum$P_\phi = q\psi + mv_\parallel Rb_\phi$ along one banana: the parts trade, the sum stays. toroidal_symmetry_breakingAxisymmetry keeps $P_\phi$; a 3-D field changes it, secularly only at resonance. Straight-field-line coordinates: one equilibrium, many angles sfl_coordinate_gridsPEST, Boozer, Hamada and equal-arc on the same equilibrium: only the angle changes. sfl_coordinate_taxonomyFlux coordinates, the straight-field-line condition, and what each named choice fixes. sfl_fourier_convergenceThe same physical perturbation has a different poloidal spectrum in each straight-field-line angle. field_line_action_angleStraight-field-line coordinates are the action-angle variables of the field-line flow. sfl_coordinate_validityWhere nested-surface straight-field-line coordinates hold, and where they fail. coordinates_vs_cocosCoordinate choice and COCOS convention are independent axes, not branches of one tree. Clebsch labels, field-aligned and ballooning representations clebsch_field_line_labelA field line is where $\psi$ = const meets $\alpha$ = const. ballooning_curvature_driveNormal curvature and the total ballooning drive along the extended angle. ballooning_newcomb_testNewcomb’s test on the extended angle: stable, unstable and second stable. ballooning_harmonic_envelopeA ballooning mode is many coupled harmonics $m \approx nq$ under one envelope. ballooning_workflowFrom global harmonics to the infinite-$n$ ballooning equation, and the coordinate genealogy. Slab resonant layers: tearing and twisting parity, harmonic coupling slab_parityTearing or twisting parity at a rational surface, as contours of the helical flux. slab_parity_comparisonTearing and twisting parity side by side, with what tells them apart. poloidal_harmonic_couplingToroidicity couples $m$ to $m \pm 1$, elongation to $m \pm 2$, at fixed $n$. resonant_layer_matchingSeveral rational surfaces, each with a tearing and a twisting channel, matched through the outer region. Disruption physics: the quench sequence, its causal chain, runaway generation and energy paths disruption_timelineA disruption on one time axis, from a 0-D reference model built of the formulas. disruption_causal_chainThe thermal-quench -> current-quench -> runaway chain as cause and effect. runaway_generationDreicer and avalanche generation against the field, and the regimes they define. disruption_energy_pathwaysWhere a disruption’s thermal and magnetic energies go. A prescribed ideal displacement on an arbitrary equilibrium kink_modeA prescribed $m/n$ ideal displacement drawn on an equilibrium’s own flux surfaces. A Kadomtsev-like sawtooth on an arbitrary equilibrium, as three distinct states sawtoothA reduced, Kadomtsev-like sawtooth crash in one of three states, on an equilibrium’s surfaces. Reduced Hamiltonian field-line topology on an arbitrary equilibrium stochastic_layerIsland overlap on an equilibrium: a Poincare section of two resonant harmonics. separatrix_lobesStable and unstable manifolds of a perturbed X-point, and the lobes between them. Vertical displacement events: hot and cold VDE, halo currents and timescales hot_vde_sequenceA hot VDE: the plasma drifts into the wall, is scraped, and its edge $q$ falls at constant $I_p$. cold_vde_bifurcationCold VDE as the loss of a centred vertical equilibrium while the current decays (schematic). plasma_wall_halo_currentWall contact in a VDE: one halo-current circuit, the eddy currents, and the force on the wall. vde_timescalesThe VDE’s timescales on one log axis, for one parameter set. The Grad--Shafranov problem: regions, boundaries, topology and problem classes grad_shafranov_domain_decompositionSame flux function, different sources: plasma, vacuum and coil regions of one elliptic problem. fixed_vs_free_boundary_equilibriumThe boundary as an input against the boundary as part of the solution. limiter_and_diverted_topologiesWhere the plasma ends: limiter contact against an X-point separatrix. equilibrium_problem_taxonomyForward/inverse and fixed/free boundary are two axes, not one. poloidal_flux_source_decomposition$\psi_\mathrm{plasma} + \psi_\mathrm{coil} = \psi_\mathrm{total}$: the topology belongs to the sum. Cylindrical (screw-pinch) geometry: q profile, rational surfaces, mode shapes, matching current_to_q_profileFrom the current profile to the safety factor: $j(r) \to B_\theta(r) \to q(r)$. cylindrical_rational_surfacesFor one $n$, every $m$ with $q_0 < m/n < q_a$ has its rational surface $q(r_s) = m/n$. cylindrical_mode_morphologyThe poloidal mode number as a shape: sausage, kink, and higher helical distortions. internal_external_kinkInternal kink: displacement inside $q = 1$; external kink: displacement reaching the boundary. plasma_vacuum_wallOne harmonic across plasma, vacuum and an ideal conducting wall. cylindrical_tearing_outerThe outer tearing solution of one rational surface on the cylinder, and where the inner layer takes over. Canonical slab field configurations and reconnection topology slab_field_configurationField direction on stacked $x$ = const sheets: uniform, sheared, reversed, guide-field. current_sheetA current sheet seen along the current: reversing field, sheet, normal, thickness, $J_z$. harris_sheet$B_y(x)$ and $J_z(x)$ of the Harris sheet on one chart. x_pointThe current-free magnetic X-point of x_point_flux: four branches and two separatrices. magnetic_reconnectionModel-neutral 2-D reconnection: inflow, outflow, diffusion region, upstream and reconnected field. island_formationFrom a sheared field to a magnetic island: slab_perturbed_flux with growing tearing amplitude. Linear ideal-MHD waves in a uniform plasma: polarization and the branch family shear_alfven_waveShear Alfven polarization: field-line bending without compression. fast_magnetosonic_waveFast magnetosonic polarization at $\mathbf k \perp \mathbf B_0$: compression and rarefaction. mhd_wave_familyThe Friedrichs diagram: phase speed against the angle to $\mathbf B_0$, three branches. Plasma-wall interaction concepts: processes, reflection, sputtering, recycling, energy partition plasma_wall_interaction_processesOne ion impact and its outcomes, the projectile and target species kept apart. plasma_wall_interaction_reflectionParticle reflection: incident and reflected energy and angle are separate quantities. plasma_wall_interaction_sputteringPhysical sputtering by a light projectile: backscatter from below ejects a surface atom. plasma_wall_interaction_recyclingReflection, re-emission and retention as flux bookkeeping. plasma_wall_interaction_energy_partitionParticle balance and energy balance, side by side: not the same bookkeeping. Spectroscopy and ionization concept diagrams, with progressive metadata spectroscopy_ionization_stagesAll ionization stages of an element, the one a term names highlighted. spectroscopy_transitionsThe transition behind one emission term, with no more metadata than exists. spectroscopy_energy_levelsThe hydrogenic level ladder, with the Lyman, Balmer and Paschen series. spectroscopy_spectrumDeclared spectral lines on a wavelength axis, each at the wavelength its label states. Neutral beam injection: the particle lifecycle and the reduced neutral attenuation nbi_particle_lifecycleWhat happens to a beam particle, and the three different ways it is lost. nbi_neutral_attenuationNeutral survival and fast-ion birth along the beam path, and the shine-through at the exit. Iteration behaviour, branch bifurcation and branch selection: why a solver does not converge iteration_behaviorFour iteration behaviours in one format: state $x_k$ against iteration $k$. branch_bifurcationStable and unstable branches, two folds, the jumps and the hysteresis loop. basin_of_attractionBranch selection by the initial condition: two stable solutions at one control parameter. grid_induced_two_cycleA numerical 2-cycle: the discrete state hops between two adjacent grid nodes. branch_selectionPhysical branch selection beside numerical cycling: the two causes of non-convergence side by side. Cold-plasma waves from their equations: O and X modes, the CMA diagram and a profile's cutoffs o_mode_cutoffO-mode refractive index against frequency: propagation above $\omega_{pe}$, evanescence below. x_mode_dispersionX-mode refractive index against frequency: two cutoffs, the upper-hybrid resonance and two gaps. cma_diagramThe Clemmow–Mullaly–Allis diagram of a cold electron plasma. profile_propagationO- and X-mode $n^2$ along the midplane of an example tokamak, with its cutoff and resonance layers. Collisionality regimes: axisymmetric neoclassical and non-axisymmetric NTV neoclassical_collisionalityBanana, plateau and Pfirsch–Schl"uter: the axisymmetric neoclassical regimes. ntv_collisionalityShaing’s NTV regimes: the non-resonant and resonant branches of the flux against collisionality. ntv_precession_regimesCollisionality alone does not fix the NTV regime: the precession plane. Wall conditioning: baking, glow-discharge cleaning and boronization as wall-state transitions wall_conditioning_bakingBaking: external heat desorbs water and gases from the wall into the pump. wall_conditioning_gdcGlow-discharge cleaning: one apparatus template, gas-specific content. wall_conditioning_boronizationBoronization: a B-containing precursor in a deposition plasma coats the wall. wall_conditioning_sequenceConditioning stages in order, each a transition of the wall state. /vaft/develop/reference/formula/boundari.title: Formula reference: boundaries
/vaft/develop/reference/formula/boundari.body: Generated from the docstrings of vaft.formula.boundaries: 7 public functions. Each entry is what vaft.formula.describe("boundaries.<name>") prints. All formula categories Overview A published limit is more than its formula. It predicts one specific quantity (line-averaged density, not “the density”). It has a permitted side. It was fitted on some machines under some assumptions. It may or may not carry a quoted uncertainty. And it comes from one paper and equation. A Boundary keeps all of that next to the evaluation rule. Then evaluate_boundary can report how far a state sits from the boundary, on which side, and whether the inputs lie inside the fitted domain. boundary_curve returns the boundary as arrays on a chosen 2-D projection, and a plot draws only that; no plotting code lives here (#1067). Existing formula functions stay where they are. An entry references one through function instead of restating its coefficients, so the Greenwald entry evaluates stability.greenwald_density itself. SymbolMeaningUnit bboundary value of the target quantity, in the target's unitvaries xoperating value of the same quantity, same unitvaries ratiox / b- marginsigned normalised distance, positive on the permitted side- Every input and target is a BoundaryQuantity with an explicit unit string, and callers pass values in exactly that unit. Nothing is converted behind the caller’s back. For allowed_side = "below" (permitted $x < b$) the margin is $(b - x)/b$. For "above" (permitted $x > b$) it is $(x - b)/b$. A positive margin is always the permitted side, and a zero margin lies on the boundary. Functions boundary_curveA boundary sampled along one input, as $(x, y) = (x_\mathrm{sweep}, b)$ arrays. Convention boundary_valueValue of a boundary’s target quantity at the given inputs. Convention evaluate_boundaryDistance and side of an operating value relative to a boundary. Convention evaluate_windowPosition of an operating value relative to an access window. Convention get_boundaryA registered boundary or window by key. hugill_coordinatesHugill-diagram coordinates of an operating state: $(\bar n_e R/B_T,\ 1/q_\mathrm{cyl})$. Convention list_boundariesKeys of the registered boundaries, optionally restricted to one family. No function matches. boundary_curve Convention-sensitive source boundary_curve(boundary, sweep, values, swap_axes=False, **fixed) A boundary sampled along one input, as $(x, y) = (x_\mathrm{sweep}, b)$ arrays. \[y_k = b\left(x_\mathrm{sweep} = v_k,\ \text{other inputs fixed}\right)\] NameTypeUnitDescription boundaryBoundary-The boundary to sample. sweepstr-Name of the input placed on the x axis. valuesarray_likevariesValues of the swept input, in its declared unit. swap_axesbool-Put the boundary’s target on x and the swept input on y, as in a Hugill diagram, whose x axis is the density-like quantity. Returns —BoundaryCurve-x is the swept input and y the boundary value. The curve carries both quantities (identity and unit), the permitted side along y, and the fixed inputs. Convention The permitted side is the boundary’s own allowed_side, read along the y axis: "below" means operating points under the curve are permitted. With swap_axes the target is read along x, so "below" becomes "left" and "above" becomes "right". Raises KeyError sweep is not an input of the boundary. TypeError A fixed input is missing, unknown, an array, or duplicates the swept one; or values is not 1-D. boundary_value Convention-sensitive source boundary_value(boundary, **inputs) Value of a boundary’s target quantity at the given inputs. \[b = C\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}\quad\text{(power law)},\qquad b = C\quad\text{(threshold)},\qquad b = f(x_1,\ldots)\quad\text{(function)}\] NameTypeUnitDescription boundaryBoundary-The boundary to evaluate. Returns —float or np.ndarrayvariesBoundary value, in the unit of boundary.target. Convention Each keyword input is a value in the unit its BoundaryQuantity declares. No unit conversion happens here; a caller holding amperes for a boundary declared in MA converts first. Raises TypeError An input is missing or not one of the boundary’s inputs. Notes Notes Array inputs broadcast with NumPy rules. evaluate_boundary Convention-sensitive source evaluate_boundary(boundary, operating_value, **inputs) Distance and side of an operating value relative to a boundary. \[\mathrm{margin} = \frac{b - x}{b}\ \ (\text{permitted below}),\qquad \mathrm{margin} = \frac{x - b}{b}\ \ (\text{permitted above})\] NameTypeUnitDescription boundaryBoundary-The boundary to compare against. operating_valuefloat or np.ndarrayvariesOperating value $x$ of the boundary’s target quantity, in the target’s unit. Returns —BoundaryEvaluation-Boundary value $b$, ratio $x/b$, difference $x - b$, signed margin (positive on the permitted side), permitted flag, the inputs that lie outside the source’s stated ranges, and warnings. Convention The margin is normalised by the boundary value. A positive margin is always the permitted side, whichever way the boundary points, so margins of different boundaries share one sign convention. allowed is strict: a state exactly on the boundary is not counted as permitted. A boundary value that is zero, negative or not finite gives NaN margin and ratio, is never permitted, and adds a warning. Pass magnitudes where a sign convention could make the boundary negative. Raises TypeError An input is missing or not one of the boundary’s inputs. Notes Notes Crossing a soft boundary is not a prediction of failure. For example, $f_G > 1$ is routinely reached. The evaluation reports the geometry, and interpreting it is left to the caller. evaluate_window Convention-sensitive source evaluate_window(window, operating_value, **inputs) Position of an operating value relative to an access window. \[b_\mathrm{lower} < x < b_\mathrm{upper}\] NameTypeUnitDescription windowBoundaryWindow-The access window. operating_valuefloat or np.ndarrayvariesOperating value of the window’s target quantity, in its unit. Returns —WindowEvaluation-One evaluation per edge and inside, true where both are permitted. Convention inputs holds the union of both edges’ inputs. Each edge receives only the inputs it declares. Raises TypeError An input is missing or unused by both edges. get_boundary source get_boundary(key) A registered boundary or window by key. NameTypeUnitDescription keystr-Registry key, for example "greenwald". Returns —Boundary or BoundaryWindow-The registered entry. Raises KeyError No entry has that key; the message lists the keys that exist. hugill_coordinates Convention-sensitive source hugill_coordinates(n_e, R_geo, B_t, a, kappa_a, I_p) Hugill-diagram coordinates of an operating state: $(\bar n_e R/B_T,\ 1/q_\mathrm{cyl})$. \[x = \frac{\bar n_e R_{geo}}{B_T},\qquad y = \frac{1}{q_{cyl}} = \frac{R_{geo}\,|I_p|}{5\,a^2\kappa_a B_T}\quad(I_p\ \mathrm{in\ MA})\] NameTypeUnitDescription n_efloat or np.ndarray1e19 m^-3Line-averaged electron density. R_geofloat or np.ndarraymGeometric major radius. B_tfloat or np.ndarrayTVacuum toroidal field at R_geo, magnitude. afloat or np.ndarraymMinor radius. kappa_afloat or np.ndarray-Area elongation $S/(\pi a^2)$. I_pfloat or np.ndarrayMAPlasma current; its sign is dropped. Returns —tuple of (float or np.ndarray)-Murakami parameter $\bar n_e R/B_T$ [1e19 m^-2 T^-1] and $1/q_{cyl}$. Convention $q_{cyl}$ is equilibrium.q_cyl_from_B_R_epsilon_kappa_I with $\varepsilon = a/R_{geo}$. The "greenwald_hugill" boundary uses the same convention, so a state at $\bar n_e = n_G$ lies exactly on it. This is the cylindrical $q$, not $q_{95}$. At VEST aspect ratio the two differ substantially, and plotting $1/q_{95}$ against this boundary is only approximate. Raises ValueError A negative density, or a non-positive field, radius, minor radius or elongation. Numerical notes Numerical notes $1/q_{cyl}$ is formed directly rather than as 1/q_cyl_from_..., so a zero current maps to the origin $y = 0$ instead of raising. A whole time trace, including start-up and termination, can therefore be projected without cropping. list_boundaries source list_boundaries(family=None) Keys of the registered boundaries, optionally restricted to one family. NameTypeUnitDescription familystr, optional-Family name, for example "density_limit". Returns —tuple of str-Sorted registry keys.

/vaft/develop/reference/equilibrium-repr.title: Equilibrium representations
/vaft/develop/reference/equilibrium-repr.body: A tokamak equilibrium reaches an analysis as $\psi(R,Z)$, a $q(\psi)$ profile, a $\rho_{tor,N}$ grid, a set of Miller numbers, Fourier boundary coefficients, a PEST grid, camera pixels, a field-line trajectory, an $m/n$ helical perturbation or a local transport input. These forms are related, but they are not interchangeable. This page names the five kinds of object VAFT derives from an equilibrium, maps the hierarchy of issue #1201 onto the functions that implement it, and lists what is not yet implemented. Every branch starts from one canonical record, vaft.data.EquilibriumData, built by vaft.process.as_equilibrium from an ODS, a GEQDSK or an analytic generator. The record keeps the source’s convention and does not convert it on construction. What follows is always canonical state + explicit transformation = derived object (with provenance) and never one object that holds every coordinate, projection and approximation at once. The five categories Category Answers VAFT examples Is not coordinate where a quantity is parameterized $\psi_N$, $\rho_{pol,N}$, $\rho_{tor,N}$, PEST $\theta^*$ $\rho_{tor,N} = \sqrt{\psi_N}$ projection where the same object is viewed R–Z plane, top view, 3-D embedding, camera pixels a camera overlay as a 2-D equilibrium representation how the state is encoded or approximated Miller surface, FourierSurface, Solov’ev fit, prescribed island Miller as an arbitrary LCFS derived quantity what physics follows from the state $q$, shear, $a/L_T$, rational surfaces, shaping $a/L_T$ as a radial coordinate solver convention how an external code stores it COCOS index, Wb vs Wb/rad, DCON/GPEC Jacobian, TGLF units a Fourier contour angle as a magnetic angle Coordinate A coordinate labels positions in the plasma. A quantity is a function of it, and changing the coordinate changes the abscissa but not the physics. Radial coordinates label flux surfaces. Poloidal coordinates label points on one surface. Two coordinates can share the range $[0,1]$ or $[0,2\pi)$ and still label different points. The definition, not the range or the name, makes a coordinate. vaft.process.derive_radial_coordinates(eq) returns psi_n, rho_pol_n and rho_tor_n as DerivedValue records. Each record gives its definition, for example sqrt(int_axis^psi q dpsi / int_axis^boundary q dpsi) for $\rho_{tor,N}$. When the record cannot form $\rho_{tor,N}$, it gives a reason and does not substitute $\sqrt{\psi_N}$. vaft.process.MappedPositions from equilibrium_mapping_thomson_scattering and equilibrium_mapping_charge_exchange gives each kinetic channel in every radial coordinate the equilibrium supports (Equilibrium and kinetic profiles). vaft.process.straight_field_line_map returns a StraightFieldLineMap that evaluates the PEST angle $\theta^*$ and $\psi_N$ at any $(R,Z)$ and tabulates theta and theta_star on a surface. vaft.formula.generalized_straight_field_line_angle gives the PEST, Boozer, Hamada and equal-arc angles of one surface. vaft.formula.sfl_toroidal_angle_shift gives the matching toroidal shift $\nu$. The family is drawn by vaft.diagram.sfl_coordinate_taxonomy (Scientific diagrams). Is not: $\rho_{tor,N}$ is not $\sqrt{\psi_N}$, and the geometric angle $\theta = \mathrm{atan2}(Z-Z_a, R-R_a)$ is not the PEST $\theta^*$. The packaged 39915 ODS stores $\sqrt{\psi_N}$ under profiles_1d.rho_tor_norm, so the stored name does not tell you the definition (see Gaps). Projection A projection shows the same physical object in another space: the poloidal plane, the machine $X$–$Y$ plane, a 3-D scene or a detector. It creates no new equilibrium, fits nothing and loses no physics that the viewing geometry does not remove. It can add calibration: a camera projection depends on a calibrated camera model as well as on the equilibrium. The R–Z flux map, drawn by the equilibrium_field_psi plot recipe from a vaft.plot.Field2D model. The top view, vaft.plot.equilibrium_geometry_topview. The camera view: vaft.omas.camera_projection_for returns a calibrated vaft.process.camera_geometry.CameraProjection, and vaft.omas.compute_camera_visible_efit_overlay projects the LCFS and flux surfaces into pixels without writing anything back. The 3-D axisymmetric embedding: vaft.process.camera_geometry.sweep_toroidal sweeps a contour toroidally, and vaft.plot.Geometry3DLayers / vaft.plot.render_geometry_3d_layers draw it. Is not: a camera overlay is not a 2-D equilibrium, and a toroidal sweep of an axisymmetric surface is not a 3-D equilibrium. Representation A representation encodes the state, or part of it, in another form, usually with fewer degrees of freedom. It is lossy, so it has to report how well it reproduces what it replaced. A representation fitted to the state describes it only within its fit validity. vaft.process.fit_miller_surface returns a MillerFitResult with rms_error, normalized_rms_error, max_error, hausdorff_distance, accepted and reason. It refuses surfaces near an active X-point. vaft.process.fit_fourier_surface / evaluate_fourier_surface / fit_fourier_surface_sequence work with vaft.data.FourierSurface, which records its curve parameter in angle_convention ("arc_length"). The analytic ladder: vaft.process.solovev_to_equilibrium and solovev_example(topology=...), vaft.process.guazzotto_freidberg_to_equilibrium for Guazzotto–Freidberg parts 1 and 2, and the inverse fit vaft.process.fit_solovev. All of them return or consume EquilibriumData, so an analytic state follows the same downstream paths as a reconstruction. A prescribed island: vaft.process.MagneticIslandSpec and magnetic_island_topology. Is not: a Miller shape is not an arbitrary LCFS. A fit that works on the nearly up-down symmetric VEST limited boundary says nothing about beans, racetracks or diverted shapes (notebooks/edge_and_boundary_representation.ipynb). Derived quantity A derived quantity is physics computed from the state: a number or profile that the equilibrium implies, not a new label for positions. It is plotted against a coordinate. Its value can depend on the coordinate and length scale used to define it, and then that choice is part of the quantity. $q$, magnetic shear and $\alpha$ on a Miller surface (MillerSurface.q, .magnetic_shear, .alpha), and $q$ recomputed from the PEST map as $F\oint dl/(R|\nabla\psi|)$. Shaping observables from vaft.process.contour_shaping_observables, and the boundary topology record from vaft.process.derive_boundary_representation (Topology, X-points, strike points, gaps). Normalized gradients: vaft.formula.normalized_gradient_scale_length(x, y, a) and SyntheticKineticProfiles.a_over_L(channel, coordinate). Is not: $a/L_T$ is not a radial coordinate. On one $T_e$ profile at $\rho_{tor,N}=0.6$, the reference notebook gets 3.0, 2.95, 2.07 and 2.95 from four gradient conventions. A gradient is defined only once its derivative coordinate and its reference length are stated. Solver convention A solver convention is how a code, a file format or an IMAS version stores a state: the COCOS index, the sign and direction choices it implies, the flux unit (Wb or Wb/rad), the poloidal-angle Jacobian of a solver mesh, and a code’s normalizations. It changes numbers without changing physics. Quantities from two sources are comparable only after their conventions are converted to a common one. vaft.data.EquilibriumConvention (cocos, psi_per_radian, sign fields, source, and contradicted when the data disagree with the declaration). vaft.process.convert_cocos(eq, target) converts it explicitly. Process reference: cocos. vaft.process.straight_field_line_tables reads the angle tables of a DCON/GPEC mesh and requires jacobian= to be named. lab_to_straight_field_line applies them. TGLFNormalisation in vaft.code.gacode.tglf.inputs gives TGLF’s $a$, $c_s$, $\rho_s$ and $B_\mathrm{unit}$ from explicit definitions, checked against locpargen. Is not: a Fourier curve parameter is not a magnetic poloidal angle. FourierSurface uses an arc-length angle, which differs from both the geometric and the PEST angle on the same surface. Reading a solver’s angle (straight_field_line_tables) is also different from constructing one from the equilibrium (straight_field_line_map). The hierarchy in VAFT The branches of #1201 §2, their category, and where each starts in the code. Status follows the acceptance audit posted on #1201: met means a public API plus a test or documentation demonstrates it. Branch Category Canonical entry points Status Radial coordinates coordinate vaft.process.derive_radial_coordinates, vaft.process.MappedPositions, vaft.process.psi_to_radial (midplane radii) partly met Poloidal / magnetic coordinates coordinate vaft.process.straight_field_line_map (native PEST), vaft.process.straight_field_line_tables (read DCON/GPEC), vaft.formula.generalized_straight_field_line_angle, vaft.formula.sfl_toroidal_angle_shift partly met Physical-space views projection Profile1D and Field2D in vaft.plot, vaft.plot.equilibrium_geometry_topview, vaft.plot.Geometry3DLayers partly met Diagnostic projections projection vaft.omas.camera_projection_for, vaft.omas.compute_camera_visible_efit_overlay partly met Compact geometric representations representation vaft.process.fit_miller_surface, vaft.process.fit_fourier_surface, vaft.process.evaluate_fourier_surface, vaft.data.MXHChebyshevRepresentation Miller and Fourier met Analytic hierarchy representation vaft.process.solovev_to_equilibrium, vaft.process.solovev_example, vaft.process.guazzotto_freidberg_to_equilibrium, vaft.process.fit_solovev partly met Kinetic / gradient representations derived quantity vaft.formula.normalized_gradient_scale_length, vaft.data.SyntheticKineticProfiles, vaft.data.GradientProfile not met Boundary / topology derived quantity vaft.process.derive_boundary_representation, vaft.data.BoundaryRepresentation, vaft.data.Topology, vaft.process.contour_shaping_observables shape vs topology met Perturbed / helical representation vaft.process.MagneticIslandSpec, vaft.process.magnetic_island_topology, GpecCylindricalOutput in vaft.code.gpec partly met Conventions (all branches) solver convention vaft.data.EquilibriumConvention, vaft.process.convert_cocos, vaft.process.make_equilibrium_field_interpolator partly met The per-function pages are under Process reference, Formula reference and the Plot reference. The provenance thread Every object derived from an equilibrium should point back to the same state. Five things identify that state, and each has a place in the code: Thread Where it lives source EquilibriumData.metadata, EquilibriumConvention.source; DerivationProvenance.source_type and .source_fields time EquilibriumData.time; DerivationProvenance.source_time COCOS and flux unit EquilibriumData.convention.cocos and .psi_per_radian; DerivationProvenance.convention method DerivationProvenance.method, .interpolation, .fit_range, .radial_coordinate residual DerivedValue.quality; MillerFitResult / FourierFitResult errors; SolovevFit.metrics; camera reproj_mean_px Same shot and time does not mean the same equilibrium. The package also ships a standalone 39915 g-file at 319 ms, which is a different EFIT run stored per radian. The source record, not the timestamp, identifies the state. The check below runs on the packaged sample. It asserts the COCOS instead of trusting it, then confirms that each derived object still names the same time and convention. index = int(np.argmin(np.abs(np.asarray(ods["equilibrium.time"]) - 0.319))) eq = vaft.process.as_equilibrium(ods, time_index=index, convention=11) assert eq.convention.cocos == 11 and eq.convention.psi_per_radian is False # psi in Wb coords = vaft.process.derive_radial_coordinates(eq) for name, item in coords.items(): p = item.provenance assert item.available, item.reason assert abs(p.source_time - eq.time) < 5e-4 and p.convention.cocos == eq.convention.cocos print(f"{name:10s} {item.definition:55s} [{p.method}]") miller = vaft.process.fit_miller_surface(eq.lcfs) fourier = vaft.process.fit_fourier_surface(eq.lcfs, modes=6) print("Miller nRMS", round(miller.normalized_rms_error, 4), "accepted", miller.accepted) print("Fourier nRMS", round(fourier.normalized_rms_error, 4), "angle", fourier.surface.angle_convention) print("Miller provenance carries a convention:", miller.provenance.convention is not None) # False: #604 eq_rad = vaft.process.convert_cocos(eq, 1) # same state, psi per radian print("flux-span ratio", (eq.psi_boundary - eq.psi_axis) / (eq_rad.psi_boundary - eq_rad.psi_axis)) # 2*pi The last lines show where the thread breaks today. A Miller fit of a bare contour carries no time or convention (#604), so the caller has to keep them. The whole chain is notebooks/equilibrium_representation_reference.ipynb. It takes the 39915 slice at 0.319 s through the four radial coordinates, the R–Z map, a PEST grid with a $q$ residual, Miller and Fourier fits, $a/L_T$ in four conventions, rational surfaces, a prescribed island with a field-line check, a 3-D embedding and a camera projection, and checks source, time, COCOS and flux unit at each step. The GPEC response step is missing because no GPEC output is packaged. Gaps These are the items the #1201 audit grades not met or partly met, with the issue that owns each. “Unowned” means no issue other than #1201 tracks it. Not met Gradient semantics. No gradient_coordinate / reference_length contract, and no $1/L$, $a/L$, $R/L$ quantity family (#551; #563 was closed as its duplicate). Partly met Radial coordinates: The process layer names coordinates psi_n / rho_*_n, while profiles and plots use *_norm. The packaged 39915 ODS stores $\sqrt{\psi_N}$ under profiles_1d.rho_tor_norm. The plot recipe detects this with vaft.data._derived.is_rho_pol_proxy, but a direct reader of the leaf does not (unowned). Geometric radii. r_minor exists only in vaft.plot as $(R_{out}-R_{in})/2$, and vaft/plot/onedim.py uses $r - r_{axis}$. r_minor_norm and r_center have no definition (#479). Flux coordinates. The native map is PEST only. There is no direct inverse $(\psi,\theta^*)\to(R,Z)$, no Jacobian output, no native Boozer or Hamada map (only the per-surface formulas), and no closure or Jacobian residual on the map (#472). Angle identity on the read path: straight_field_line_tables returns bare (lab, sfl) tuples. vaft/machine_mapping/mhd_linear.py defaults an unrecorded Jacobian to "hamada" (unowned). On-surface view. There is no first-class $f(\theta \mid \psi)$ view; the notebook builds one from StraightFieldLineMap.surface() (#1201 phase E). Projections: There is no projection abstraction and no general 3-D embedding. sweep_toroidal is a camera helper that works in centimetres and calls the toroidal angle theta. The camera overlay reads raw ODS paths instead of going through as_equilibrium. The camera’s toroidal frame is not reconciled with the port frame (#746). Compact representations: MillerSurface mixes geometry with $q$, shear and $\alpha$. BoundaryRepresentation.fourier_coefficients and MXHChebyshevRepresentation do not record their angle convention (#942). Flow equilibria. EquilibriumData has no governing-equation field. A Guazzotto–Freidberg flow case is kept distinct only because exporting it raises (#1149). Code presets. Only TGLF resolves its normalization. CGYRO, GS2, GENE and GKW are absent (#551). Advanced divertors. Snowflake, X-divertor and Super-X exist only as a TES input (#950). Islands and perturbations (unowned; #886 covers the prescribed island): The solver-derived island separatrix is reconstructed only inside the plot backend. No island record says whether it is prescribed or solver-derived. There is no public real-space or diagnostic-space projection of a complex GPEC perturbation. Conventions: A default-constructed record falls back to Wb/rad (#603). Miller provenance carries no convention (#604). Discovery. No API lists the available coordinates, projections and representations with their required source data (#1201 phase H). Two audit findings have been fixed since the audit: The kinetic plot recipes drew $\sqrt{\psi_N}$ under a $\psi_N$ label (#1314). make_equilibrium_field_interpolator assumed Wb/rad when no COCOS was given. It now reads the convention from the record (#1313). See also Equilibrium and kinetic profiles: radial mapping of kinetic channels. Geometric approximations: slab, cylinder and torus as model geometries, which are a different axis from the representations here. Scientific diagrams: the tokamak-geometry and straight-field-line sections. Notebooks: equilibrium_representation_reference.ipynb, edge_and_boundary_representation.ipynb, compact_equilibrium_representation.ipynb, local_miller_equilibrium_fitting.ipynb, analytic_solovev_equilibrium.ipynb, analytic_island_model_and_synthetic_response_model.ipynb.

All formula categories Overview A non-axisymmetric $\delta B$ makes the radial particle flux of each species non-ambipolar. Quasineutrality forces a return (polarisation) current that cancels the net radial current, and its $\mathbf J	imes\mathbf B$ is the toroidal torque on the plasma – NTV, equal and opposite to the $\mathbf J	imes\mathbf B$ of the non-ambipolar current itself. The size of the flux needs the bounce-averaged drift-kinetic response (PENT/PENTRC, NEO, kinetic GPEC; vaft.code). What is here is the part that is exact and convention-bearing: the precession frequency whose zero is the superbanana-plateau resonance, and the flux-force relation that turns non-ambipolar fluxes into torque. Shaing’s asymptotic regimes lie on two branches, in order of decreasing collisionality: non-resonant ($\omega_d$ bounded away from zero): $1/
u$ while $
u_\mathrm{eff}$ exceeds the precession, flux $\propto 1/
u$; then the $
u$–$\sqrt
u$ regime, a collisional boundary layer at the trapped-passing boundary, whose $\sqrt
u$ part dominates as $
u 	o 0$; resonant ($\omega_d 	o 0$ for some trapped particles): $1/
u$, then the superbanana plateau, flux independent of $
u$, then the superbanana regime, flux $\propto
u$, at the lowest collisionality. Shaing states the $1/
u$ boundary as $
u/\epsilon$ against $|q\omega_E|$ with the magnetic precession neglected; with it kept the comparison is with $|\omega_d|$. The connected formula that joins the regimes (Shaing, Sun and Sabbagh 2010) is not implemented: its kernels need the bounce-averaged $\delta B$ spectrum and source-specific normalisations. The diagrams draw the exponents only. abla Vangle$, particles of species s crossing the surface1/s psi$RA_\phi$, poloidal flux per radian, IMAS $\phi$Wb/rad Vvolume enclosed by the surfacem^3 Precession frequencies are toroidal and positive along the plasma current, as VAFT’s kinetic-profile omega_exb is ($-d\Phi/d\psi_\mathrm{out}$ with $\psi_\mathrm{out}$ the poloidal flux per radian increasing outward, e.g. TRANSP PLFLX); omega_exb is never the toroidal fluid rotation omega_tor. The torque is positive along the IMAS $\phi$ (counter-clockwise from above), with $\psi = RA_\phi$ as vaft.formula.particle.psi_per_radian_from_cocos returns it. Functions nonambipolar_torque_densityFlux-surface-averaged toroidal torque density on the plasma from non-ambipolar radial fluxes (NTV). Convention ntv_precession_frequencyBounce-averaged toroidal precession of trapped particles, whose zero is the superbanana-plateau resonance. abla Vangle$ of each species along axis 0, shape (S, ...): particles crossing the surface outward per second. dpsi_dVfloat or np.ndarrayWb/(rad m^3)$d\psi/dV$ of $\psi = RA_\phi$, broadcast against the trailing axes of particle_flux; negative for a plasma current along $+\phi$ Returns —float or np.ndarrayN m/m^3Torque density on the plasma about the symmetry axis, positive along the IMAS $\phi$, averaged over the surface. Convention With $\mathbf B = 
abla\psi	imes
abla\phi + F
abla\phi$ and $\psi = RA_\phi$ per radian (psi_per_radian_from_cocos; IMAS COCOS 11 stores $-2\pi\psi$), $R\hat\phi\cdot(\mathbf J	imes\mathbf B) = -\mathbf J\cdot
abla\psi$ exactly. The non-ambipolar current $\mathbf J_\mathrm{na} = \sum_s Z_se oldsymbol\Gamma_s$ is cancelled by a return current $-\mathbf J_\mathrm{na}$, whose $\mathbf J	imes\mathbf B$ – equivalently, the sum of each species’ toroidal viscous force – is the torque on the plasma: $T_\phi = +\langle\mathbf J_\mathrm{na}\cdot 
abla\psiangle = (d\psi/dV)\sum_s Z_se\langle oldsymbol\Gamma_s\cdot 
abla Vangle$. In Shaing’s $\psi = -RA_\phi$ this reads $-(d\psi/dV)\sum_s Z_se\Gamma_s$. A torque density; integrate over $V$ for the torque. Ambipolar fluxes give zero. Raises ValueError Species counts differ, or an input is not finite. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation An outward non-ambipolar ion flux in a plasma with current along $+\phi$ ($d\psi/dV < 0$) drives rotation against the current – the counter-current torque of fast-ion ripple loss and of ion-root NTV. Assumptions Steady state on the transport time scale, quasineutrality; the fluxes are the non-ambipolar parts from a kinetic calculation this function does not make. No phenomenological $-
u_\mathrm{NTV}(\Omega - \Omega_0)$ damping model is implied. References K. C. Shaing, Phys. Plasmas 10 (2003) 1443. P. Helander and D. J. Sigmar, Collisional Transport in Magnetized Plasmas, Cambridge University Press (2002), Ch. 8. ntv_precession_frequency Convention-sensitive source ntv_precession_frequency(omega_exb, omega_magnetic) Bounce-averaged toroidal precession of trapped particles, whose zero is the superbanana-plateau resonance. \[\omega_d = \omega_E + \omega_B \qquad (= q\,\omega_E^\mathrm{Shaing} + \omega_B)\] NameTypeUnitDescription omega_exbfloat or np.ndarrayrad/sToroidal E x B rotation frequency $\omega_E = -d\Phi/d\psi_\mathrm{out}$, $\psi_\mathrm{out}$ the poloidal flux per radian increasing outward – VAFT’s kinetic-profile omega_exb, positive along the plasma current, not the toroidal fluid rotation. omega_magneticfloat or np.ndarrayrad/sBounce-averaged toroidal precession by the grad-B and curvature drifts, for the species and energy considered, positive along the plasma current. Returns —float or np.ndarrayrad/s$\omega_d$, positive along the plasma current; zero on the superbanana-plateau resonance. Convention Both inputs must be measured in the same toroidal orientation; VAFT’s is along the plasma current, the orientation of omega_exb. A rigid rotation $\omega\hat\phi$ has $\mathbf E = -\omega
abla(RA_\phi)$, so $-d\Phi/d\psi_\mathrm{out}$ is the rotation along the current whichever way the current flows. Shaing writes $q\omega_E + \omega_B$ with his $\omega_E$ taken against the toroidal flux; since $d\psi_t = q\,d\psi$, his $q\omega_E$ is this omega_exb. The toroidal rotation $\omega_\phi$ differs from $\omega_E$ by the diamagnetic and poloidal-flow terms of radial force balance, and substituting it moves the resonance. $\omega_B \propto$ energy over charge, so each species and energy has its own $\omega_d$. This is the $\ell = 0$ case of vaft.formula.particle.bounce_harmonic_detuning with $n = -1$. Raises ValueError A non-finite input. Physical interpretation · Assumptions · References Physical interpretation A trapped orbit precessing at $\omega_d$ sees a static $\delta B$ at a Doppler-shifted frequency; where $\omega_d 	o 0$ it sits in a fixed phase of the perturbation and its radial step accumulates – the superbanana plateau, whose flux no longer depends on collisions. Away from it, $
u_\mathrm{eff}$ against $|\omega_d|$ separates the $1/
u$ regime from the $
u$–$\sqrt
u$ regime. Assumptions Bounce-averaged guiding-centre motion; $\omega_E$ constant across the banana width. References K. C. Shaing, Phys. Plasmas 10 (2003) 1443. J.-K. Park, A. H. Boozer and J. E. Menard, Phys. Rev. Lett. 102 (2009) 065002.
